Once upon a time there was a little boy named Ben. Ben loved to explore the world around him. He saw many amazing things, like beautiful vases that were on display in a store. One day, Ben was walking through the store when he came across a very special vase. When Ben saw it he was amazed!
He said, "Wow, that is a really amazing vase! Can I buy it?"
The shopkeeper smiled and said, "Of course you can. You can take it home and show all your friends how amazing it is!"
So Ben took the vase home and he was so proud of it! He called his friends over and showed them the amazing vase. All his friends thought the vase was beautiful and couldn't believe how lucky Ben was.
And that's how Ben found an amazing vase in the store!


Once upon a time, there was a reliable otter named Ollie. He lived in a river with his family. They all loved to play and swim together.

While Ollie was catching fish, he found a big shiny stone. He thought, "This is not a fish, but it is so pretty!" Ollie took the shiny stone home to show his family. They all looked at the shiny stone and smiled. The shiny stone made everyone happy, and they forgot about the fish for dinner.

His friends were very excited. They told him to pick it up and take it home to show his family. So Bob carefully picked up the friendly thumb and carried it back home. When he arrived, Bob happily showed the thumb to his family. His dad was amazed and hugged Bob to show his appreciation.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a deaf boy named Tom. Tom could not hear, but he was very good at seeing and feeling things. He had many friends who loved to play with him. They would play games like tag and hide-and-seek. Tom was very fast and good at finding his friends.
One day, the town bell would ring at noon. Everyone was excited to hear the bell, but Tom knew he could not hear it. He felt sad, but his friends had a plan. They decided to help Tom feel the bell ring too. They took Tom to the big bell and let him touch it while it rang. When the bell rang, Tom could feel the strong vibrations and he smiled.
The moral of the story is that even if someone is different or has a problem, like Tom being deaf, we can still find ways to help them and make them happy. We should always be kind and caring to everyone, no matter how different they are.


Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a large maze made of green bushes. They wanted to try it and find the way out.
They ran inside the maze and followed the paths. Sometimes they turned left, sometimes they turned right. They saw many flowers and birds, but they did not see the exit. They started to feel lost and scared.
They heard a loud roar behind them. It was a big lion who lived in the maze. He was hungry and angry. He wanted to catch Tom and Lily and eat them.
Tom and Lily ran away from the lion. They looked for a place to hide. They saw a small hole in the bushes. They crawled inside and hoped the lion would not find them.
The lion came closer and closer. He smelled Tom and Lily in the hole. He reached his paw inside and tried to grab them. He pinched Lily's leg with his sharp claws. Lily cried out in pain.
Tom was brave and smart. He saw a stick on the ground. He picked it up and poked the lion's eye with it. The lion howled and backed away. He was hurt and afraid.
Tom and Lily saw their chance. They ran out of the hole and out of the maze. They found their mom and dad waiting for them. They hugged them and told them what happened. They were happy and safe. They never went back to the maze again.

Once upon a time, there was a big pumpkin. It was hot outside, and the pumpkin was sad. It wanted to be cool like the other pumpkins in the garden. The pumpkin saw a bird sitting on a tree branch and asked, "Can you teach me how to be cool like the other pumpkins?"
The bird said, "I can teach you how to make a big shade. Then you will be cool like the other pumpkins." The pumpkin was happy to learn from the bird. So, they worked together to make a big shade using leaves and sticks.
But then, a strong wind came and blew the shade away. The pumpkin was sad again. The bird told the pumpkin, "It's okay. Sometimes things don't work out the way we want them to. The important thing is to keep trying and never give up."
The pumpkin learned to be strong and keep trying, even when things were hard. And soon, the weather changed, and the pumpkin was cool and happy like the other pumpkins. The moral of the story is to never give up and keep trying, even when things are tough.


Sara and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to look for bugs and flowers. Sara had a mint plant in a pot. She liked to smell it and taste it. Tom wanted to try it too.
"Can I have some mint?" he asked Sara.
"Sure, here you go," Sara said. She gave him a leaf. Tom put it in his mouth. He made a face. It was very strong and spicy.
"Yuck, I don't like it!" he said. He spat it out. Sara laughed.
"It's good for you," she said. "It makes your breath fresh."
Just then, they heard a loud noise. It was a dog barking. They looked up and saw a big black dog running towards them. It had sharp teeth and a long tongue. It looked angry.
"Help, help!" Sara and Tom shouted. They were frightened. They dropped the mint and ran to the house. The dog chased them.
"Go away, go away!" they cried.
Their mom heard them and came out. She saw the dog and yelled at it.
"Bad dog, bad dog! Leave my kids alone!" she said. She picked up a stick and waved it at the dog. The dog stopped and ran away.
Sara and Tom hugged their mom. They were safe.
"Thank you, mom," they said.
"You're welcome, my loves," she said. "Are you okay?"
"Yes, we're okay," they said.
They told her about the mint and the dog. She smiled and kissed them.
"I'm glad you're okay," she said. "But next time, be careful. Don't go near strange dogs. And don't eat too much mint. It might give you a tummy ache."

Once upon a time there was a fish who was very happy in the water. He swam around with his fish friends and spent all day exploring the deep blue ocean.

The moral of this story is to always be kind and to forgive those who make mistakes. It's important to be patient and understanding with others, even when they do something foolish.

Tim and Jen were twins who liked to play in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat, a scarf and a carrot nose. They named him Bob and gave him a hug.
"Bob is our friend," Tim said. "He will stay with us forever."
"No, he won't," Jen said. "He will melt when the sun comes out. Then he will be gone."
Tim did not like that. He wanted Bob to stay. He got angry at Jen. He threw a snowball at her. Jen threw one back. They started to fight.
"Stop it, you two!" Mom said. She came out of the house. She saw Bob and smiled. "What a nice snowman you made. But you should not fight. Fighting is bad."
"Jen said Bob will melt," Tim said. "I don't want him to melt. I want him to stay."
"Tim, Jen is right," Mom said. "Bob will melt sooner or later. That's what happens to snow. But you can always make another one. And you can take a picture of Bob to remember him."
Tim and Jen did not like that. They did not want another snowman. They wanted Bob. They did not want a picture. They wanted Bob. They cried and hugged Bob.
But Mom was right. The next day, the sun came out. It was warm and bright. Bob started to melt. His hat fell off. His scarf slipped. His carrot nose dropped. His chubby body got smaller and smaller. Tim and Jen watched and cried. Bob was gone. They had no friend. They had no snowman. They had nothing. They were sad.


Once upon a time, in a deep, deep forest, there lived a rabbit and a bear. They were good friends and liked to play together. One day, they decided to play a game called "freeze."
"Let's take turns," said the rabbit. "When I say 'freeze,' you stop moving. When you say 'freeze,' I stop moving."
"Okay," said the bear. "That sounds fun!"
They started to play. The rabbit hopped around and the bear stomped his big feet. The rabbit said, "Freeze!" The bear stopped moving. He stood very still. The rabbit laughed and hopped around him.
Then, it was the bear's turn. He said, "Freeze!" The rabbit stopped hopping and stood very still. The bear laughed and stomped around the rabbit.
After playing for a while, they sat down to rest. The rabbit said, "I like this game. What is your opinion?"
The bear thought for a moment and said, "I like it too. It's fun to play with you."
And so, the rabbit and the bear played "freeze" many more times in the deep, deep forest, always having lots of fun together.

Tom looked at the drain. He was not scared of it. He was curious. He wanted to see how it worked.
"Don't worry, Lily," Tom said. "The drain is not bad. It is just a little hole. It cannot take us away. We are too big. Only the water can go through it. See?"

Lily shook her head. She did not want to try. She did not like the game. She wanted the water to stay.

"Thank you, Tom," Lily said. "You are a good brother. I like the water. I like the toys. I like you."
Tom smiled too. He was a good brother. He liked the water. He liked the toys. He liked Lily.

Lily and Ben were bored. They wanted to play outside, but it was raining. They looked around the house for something fun to do. They saw a big box in the corner. It had a sign that said "Do not open".
"What is in there?" Lily asked.
"I don't know. Let's find out," Ben said.
They opened the box and saw many smaller boxes inside. They had holes and flaps and strings. They looked like a maze.
"Wow, this is cool. Let's make a maze with the boxes," Lily said.
They took out the boxes and arranged them on the floor. They made a long and twisty maze with many turns and dead ends. They crawled inside and explored the maze. They had fun finding each other and hiding and making noises.
They did not hear their mom come home. She walked into the living room and saw the mess. She was grumpy.
"What are you doing? Look at this mess. You are not supposed to open that box. It is for the charity sale," she said.
Lily and Ben came out of the maze. They looked at their mom. They were sorry.
"We are sorry, mom. We were bored. We wanted to play. We discovered a maze in the box. It was fun," Lily said.
Ben nodded. He said, "We are sorry, mom. We did not know. We will help you clean up."
Their mom sighed. She was not so grumpy anymore. She saw that they were just curious and creative. She smiled.
"It's okay, kids. I understand. But next time, please ask me before you open a box. And please be careful with the boxes. They are for a good cause. Now, let's clean up and then we can have a snack. How about that?" she said.
Lily and Ben smiled. They said, "Okay, mom. Thank you, mom. We love you, mom."
They hugged their mom and helped her clean up the maze. They learned a lesson and had a snack. They were happy.

"Hey, stop!" Lila yells. "That's our skull! Give it back!"

Lila and Ben are sad and scared. They cry and hug each other. They order Rex to go away, but Rex does not care. He eats Fluffy and licks his lips.
The end.

The boy was scared of her mom. He dropped Lily and ran away. Her mom picked up Lily and gave her to Anna. She hugged Anna and said, "It's okay, Anna. You have Lily back. She is your angel."
Anna hugged Lily and said, "Thank you, mom. Thank you for saving Lily. I love you and I love Lily."
Her mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Anna. And I love Lily. She is a very special angel."

The monkey smiled. He said, "Yes, I have an idea. I can get my whip and swing it at the trees. Then the trees will fall and you'll have enough wood to build your house!"
The lion liked the idea. He said, "Thank you little monkey! You are so smart!"
The monkey smiled. He grabbed his whip and started swinging it. Soon, enough trees had fallen and the lion was able to build his strong tall house. He was very happy and thanked the little monkey again.
The little monkey was happy too. He was glad he could help his strong lion friend solve his problem.
The end!

She liked to smell the sweet aroma of the cake as it baked. But most of all, she liked to taste the cake when it was done.

She put too much sugar, too little butter, and forgot the eggs. She also added some salt, pepper, and ketchup, because she thought they would make the cake more colorful and spicy.
When the cake was ready, Anna took it out of the oven and put it on a plate. She was very proud of her work. She called her mom and dad to the kitchen and said, "Look, I made a cake for you! Do you want to taste it?"

They said, "Wow, Anna, this is a very...interesting cake. You are very creative and brave to try new things. But you know, sometimes it is better to follow a recipe and measure the ingredients. That way, the cake will be more delicious and more balanced. Do you want to learn how to bake a cake with us next time?"
Anna nodded and said, "Yes, please. I want to learn how to bake a cake like you. I'm sorry, I did not mean to make a bad cake. I just wanted to make you happy."
Her mom and dad hugged her and said, "We are happy, Anna, because you are our daughter and we love you. You are very intelligent and kind, and we are proud of you. But remember, not everything that looks good tastes good. And not everyone who tastes your cake will be as nice as us. Some people might be mean and judge you. So, be careful and listen to your mom and dad, okay?"
Anna said, "Okay, mom and dad. I love you too. And I love cake. Can we bake a cake together now?"
They said, "Of course, Anna. Let's bake a cake together. And let's taste it together too."
The end.

The smart deer and the little girl walked together through the forest. They saw pretty flowers, tall trees, and happy birds. Soon, they found the girl's home. The little girl was so happy and thanked the deer for its help. The smart deer smiled and went back to the forest. From that day on, the girl and the smart deer were the best of friends.


Once upon a time, there was a seal who lived in the sea. The seal liked to play with his friends, the fish. One day, the seal wanted to escape and see the original big world outside the sea.
The seal swam and swam until he reached the land. There, he met a big bird. The seal said, "Hi bird, I escape from the sea to see the big world. Can you show me around?" The bird nodded and said, "Yes, I can show you the big world."
As they went around, the seal became very tired. He missed his friends, the fish, and his home in the sea. The bird took the seal to a very high place. The seal was scared and wanted to go back to the sea. But he could not escape from the high place. The seal was sad and could not go back to his home.

Once upon a time, there was a prince who loved to play. He wore a blue cape and loved to swing around in it while playing. One day, a mean dragon came and wanted to turn him into a puppet.
The prince asked the dragon, "What do you want me to do?"
The dragon laughed and said, "I'm going to turn you into a puppet and I'll pull the strings."
The prince was very scared but he was determined not to let the dragon win. He tried to run away, but the dragon was too fast. He tried to fight back, but the dragon was too strong.
Just when it seemed like the prince was going to give up, a magical fairy appeared. She told the prince, "Be brave and your courage will help you." She gave him a wand and said, "Use this and you will be safe!"
The prince was so thankful and bravely took the wand. With one wave of the wand, a colorful rainbow appeared in the sky. "Follow the rainbow to safety," said the fairy.
The prince did as he was told and followed the rainbow, away from the mean dragon. He was safe at last and felt very playful. He spun around in his cape and laughed with joy.
The prince had learned an important lesson, that courage can help you defeat your enemies.

She runs to her room and takes out her dolls. She picks one doll and puts on a pink dress and a purple hat. She thinks the doll looks very nice. She picks another doll and puts on a blue skirt and a yellow shirt. She thinks the doll looks very cute.
She wants to show her new fashion to her mom. She carries her dolls to the living room, where her mom is reading a book. She says, "Mom, look at my dolls! Auntie sent me new clothes and shoes for them. They are very pretty, right?"
Her mom looks up and smiles. She says, "Yes, they are very pretty, Sara. Auntie is very nice to send you such a nice gift. You are very lucky."
Sara is very happy. She hugs her mom and says, "Thank you, mom. I love you. And I love auntie too."
She wants to show her new fashion to her dad. She carries her dolls to the kitchen, where her dad is making a sandwich. She says, "Dad, look at my dolls! Auntie sent me new clothes and shoes for them. They are very cute, right?"
Her dad looks up and frowns. He says, "Sara, what are you doing? You are making a mess. You dropped some clothes and shoes on the floor. And you are getting crumbs on your dolls. Go back to your room and clean up."
Sara is very sad. She feels angry. She says, "But dad, I just wanted to show you my new fashion. Auntie sent me a nice gift. You are not nice. You are mean."
She runs back to her room, crying. She hugs her dolls and says, "Don't worry, dolls. I still love you. And auntie loves you too. And mom loves you too. But dad is angry. He doesn't like fashion. He is silly."

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Jane. She had the patience of an elephant, and was always happy to help those in need. One day, her mother asked her to iron her dress. Jane had never ironed a dress before, so she was a bit nervous. She asked her mother for help. Her mother told her very patiently, "Just remember, the iron needs to shine."
With a deep breath, Jane started ironing her mother's dress. She was very careful, gently moving the iron on the dress, and letting it shine. She was proud of her work, and even more proud when her mother praised her.
The next day, Jane tackled a bigger challenge - her father's shirt. It was a little tricky, but she remembered her mother's words and patiently ironed it until it shone. She showed it to her father, who gave her an extra hug and said, "Well done, Jane!"
From then on, Jane was known in her family as the "iron queen."

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a ball, a bike and a bell. The bell is on the bike. Lily likes to ring the bell. Ben likes to ride the bike.
One day, they go to the park. Lily says, "Can I ring the bell?" Ben says, "Yes, you can. But be careful. Do not ring it too loud. Some people do not like loud noises." Lily nods. She takes the bell and rings it softly. It makes a nice sound.
Ben gets on the bike. He pedals fast. He feels the wind on his face. He smiles. He sees a big hill. He wants to go down the hill. He thinks it will be fun.
But he is careless. He does not look where he is going. He does not see a dog. The dog is sleeping on the grass. Ben rides the bike over the dog. The dog wakes up. The dog is angry. It barks and chases Ben.
Lily hears the dog. She sees Ben. She is scared. She rings the bell loud. She hopes the dog will stop. But the dog does not stop. It runs faster.
Ben hears the bell. He looks back. He sees the dog. He is scared too. He tries to pedal faster. But he loses his balance. He falls off the bike. He hurts his knee. He cries.
Lily runs to Ben. She drops the bell. She hugs Ben. She says, "I am sorry. I wanted to help you. Are you okay?" Ben says, "I am okay. But my knee hurts. And the bike is broken. And the dog is still here." They look at the dog. The dog is not angry anymore. It is wagging its tail. It licks Ben's knee. It wants to play.
Lily and Ben learn a lesson. They learn to be careful. They learn to look where they are going. They learn to respect the dog. They also learn to share. They give the dog the ball. The dog is happy. They are happy too. They are still friends.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Zoe and Louis. Every day, they would go exploring in the forest to find unusual things.
One day, as they were walking around, they saw a bright diamond. They were so excited to see it and rushed to pick it up.
As soon as they touched it, the diamond started to shine brighter and brighter until it became very hot. Terrified, they threw it away and ran away from it.
Suddenly, an old man appears from behind a tree. He said, "Don't worry! This diamond can serve a special purpose. It can help us find something very unusual!"
The two friends were amazed! They asked how they could use the diamond and the old man told them it was simple. They just had to hold it up in the air and spin in circles.
The two friends followed the instructions and, sure enough, they soon found a hidden cave. Louis and Zoe couldn't wait to find out what was inside!
The old man smiled and said, "This diamond has served its purpose! It has helped you to find something very unusual".
The two friends thanked the old man and, with the diamond in hand, they set off to explore the cave together.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby monkey named Momo. Momo loved to climb trees in the big forest. One day, Momo met a new friend, a small bird named Tweet. Tweet said, "Momo, I can't climb trees like you. Can you help me?"
Momo thought for a moment and said, "Yes, Tweet! I will help you climb the tree." Momo had a plan. He found a long vine and tied it to a high branch. He told Tweet, "Hold on to the vine, and I will pull you up."
As Momo began to pull the vine, something unexpected happened. Tweet was not going up, but Momo was going down! The chubby monkey was too heavy for the little bird. They both laughed and said, "We can't climb the tree together, but we can still play on the ground."
From that day on, Momo and Tweet played together on the ground, and they were the best of friends. And sometimes, Momo would still climb the trees, but he always came back down to play with his friend Tweet.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Jack. He was three years old and loved exploring. One day Jack found a screw on the ground. He picked it up and looked at it. It was a shiny screw with an interesting shape.
Jack paused for a moment, not sure what to do with it. He wanted to keep it as a treasure but he was afraid of getting hurt. Finally, he decided to keep it. He said to himself "This will be my special thing".
Jack took the screw home and kept it in a safe place. But one day, he thought it would be fun to play with it. Without thinking, he put it in the wall and started turning it. Suddenly, the screw got stuck! Jack tried to remove it but he couldn't. He felt bitter because he had made a mistake.
The next morning Jack's dad looked at the wall and saw the screw. He became angry at Jack and yelled "You shouldn't play with these things!" Jack apologized but it was too late. He had to pay a lot of money to repair the wall.
Jack learned a lesson that day. He was very sad and bitter and he never touched a screw again.

Lily and Tom start to fight. They pull and push each other. They knock over the lamp. The lamp falls on the carpet. The carpet catches fire. Lily and Tom are scared. They run out of the room. Lily's mom smells the smoke. She calls the firemen. The firemen come and put out the fire. But the carpet is ruined. The cars are melted. Lily and Tom cry. They are in trouble. They are not friends anymore.

Once upon a time, there lived a vain and ignorant fox. He lived alone in a deep wood, and was happy to be left alone. He never wanted to care for anybody else.
One day, the fox saw a piece of paper lying on the ground. He picked it up and studied it. Suddenly, he heard a family of rabbits scurrying about in the nearby meadow. The fox realised that the lucky rabbits must have dropped the paper!
He called out to them, asking if the paper belonged to them. The father rabbit replied that it did, and the fox offered to return it to them. He left the deep wood and brought the paper to the rabbits.
The fox was a bit surprised by his own kindness. He had never cared for others before. From that day on, he promised to always help others if he could, no matter how ignorant he had been before.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy little fish named Fin. Fin loved to travel in the big blue sea. One day, he saw a big bubble. The bubble had something called oxygen inside it. Fin wanted to play with the bubble.
As Fin swam closer to the bubble, he bumped into it. The bubble wiggled and jiggled. Fin laughed and tried to push the bubble. But he was too clumsy and the bubble popped. The oxygen went out into the water.
Fin was sad that the bubble popped. But then he saw more bubbles with oxygen. He swam and played with them. He was still clumsy, but he had fun. And that is how Fin the fish learned to enjoy his travels in the big blue sea.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lola. She was three. Lola had a key and she wanted to measure it. She took it to her mum and said, "Mum can you help me measure my key?"
Mum smiled and got out a ruler. She measured the key, then said, "It's 8 cm long! Now, why do you need to measure it?"
Lola replied, "Because I was feeling uncomfortable and I needed to see how big the key was."
Mum smiled and said, "That's a good reason! Maybe having the key measured will make you feel better."
Lola smiled and said, "It did! Thanks for helping me, Mum. Now I feel much better."

The engine was very happy and went on its way. But then, something unexpected happened. The engine saw a big pile of rocks on the track. The sneeze made the rocks change into a big, friendly bear. The bear helped the engine move the rocks off the track, and they became good friends.

Sam was a mule who lived on a farm. He liked to eat grass and hay, but he did not like to work. He was lazy and stubborn, and he always said no to the farmer. The farmer was angry with Sam, and he did not give him any treats or hugs.
One day, the farmer had to take some apples to the market. He asked Sam to help him pull the cart, but Sam said no. He wanted to stay in his barn and eat more hay. The farmer was very angry, and he said, "Fine, you can stay here, but you will get no apples or carrots or anything else. You will only eat hay and water, and you will be alone and gloomy."
The farmer left with another mule, who was nice and helpful. Sam did not care. He thought he was smart and happy. He ate some hay and drank some water, and then he took a nap. He did not notice that the sky was getting dark and cloudy, and that a storm was coming.
Soon, it started to rain and thunder and lightning. Sam woke up and felt scared. He did not like the loud noises and the wet wind. He wished he had gone with the farmer and the other mule. He wished he had some apples or carrots or something else to eat. He wished he had someone to hug and talk to. He felt very gloomy and lonely.
He looked out of his barn and saw a little girl walking by. She had a red coat and a yellow hat, and she was holding a basket. She saw Sam and smiled. She said, "Hello, mule. You look sad. Do you want to be my friend?" Sam nodded and said yes. He wanted to be her friend. The girl came closer and opened her basket. She said, "I have some cookies and milk for you. Do you want to eat them?" Sam nodded and said yes. He wanted to eat them. The girl gave him some cookies and milk, and then she hugged him and said, "You are a nice mule. I like you. Do you want to come with me to my house?" Sam nodded and said yes. He wanted to go with her to her house. He felt happy and warm.
The girl and Sam walked away from the barn, and the rain stopped. The sun came out and made a rainbow. Sam looked at the rainbow and smiled. He was glad he had met the girl. He was glad he had eaten the cookies and milk. He was not gloomy anymore. He was a happy mule.

Suddenly, the hole became a big door! Tom walked through the door and found a room full of toys and treats. He was so happy and played all day. The hole in the wall was a magic door, and it made Tom's day full of fun.

Sam liked to watch the fisherman on the lake. He had a small boat and a long rod. He threw the rod into the water and waited for a fish to bite. Sometimes he caught a big fish, sometimes a small fish, sometimes no fish at all. But he always smiled and waved at Sam.
One day, Sam asked his mom if he could go to the lake and talk to the fisherman. His mom said yes, but he had to be careful and not go too close to the water. Sam ran to the lake and saw the fisherman in his boat. He shouted, "Hello, fisherman! Can I see your fish?"
The fisherman heard Sam and rowed his boat to the shore. He said, "Hello, little boy! I'm glad you like my fish. Do you want to see them?" He opened a basket and showed Sam his catch. There were three fish in the basket. One was big, one was medium, and one was tiny.
Sam looked at the fish and said, "Wow, you have a lot of fish! The big one is very big, the medium one is very medium, and the tiny one is very tiny. You are a good fisherman!"
The fisherman smiled and said, "Thank you, little boy. You are very kind. But I am not a good fisherman. I am a modest fisherman. I don't need a lot of fish. I only need enough for me and my cat. The big one is for me, the medium one is for my cat, and the tiny one is for you."
Sam was surprised and happy. He said, "For me? Really? Thank you, fisherman! You are very generous. But how can I eat the fish? I don't have a fire or a pan."
The fisherman said, "Don't worry, little boy. I have a fire and a pan in my boat. Come with me and I will cook the fish for you. But we have to be quick. The sun is going down and it will be dark soon."
Sam agreed and followed the fisherman to his boat. They got in and the fisherman rowed away from the shore. He lit a fire and put a pan on it. He cleaned the fish and put them in the pan. They sizzled and smelled good. Sam and the fisherman waited for the fish to be ready. They talked about the lake, the fish, and the cat. They became friends.
Soon, the fish were cooked. The fisherman gave Sam a plate and a fork. He said, "Here you go, little boy. Enjoy your fish. It is fresh and tasty. But be careful, it is hot."
Sam took the plate and the fork. He said, "Thank you, fisherman. You are very nice. I will enjoy my fish. But I have to hurry. My mom is waiting for me at home. She will be worried if I am late."
The fisherman said, "You're welcome, little boy. I understand. You have to go home. But come back tomorrow and we can fish again. Maybe we will catch more fish. Maybe we will catch a bigger fish. Maybe we will catch a fish that can speed in the water."
Sam said, "That sounds fun, fisherman. I will come back tomorrow and we can fish again. Maybe we will catch a fish that can speed in the water. That would be amazing. Goodbye, fisherman. See you tomorrow."
Sam ate his fish and gave the plate and the fork back to the fisherman. He got out of the boat and ran to his mom. He told her about his adventure and his new friend. He showed her his fish bone. He said, "Look, mom. This is my fish. It was delicious. The fisherman gave it to me. He is modest and generous and nice. He has a cat and a fire and a pan. He cooked the fish for me. He invited me to fish with him tomorrow. Maybe we will catch a fish that can speed in the water. Can I go, mom? Please?"
His mom hugged him and said, "Of course, you can go, Sam. I'm happy you had a good time and made a new friend. The fisherman sounds like a wonderful person. But remember to be careful and not go too close to the water. And don't stay too long. The sun goes down fast and it gets dark soon."
Sam nodded and said, "I will, mom. I will be careful and not stay too long. But I can't wait to fish with the fisherman again. He is my friend. And maybe we will catch a fish that can speed in the water. That would be awesome. Good night, mom. I love you."

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy monkey who liked to climb. Everywhere he went, he was grumpy. One day, he decided to climb a tall wood. He climbed and climbed and climbed, until he was almost at the top. But then, he spotted something. Another monkey was stuck at the highest point of the wood.
The grumpy monkey quickly climbed the rest of the way and reached the other monkey. He asked why the monkey was there, but the other monkey just shrugged. The grumpy monkey figured out that the other monkey had been too grumpy to ask for help and had gotten stuck.
So the grumpy monkey helped his new friend, and they climbed down together. As they were climbing, the grumpy monkey said, "It's important to be nice and ask for help when you need it - even if you don't want to!" The other monkey smiled and agreed.
When they reached the ground, the grumpy monkey went back to his own monkey life, no longer grumpy. He reminded himself that it's important to be kind and to be ready to ask for help - even if you don't want to.

Lena and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big door. The door is red and shiny. It has a sign that says "Do not enter".
"Let's go inside!" Tom says. He is lively and curious. He wants to see what is behind the door.
"No, Tom, we can't!" Lena says. She is careful and scared. She does not want to break the rule. "The sign says no. It is bad to go inside."
But Tom does not listen. He urges Lena to follow him. He pulls her hand and runs to the door. He pushes the door. It is not locked. It opens with a loud creak.
"Wow, look!" Tom says. He sees a lot of toys and games. He sees a train, a doll, a ball, a puzzle, and more. He is happy and excited. He wants to play with everything.
"Tom, we have to go!" Lena says. She sees a man. The man is angry and stern. He is the owner of the toys and games. He does not like children to touch his things. He shouts at Tom and Lena.
"Hey, you two! What are you doing here? This is my room! Get out of here, now!"
Tom and Lena are afraid and sorry. They drop the toys and games. They run to the door. They close the door behind them. They run back to the park.
"Tom, that was bad!" Lena says. She is sad and mad. She does not want to be Tom's friend anymore.
"Sorry, Lena," Tom says. He is ashamed and sorry. He wants to be Lena's friend again. "I was wrong. I should have listened to you. Can we still be friends?"
Lena thinks for a moment. She sees that Tom is sincere and sorry. She decides to forgive him. She nods and smiles.
"Okay, Tom," Lena says. "We can still be friends. But next time, do not urge me to do bad things. And do not go inside doors that say no. It is dangerous and rude."
Tom agrees and hugs Lena. They promise to be good and careful. They go to play in the park again. They have fun and learn. They are friends.

After fixing the hose, Lily and Max took turns watering the flowers. The flowers grew big and colorful, making their garden even more beautiful. Lily felt happy and proud that she had fixed the hose with her dad's help. From that day on, Lily and Max always took care of their garden and their flowers.


Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy robot with a useful arm. He loved to play with his robot all day long.
One day, Tim wanted to test his robot's arm to see how strong it was. So, he asked the robot to pick up a big ball. The robot tried and tried, but it could not pick up the ball. Tim was sad.
Just then, a tiny ant walked by and saw Tim and the robot. The ant said, "I can help you!" The ant walked up to the ball and, with a big push, the ball moved! Tim was so surprised. The ant was so small, but it was very strong. Tim learned that even small things can be useful and strong. And they all played happily together.


Tom and Lily are playing with blocks. They have many blocks of different shapes and colors. They like to build towers and houses with them.
"Look, I made a big tower!" Tom says. He shows Lily his tower of red and blue blocks. It is very tall and has a circle on top.
"Wow, that is nice!" Lily says. She likes Tom's tower, but she wants to make something different. She has a yellow and green block in her hand. It is not a circle, it is a square.
"I want to put this on your tower," Lily says. She tries to put the square on the circle, but it does not fit. It falls down and makes a loud noise.
"Hey, don't do that!" Tom says. He is angry. He does not want Lily to ruin his tower. He pushes Lily away and grabs the square.
"No, this is mine!" Lily says. She is sad. She wants to play with Tom, but he does not share. She pulls the square and tries to take it back.
They both pull and tug on the block. They do not see that their tower is shaking. It is about to fall.
"Stop, stop!" a voice says. It is Mom. She sees the children fighting and the tower wobbling. She runs to them and catches the tower before it crashes.
"Tom, Lily, what are you doing?" Mom says. She is not happy. She does not like to see them fight. She puts the tower on the floor and looks at them.
"Sorry, Mom," Tom and Lily say. They feel bad. They know they were wrong.
"Can you say sorry to each other?" Mom says. She wants them to be nice and make up.
"Sorry, Tom," Lily says. She gives him the square. She does not need it. She can find another block.
"Sorry, Lily," Tom says. He gives her the circle. He does not mind. He can use another block.
They hug and smile. They are friends again.
"Good, now can you play nicely?" Mom says. She is glad. She likes to see them happy.
"Yes, Mom," Tom and Lily say. They nod and look at their blocks.
They have an idea. They can make something together. They can use the circle and the square and the other blocks. They can make an open house. They can put the circle on the door and the square on the window. They can invite Mom to see their house.
They start to build. They are having fun. They are playing with blocks.

Once upon a time there were two children, a brother and a sister, out kayaking together on a quiet lake.
"Watch out!" shouted the brother, as his kayak bumped against the sister's.
Suddenly, a loud noise filled the air, and everything around them seemed to freeze. The brother and sister couldn't move.
"What's happening?" asked the sister.
The brother squinted in the direction of the noise. "There's a big bird over there," he said.
They looked up and saw a huge, white bird hovering in the sky, looking down at them.
The bird flew away and the spell was broken. The brother and sister continued paddling on the quiet lake, and all was as it should be.

Once, there was a parrot who loved flying around the neighbourhood. One day, he saw a rough looking man walking along the path. The parrot recognized him from across the street and swooped down to say hello.
"Hello!" he yelled gleefully. The man stopped and looked at him.
"Ugh," he said, "Get away from me, bird."
The parrot flew away, feeling sad and rejected. He wanted to make friends but it seemed like the rough man didn't want that.
The next day, the parrot spotted the same man walking down the street again. He flew over, determined to make friends this time. He was surprised to see the man pick up a rock and throw it at him.
The rock hit the parrot and he fell to the ground. He didn't move. The man turned and walked away, not recognizing what he had just done.
The parrot never flew again. He lay on the path, lifeless, with no one to recognize him.

Tom and Lily liked to play with their toys. They had a big box of toys in their room. They had dolls, cars, blocks, books, and more. One day, they found a new toy in the box. It was a fake sheep. It was white and soft, and it had wool on its body. It also had a button on its ear.
"What is this?" Tom asked, picking up the sheep.
"Let me see!" Lily said, grabbing the sheep from Tom. She pressed the button on its ear. The sheep made a sound. "Baa, baa, baa!"
Tom and Lily laughed. They liked the sheep. They decided to name it Fluffy.
"Can we keep Fluffy?" Lily asked.
"Sure, why not?" Tom said. "He is our new friend."
They played with Fluffy for a while. They made him jump, run, and eat grass. They also gave him a hat and a scarf. They had fun with Fluffy.
Then, Tom had an idea. He saw a record player on the shelf. It was a toy that could play music and sounds. Tom liked to record his voice and listen to it.
"Hey, Lily, let's record Fluffy!" Tom said.
"Record Fluffy? How?" Lily asked.
"Watch me!" Tom said. He took Fluffy and the record player. He pressed the button on Fluffy's ear and the record button on the player at the same time. Fluffy said, "Baa, baa, baa!" and the player recorded it.
"Wow, that's cool!" Lily said.
Tom pressed the play button on the player. Fluffy's voice came out. "Baa, baa, baa!"
Tom and Lily laughed again. They liked to hear Fluffy's voice. They recorded Fluffy many times. They made him say different things. They made him say, "Hello, I am Fluffy!" and "I love Tom and Lily!" and "I am a happy sheep!"
They had a lot of fun with Fluffy and the record player. They played with them until it was time for dinner. They put Fluffy and the record player back in the box. They hugged Fluffy and said goodbye.
"See you tomorrow, Fluffy!" Tom said.
"We love you, Fluffy!" Lily said.
Fluffy smiled and said, "Baa, baa, baa!"


One day, John went for a walk in a very hot place. It was so hot that he was sweating and scratching an itch on his arm. Then he heard someone talk.
John stopped to listen. It was an old man's voice and he was saying, "Beware, it's a dangerous path ahead!" But John was curious and he wanted to know what was so dangerous, so he decided to keep walking.
As he kept walking, the heat got even hotter and the itch on his arm got worse. Finally, he reached the end of the path and he saw the old man. But he was too late to learn why the old man had warned him - a giant fire was about to engulf John!
John screamed for help but the fire was too big and too hot. He was never seen again.
The old man had been right - he should have listened!

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a big beetle. It is shiny and green. They think it is pretty.
"Let's use the beetle for a game," Tom says. "We can pretend it is a jewel. We are rich and we have a treasure."
"OK," Sam says. "But we have to be careful. We don't want to hurt the beetle. It is alive and it can fly."
They take the beetle to a bench. They put it in a box. They make up a story. They are kings and they have a castle. The beetle is their magic jewel. It can make their wishes come true.
They have fun with the beetle. They wish for candy, toys, and books. They share their wishes with each other. They are happy and kind.
But then, the beetle starts to move. It wants to get out of the box. It makes a noise. It flaps its wings.
"Look, the beetle is awake," Tom says. "It wants to go home. We should let it go."
"Yes, you are right," Sam says. "We had fun with the beetle, but it is not ours. It belongs to the park. We should say thank you and goodbye."
They open the box. They hold the beetle gently. They say thank you and goodbye. They watch the beetle fly away. They smile and wave.
They are still friends. They are still rich. They have each other. And they have a memory.

Sam and Mia were playing in the park. They saw a big bottle on the grass. It was shiny and blue. They ran to the bottle and picked it up.
"Look, it has a cork!" Sam said. "Maybe there is something inside."
"Let's open it and see!" Mia said. She tried to pull the cork, but it was too tight. She could not make it move.
"Here, let me try!" Sam said. He took the bottle from Mia and pushed the cork with his thumb. He pushed hard and hard, until the cork popped out.
"Wow, you did it!" Mia said. She looked inside the bottle. There was nothing but air.
"Maybe it's magic!" Sam said. "Maybe we can make a wish!"
"Okay, let's try!" Mia said. She closed her eyes and said, "I wish for a big cake!"
Sam closed his eyes and said, "I wish for a new bike!"
They opened their eyes and waited. But nothing happened. The bottle was still empty.
"That's not fair!" Sam said. He was angry. He threw the bottle on the ground. It broke into many pieces.
"Hey, don't do that!" Mia said. She was scared. She saw a man coming towards them. He was wearing a uniform and a hat. He looked angry too.
"Who are you?" Sam asked.
"I'm the park ranger," the man said. "And you are in big trouble. Do you know what you did? You released a rare bird that was in that bottle. It was part of a conservation project. Now it's gone and we can't find it. You also littered the park with glass. That's very dangerous and bad for the environment. You should be ashamed of yourselves."
Sam and Mia felt very sorry. They did not know about the bird. They did not mean to be bad. They wanted to say sorry, but they could not find the words. They started to cry.
The man shook his head. He took them by the hand and led them to his car. He said he would take them to their parents and tell them what they did. He said they would have to pay a fine and do some community service. He said they would learn their lesson.
Sam and Mia wished they never found the bottle. They wished they never made a wish. They wished they could go back and do things differently. But it was too late. They had made a big mistake. And they had to face the consequences.

"Maybe we can have just one," Sara said. "Mom won't notice." Tom agreed and they reached for the basket. But Molly saw them and shook her head. She knew they were not supposed to touch the grapes. She made a loud noise and kicked the basket away. The grapes spilled all over the floor and some of them got squashed.
Sara and Tom were scared and angry. They thought Molly was mean and rude. They yelled at her and threw some grapes at her. Molly felt sad and hurt. She did not understand why they were mad at her. She only wanted to help them. She turned away and walked to the corner of the barn.
Soon, their mom came to the barn and saw the mess. She was very upset and asked what happened. Sara and Tom tried to lie and said Molly did it. But their mom did not believe them. She saw the grape juice on their hands and mouths. She knew they were the ones who touched the basket. She scolded them and told them to clean up the barn. She also told them they could not ride Molly for a week.
Sara and Tom felt ashamed and sorry. They realized they had been wrong and unfair to Molly. They cried and said they were sorry to their mom and to Molly. They hugged Molly and gave her some carrots. Molly forgave them and licked their faces. She was happy to have them as friends again.
The moral of the story is: Don't be greedy and dishonest. Listen to your mom and respect your animals. They are your friends and they care for you.

Lily felt sorry for Anna. She said, "Don't weep. Maybe I can help you. Let's look for your flute together."

Anna was happy. She said, "Thank you, Lily. You are very kind. You helped me find my flute."
Lily said, "You're welcome, Anna. I'm glad you have your flute back. Can I play with it too?"
Anna said, "Yes, you can. I'm sorry I was mean to you before. I learned that sharing is good. Sharing makes friends."
They played the flute together and had fun.
The moral of the story is: Sharing is good. Sharing makes friends.

A little bird had an idea. She told the animals to sing a song. They sang together, "Sun, sun, please rise again. We miss your light, our dear friend." The bright sun heard the song and started to rise. The valley was warm and happy again. The animals were so glad that their song worked.


One day, a little rabbit named Tim was playing near his home. He saw a big ball roll past him. Tim wanted to get the ball back. He went to the underground hole where he thought the ball went.
In the underground hole, Tim met a dead tree. The dead tree said, "I'm very sad because I can't grow anymore." Tim felt bad for the tree and wanted to help.
Tim had an idea. He said, "I will pass you some water and soil from outside. Maybe that will help you grow again!" The dead tree was happy and thanked Tim. Tim passed the water and soil to the dead tree. Soon, the tree started to grow again. The tree was happy, and Tim found his ball. They both became good friends and played together every day.

Tim had an idea. He would suggest to his mom that they take Max to the doctor. Tim's mom agreed, and they all went to the doctor. The doctor helped Max feel better, and Tim was happy again. They all went home and had a good rest.

Mia's mommy filled a small tub with water and soap. She told Mia to shut her eyes so she wouldn't get soap in them. Mia shut her eyes tight and put her pink doll in the water. She washed the doll until it was clean. Then, she took it out and let it dry.
Mia was happy that her pink doll was clean again. She promised to take better care of her doll so it wouldn't get dirty again. From that day on, Mia and her pink doll had many more fun days together.

Then, a wise old man came. He said, "You can both have the cane. I will cut it in half." The friends agreed. They both got a piece of the cane. They were happy. They learned to share and yield. The village was happy too.

The brothers kept playing until the sun went down. Then, it was time for them to go home. But first, they split the kite back in two so each brother could take his own half home.
And from then on, the brothers remembered that day and all the fun they had splitting a kite in half.

Susie's mom came over and said, "Come on Susie, let's take a look inside the bag."
So they opened the bag, and it was full of bananas!
The monkey jumped up on Susie's shoulder and started to eat the bananas. He seemed to really like them!
Susie turned to her mom and said, "So what do we call the monkey?"
Her mom smiled and said, "Why not Banana? That would be a perfect name for him."
And so, from that day on, the monkey in the park was known as Banana. Susie's questions had been answered!

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mom and dad. Lily loved to eat fruits because they had a good taste. Her favorite fruit was apple.

Lily and her mom went to Tom's house. Lily and Tom shared the apple and took a bite. Suddenly, they both become very small, just like ants! They were scared, but they knew they had to be brave. They worked together to climb up the table and find a way to become big again.

Tom and Lily were hungry. They wanted to eat pizza for dinner. But Mom said no. She said pizza was not good for them. She said they had to eat soup and salad.
"But Mom, we love pizza!" Tom said. "Pizza is yummy and cheesy and round. Soup and salad are boring and green and wet."
Mom shook her head. "Pizza is not healthy. It has too much fat and salt. Soup and salad have vitamins and fiber. They make you strong and smart. You can have pizza once in a while, but not every day."
Tom and Lily did not like Mom's answer. They made sad faces and crossed their arms. They did not want to eat soup and salad. They wanted to eat pizza.
Dad came home from work. He saw Tom and Lily's sad faces. He asked them what was wrong. They told him that Mom said no pizza for dinner.
Dad looked at Mom. He smiled. He said, "I have a surprise for you. I brought pizza for dinner!"
Tom and Lily's eyes lit up. They jumped up and down. They cheered. They hugged Dad. They said, "Yay! Pizza! Pizza! Pizza!"
Mom looked at Dad. She frowned. She said, "You brought pizza? But I made soup and salad. I told them pizza was not good for them."
Dad shrugged. He said, "I know, I know. But pizza is fun and tasty and easy. Soup and salad are good for you, but they can wait for another day. Sometimes, you have to treat yourself and your family. Don't worry, we'll eat healthy tomorrow."
Mom sighed. She said, "You're right, you're right. Pizza is fun and tasty and easy. And you're a good dad and a wise husband. I love you."
She kissed Dad. She said, "Okay, let's eat pizza. But only one slice each. And we'll have some salad too."
Tom and Lily did not care. They were happy. They had pizza for dinner. They thanked Dad. They said, "You're the best dad ever!"
They ate pizza and salad. They were full and satisfied. They had a good night. They learned that sometimes, pizza is okay. And sometimes, Mom and Dad are wise.

Once upon a time, there was a tall red barn. The barn was home to many animals. The animals liked to play and have fun. One day, a little mouse and a big cow were playing near the tall barn.
The little mouse had a secret. He would whisper the secret to the big cow. The big cow liked secrets. The little mouse said, "I know a fun game. Let's play near the tall tree by the barn."
They went to the tall tree. The little mouse climbed the tree. The big cow tried to climb too, but she was too big. The little mouse laughed and laughed. The big cow felt sad.
The big cow walked away from the tall tree. She was very sad. She went to the barn and cried. The other animals heard her crying. They did not want to play with the little mouse anymore. The little mouse was all alone.


Once upon a time, there was a friendly dog named Spot. Spot lived in a small house with a big yard. Around the yard, there was a fence.
One day, Spot saw a little bird on the fence. Spot said, "Hello, little bird! Do you want to play with me?" The little bird said, "Yes, I want to play with you, Spot!"
They played and played until the sun went down. When it was time for the little bird to go home, it said, "Goodbye, Spot!" Then, the little bird disappeared into the sky. Spot went back to his house and slept, happy to have a new friend.


One day, a boy named Tom found a big, expensive helmet in his yard. He did not know where it came from. Tom thought it was very cool and wanted to play with it. He called his friend, Sue, to come over and see the helmet.
"Look, Sue! I found this big helmet!" Tom said. "Let's play hide and seek with it!" Sue agreed and they started to play. Tom put on the helmet and began to hide. Sue closed her eyes and counted to ten.
When Sue opened her eyes, she saw the helmet moving all by itself! She was very surprised. "Tom, is that you?" she asked. The helmet stopped moving and Tom came out from behind it. "Yes, it's me!" he said, laughing. "I was just hiding behind the helmet!"
Just then, a big wind came and blew the helmet away. Tom and Sue were sad to see it go, but they had fun playing together. They knew they would always remember the day they found the big, expensive helmet.


Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to play sport. He would run, jump, and throw balls all day. One day, while playing, Tim saw a distant balloon in the sky. It was big and round and very far away.
Tim had an idea. He wanted to weigh the balloon. So, he ran to his mom and asked her for help. Mom said, "Let's go to the big tree and see if we can catch the balloon."
As they got closer to the big tree, they saw that the balloon was not a balloon at all. It was a big, round, and very heavy elephant! The elephant had been playing sport too, and he had kicked a ball so high that it had looked like a distant balloon.
Tim and his mom laughed and laughed at the mix-up. They played sport with the elephant all day long, and they all became the best of friends. And that's how Tim learned that sometimes, things are not always what they seem.


Once upon a time, in a big jungle, there was a little monkey named Momo. Momo loved to play with his friends. They liked to jump, run, and call each other's names. One sunny day, Momo and his friends were playing near a clear river.
"Let's jump in the river!" Momo called to his friends. They all jumped in the clear water and splashed around. They were having so much fun. Then, Momo saw something shiny under the water. He swam down and picked it up. It was a shiny, round thing.
Momo showed it to his friends. "What is it?" they asked. Just then, a big frog came hopping by. "That is my special ball!" said the frog. The friends were surprised. They gave the ball back to the frog, and he thanked them with a big smile. From that day on, Momo and his friends played with the frog and his special ball, making their jungle days even more fun.

Suddenly, something caught his eye. He saw a bird in the distance. The bird was flapping its wings and it looked like it was raising its own match.

So, the boy raised his match once again and carefully watched the bird's every move. They kept raising their matches high in the air, and it was a wonderful moment.
In the end, the boy was happy he was able to share a harmless moment with the bird. It was a beautiful sight to see.


Lisa was a little girl who liked to imagine. She had many toys, but her favorite was a rag doll. She called her doll Anna and pretended that Anna was her best friend. They would talk, play, and hug every day.
One day, Lisa's big brother Tom came into her room. He saw Lisa and Anna on the bed and laughed. "What are you doing with that old rag?" he asked. "That's not a real doll. It's ugly and dirty. You should throw it away and get a new one."
Lisa felt sad and angry. She loved Anna and did not want to lose her. She said to Tom, "Anna is not a rag. She is my friend. She is beautiful and kind. You are mean and rude. Go away and leave us alone."
Tom did not listen. He grabbed Anna and ran out of the room. He wanted to tease Lisa and make her cry. He threw Anna into the trash can outside and shouted, "Bye-bye, rag!"
Lisa ran after him and saw what he did. She screamed and cried. She tried to get Anna out of the trash, but it was too high and dirty. She felt helpless and alone.
Mom heard the noise and came outside. She saw Lisa and Tom and asked what happened. Tom told her the truth and said he was sorry. He realized he was wrong and hurt Lisa's feelings. Mom scolded him and told him to apologize to Lisa and give her back Anna.
Tom said he was sorry to Lisa and lifted her up to the trash can. Lisa reached for Anna and hugged her tight. She was happy to have her friend back. She thanked Tom and forgave him.
Mom smiled and hugged them both. She said, "I'm glad you made up. You are brother and sister, and you should love and respect each other. It doesn't matter what your toys look like, as long as they make you happy. And it doesn't matter what others think, as long as you are kind and honest. Remember, the most important thing is what's in your heart."
Lisa and Tom nodded and agreed. They learned a lesson and felt sorry for their fight. They decided to play together and share their toys. They went inside and had a peaceful afternoon. Lisa and Anna were happy, and so was Tom.

The boys learned that sharing their toys and discoveries made playtime more fun. And that day, they also learned that even little things can be amazing when you look closer.

Mia and Leo are best friends. They love to play together in the park. One day, they see a big basket of fruit on a bench. There are apples, bananas, oranges and grapes. Mia and Leo are hungry and curious.
"Can we have some fruit?" Mia asks Leo.
"I don't know. Maybe they belong to someone," Leo says.
They look around, but they don't see anyone. The fruit looks yummy and juicy. Mia and Leo decide to take one apple each. They bite into the apples and smile.
"Mmm, this is so good!" Mia says.
"I agree. This is the best fruit ever!" Leo says.
They finish their apples and throw the cores in the trash. They are about to take another fruit, when they hear a voice.
"Hey, what are you doing with my fruit?" the voice says.
Mia and Leo turn around and see a lady with a big hat and a basket. She looks angry and surprised. Mia and Leo feel scared and sorry.
"We are sorry, lady. We were hungry and we saw your fruit. We only took one apple each. Please don't be mad," Mia says.
The lady looks at them and sees their adorable faces. She sees that they are honest and polite. She feels sorry for them and changes her tone.
"It's okay, kids. I understand. You can have some more fruit if you want. But next time, you should ask before you take something that is not yours. Do you understand?" the lady says.
Mia and Leo nod and say thank you. The lady smiles and gives them each a banana and a grape. Mia and Leo are happy and grateful. They eat the fruit and thank the lady again.
"Can we be your friends?" Mia asks the lady.
"Of course, you can. I'm Lila, by the way. What are your names?" the lady says.
"I'm Mia and this is Leo. We love fruit and we love you, Lila," Mia says.
Lila hugs them and says she loves them too. They become friends and share the fruit. They have a fun and sweet day in the park.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Daniel, who was very gifted in solving puzzles. He feeling excited and curious to try out a challenging puzzle he had just found. He enthusiastically grabbed the puzzle and started to solve it. After a few hours, Daniel had almost solved the entire thing when a strange old man appeared from the shadows of the chamber. He nodded and the old man stepped forward and started to explain the puzzle's solution to him.
At the end of the explanation, the old man said to Daniel: "Now you know the power of knowledge and perseverance. If you use your gifts appropriately, you can achieve anything you want in life". Daniel nodded, feeling grateful and inspired by the old man's wise words.
The moral of the story is that if you use your gifts wisely and with dedication, you can achieve whatever you desire.

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play at the park. They loved to slide on the big slide, but they were afraid of the small slide. The small slide was very high and had a scary view of the road and the cars. Anna and Ben always said, "No, thank you!" when their moms asked them to try the small slide.
One day, Anna and Ben saw a new kid at the park. His name was Sam and he had a red hat. Sam was not afraid of the small slide. He ran to the top and slid down with a big smile. He said, "This is fun! You should try it!"
Anna and Ben looked at each other. They wanted to be brave like Sam, but they were still scared. They decided to watch Sam slide a few more times. Maybe they would feel better.
Sam slid down the small slide again and again. He laughed and waved at Anna and Ben. He said, "Come on, it's not so bad! You can see the trees and the birds and the clouds from up here. It's a beautiful view!"

They smiled at Sam and said, "Thank you for showing us the view. We are ready to slide!" They slid down the small slide together, feeling happy and proud. They had fun and made a new friend. They learned that sometimes, trying new things can be good.


Once upon a time a lonely pup stayed in a big city. Every day this pup sat and watched all of the people go by in their busy lives. The pup wanted to understand why the people were so different, and so he decided to study what they were doing.
One day the pup saw a man who looked kind and gentle. He was walking with a newspaper under his arm, and he smiled when he saw the pup. The pup wagged his tail in excitement and the man stopped to crouch down beside him.
"Why don't you come with me?" said the kind man. "I'm sure you could learn lots of things, if you come and study with me."
The pup was very excited and followed the man, delighted to have found a friend. Every so often, the man would wink at the pup or throw a stick for him to fetch. Soon, the pup admired the man so much and he was so happy to be his friend.
At night, the pup would feel lonely and long for another pup to play with, but even then he still enjoyed studying with the man and learning all he could.
The pup and the kind man spent many happy days together, until one day the pup had to move onto a new home. But the pup will always remember the wonderful friendship they had, and the things he learnt to study.  The pup was never lonely again.


Anna likes to write in her journal every day. She writes about what she sees, what she feels, and what she dreams. She has a journal with many colors and stickers. She keeps it in her drawer under her bed.
One day, Anna goes to the park with her mom and dad. She sees many flowers that bloom. They are pink, yellow, and purple. They smell good and look pretty. Anna wants to write about them in her journal. She asks her mom if she can borrow her pen.
"Sure, sweetie, you can use my pen. But be careful with it, okay? It is a special pen that your grandma gave me. It has a flower on the top that changes color when you write." Mom says.
Anna takes the pen and opens her journal. She writes: "I see flowers that bloom. They are..." But before she can finish, she hears a loud bark. A big dog runs towards her and jumps on her. The dog is friendly, but he is also bad. He knocks down Anna and makes her drop the pen and the journal. The pen breaks and the ink spills on the journal. The flower on the top stops changing color. The journal is ruined.
Anna cries. She is sad and scared. The dog's owner comes and takes the dog away. He says he is sorry and that the dog is just playful. He gives Anna a hug and a candy. But Anna is still sad. She looks at her mom and says: "Mom, I'm sorry. I broke your pen and your journal. I didn't mean to. I was just writing about the flowers that bloom."
Mom hugs Anna and says: "It's okay, honey. I know you didn't mean to. Accidents happen. I'm not mad at you. I'm glad you're not hurt. And I'm proud of you for writing in your journal. You are a good writer. You can always get a new pen and a new journal. But you can't get a new Anna. You are my special flower that blooms. I love you."


Ben and Mia were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big puddle on the grass. It was shiny and wet.
"Let's splash in the puddle!" Ben said. He ran to the puddle and jumped in. He made a big splash. Water went everywhere.
Mia followed him. She jumped in the puddle too. She laughed and clapped. She liked the water on her face and feet.
But then, something bad happened. Ben slipped and fell in the puddle. He got wet and muddy. He started to cry. He felt helpless. He could not get up.
"Mia, help me!" Ben said. He reached out his hand.
Mia saw Ben. She felt sorry for him. She ran to him and grabbed his hand. She tried to pull him up. But she was too small. She could not move him.
She looked around. She saw a big stick on the ground. She had an idea. She let go of Ben's hand and picked up the stick. She went back to the puddle.
"Ben, don't cry. I have a stick. I will poke you with the stick. Then you can push yourself up." Mia said.
She poked Ben with the stick. Ben felt the stick on his back. He pushed himself up. He got out of the puddle. He was still wet and muddy, but he was happy.
"Thank you, Mia. You are a good friend. You helped me." Ben said.
He hugged Mia. Mia hugged him back. They smiled at each other.
They went to the bench. They found their mom. She had a towel and a change of clothes. She cleaned them and dressed them. She gave them a hug and a kiss.
They were happy. They learned a lesson. They learned to help each other. They learned to be careful with puddles. They learned to have fun.

Tom and Lily were very happy. They were going on a holiday with Mum and Dad. They packed their bags and got in the car. They drove for a long time and saw many things. They saw cows and sheep and trees and flowers.
They arrived at a big house near the sea. It was their holiday home. They ran inside and chose their rooms. Tom picked a room with a big bed and a window. Lily picked a room with a small bed and a shelf. On the shelf, there was a toy. It was a orange dinosaur. Lily liked dinosaurs. She took the toy and hugged it.
"Look, Tom, I found a dinosaur!" Lily said.
"Wow, that's cool!" Tom said. "Can I see it?"
Lily gave the toy to Tom. He looked at it and pressed a button. The toy made a loud roar. Tom and Lily laughed. But then, something strange happened. The toy started to shrink. It became smaller and smaller until it was the size of a coin.
"Tom, what did you do?" Lily cried.
"I don't know!" Tom said. "I just pressed the button!"
They tried to press the button again, but nothing happened. The toy was too small. They could barely see it.
"Mum, Dad, help!" Tom and Lily shouted.
Mum and Dad came to their room. They saw the tiny toy on the floor.
"What happened?" Mum asked.
"The dinosaur shrank!" Lily said.
"How did that happen?" Dad asked.
"Tom pressed the button!" Lily said.
"I'm sorry, Lily," Tom said. "I didn't mean to."
Mum and Dad looked at the toy. They saw a label on it. It said: "Shrink-o-saur. The toy that shrinks when you press the button. Fun for all ages. Batteries not included."
"Oh, dear," Mum said. "This is a very silly toy. Who would make such a thing?"
"I don't know," Dad said. "But maybe we can find a way to make it big again."
They took the toy and went to the kitchen. They looked for something that could make it grow. They tried water, milk, bread, honey, and salt. But nothing worked. The toy stayed small.
"Maybe we should just leave it alone," Mum said. "Maybe it will grow back by itself."
"Or maybe we can buy a new one," Dad said. "A bigger one. A better one."
Tom and Lily felt sad. They liked the orange dinosaur. They didn't want a new one. They wanted the old one.
"Can we keep it?" Lily asked.
"Of course, you can," Mum said. "But you have to be very careful. It's very small. You might lose it."
Tom and Lily nodded. They put the toy in a box. They made a bed for it with cotton and paper. They gave it a name. They called it Tiny.
They hoped that Tiny would grow back. But they also loved it as it was. They played with it every day. They took it to the beach, to the park, to the shops. They showed it to their friends. They told them the story of how it shrank.
They had a lot of fun with Tiny. They had a good holiday. They never forgot the orange dinosaur.

Their mom hugged them back and said, "I love you too, Lily and Ben. But you have to be careful and follow the rules. The road is not a place to play. The park is a place to play. Let's go back to the park and play with the ball. But first, let's wash our faces and hands. The smoke made them dirty."
Lily and Ben agreed. They followed their mom back to the park. They washed their faces and hands in a fountain. They felt better. They saw their ball. Mom says, "It is okay to say sorry, but you also need to learn to share. Sharing is caring. How about you take turns playing with the motorcycle? You can each have five minutes. Then you can switch. Does that sound fair?" Sam and Lily nod. They say, "Okay, Mom."

But the dog was scared of people. He would not come to Lily and her mom. Lily had an idea. She took her crayons and paper and made a big sign. The sign had a picture of a happy dog and said, "You are welcome here."
Lily and her mom put the sign near the dog. The dog saw the sign and knew he was safe. He came to Lily and her mom. They gave him food and love. The dog was happy and did not suffer anymore. They all became good friends and lived happily ever after.


Once upon a time, there was an otter who was very clumsy. He stumbled around, always making a huge mess. He realized that he was not very neat and decided to clean up.
But, even when the otter cleaned, he was still very clumsy. No matter how hard he tried, he just could not seem to keep things neat. The otter got very frustrated and started to cry.
Soon, someone noticed the otter's mess and came to help him. But instead of cleaning up, the person just shook their head and walked away.
The otter was now all alone and he cried even harder. He accepted that he could not clean and that his mess would stay forever. He was very sad and his bad ending had come true.


Once upon a time, there was a big cat named Tom. Tom was not a normal cat. He had a very special taste for food. He liked to eat fish, but he did not like to eat mice like other cats. One day, Tom saw a big fish in the pond. He wanted to catch the fish and eat it.
Tom met his friend, a little bird named Sue. Sue asked Tom, "What are you doing?" Tom said, "I want to catch the fish." Sue had an idea. She told Tom to lie down and pretend to be asleep. She said, "When the fish comes near, you can catch it."
Tom did what Sue said. He lied down and closed his eyes. The fish saw Tom and thought he was asleep. The fish swam closer and closer to Tom. Just as the fish was about to touch Tom's nose, Tom opened his eyes and caught the fish.
Tom was very happy. He thanked Sue for her help. They both sat down to eat the fish together. From that day on, Tom and Sue were the best of friends. And Tom learned that it was good to have a friend who could help him catch his food.

Then, something unexpected happened. Tim heard a soft sound behind him. He turned around and saw a little bird hiding too! The bird was playing hide and seek with its family. Tim smiled and felt happy. He had found a new friend to play with, and they played hide and seek together all day long.

Then, something unexpected happened. The stone started to glow! Tim and the dog were surprised. The stone turned into a beautiful, shiny toy. Tim and the dog played with the toy and became best friends.

One day, Tom and Sue were playing in the park. They saw a long piece of paper on the ground. "Let's make a big picture!" said Sue. They needed scissors to cut the paper, so they started to search for them.
Tom looked under a big tree and Sue looked near the swings. Then, they heard a funny sound. "Ribbit, ribbit!" said a frog. "Hello, frog! Do you know where we can find scissors?" asked Tom. The frog jumped and showed them a hidden box.
When they opened the box, they found big scissors inside. But, the scissors were not normal scissors. They were magic scissors! As they started to cut the paper, the pictures they made came to life. A big, happy sun and a cute dog jumped out of the paper. Tom and Sue were very surprised and played with their new friends all day.

One day, the stream looked troubled. The water was not clear, and it had a bad smell. Bobo was sad because he could not drink from the stream. He did not want to play near it anymore.
Bobo decided to find out what made the stream troubled. He followed the stream and found a big pile of trash. Bobo knew he had to clean it up. He asked his friends, the birds and the squirrels, to help him. They all worked together to clean the trash. After they finished, the stream was clear and pretty again. Bobo was happy, and he could spring and play by the stream once more.

They took the boat outside and ran to the pond. They put the boat in the water and watched it float. It was a regular boat, with a sail and a flag. They were happy.
But then, they saw a duck. The duck was hungry. It saw the boat and thought it was food. It swam to the boat and bit the sail. The boat tipped over and sank.
Tom and Sam were sad. They ran to the duck and shouted. "Bad duck! Give us back our boat!" The duck was scared. It quacked and flew away.
Tom and Sam looked at the pond. They could not see their boat. It was gone. They cried and hugged each other. They wished they had a different toy.


Once upon a time, in a big green forest, there was a little red bird named Tim. Tim was a very foolish bird. He liked to carry things in his beak and show off to his friends. One day, Tim found a shiny stone near a pond. He was so happy and wanted to show everyone.
Tim carried the shiny stone to his friend, the big brown bear. "Look at my shiny stone!" said Tim. The big brown bear looked at the shiny stone and said, "That's nice, Tim. But be careful not to drop it in the pond!"
Tim did not listen to the big brown bear. He wanted to show the shiny stone to his friend, the tiny green frog. As Tim flew over the pond, he dropped the shiny stone. It fell into the water with a big splash. Tim was so sad.
The tiny green frog saw what happened and jumped into the pond. With a big smile, the tiny green frog carried the shiny stone back to Tim. Tim was so happy and said, "Thank you, tiny green frog! I will be more careful next time."
From that day on, Tim was not foolish anymore. He learned to be careful and listen to his friends. And they all lived happily ever after in the big green forest.

While her mom was gone, Sue saw a cookie sheet on the table. She thought, "Maybe I can put the cookies in the oven for my mom." She forgot her mom's warning and opened the oven. The hot air came out and Sue felt scared. She quickly closed the oven door and decided to wait for her mom.
When her mom came back, Sue told her what happened. Her mom was happy that Sue was safe and said, "Thank you for telling me, Sue. Remember to always listen to warnings. They are there to keep you safe."
From that day on, Sue always listened to warnings and stayed safe. She learned that it's important to listen to her mom and to not do things she's not ready for.

"Look, Lily, the sun is smiling at us!" Tom says. He points to the sun.
Lily laughs. She thinks Tom is silly. "The sun is not smiling, Tom. The sun is just a light. It does not have a face."
Tom does not agree. He thinks Lily is silly. "The sun does have a face, Lily. It has eyes and a nose and a mouth. It is happy to see us."
They start to argue. They yell at each other. They do not listen to each other. They are not having fun.
A bird flies by. It sees Lily and Tom. It hears them yell. It thinks they are silly too. It lands on a branch near them. It makes a loud noise. It sounds like "squawk, squawk, squawk!"
Lily and Tom stop yelling. They look at the bird. They are surprised. They think the bird is funny. They laugh.
The bird flies away. It is happy. It likes to make people laugh.
Lily and Tom look at each other. They are sorry. They hug.
They look at the sun again. They see it is still bright. They think it is beautiful.
They decide to play together. They do not yell anymore. They are happy too.
