Once upon a time, there was a little train. Its engine was old and loud, but the little train was very happy with it. Every day it would meet all the other trains on the railway, and they would talk and share stories. But one train was very envious. It was brand new and had a much better engine than the little train. It wished that its engine could be just like the little train's engine.
One day, the little train's engine broke down. It couldn't move. The envious train was thrilled. It thought this was the perfect chance for it to get its wish. It slyly suggested to the little train that it should switch engines.
But the little train answered, "No thank you. Even though my engine is old, it is still my best friend. We can't switch."
The envious train was so surprised. It had never had a friend like that before. It quickly made a new friend with the little train and they have been friends ever since. The little train taught the envious train that there is more to friendship than having the best engine.


Lily and Max were twins who liked to play and have fun. But sometimes they did not behave very well. They did not listen to their mom or dad, and they made a lot of noise and mess.
One day, mom and dad had to go to work, and they left Lily and Max with their grandma. Grandma was very kind and sweet, but she also had some rules. She told Lily and Max to behave and to eat their lunch when she made it.
Lily and Max nodded, but they did not really mean it. As soon as grandma went to the kitchen, they started to run around the house, playing with toys, books, and clothes. They threw things on the floor, on the sofa, and on the bed. They laughed and shouted and did not care about anything.
Grandma heard the noise and came back to the living room. She saw the mess and was very angry. She said, "Lily and Max, what are you doing? This is not how you behave! You have to clean up this mess right now, and then you have to eat your lunch!"
Lily and Max looked at grandma and felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, grandma. We were just having fun. We will clean up and eat our lunch."
Grandma smiled and said, "Thank you, my dears. I know you like to have fun, but you also have to be respectful and polite. Now, come and see what I made for you. It is something very unusual and yummy!"
Lily and Max followed grandma to the kitchen and saw their lunch. It was a big plate of pancakes with bananas, chocolate, and whipped cream. They had never seen such a lunch before. They said, "Wow, grandma, this is unusual! But it looks so good! Can we try it?"
Grandma said, "Of course, you can. This is a special treat for you, because I love you very much. But you have to promise me that you will behave better from now on, okay?"
Lily and Max nodded and said, "We promise, grandma. We love you too. And we love your unusual lunch!" They hugged grandma and then ate their pancakes with joy. They learned their lesson and decided to behave better from then on.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the park. They saw a big slide and ran to it. Tom wanted to go first, but Sam was faster. He climbed up the ladder and sat on the slide. Tom was angry and shouted, "Move, Sam! It's my turn!"
Sam did not listen. He smiled and said, "No, Tom. I go first. You are too slow." He pushed his feet and slid down the slide. He laughed and said, "That was fun!"
Tom was more angry. He climbed up the ladder and saw Sam waiting at the bottom. He wanted to make Sam fall. He thought, "I will push him hard and he will cry." He did not see the guard who was watching them.
The guard saw Tom and knew he was going to be foolish. He said, "Stop, Tom! Don't push your brother. That is not nice. You can hurt him and yourself." He walked to the slide and reached for Tom.
But Tom did not stop. He pushed Sam with his hands and said, "Ha, ha, Sam! Take that!" He did not know that Sam was ready. Sam moved to the side and dodged Tom's push. Tom lost his balance and fell off the slide. He landed on the ground and hurt his knee. He cried and said, "Ow, ow, ow!"
The guard picked up Tom and said, "See, Tom? That was foolish. You should not push your brother. You should share and be kind. Now you have a boo-boo and you need a band-aid." He took Tom to his mom and gave him a band-aid.
Sam felt sorry for Tom. He said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I should not have teased you. You can go first next time." He hugged Tom and said, "Let's play something else. How about the swings?"
Tom said, "Okay, Sam. I'm sorry, too. I should not have pushed you. You are my brother and I love you." He hugged Sam and said, "Let's go to the swings. Maybe the guard will push us." They ran to the swings and had fun. The guard smiled and said, "That's better. Good boys."

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim was a happy boy who loved to play with his friends. One day, Tim and his friends wanted to have a meeting. They wanted to talk about a new game they could play.
At the meeting, Tim's friend, Sam, showed everyone a big, fake toy. It looked like a real toy, but it was not. Sam told everyone that they could play a game with the fake toy. They would take turns trying to make the toy yield, or give in, by pressing a button.
Tim and his friends started to play the game. They took turns pressing the button on the fake toy, but nothing happened. They tried harder and harder, but the toy would not yield. They started to get sad and upset. The game was not fun anymore.
In the end, the friends stopped playing with the fake toy. They were not happy, and the meeting was a bad one. Tim and his friends learned that sometimes, it is better to play with real toys and have fun together, rather than trying to make something fake work.

Bill and the flower said goodbye and Bill flew back home. He felt so happy that he had helped the sad flower find its friends.

Tom and Sam wanted to be rich too. They thought, "Maybe if we study more, we will be rich like Mr. Rich." They decided to study more and more and more. They stopped playing with dough and other toys. They only studied all day and all night.

They decided to go to Mr. Rich's house and ask him how he became rich. They knocked on his door and waited. Mr. Rich opened the door and looked at them. He said, "Who are you and what do you want?"
Tom and Sam said, "We are Tom and Sam. We are your neighbors. We want to know how you became rich. We want to be rich like you."
Mr. Rich smiled and said, "Come in, come in. I will tell you my story. But first, do you want to play with some dough? I have a lot of dough in my kitchen. I like to play with dough and make things. It makes me happy."
Tom and Sam were surprised and happy. They said, "Yes, we love to play with dough. We used to play with dough a lot, but then we stopped. We thought we had to study more to be rich."
Mr. Rich said, "Studying is important, but so is playing. You need to do both. You need to learn new things, but also have fun and be creative. That is how I became rich. I studied hard, but I also played hard. I used my dough to make inventions and sell them. I also made friends and helped others. That is how I became rich and happy."
Tom and Sam learned a valuable lesson. They thanked Mr. Rich and went back to their homes. They decided to study and play with dough every day. They also invited their other friends to join them. They were not rich in money, but they were rich in happiness.

Tom said, "No, Sara, that is not a turkey. That is a chicken."
Sara said, "How do you know, Tom? Did you ask the bird?"
Tom said, "No, I did not ask the bird. I just guess. I know what a turkey looks like. A turkey has a big tail that opens like a fan. This bird does not have a big tail."
Sara said, "Maybe this bird is a baby turkey. Maybe its tail will grow bigger when it gets older."
Tom said, "No, Sara, you are wrong. This bird is a chicken. I am sure."
Sara and Tom started to argue. They did not agree on what the bird was. They did not listen to each other. They did not have fun.
Then, they heard a voice from the house. It was Mom. She said, "Sara, Tom, come inside. It is time for lunch. I made you a sandwich with turkey and cheese."
Sara and Tom ran to the house. They were hungry. They said, "Sorry, Mom, we were playing."
Mom said, "That is okay, my loves. But next time, try to be more honest with each other. If you are not sure about something, you can say, 'I think' or 'I wonder' instead of 'I know' or 'I guess'. That way, you can learn from each other and have more fun."
Sara and Tom nodded. They said, "Okay, Mom, we will try to be more honest. Thank you for the lunch. We love turkey and cheese."
Mom smiled. She said, "You are welcome, my loves. I love you too. Enjoy your lunch."

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to dig holes and find bugs and worms. They also liked to eat snacks that Mom gave them. Today, Mom gave them some crackers and cream. Cream was white and soft and yummy.
"Look, I found a big worm!" Tom said, holding a long, brown thing in his hand.
"Let me see!" Lily said, running to him. She saw the worm and made a face. "That's not a worm, Tom. That's a snake!"
"A snake?" Tom said, dropping it. "But it's not scary. It's not moving."
"That's because it's dead, Tom. It's rotting. That means it's old and bad and smelly. You don't want to touch it. It can make you sick."
"Yuck!" Tom said, wiping his hand on his shirt. "I don't like rotting things. They're gross."
"Me neither," Lily said. "Let's go eat our snacks. They're fresh and good and tasty."
They ran to the picnic blanket where Mom had left their snacks. They picked up their crackers and cream and took big bites. They smiled and chewed.
But they didn't notice that the cream had been in the sun for too long. It had turned sour and lumpy. It was rotting too.
Soon, they felt sick in their tummies. They spit out the cream and cried.
"Mom! Mom!" they called. "The cream is bad! It's rotting!"
Mom heard them and came running. She saw the cream and smelled it. She made a face too.
"Oh, no!" she said. "I'm sorry, kids. I forgot to put the cream in the cooler. It went bad in the heat. You shouldn't eat it. It can make you sick."
She hugged them and gave them some water to drink. She threw away the cream and the crackers.
"Are you okay?" she asked.
Lily and Tom nodded. They felt better after drinking the water. They learned their lesson.
They never ate rotting things again. They only ate fresh and good and tasty things.
And they stayed away from distant snakes.

Tim and Sam smiled and hugged the card and the gift. They thanked the mailman and said they loved their grandma. They said they would not play with the mailbox anymore. They said they would play with the puzzle instead. They ran inside to show their mom and dad.
The mailman smiled and got back in his truck. He was glad that Tim and Sam learned their lesson. He hoped they would have fun with the puzzle and be more clever and kind. He drove away to deliver more mail.

"Hi, bear!" said the bunny. "Yes, I want to play with you. Let's make a snowman!"

The bear and the bunny were happy with their snowman. They played all day in the icy snow, and they were the best of friends.

The sun shone brightly, lighting up the sky like a bulb. Little Manny and his mother were excited. They had seen a poster and knew that today was 'Display Day' at the museum.
Manny ran around the grounds, looking at each and every display that he could find. His mother watched with admiration, thankful for his little bursts of energy. At the very end of the grounds, Manny found a unique display. In the centre of a garden was a glass bulb filled with a beautiful glowing light. Suddenly, Manny ran forward, reaching out to grab the bulb.
"No, Manny!" his mother called out, moving quickly to grab him. But it was too late. Manny had already touched the bulb and it started spinning rapidly. Manny and his mother stepped back in shock.
The sound of an alarm filled the air and the museum guards ran towards them. In a voice that was surprisingly calm, the chief guard explained that the bulb was part of a special display to show what happened when things weren't handled with care.
Little Manny looked down at the ground, feeling guilty and sad. His mother hugged him and told him that it was okay, even though she knew it wasn't. Manny had learned a special lesson today - to always handle things with gentleness and care.

"Oh, no!" grandma and grandpa say. They are worried. They call Sara and Ben. They call Spot. They want them to come back.
But Sara and Ben do not hear them. They are too far. They are on the street. They see Spot and the cat on the roof of another house. They see a ladder. They climb the ladder. They want to get Spot and the cat.
But the ladder is old. It is weak. It breaks. Sara and Ben fall. They land on a pile of leaves. They are not hurt. But they are scared. They cry.
Spot and the cat hear them. They stop fighting. They look at them. They feel sorry. They come down from the roof. They go to them. They lick them. They are not loud. They are quiet.
Sara and Ben hug them. They are happy. They are not scared. They stop crying.
Grandma and grandpa find them. They are relieved. They hug them. They are glad. They are not angry. They smile.
They take them back to the house. They fix the fence. They give them cookies and milk. They read them the book. They are not loud. They are calm.
Sara and Ben say thank you. They say sorry. They say goodbye. They love their grandma and grandpa. They love Spot and the cat. They had a good visit. They will come back soon.

One day, a little bear and his mama went to look for honey in the forest. The little bear loved honey very much and wanted to eat it all the time. His mama told him to listen carefully and follow her, because there were many dangers in the forest.
"Listen, little bear, we have to be quiet and sneaky. There are big bees that guard the honey, and they can sting us if they see us. There are also other animals that like honey, and they can be mean and scary. Do you understand?" his mama said.
"Yes, mama, I understand. I will listen and follow you. I want to eat honey, but I don't want to get hurt or scared," the little bear said.
They walked and walked until they found a big tree with a hole in it. The little bear smelled honey and got very excited. He ran towards the tree, forgetting to listen and follow his mama. He stuck his head inside the hole and saw a lot of honey. He licked his lips and reached his paw inside.
But then he heard a terrible buzz. The big bees had seen him and were angry. They flew out of the hole and started to sting the little bear. The little bear cried out in pain and fear. He pulled his head and paw out of the hole, but it was too late. He was covered in stings and bumps.
His mama heard his cry and ran to help him. She scared away the bees and hugged the little bear. She licked his wounds and comforted him.
"I'm sorry, mama, I didn't listen and follow you. I was too greedy and foolish. The honey was not worth it. The bees were terrible and hurt me a lot," the little bear said.
"It's okay, little bear, I forgive you. You made a mistake, but you learned a lesson. Next time, you will listen and follow me, and we will find honey safely and happily. Now let's go home and rest. I love you, little bear," his mama said.
They walked back home, holding paws. The little bear felt sorry and sore, but also loved and grateful. He decided to listen and follow his mama from then on, and to share the honey with her and his friends. He realized that honey was sweet, but love was sweeter.

"Look, Ben, look!" Lily said. "Strawberries! Let's pick some and eat them!"
"OK, Lily, OK!" Ben said. "But we have to be quick. Mom said not to go near the plant. She said it belongs to Mr. Fox, the mean old man who lives next door."
Lily and Ben did not listen to Mom. They ran to the plant and picked some strawberries. They put them in a basket and hid behind a bush. They talked and laughed and ate the strawberries. They did not see Mr. Fox watching them from his window.
Mr. Fox was angry. He did not like children. He did not like sharing his strawberries. He grabbed his cane and went outside. He walked to the bush where Lily and Ben were hiding. He shouted and waved his cane.
"Hey, you little thieves! Get away from my plant! Give me back my strawberries! Or I will hit you with my cane!"
Lily and Ben were scared. They dropped the basket and ran away. But Mr. Fox was faster. He caught Ben by his shirt and pulled him back. He raised his cane and hit Ben on his head. Ben cried and fell to the ground.
Lily saw what happened. She screamed and ran to Ben. She tried to help him. But it was too late. Ben was not moving. He was not talking. He was not breathing. He was dead.
Lily was sad. She was alone. She wished she had listened to Mom. She wished she had never seen the large strawberry plant. She wished she had never met Mr. Fox.


Ben liked to play with his toy soldiers. He had many of them, and he gave them names and voices. He made them march and fight and hide in his room. He was very adventurous and liked to pretend he was a soldier too.
One day, he found a new soldier in his toy box. He was shiny and red, and he had a big hat and a sword. Ben was curious and picked him up. He said, "Hello, soldier. What is your name?"
The soldier did not reply. He was very still and quiet. Ben shook him and tapped him, but he did not make a sound. Ben was puzzled and sad. He wanted to play with the new soldier, but he did not talk.
He put the soldier on his bed and went to look for his mom. He found her in the kitchen and said, "Mom, I have a new soldier, but he does not reply. Why is he so quiet?"
Mom smiled and hugged Ben. She said, "That is a special soldier, Ben. He is not a toy, he is a decoration. He is made of metal and he does not have a voice. He is very pretty, but he is not for playing."
Ben was disappointed and confused. He said, "But I want to play with him. He looks so adventurous and brave. Can I not make him talk?"
Mom shook her head and said, "No, Ben, you cannot. He is not like your other soldiers. He is for looking, not for touching. He might break or scratch if you play with him. Why don't you leave him on your shelf and play with your other soldiers? They are more fun and they reply to you."
Ben nodded and said, "Okay, Mom. I will do that. But can I still look at him sometimes?"
Mom said, "Of course, Ben. You can look at him as much as you want. He is very handsome and he is yours. But remember, he is a decoration, not a toy."
Ben said, "I understand, Mom. Thank you for the new soldier. He is very nice, even if he does not reply."
He gave Mom a kiss and ran back to his room. He put the shiny red soldier on his shelf and looked at him. He smiled and said, "Hello, soldier. You are very pretty. I hope you like your new home. Maybe one day, you will reply to me."

Anna does not know what a birth certificate is. She says, "I don't know. What is that?"
The man says, "It is a paper that says when and where you were born. It has your name and your mom's name. Do you have it in your backpack?"
Anna shakes her head. She says, "No, I don't have it. I have toys and books."
The man says, "Hmm, that is a problem. You can't go on the plane without a passport or a birth certificate. You have to stay here."
Anna is scared. She does not want to stay here. She wants to go with mom and see grandma. She starts to cry. She says, "Please, let me go. I want to see grandma. I don't have a passport, but I have a backpack. Can I try to go with my backpack?"
The man sees that Anna is very sad. He feels sorry for her. He says, "OK, little girl, I will let you try. But you have to promise me something. You have to promise me that you will get a passport as soon as you can. A passport is very important. Do you promise?"
Anna nods. She says, "Yes, I promise. Thank you, thank you, thank you!"
The man says, "You're welcome, little girl. Now, go and hug your mom and get on the plane. Have a nice trip and say hello to grandma for me."
Anna runs to mom and hugs her. She says, "Mom, I can go. The man let me try. He said I need a passport, but I can go with my backpack. He was very nice."
Mom is surprised and relieved. She says, "Oh, Anna, I'm so glad. I'm sorry, I forgot to bring your birth certificate. We will get you a passport as soon as we can. Now, let's go and see grandma. She is waiting for us."
They go to the plane and find their seats. Anna looks out the window and sees the clouds. She is very happy. She says, "Mom, I love you. I love grandma. I love my backpack. And I love the man who let me try."

Their friends laughed at them. They said the new ball was silly and useless. They said the old ball was better and more fun. They said Tom and Lily were mean and greedy. They did not want to play with them anymore. They took the old ball and played with each other.
Tom and Lily felt sad and sorry. They wished they had listened to mom and dad. They wished they had not taken the money and bought the new ball. They wished they had been kind and generous to their friends. They learned a lesson. They decided to take the new ball back to the shop and get their money back. They decided to apologize to mom and dad and to their friends. They decided to play with the old ball and share it with everyone. They decided to be happy with what they had.

Anna liked to draw with her crayons. She had many colors and shapes on her paper. She was happy and proud of her art. But then she saw a big mistake. She had drawn a blue sun instead of a yellow one. She wanted to fix it, but she did not have a yellow crayon.
She looked around and saw an eraser on the table. It was enormous, bigger than her hand. She thought it could erase her blue sun. She grabbed it and rubbed it on her paper. But nothing happened. The blue sun was still there. She rubbed harder and harder, but the eraser did not work.
She was confused and sad. She asked her mom, who was sitting next to her. "Mom, why does this eraser not erase?" She showed her mom the eraser and the paper.
Her mom smiled and hugged her. "That is not an eraser, my dear. That is a sponge. It is for cleaning, not for erasing. It can make things wet, but not vanish. If you want to erase something, you need a different kind of eraser. Like this one." She gave Anna a small pink eraser that fit in her hand.
Anna tried the pink eraser on her paper. It worked! The blue sun vanished and left a white space. Anna was happy and thanked her mom. She found a yellow crayon and drew a new sun. She liked her art again. She learned that not all things that look like erasers are erasers. And that sometimes, mistakes can be fixed.


Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. He liked to play near the stream. One day, he saw a weak frog sitting by the water. "Hello, little frog," said Tom. "Why are you so weak?"
The frog looked up at Tom and said, "I need help. I need to add some water to my pond so I can swim and get strong again." Tom thought for a moment and had an idea.
He ran to his house and got a big cup. He filled it with water from the stream and carried it back to the frog's pond. He added the water to the pond, and the frog started to swim. But then, something unexpected happened. The frog turned into a beautiful fairy!
"Thank you, Tom," said the fairy. "You helped me, and now I am strong again. I was under a spell, and you broke it by adding water to my pond. Now, I can fly and help others too." Tom smiled, happy that he could help his new friend.

Lily was sick. She had a fever and a cough. Her mom put a thermometer in her mouth to check her temperature. Lily did not like the thermometer. It was cold and hard. She wanted to spit it out.
"Keep it in, Lily. I need to see how hot you are," her mom said.
Lily tried to be brave, but she was scared. She did not want to go to the doctor. She did not want to get a shot. She closed her eyes and waited for the thermometer to beep.
Suddenly, she heard a loud noise outside. She opened her eyes and saw a big dog. The dog was barking and running towards her window. Lily screamed and dropped the thermometer. It broke on the floor.
"Mommy, mommy, there's a dog!" Lily cried.
Her mom ran to the window and saw the dog. It was not a mean dog. It was a friendly dog. It had a red collar and a tag. It was looking for its owner.
"It's okay, Lily. It's just a lost dog. He won't hurt you," her mom said.
She opened the window and called the dog. The dog wagged its tail and came closer. He licked her hand and sniffed her face. He was a nice dog.
Lily calmed down and looked at the dog. He had brown fur and black spots. He had big ears and a wet nose. He was cute.
"Can I pet him, mommy?" Lily asked.
"Sure, honey. He likes you," her mom said.
Lily reached out and touched the dog. He was soft and warm. He licked her cheek and made her giggle. He was a good dog.
"Can we keep him, mommy?" Lily asked.
Her mom smiled and shook her head. She saw a phone number on the dog's tag.
"No, sweetie. He belongs to someone else. We have to call his owner and tell them we found him," she said.
Lily was sad, but she understood. She gave the dog a hug and a kiss. The dog wagged his tail and bowed his head. He was grateful.
"Bye, doggy. I hope you find your home," Lily said.
Her mom picked up the phone and dialed the number. She hoped the dog's owner would come soon. She also hoped Lily's fever would go down. She was glad the dog made Lily happy. She was a good mom.

Lila and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big swamp near their house. They wanted to explore it, but their mom said no.
"Swamp is dirty and wet. You can get sick or lost. Stay away from swamp," mom said.
But Lila and Ben did not listen. They waited until mom was busy and ran to the swamp. They saw frogs, bugs, and plants. They thought it was fun.
"Look, a big frog!" Lila said.
"Ribbit, ribbit," Ben said. He liked to repeat what animals said.
They followed the frog to a deeper part of the swamp. They did not see the sign that said "Danger".
"Ribbit, ribbit," the frog said.
"Ribbit, ribbit," Ben said.
Suddenly, they heard a loud roar. A big alligator came out of the water. It had sharp teeth and a long tail. It looked hungry.
"Help, help!" Lila and Ben screamed.
They ran back to the swamp edge. They were scared and wet. They saw mom coming. She looked angry and worried.
"What are you doing here? I told you to stay away from swamp!" mom said.
"Sorry, mom. We saw a frog and wanted to play. But then an alligator came and we ran away. We are fine, mom. Please don't be mad," Lila and Ben said.
Mom hugged them and checked them for injuries. She was glad they were fine, but she was also mad.
"You did not listen to me. You could have been hurt or eaten by the alligator. Swamp is not a place to play. Repeat after me: swamp is not a place to play," mom said.
"Swamp is not a place to play," Lila and Ben said.
They learned their lesson. They never went to the swamp again. They played in the yard or the park instead. They still liked to repeat what animals said, but only the safe ones.

Once upon a time, there lived a mouse named Mimi. Mimi was always looking for a safe place to sleep. One day, she saw a large house with a tall chimney on top.
Mimi said to herself:"This looks like the perfect place for me to sleep." She hurried to the chimney and tried to fit in. To her surprise, she was too big!
Mimi talked to a bird that was nearby and asked, "Do you know a way that I can fit in this chimney?"
The bird replied, "Yes, you need to run and spin around in circles really fast."
So Mimi ran and spun as fast as she could. After a few turns, she became smaller and fit in the chimney perfectly!
"Whew! I'm glad I found a safe place to rest", said Mimi.
The end.

Once upon a time there was an adorable little girl. She lived in the forest with her mother. Every day she would go outside to play.
One day, when she was walking in the forest, she found an axe. It was very shiny and looked very interesting. She wanted to carry it with her, so she did.
Suddenly, her mother saw her and yelled, "No! You can't carry an axe, it's too dangerous. Give it back now!"
The little girl shouted, "No! It's mine. I want to keep it!"
The mother said firmly, "No, you must return it. It is much too dangerous for a little girl like you."
The little girl sadly returned the axe and said, "I still want an axe, mommy."
Her mom smiled and said, "If I can find one for you, you can have it. But until then, you'll have to be safe."
The little girl nodded, and they went home together. And the little girl was more careful the next time she was walking in the forest.

"You're welcome, my sweeties. I love you," mom says.
They hug and kiss mom. They finish their snack. They go to their room. They play with their toys. They tell each other stories. They fall asleep. They dream of snow and cinnamon.

Tim and Kim were curious. They liked to try new things. They asked Dad if they could try some spicy sauce. Dad said, "OK, but be careful. It might be very hot." He gave them each a small spoon. They dipped the spoon in the sauce. They put the sauce in their mouths.
Tim and Kim made a funny face. The sauce was very spicy. It burned their tongues. It made them cough. It made their eyes water. They did not like the sauce. They ran to the truck. They drank some water. They ate some apples. They felt better.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy little rabbit named Remy. Remy loved to hop around and ask questions to all his friends in the forest. One sunny day, Remy found a big, orange carrot on the ground. He wanted to know who dropped the carrot, so he decided to ask his friends.
First, Remy hopped to his friend Sally the squirrel. "Sally, did you drop this carrot?" Remy asked. Sally shook her head and replied, "No, Remy, I did not drop the carrot. I like nuts, not carrots." Remy thanked Sally and continued his search.
Next, Remy went to see his friend Benny the bird. "Benny, did you drop this carrot?" Remy asked. Benny looked at the carrot and replied, "No, Remy, I did not drop the carrot. I like seeds, not carrots." Remy thanked Benny and hopped away.
Finally, Remy found his friend Tommy the turtle. "Tommy, did you drop this carrot?" Remy asked. Tommy smiled and replied, "Yes, Remy, I dropped the carrot. Thank you for finding it!" Remy gave the carrot back to Tommy, and they all played together for the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Tom and Jerry. They always had fun outside and were best friends. One day, they were out playing in the woods. Suddenly, they heard a noise.
Tom said to Jerry, "Let's go see what it is!" So they went to investigate. To their surprise, they saw an owl. It was very big and it was fighting with a mouse!

Sam heard his brother's cry and ran to the kitchen. He saw Tim holding his finger and blood on the counter. He was scared and worried. He said, "Tim, what did you do? Why did you use the knife? It is sharp and dangerous. You should not play with it. You should ask Mom or Dad for help."

Tim learned his lesson and never played with knives again. He also thanked Sam for being kind and helpful. They enjoyed their toast and had a happy breakfast. They learned that being careful and asking for help are important, and that being tough and sharp are not always good.

But one day, a big wind came and blew away all the food. The animals were sad and scared. The wise, hairy cat told them not to worry. She said that the wind was a test for them. The cat told them to use their wisdom and imagine a way to find more food.
The animals thought hard and came up with a plan. They worked together to find more food and shared it with everyone. In the end, the animals learned that they could overcome any problem if they used their wisdom and worked together.


One day, a furry cat named Kitty went for a walk. Kitty saw a door with a shiny knob. The door was open a little bit. Kitty was curious and wanted to see what was behind the door.
Kitty pushed the door open and went inside. It was very cold! Kitty started to shiver and shake. The room was so cold that Kitty began to freeze. Kitty knew she had to find a way to get warm again.
Kitty saw a big, soft blanket on the floor. She ran to the blanket and wrapped herself in it. The blanket was warm and cozy. Kitty was happy and not cold anymore. She learned to stay away from the cold room with the shiny knob.


One day, Tom and Sue were playing in the yard. Tom had a big ball and Sue had a little doll. They were very happy. The sun was shining and the birds were singing.
Suddenly, Tom kicked the ball too hard and it hit Sue's doll. The doll's arm broke. Sue was very sad and cried. "You broke my doll! That's bad!" she said. Tom felt bad too. He wanted to find a way to make Sue happy again.
Tom had an idea. He ran inside the house and brought out a cup of juice. He gave it to Sue and said, "I'm sorry I broke your doll. Here's some juice to make you feel better." Sue stopped crying and took a sip of the juice. But it was not just any juice. It was magic juice! As soon as Sue drank it, her doll's arm was fixed! Sue and Tom were both very surprised and happy. They played together all day, and from then on, they were more careful with their toys.

I can't pick a winner, so let's just settle and say you both win!" Lucy and Tom were happy and enjoyed eating their toast together.

One day, a nosy cat named Tim saw a big red ball. The ball had the word "zoom" on it. Tim was very curious about the ball. He wanted to play with it, but the ball was in a tall tree. Tim tried to jump and reach it, but he could not.
A small bird named Sue saw Tim trying to get the ball. Sue flew up to the tree and said, "I can help you get the ball. I will give it to you." Tim was happy and said, "Thank you, Sue!" Sue flew to the top of the tree and pushed the ball down.
The ball fell from the tree and went "zoom" on the ground. Tim chased after the ball, laughing and having fun. Sue watched from the tree, happy to see her new friend play. Tim and Sue became best friends, and they played with the zoom ball every day.


Anna was a big girl who wanted to go to university. She liked to learn new things and read many books. She had a brown bag where she kept her pencils and papers. She dreamed of going to a big school where she could study more and make new friends.
One day, her mother told her that they had to move to another town. Anna was very sad and angry. She did not want to leave her home and her friends. She did not want to go to a new school where she did not know anyone. She cried and cried and said, "I don't want to go! I want to stay here and go to university!"
Her mother hugged her and said, "I know, my dear, I know. But sometimes we have to do things that we don't like. We have to move because daddy got a new job. He will work hard to save money for us. And you can still go to university when you grow up. You can study anywhere, as long as you have your brown bag and your books. And you can make new friends in the new school. They will like you because you are smart and kind."
Anna wiped her tears and looked at her mother. She felt a little better. She said, "OK, mommy, I will try. But can I keep my brown bag and my books?"
Her mother smiled and said, "Of course, my dear, of course. They are yours. And you can always write to your old friends and visit them someday. Now, let's pack your things and get ready to go. We have a big adventure ahead of us."
Anna nodded and hugged her mother. She still felt sad, but she also felt brave. She knew that she could face the change and still follow her dreams. She learned that sometimes we have to cry, but we also have to try.
The moral value of the story is: We should be adaptable and resilient when we face challenges or changes in life. We should not give up on our goals or our friends, but we should also be open to new opportunities and experiences.


One day, a thoughtful cat named Tim went for a walk. He saw a rag on the ground. He picked it up and took it with him. Tim thought he could use it later. As he walked, he met a dog named Sam.

"I found it," said Tim. "I thought I could use it for something."
Sam and Tim walked together. They saw a little girl crying. She had lost her toy. Tim had an idea. He would act like a toy for the girl.
"Look, I can be your toy," said Tim. He put the rag on his head and started to dance. The girl laughed and clapped her hands. She was happy again.
Then, something unexpected happened. The girl's toy was hiding behind a tree. It saw Tim and the rag, and it thought the rag was a toy too. The toy came out and took the rag from Tim. The girl was so happy to have her toy and the rag back. Tim felt proud that he could help the girl find her toy and make her happy.

The two friends smiled and agreed to share it and play with it together forever.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He lived near a big icy pond. One day he got an idea. He had a sled and wanted to pull it to the pond. He loaded the sled with some supplies and set off.

A man came out from behind some trees. He shouted, "What are you doing here?"
The little boy explained his plan. He wanted to go sledding on the ice. The man said, "That sounds like fun! I have a sled too, let's go sledding together!"
So they loaded up the sleds and went out on the ice. They had so much fun sledding. They sledded until their faces were red and their toes were icy.
At the end of the day, they said their goodbyes and the little boy went home with a big smile on his face. He couldn't wait to go back out on the ice!

One day, a cat named Mimi and a dog named Bobo were playing in the park. They saw a delicate flower that was very pretty. Mimi wanted to stretch her paw to touch the flower, but Bobo said, "No, Mimi! Don't touch it!"
Mimi asked, "Why not?" Bobo said, "It's too delicate! We might break it." Mimi had a different opinion. She thought that she could touch it very gently without breaking it.
They started to argue about whether or not to touch the flower. Mimi said, "I think I can do it!" But Bobo said, "No, it's too risky!" They couldn't agree.
Just then, a butterfly landed on the flower. The butterfly said, "Hello, friends! I see you're having a problem. Why don't you just look at the flower and enjoy its beauty without touching it?"
Mimi and Bobo thought about what the butterfly said. They decided to follow the butterfly's advice. They looked at the flower together and enjoyed its beauty. And they both learned that sometimes it's better to just look and not touch.

Tom and Lily were playing in the woods. They liked to find sticks and stones and make things with them. They saw a big tree with red apples. "Look, Lily, yummy apples!" Tom said. "Let's get some for our picnic."
They tried to reach the apples, but they were too high. Tom had an idea. He saw an axe near a log. "I can use this to cut the tree," he said. He picked up the axe and swung it at the tree.
But the axe was too heavy for Tom. He lost his balance and fell to the ground. The axe hit his leg and made a cut. Tom cried out in pain. "Ow, ow, ow! It hurts!"
Lily heard Tom's cry and ran to him. She saw the blood on his leg and felt scared. But she wanted to help her brother. She took off her scarf and wrapped it around his wound. She hugged him and said, "Don't cry, Tom. I'm here. I'll comfort you."
Tom felt his sister's hug and heard her words. He stopped crying and smiled a little. "Thank you, Lily. You're a good sister. I love you."
Lily smiled back and said, "I love you too, Tom. Come on, let's go home. Mom will make it better."
They left the axe and the apples behind and walked home, holding hands. They learned a lesson that day. Axes are not for children. And sisters are for comforting.

Ben and Lily were best friends. They liked to play in the park near their homes. One day, they saw a big hill with a lot of grass and flowers. They wanted to climb the hill and see what was on the other side.
"Let's go, Ben!" Lily said. "Maybe we can find a new land to play in."
"OK, Lily, but be careful. The hill is very high and steep. We have to test the ground before we step on it. It might be slippery or have holes." Ben said. He was a thoughtful boy who always looked out for Lily.
They held hands and started to climb the hill. They tested the ground with their feet and avoided the rocks and the thorns. They saw some birds and butterflies on the way. They also heard some strange noises, like growls and roars.
"What is that, Ben?" Lily asked, feeling scared.
"I don't know, Lily. Maybe it's some animals that live on the hill. Don't worry, they won't hurt us. We are almost at the top." Ben said, trying to be brave.
They reached the top of the hill and looked around. They saw a beautiful land with trees, lakes, and flowers. They also saw some animals that they had never seen before. They saw a big lion, a tall giraffe, a striped zebra, and a funny monkey.
"Wow, Ben, look at that! It's a new land! It's like a zoo, but without cages. Can we go and play with the animals?" Lily said, feeling excited.
"Sure, Lily, but we have to be gentle and quiet. The animals might be shy or scared of us. We have to respect their home." Ben said, being thoughtful.
They walked down the hill and approached the animals. The animals were curious and friendly. They let Ben and Lily touch them and feed them. Ben and Lily had a lot of fun playing with the animals. They felt like they had found a new land to explore. They were very happy.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Bob and Martha. Both were very thoughtful and liked to do things together. One day Bob and Martha were looking for something to do. Suddenly, Bob had a good idea.
He pointed to a tree in the distance and said, "Let's go snap it down!". Martha thought for a moment and shook her head. She said, "No, that won't be a good idea. We should be more thoughtful."
Bob looked at Martha in surprise, but then he saw the wisdom in her words. He nodded and said, "You're right. Let's walk around the tree instead." So they did, and as they circled the tree, they talked about what a nice tree it was, and the kindness of being thoughtful to all the creatures that made their home in the tree.
The moral of the story is that being thoughtful is important. Next time you have an idea, think it through and consider how it might affect other living things before you act.

Lily sighed and followed mom. She left her toys and the rotten vegetables in the garden. She was sad to leave her story. But she was also curious to see what mom had to show her. The two of them started hopping around the room, trying to find the best spot to watch TV. The cat jumped onto the couch, while Tim hopped up onto a chair. They both agreed it was the best place to watch TV.
So every day, Tim and the orange, hairy cat would hop to the TV together and watch their favourite shows. They had so much fun together and it was the best TV time ever!


Once upon a time, there was a mighty cat named Tom. Tom loved to catch things. He would catch balls, mice, and even his own tail. One day, Tom heard a sound coming from the garden. It was a bird singing a pretty song.
Tom went to the garden to see the bird. He saw it sitting on a tree branch. Tom said to the bird, "Hey bird, can I catch you?" The bird looked at Tom and said, "No, Tom, you cannot catch me. I am too fast for you."
Tom was sad but he did not give up. He tried to catch the bird every day. The bird would always fly away, laughing. One day, Tom thought of a plan. He hid behind a bush and waited for the bird to come near. When the bird came close, Tom jumped out and caught it.
The bird was surprised and said, "Wow, Tom, you are a mighty cat. You caught me!" Tom let the bird go and they became friends. From that day on, they played together in the garden, and Tom never tried to catch the bird again.

Then, a wise old owl saw them fight. The owl said, "Stop! The ball has value to both of you. You should share it and play together." Spot and Whiskers thought about it, and they agreed. They played with the ball together and had lots of fun. They learned that sharing was better than fighting.

Once upon a time there was a charming bird. She wanted to fly around the world. One day, she set off with her wings spread wide. But when she arrived at her destination, she saw a tear in her left wing. She was so sad and worried that she wouldn't be able to fly again.
Suddenly, she heard a voice behind her. "Don't worry, my little birdy," said a kind, old woman. "I'll help you make your wing better again."
The kind old woman took out a needle and some thread. Carefully, she sewed the tear up with the stitch. The bird watched, amazed at the woman's skill.
After some time, the woman said, "There, all done! Now you can fly again."
The bird was so happy and thanked the kind old woman. Then, with a smile on her face, she spread her wings wide again and flew off into the sky.

Once there was a deaf bear who lived in a small cave near the forest. One day, the bear was feeling hot, so he decided to go for a bath in the river.
He slowly made his way down the rocky path, but when he arrived at the river he found that the water was too deep for him to stand. He tried to turn around, but he had gone so far he couldn't make it back.
He tried to call for help, but he was deaf, so nobody heard him. He looked around, and he saw a switch next to the river bank. He pressed the switch and a bridge appeared out of nowhere. With the bridge, the bear was able to cross the river and bathe in the cool water.
When the bear was done bathing, he thanked the switch and scampered back home. He was squeezy clean and refreshed. It was the best bath he had ever had.

Anna was very embarrassed. "It's mine," she said, her voice squeaking.

Anna thought for a moment. Then she reluctantly opened her hand and gave the steak to her brother. "Here you go," she said.
Her brother smiled and thanked her.  Then he closed the hand around the steak and ran off to share it with their friends.

Lila and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run, slide and swing. They saw a big hill with colorful flowers. They wanted to climb the hill and smell the flowers.
"Come on, Ben, let's go up the hill!" Lila said.
"OK, Lila, but be careful. The hill is steep and there might be spikes on the flowers," Ben said.
They started to climb the hill. They held hands and helped each other. They saw many beautiful flowers. Some were red, some were yellow, some were blue. They smelled sweet and fresh.
"Wow, these flowers are so pretty! Can we pick some?" Lila asked.
"No, Lila, we can't. The flowers belong to the hill and the bees. If we pick them, they will die and the hill will be sad. And the bees might sting us if we take their food," Ben said.
"But I want to have a flower for Mommy. She will be happy if I give her a flower," Lila said.
"Lila, you don't need to give Mommy a flower to make her happy. She loves you no matter what. And you can draw her a picture of the flowers instead. That way, the flowers can remain on the hill and the bees can have their food," Ben said.
Lila thought about it. She realized that Ben was right. She didn't want to hurt the flowers or the bees. She wanted to be kind and respectful to nature. She smiled and hugged Ben.
"OK, Ben, you are a good brother. Let's go down the hill and draw Mommy a picture of the flowers. Maybe we can also draw a bee and a hill," Lila said.
They went down the hill and found some paper and crayons. They drew a colorful picture of the flowers, the bee and the hill. They wrote "We love you, Mommy" on the bottom. They ran to Mommy and gave her the picture. Mommy was very happy and proud. She hugged them and kissed them.
"Thank you, Lila and Ben, for this beautiful picture. You are very sweet and thoughtful. And I'm glad you didn't pick the flowers. You showed respect and care for the hill and the bees. That's a very good thing to do," Mommy said.
Lila and Ben smiled. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that sometimes it's better to leave things as they are and enjoy them from a distance. They learned that nature is precious and needs our protection. They learned that love is more than a flower. It's a feeling that remains in your heart.

But one day, Tim wants to play with the faucet by himself. He pushes Mia away and says, "This is my faucet. Go away!"
Mia is sad and angry. She says, "No, this is our faucet. We share!"
Tim says, "No, we don't. I am bigger and stronger. You are small and weak."
Mia says, "That is not nice. You are mean and fierce."
Tim says, "I don't care. You can't have the faucet."

She ran to Tom and hugged him. She tried to make him feel better. She said, "It's okay, Tom. I'm here. We'll go home soon." She looked for help. She saw a man. He was a park ranger. He had a hat and a badge. He had a radio and a first aid kit. He heard Tom and Lily. He came to them.
He saw Tom's wound. He said, "Don't worry, kids. I'm here to help. I'll strike a bandage on your head, Tom. It will stop the bleeding and the pain. Then I'll take you both to your parents. They're waiting for you at the gate. They're anxious to see you."
He did what he said. He struck a bandage on Tom's head. He picked up Tom and Lily. He took them to his truck. He drove them to the gate. He found their parents. They were happy and relieved to see them. They thanked the park ranger. They hugged Tom and Lily. They said, "We're so glad you're safe. We love you."
Tom and Lily said, "We love you too. We're sorry we climbed the hill. We won't do it again. It was scary and dangerous. We learned our lesson."
They went home. They had hot chocolate and cookies. They told their parents what happened. They said, "We're lucky the park ranger was there. He was nice and helpful. He struck a bandage on Tom's head. He saved us."
Their parents said, "Yes, he did. He was a hero. You should thank him again. And you should be careful next time. Don't go near the cliff. It's not a place for kids. It's a place for birds."
Tom and Lily nodded. They agreed. They said, "We will. We promise." They smiled. They felt better. They cuddled with their parents. They watched a movie. They fell asleep. They dreamed of the park, the hill, the cliff, and the birds. But they did not dream of the storm, the rock, or the blood. They dreamed of the sun, the grass, and the flowers. They dreamed of happy things.

Max did not listen. He thought it was funny. He made silly faces and silly sounds. He swung the violin in the air.
"Max, you are being silly. You will break it. Give it back to me!" Lily said. She tried to grab the violin.
Max ran away. He ran to the living room. He tripped on the rug. He fell down. The violin fell too. It broke into pieces.
Lily and Max heard a loud crash. They saw the broken violin. They felt sad. They knew they did something bad.
Mom heard the noise too. She came to the living room. She saw the mess. She saw Lily and Max. She was angry.
"What happened here?" Mom asked. "Who broke the violin?"
Lily and Max looked at each other. They did not know what to say. They were sorry. They knew they had to tell the truth.
"It was me, Mom," Max said. "I was being silly. I wanted to play with the violin. I did not care. I broke it. I am sorry."

She hugged them both. She said, "I am glad you told the truth, Max. But you have to learn to care for other people's things. The violin was Lily's. She loved it. You hurt her feelings. You have to say sorry to her too."

Lily nodded. She said, "I promise, Mom. I will practice more. I will care for the violin. I will make beautiful music with it."
Mom smiled. She said, "That's good, Lily. I am proud of you. And I am proud of you too, Max. You learned a lesson today. You learned to care for others. You learned to say sorry. You learned to tell the truth. You are both good kids. I love you both."

Once upon a time, there was a regular mill by a big blue river. In the mill, there was a nice man named Tom. Tom liked to make things with the mill. He enjoyed his work a lot.
One day, a talking frog came to the mill. The frog said, "Hi Tom! Can I see your mill?" Tom was very surprised. He had never seen a talking frog before. But he said, "Yes, you can see my mill."
While the frog looked at the mill, he found a big red button. The frog asked, "What does this button do?" Tom didn't know. He had never seen it before. The frog pushed the button. Suddenly, the mill turned into a giant cake! Tom and the frog laughed and enjoyed eating the cake together.


One day, a little girl named Mia was playing with her dog, Max. They were having lots of fun in the park. Mia loved to throw a ball and Max would run very fast to get it. They played this game many times.
Then, Mia heard a boy crying. She looked around and saw a boy with a broken toy. Mia walked to the boy and asked, "Why are you sad?" The boy said, "My toy is broken and I am sorry I can't fix it." Mia saw the toy was broken at the waist.
Mia wanted to help the boy feel better. She said, "Don't be sorry. I can help you fix your toy." Mia and the boy worked together to fix the toy's waist. Soon, the toy was like new and the boy was happy. They all played together with Max and the toy until it was time to go home.


Once upon a time, there was a noisy bell that loved to ring. It lived in a big room with a pretty curtain. The bell was very happy when it rang, and everyone could hear it.
One day, the bell was ringing, and the pretty curtain started to move. The noisy bell was surprised. It had never seen the curtain move before. Behind the curtain, there was a little mouse. The mouse was afraid of the noisy bell.
The bell did not want to scare the little mouse. So, it stopped ringing. The mouse came out from behind the curtain and became friends with the bell. They played together every day. The noisy bell learned to ring softly, so it would not scare its new friend. And they all lived happily ever after.


Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a chubby cat named Mimi. Mimi loved to play with her ball and eat mint leaves. One sunny day, Mimi went outside to find her ball.
As Mimi walked, she saw her friend, a little bird named Lulu. Lulu was sad because her favorite toy was stuck in a tree. "Don't worry, Lulu," Mimi said. "I will help you!" Mimi tried to lift her paw to reach the toy, but the tree was too tall.
Just then, a big, kind dog named Buddy came by. "I can help you," Buddy said. He lifted Mimi onto his back, and together they reached the toy. Lulu was so happy! Mimi, Lulu, and Buddy played together all day, and they became the best of friends.


One day, a scary hurricane came to the town. The wind was so strong, it could break things. People were scared and stayed in their homes. They did not want their things to break or get hurt by the hurricane.
A little boy named Tim was in his home too. He was scared of the hurricane. He could hear the wind and see the trees outside moving. He held his favorite toy, a small red car, very tight. He did not want his toy to break.
But then, something unexpected happened. The scary hurricane stopped. The wind was not strong anymore. People went outside and saw that their things were not broken. They were happy and not scared anymore. Tim looked at his favorite toy and saw that it was not broken. He smiled and knew that everything was okay.

Tim worked hard, and his stack grew taller and taller. His friend, Sam, saw him and wanted to help. They worked together, taking turns to put blocks on the stack. They were having lots of fun.
But then, Tim wanted to finish the stack by himself. He didn't want to share with Sam. Sam felt sad and went away. The stack was almost done, but it fell down because Tim was not careful. Tim learned that sharing and working together is better than doing things alone.


Once there was a pale piano. It was very shiny and looked like it had just been polished. Bob was a 3 year old boy who loved the piano. Every day, he would come and polish it. He always used his special color polishing cloth. Making the piano shiny and prettier was so much fun for him.
One day, Bob was very excited. He had some new, sparkly polish that he wanted to use. He was so happy that he was dancing around the piano as he polished it. Suddenly, he knocked off one of the keys and it fell to the ground. Bob was so sad. He didn't know what to do.
Luckily, his dad was there. He quickly fixed the piano and made it look as good as new. When he was finished, Bob was so proud. The piano was so pale and shiny. He gave his dad a big hug and thanked him for making the piano look so beautiful. From that day on, Bob always remembered to be very careful when polishing the piano.


Bella and Max are two cats who live in a big house with a nice family. They like to play together, chase mice, and nap on the sofa. But sometimes they also like to have their own space and do different things.
One day, Bella wanted to explore the garden and see the flowers and the birds. She asked Max to come with her, but Max wanted to stay inside and play with a ball of yarn. He said, "No, thank you, Bella. I like the yarn. It is soft and fun. You go and have fun in the garden."
Bella was a little sad, but she understood that Max had a different idea of fun. She said, "Okay, Max. Maybe we can play together later. Bye-bye." She went out the door and into the garden. She smelled the roses, watched the butterflies, and climbed a tree.
Max played with the yarn for a while, but then he got bored. He wondered what Bella was doing in the garden. He decided to go and find her. He went out the door and into the garden. He looked around, but he could not see Bella. He called, "Bella, where are you? I want to play with you."
Bella heard Max's voice and jumped down from the tree. She ran to him and said, "Hi, Max. I'm here. I had fun in the garden. Did you have fun with the yarn?" Max nodded and said, "Yes, I did. But I missed you. Can we play together now?" Bella smiled and said, "Of course we can. What do you want to play?"
Max saw a big cardboard box in the corner of the garden. He said, "Let's play with the box. Maybe we can make a fort or a spaceship." Bella agreed and they ran to the box. They pushed and pulled and scratched and bit until they made a hole in the box. They crawled inside and found that it was cozy and dark. They said, "Wow, this is a great box. It fits us perfectly."
They curled up in the box and licked each other's paws. They were happy to be together again. They said, "We love each other, even when we separate. We are the best cats in the world." They closed their eyes and fell asleep in the box. The end.

Ben was so worried. He looked around and saw his toy truck, but it wasn't moving. He asked his dad for help.
His dad smiled and said, "Don't be worried, Ben. We just need some oil to rock the truck."
So, Ben and his dad went to the store and bought some oil.
Back at home, Ben's dad poured the oil into the truck and said, "Okay, now rock the truck and see if it works!"
Ben rocked the truck back and forth and then it came alive! The truck moved forward and Ben was so excited. He shouted, "It's working! It's working!"
Ben was so happy his toy truck was finally running. He thanked his dad and they both smiled.


Once upon a time, there was a girl named Mina who was three years old. Mina had a sight; she could see things that other people couldn't. This made her feel different and uncomfortable.
One day, Mina decided to go on an adventure. She started walking and soon came to a special place. All of a sudden, Mina noticed something in the distance. It was a man who was trying to get away from someone.
Mina watched as the man stumbled and almost fell. Then she heard someone call out for help. She knew it was the man who had been trying to get away.
Mina felt very uncomfortable because she was scared of the man. She wanted to help him but was afraid. Eventually, Mina plucked up the courage and ran to the man. Together, they were able to escape.
Mina felt proud of herself for being brave. Even though it was uncomfortable, she was happy to have used her sight to help someone in need.


One day, a little girl called Anna went to the beach with her parents. She was very excited to go sailing on a big, colorful yacht. Her parents showed her the big, beautiful boat.
"Wow," said Anna.
Anna's Dad smiled and said, "Let's start."
Anna and her parents hopped on the yacht. Dad started the engine and the yacht gradually moved away from the shore. The colorful sails unfurled in the wind.
Anna's Mom pointed out at the ocean, "Look Anna, those dolphins are so fast!"
The wind blew gently and Anna and her family sailed away. It was a beautiful sight, with the blue water, white sails and the colorful boat.
Anna smiled and said, "Can we go sailing again?" Her parents laughed and nodded.

Once upon a time, there was a very friendly puppy. Every day, the puppy prayed for a new home. But, no matter how much he prayed, no new home would come. One day, he noticed a teaspoon shining in the sun. It was a beautiful teaspoon. He thought of how much he could do with it. He could even use it for a home! So, he collected some sticks and leaves and built himself a small, cozy home with the teaspoon.
And from then on, the puppy had a home. He learned that you don't need to pray for something big to get it. All you need to do is to be creative and make the best of what you have.
Moral of the story: Be creative and make the best of what you have.


Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy he loved a lot. One day, Tim lost his toy. He looked and looked, but he could not find it. Tim felt very sad.
Tim's mom saw him looking for his toy. She knew it was lost, but she also knew where it was. She had put it in a hot place to dry after it got wet. Tim's mom wanted to teach him a lesson, so she did not tell him where the toy was.
Later, Tim's mom felt guilty for not telling him. She knew Tim was very sad. She gave him a big hug and told him where the toy was. Tim was so happy to find his toy! He promised to take better care of it.
The moral of the story is to always take care of the things you love and to help others when they need it.


Tim was a lonely boy. He had no friends to play with. He only had his toys and his books. He liked to dream about going to the sea. He wanted to see the big waves and the fish and the boats. He wanted to taste the salt in the water and feel the sand on his feet.
One day, his mom said they could go to the sea. Tim was very happy. He packed his toys and his books in a bag. He put on his hat and his sunscreen. He got in the car with his mom and they drove to the sea.
When they got there, Tim ran to the water. He saw the big waves and the fish and the boats. He tasted the salt in the water and felt the sand on his feet. He was so happy. He said to his mom, "Mom, this is my dream. I love the sea. Can we stay here forever?"
His mom smiled and said, "No, Tim, we can't stay here forever. We have to go back home soon. But we can come back another day. Now, let's have some fun. Do you want to build a sandcastle?"
Tim nodded and said, "Yes, mom, I want to build a sandcastle. Can you help me?"
His mom said, "Of course, Tim, I will help you. Let's find a good spot."
They walked along the shore, looking for a good spot. They saw a big rock with a hole in it. Tim thought it looked like a cave. He said, "Mom, look, a cave. Can we build our sandcastle near the cave?"
His mom said, "Sure, Tim, we can build our sandcastle near the cave. But be careful, don't go inside the cave. It might be dangerous. There might be crabs or snakes or spiders inside."
Tim said, "OK, mom, I won't go inside the cave. I will stay with you."
They started to build their sandcastle near the cave. They used a bucket and a shovel and some shells and some seaweed. They made a big tower and a wall and a door and a flag. Tim was very proud of their sandcastle. He said, "Mom, look, our sandcastle is the best. It is bigger and prettier than the others. Can we take a picture of it?"
His mom said, "Yes, Tim, we can take a picture of it. Let me get my phone from the car. You stay here and watch our sandcastle. Don't let anyone destroy it. And don't go inside the cave. I will be right back."
His mom left to get her phone from the car. Tim stayed and watched their sandcastle. He was very happy. He thought, "This is the best day ever. I love the sea. I love my mom. I love our sandcastle."
But then, he heard a strange noise. It came from the cave. It sounded like a growl. Tim was curious. He wanted to see what was inside the cave. He thought, "Maybe it is not dangerous. Maybe it is a friendly animal. Maybe it is a dog or a cat or a bunny. Maybe it wants to play with me."
He forgot what his mom said. He forgot to be careful. He forgot to stay with their sandcastle. He walked towards the cave. He said, "Hello, who is there? Do you want to be my friend?"
He went inside the cave. He saw a dark shadow. He saw two yellow eyes. He saw sharp teeth. He saw a big bear. The bear was angry. The bear was hungry. The bear roared and attacked Tim.
Tim screamed. He was scared. He was hurt. He wanted his mom. He wanted to go back to their sandcastle. He wanted to go back to his dream. But it was too late. The bear ate him. He was gone.
His mom came back with her phone. She saw their sandcastle. She saw the cave. She saw the blood. She saw the bear. She screamed. She was sad. She was angry. She wanted her son. She wanted to go back to their home. She wanted to go back to their life. But it was too late. He was gone.


Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a wish. He wanted to ride his bike all by himself. But every time he tried, he would fall. Tim was sad.
One day, his friend Amy came over. "Why are you sad, Tim?" she asked. "I can't ride my bike," he said. "I always fall." Amy had an idea. "Let's try together!" she said.
Tim and Amy tried many times, but Tim still couldn't manage to ride his bike. Then, they saw a big hill. "Let's try going down the hill!" said Amy. Tim was scared, but he said, "Okay."
They went down the hill very fast. Tim was scared, but he didn't fall. At the bottom of the hill, Tim was happy. "I did it!" he said. "I rode my bike!" Tim's wish came true, and he and Amy rode their bikes together all day.


Once upon a time, there was a little boat named Bob. Bob lived in a harbor with his boat friends. One day, Bob saw a big, shiny rock near the water. He wanted to show his friends the rock.
Bob called his friend, "Hey, look at this big rock!" His friend came over, but as he got close, he started to feel dizzy. "Oh no, I don't feel good," said his friend. But Bob didn't listen. He wanted to show the rock to all his friends.
One by one, Bob's friends came to see the rock. They all felt dizzy too. They knew something was wrong, but Bob didn't listen. He was so happy to show the rock. Then, it started to rain. The water became slippery, and the boats began to slip and slide in the harbor.
Bob's friends tried to tell him to stop, but he didn't listen. The rain got harder, and the boats slipped more and more. They all felt dizzy and scared. The big, shiny rock was not fun anymore.
In the end, all the boats slipped and crashed into each other. The harbor was a mess, and the boats were sad. Bob learned that he should have listened to his friends when they felt dizzy. Sometimes, things that look fun can be bad.

Once on a dark night, Tom was walking in the woods by himself. He was feeling fearless until he heard a mysterious sound coming from behind the trees. He stopped and listened. The sound was like a rail reverberating in the distance. Tom, feeling scared, started walking faster. Suddenly, he heard the sound of the rail coming closer. Tom was so scared he ran, making his way back home.
When he finally stopped running, Tom looked behind and he saw a mysterious figure standing there. Tom was so scared he froze. The figure was so tall and with a very strange look he could barely move. The figure started walking closer, and Tom tried to run away but he could not. Just at that moment, the figure spoke, and he said: "I will be back soon."
Tom was paralyzed with fear, but he still ran as fast as he could. He ran for a long time, until he arrived back home. Unfortunately, Tom never forgot that mysterious figure. The figure still scared him, even after all this time. He was often worried that one day the figure would return, just as the figure had promised. Sadly, Tom was right and the figure eventually returned, making Tom's story have a bad ending.

But when they reached the top, Joe and Ann could see for miles. Suddenly, they felt the wind start to push them away from each other. Joe and Ann were separating.
Joe started flying backward, away from Ann. He was scared and had no idea what to do. Meanwhile, Ann started to cry. She had never been so far away from Joe before.

They flew back home, both thankful for their long, but exciting adventure. From that day forward, Joe and Ann never wanted to be separated again.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to run, jump and slide. They had a lot of fun. But they did not see the big cloud that came over the sun. The cloud was dark and loud. It made a scary noise. Boom!
Lily and Tom were scared. They ran to their mom. "Mom, mom, what is that?" they cried.
Mom hugged them and said, "Don't worry, my loves. That is just thunder. It is the sound of the cloud. Sometimes the cloud makes thunder and rain. But it will not hurt you. It is just water."
Lily and Tom looked at the sky. They saw drops of rain falling. They felt the rain on their skin. It was wet and cold. They did not like it.
"Can we go home, mom?" they asked.
"Sure, we can go home. But first, let me tell you something. Do you know why the cloud makes thunder and rain?" mom asked.
Lily and Tom shook their heads.
Mom said, "The cloud makes thunder and rain because it is tired. It has been carrying a lot of water for a long time. It needs to let go of some water. That is why it rains. And when it rains, it makes room for the sun to come back. The sun is always there, behind the cloud. It is waiting for its turn to shine. The sun is not scared of the thunder. It knows that the thunder is just a noise. And the sun is not angry at the cloud. It knows that the cloud is just tired. The sun and the cloud are friends. They share the sky. They take turns to give us light and water. They are both good for us."
Lily and Tom listened to mom. They felt less scared. They understood that the thunder and rain were not bad. They were just part of nature. They learned to respect the sun and the cloud. They thanked mom for her story. They said, "We love you, mom. And we love the sun and the cloud too."
Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, my loves. And I am proud of you. You are brave and smart. Now, let's go home and have some hot chocolate. How does that sound?"
Lily and Tom nodded and cheered. They held mom's hand and walked home. They were happy.

The daring man accepted the judge's answer, but he still wanted to prove he was smarter. So, he tried to think of something he could forget.

The man went away embarrassed, realising that the judge had known he would forget something all along. He had been trying to prove something to the judge and all he had done was make himself look stupid.

"It did not bite you," Ben says. "It poked you with its spikes. It is trying to protect itself."
He looks at the hedgehog and says in a gentle voice, "Don't be afraid, little hedgehog. We are not going to hurt you. We just want our ball back. Can you please move away from the ball?"
The hedgehog hears Ben's voice and uncurls a little. It sees that Ben and Lila are not mean. It waddles away from the ball and hides under a leaf.

Ben and Mia were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two rocks for eyes.
"Hello, Mr. Snowman!" Ben said. "Do you like our town?"
The snowman did not say anything. He was very still and cold.
"Maybe he is shy," Mia said. "Or maybe he is dead."
Ben and Mia looked at each other. They did not know what dead meant. They had heard it on TV, but they did not understand.
"What is dead?" Ben asked.
Mia shrugged. She did not know either.
"Let's ask Mom," she said.
They ran to their house and knocked on the door. Mom opened it and smiled.
"Hi, kids. Did you have fun in the snow?"
"Yes, Mom. But we have a question," Ben said.
"What is it?"
"What is dead?" Mia asked.
Mom looked surprised. She knelt down and hugged them.
"Dead is when something is not alive anymore. When it does not breathe or move or feel. Like a flower that withers or a toy that breaks."
"Is Mr. Snowman dead?" Ben asked.
Mom shook her head.
"No, honey. Mr. Snowman is not dead. He is just frozen. Frozen is when something is very cold and hard. Like ice or snow. But frozen things can melt and change. Like when the sun comes out and makes the snowman smaller."
"Will Mr. Snowman come alive then?" Mia asked.
Mom smiled.
"No, sweetie. Mr. Snowman is not alive. He is just a fun thing we made with snow. But we can pretend he is alive and talk to him and play with him. And we can make him again next time it snows."
Ben and Mia nodded. They understood a little bit better.
"Can we go back and play with Mr. Snowman?" Ben asked.
"Sure, but wear your coats and gloves. It is very cold outside."
"Okay, Mom. Thank you," Mia said.
They kissed Mom and ran back to the snowman. They said hello to him and gave him a hug. They did not care if he was frozen or dead. They liked him anyway.

She pointed to the door. "Look, Mommy is coming. She'll make you feel better."
Mommy came out with an umbrella. She saw Ben's knee and said, "Oh, poor Ben. What happened?"
"He fell down," Lily said. "The grass was slippery. And there was thunder."
Mommy nodded. "Yes, there was thunder. It's very loud, isn't it? But it's not scary. It's just the sound of the clouds bumping into each other."
She took Ben and Lily inside. She cleaned Ben's knee and put a band-aid on it. She gave them both a glass of milk and a cookie.
"Thank you, Mommy," Ben said. "You're the best."
Lily smiled. She was glad Ben was okay. She was also a little embarrassed. She had been afraid of the thunder, too. But she didn't want to tell Mommy. She wanted to be brave like Ben.

Lily and Max were having lunch with their mom. They liked to eat bread and cheese and fruit, but they did not like salad. Salad was green and leafy and bitter. Mom said salad was good for them, but they did not care.
"Please, try some salad, kids," Mom said. "It will make you strong and healthy."
"No, thank you, Mom," Lily said. She pushed her plate away. "Salad is yucky."
"No, no, no, Mom," Max said. He shook his head. "Salad is gross."
Mom sighed. She wanted her kids to eat well, but they were very picky. She decided to try a different approach.
"Okay, how about this?" Mom said. "If you eat some salad, I will tell you a story. A story about a big, scary monster who loves salad."
Lily and Max looked at each other. They liked stories, especially scary ones. They wondered what kind of monster liked salad.
"Okay, Mom, we will eat some salad," Lily said. She took a small bite. "But only a little bit."
"Okay, Mom, we will eat some salad," Max said. He took a tiny bite. "But only a tiny bit."
Mom smiled. She was happy that her kids were willing to try something new. She began to tell them the story.
"Once upon a time, there was a big, scary monster who lived in the woods. He had sharp teeth and claws and horns and a long tail. He liked to roam around the woods and look for food. But he did not like meat or fruit or nuts. He only liked salad. He liked to eat all kinds of salad: lettuce, spinach, kale, cabbage, carrots, tomatoes, cucumbers, and more. He liked to mix them all together and make a big salad bowl. He liked to add salt and pepper and vinegar and oil and make a tasty dressing. He liked to eat his salad with a big spoon and make loud noises. He liked to scream, 'Salad, salad, I love salad!'"
Lily and Max listened to the story with wide eyes. They imagined the big, scary monster and his big salad bowl. They wondered if he would eat them if he saw them.
"Did anyone ever see the monster, Mom?" Lily asked.
"Did he ever eat anyone, Mom?" Max asked.
Mom smiled. She had a surprise for them.
"Well, one day, a little girl and a little boy were walking in the woods. They were looking for berries and mushrooms. They did not know that the monster was nearby. They did not hear him scream, 'Salad, salad, I love salad!' They did not see him coming. They did not notice his big spoon. They did not feel his breath. They did not see his teeth. They did not..."
"Mom, stop!" Lily and Max screamed. They were scared. They did not want to hear the end of the story. They did not want to know what happened to the little girl and the little boy.
Mom laughed. She hugged them and kissed them.
"Don't worry, kids, it's just a story. The monster is not real. The little girl and the little boy are fine. They ran away and hid behind a tree. The monster did not see them. He only saw their basket of berries and mushrooms. He thought they were part of his salad. He added them to his bowl and ate them. He screamed, 'Salad, salad, I love salad!' And he was happy."
Lily and Max looked at each other. They were relieved. They were glad that the monster did not eat the little girl and the little boy. They were glad that he only ate berries and mushrooms. They were glad that he was happy.
"Mom, can we have some berries and mushrooms, too?" Lily asked.
"Mom, can we have some cheese and bread, too?" Max asked.
Mom nodded. She gave them some berries and mushrooms and cheese and bread. She also gave them some more salad.
"Here you go, kids. Enjoy your lunch. And remember, salad is good for you. Maybe you will grow up to be big and strong like the monster."
Lily and Max smiled. They ate their lunch. They ate some salad, too. They did not scream. They did not make loud noises. They did not say, 'Salad, salad, I love salad!' But they did say, 'Thank you, Mom, for the story and the food. We love you.'
Mom smiled. She loved them, too. She was proud of them. She was happy.

Once, in a small town, there was a church. It was a big church. People went there to pray. The church had a bell that rang loud. But, there was a deaf boy named Tom who could not hear the bell.
One day, Tom saw some kids playing. They were adding rocks to a pile. Tom wanted to play too. He went to add a rock. But the kids said, "No, you can't play. You can't hear the bell."
Tom was sad. He wanted to play with the kids. He wanted to hear the bell. He went to the church and prayed. He asked, "Please help me hear the bell."
The next day, Tom went to the church. He put his hand on the wall. He could feel the bell ring. He was happy. He went to the kids and said, "I can feel the bell. Can I play now?"
The kids said, "Yes, you can play." They all played together, adding rocks to the pile. Tom was happy. He could not hear the bell, but he could feel it.
