Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to eat broccoli. One day, he saw a broken toy on the floor. Tim felt sad because it was his favorite toy. He asked his mom, "Mom, can you fix it?"
His mom said, "I will try, Tim. But first, let's eat dinner." They went to the kitchen and Tim saw a big plate of broccoli. His face lit up with joy. As they ate, Tim's mom told him a story about what happened to the broken toy.
She said, "A little bird came into the house and played with your toy. The bird didn't know it was a toy and thought it was a friend. When the bird tried to fly away, the toy fell and broke." Tim listened carefully and understood.
After dinner, Tim's mom fixed the broken toy. Tim was happy and thanked his mom. From that day on, whenever Tim ate broccoli, he remembered the story of the little bird and his broken toy.

So his dad said, "Come on Rhys, let's go sit over there and we can watch the deer together".

So with a big smile on his face, he waved goodbye to the deer and walked away.

Tim's mom called him, "Tim, come here! It's time to wash your hands before lunch." Tim went to the bathroom and washed his hands. He was happy to see the water wash away the colors from his hands.
While Tim was washing his hands, he heard a strange noise from his room. He went back to see what it was. To his surprise, he saw that his red color was gone! He looked around and saw a tiny red bug holding his red color. Tim was not fearful anymore. He smiled and said, "Hello, little bug! Can I have my red color back?" The bug gave him the color back and flew away. Tim was happy and not scared of red anymore.

The fox looked angry and had taken the weapon from a nearby farm. Bob was scared but knew he had to help.
He hopped closer to the fox and made a loud noise. The fox got scared and dropped the weapon. Bob hopped away to bring help.
The other animals came to help Bob and the fox got taken away by the farmer. Bob was a hero and all the animals cheered for him. They thanked Bob for being brave and alert.
The End.

But then, something unexpected happened! When Spot rubbed his foot on the grass, his foot changed colors! Now, his foot was not just different, it was also colorful! Spot and Whiskers were very surprised. They laughed and played together all day, and Spot's colorful foot didn't hurt anymore.

One day, they want to see who can make the highest tower. They are competitive. They each take some blocks and start to build. They count the blocks as they add them. "One, two, three, four, five..." they say.
Lily has a big black block. She thinks it will make her tower stronger. She puts it on top of her other blocks. But the black block is too heavy. It makes her tower fall down. The blocks snap and crash on the floor. Lily is sad. She cries.
Ben sees what happens. He feels sorry for Lily. He does not want to win like this. He says, "Lily, don't cry. It's okay. We can share the blocks and make a new tower together. We can use the black block as the base. It will be fun."
Lily stops crying. She smiles. She says, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good brother. I like to play with you." They hug. They take the blocks and make a new tower together. They are happy.

Sara and Tom were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, they found a big box in the garage. It had many old things inside, like books, hats, and a belt. Sara and Tom wanted to see what was in the box, so they opened it and took out the things.
Sara liked the belt. It was brown and shiny, and it had a buckle that made a noise when she moved it. She put it around her waist and pretended to be a cowboy. Tom liked the books. They had pictures and words, and he tried to read them. He opened one book and saw a story about a lion and a mouse.
Sara saw the book and wanted it too. She said, "Give me that book, Tom. It is mine." Tom said, "No, Sara. It is mine. I saw it first." Sara and Tom started to fight over the book. They pulled and tugged, and the book ripped in half. They both heard a loud tear and stopped.
They looked at the book and saw that it was ruined. The pages were torn and the cover was ripped. They felt sad and sorry. They had broken the book that they both liked. They wished they had shared it instead of fighting.
They heard their mom coming. They quickly put the book and the other things back in the box. They hoped their mom would not see the broken book. They hid the belt under Sara's shirt. They tried to act normal.
Their mom came in and said, "Hi, Sara and Tom. What are you doing?" Sara and Tom said, "Nothing, mom. Just playing." Their mom smiled and said, "That's good. Do you want some cookies? I made them for you. They are warm and yummy."
Sara and Tom said, "Yes, please, mom. We love cookies." They followed their mom to the kitchen. They felt the belt around Sara's waist. It was tight and uncomfortable. They felt the book in the box. It was torn and sad. They felt their hearts. They were heavy and guilty.
They decided to tell their mom the truth. They said, "Mom, we are sorry. We found a box in the garage and we played with the things inside. We fought over a book and we tore it. We also took a belt and we hid it. We were wrong and we are sorry."
Their mom listened and said, "Thank you for telling me the truth, Sara and Tom. I am glad you are honest. The book and the belt belonged to your grandpa. He gave them to me when I was little. They were very special to him and to me. I was going to give them to you when you were older. But now they are broken and lost. That makes me sad."
Sara and Tom felt very sorry. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We did not know. We were selfish and greedy. We did not think about you or grandpa. We only thought about ourselves. We are sorry, mom. Can you forgive us?"
Their mom hugged them and said, "Of course I forgive you, Sara and Tom. I love you very much. But you have to learn to share and care for your things and for others. That is what grandpa taught me. That is what I want to teach you. Sharing and caring are more important than fighting and breaking. Do you understand?"
Sara and Tom nodded and said, "Yes, mom. We understand. We will try to share and care more. We will try to be like you and grandpa. We love you, mom." Their mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Sara and Tom. Now, let's have some cookies. They are still warm and yummy." They ate the cookies and felt warm and happy. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to share and care.

Once, a selfish whale was swimming around in the sea. Suddenly, he noticed other fish swimming by. He wanted the fish for himself, so he swam faster and ate the fish. But he did not feel happy in his stomach.
The whale approached a crab and said, "Why am I not happy in my stomach?"
The crab said, "Maybe it is because you are being selfish. You have destroyed the homes of other sea creatures and now it makes your stomach sad."
The whale thought hard and realised that the crab was right. So, he decided to share the sea with others. From then on, he was no longer selfish, and he felt much happier.

One day, Lily wanted to show her pictures to her friend Sam. She took her folder and went to his house. She knocked on the door and Sam opened it.
"Hi, Lily! What do you have?" Sam asked.
"I have my pictures. Do you want to see?" Lily said.
"Yes, please!" Sam said. He invited Lily inside.
Lily opened her folder and showed Sam her pictures. Sam liked them very much. He said they were pretty and colorful.
"Can I have one?" Sam asked.
"Sure, you can have one. Which one do you like?" Lily said.
Sam looked at the pictures and picked one. It was a picture of a butterfly. It had yellow and black wings and a red body.
"I like this one. It is a butterfly. It can fly and change. Sometimes it is a caterpillar, sometimes it is a butterfly." Sam said.
Lily smiled and gave him the picture. She was happy that Sam liked her picture.

"Yes, I do. What do you want to play?" Lily said.

Mom pulled out a bright, colorful swimming suit. "Do you want to wear this?" she asked.
Molly looked at it, her eyes widening. The suit was so colorful and pretty. Smiling, she put it on, and felt much braver.
Mom smiled back. She put her arm around Molly and they stepped into the pool together. Molly felt more brave, so she started to swim.
Mom clapped and cheered, encouraging Molly every step of the way. Little by little, she swam around the whole pool.
When they got out, Mom said, "Well done, Molly! You did great!"
Molly smiled. She was so happy she had taken a chance. Swimming was harmless and much more fun than she had expected.

"Thank you, Mom. You are very helpful too," Lily says.

"Yes, he does. And he has two helpful gloves," Lily says.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with cars and trucks. One day, Tom has a new toy. It is a big red truck that can make noise and move by itself. Tom is very happy and proud of his truck.
"Look, Mia, this is my new truck. It can go vroom vroom and beep beep. Do you want to play with it?" Tom asks Mia.
Mia is curious and enthusiastic. She likes trucks too. She nods and smiles. "Yes, Tom, I want to play with it. Can I hold it?"
Tom is kind and generous. He accepts to share his truck with Mia. He gives it to her and says, "Here you go, Mia. You can hold it. But be careful, it needs gas to work. See this button? It makes gas come out. Don't press it too much or it will run out of gas."
Mia takes the truck and thanks Tom. She holds it and presses the button. The truck makes noise and moves by itself. Mia is amazed and excited. She presses the button again and again. She likes the gas sound.
Tom watches Mia and laughs. He is happy that Mia likes his truck. But he also notices that the truck is slowing down. He knows that it is running out of gas. He says to Mia, "Mia, stop pressing the button. The truck needs gas to work. If you press it too much, it will stop and we can't play with it."
Mia hears Tom and stops pressing the button. She looks at the truck and sees that it is not moving anymore. She is sad and sorry. She says to Tom, "Oh no, Tom, I'm sorry. I pressed the button too much. I used all the gas. Now the truck is broken. Can we fix it?"
Tom is not angry or upset. He is understanding and helpful. He says to Mia, "Don't worry, Mia. The truck is not broken. It just needs more gas. We can fix it. We just need to find some gas. Do you know where we can find some gas?"
Mia thinks and remembers. She says to Tom, "Yes, Tom, I know. We can find some gas in the kitchen. Daddy has a gas can for the grill. We can use some of his gas. Come on, let's go."
Tom and Mia run to the kitchen. They find the gas can and fill the truck with some gas. They are careful and safe. They don't spill or touch the gas. They take the truck back to the living room. They press the button and the truck makes noise and moves by itself again. They are happy and relieved. They play with the truck and have fun. They share and take turns. They are good friends.

One day, a bird and a squirrel were playing in a big tree. They liked to jump from branch to branch and sing and chatter. They were happy and free.
But then, they saw a human walking near the tree. The human had a long stick and a loud thing. The human pointed the stick at the tree and made a loud bang. The bird and the squirrel were scared and hid behind the leaves.
"Who is that?" the squirrel asked the bird.
"That is a human. They are bad and mean. They want to hurt us and take our home. We have to be careful and stay away from them." the bird said.
"Why do they do that?" the squirrel asked.
"I don't know. They are not like us. They don't love the tree and the sky and the sun. They only love the loud thing and the stick. They are silly and cruel." the bird said.
The human made another loud bang and a branch fell down. The bird and the squirrel saw another bird fall with the branch. The bird was not moving and had a red spot on its chest. The bird and the squirrel felt sad and angry.
"Let's go. We have to find another tree. This one is not safe anymore. We have to warn the other animals. Maybe they can help us stop the human." the squirrel said.
"Okay. Let's go. But be careful. The human can see us if we fly or run too high. We have to be low and fast. And we have to stick together. We are stronger when we are friends." the bird said.
The bird and the squirrel left the big tree and looked for a new home. They hoped that the human would not find them again. They hoped that the other animals would listen to their warning. They hoped that one day, the human would learn to be kind and share the world with them.

"Hello, elephant!" Kim said. "What is your name?"
The elephant did not answer. It was very tired and wanted to nap. It lay down on the ground and closed its eyes.
"Let's go inside and say hi," Tim said. He saw a small hole in the door and pushed it open. He crawled inside the cell and Kim followed him.
They walked towards the elephant and touched its nose. It was soft and warm. They smiled and hugged it.
The elephant felt something on its nose and opened its eyes. It saw two small children on its face. It was surprised and scared. It made a loud noise and shook its head.
Tim and Kim screamed and ran back to the door. They tried to open it, but it was locked. They were trapped in the cell with the elephant.
"Help! Help!" they cried. "We want to go out!"
A man heard their cries and came to the cell. He was the zookeeper. He saw Tim and Kim inside and the elephant outside. He was angry and worried.
"What are you doing here?" he asked. "How did you get in?"
"We wanted to see the elephant," Tim said. "We are sorry."
The zookeeper unlocked the door and let them out. He scolded them and told them to never go inside the cells again. He said it was dangerous and rude.
Tim and Kim nodded and said they were sorry. They hugged the zookeeper and thanked him. They learned their lesson and never went inside the cells again. They still liked to see the animals, but from a safe distance. They also liked to nap after playing in the park.

John asked his mum, "Can I go in? Can I? Please, Mum!"
Mum smiled and said, "Yes, you can. Be careful, John."
John stepped inside the hut and he saw something had fallen. He was excited. He looked at what had fallen and he saw it was an apple. John picked up the apple and shouted, "I found something!"
Mum laughed and said, "Good job!"
John smiled, he was happy with his discovery. He wanted to keep the apple and take it home. He went back to the hut and said, "Let's go home, Mum."
Mum nodded, "Of course, John."
John held his apple tight and skipped home. He was so eager to show his mum what he had found!

Tim cries. He says, "I made a mistake. I hurt Jen's feelings. I lost my friend. I wish I had a nice toy. I wish I had a nice doll." He hugs the rag. He says, "Maybe you are not so bad. Maybe you are my only friend." He feels lonely and sad.

Once upon a time there lived a mouse named Max. He lived in a small house with a chimney in the middle. Max was a normal mouse, he loved to run and spread around the house.
One morning, Max was spreading around his house when he noticed a huge pile of soot in the Chimney. He had never seen this before!
Max wondered what could have caused so much soot. He decided to stand on his hind legs to get a better look. When he did, he heard a quiet whisper, "Help me out!".
Max was quite scared. He couldn't see anyone in the Chimney.
He asked, "Who said that?".
The whisper replied, "I'm a little baby bird here stuck in the Chimney. Please help me out".
Max was so glad that the voice belonged to a baby bird and not something scary.
He spread a haystack against the Chimney and then climbed up to help the baby bird out.
The baby bird thanked Max and flew away. Max waved goodbye and then spread around his house, happy that he had helped the bird. He was back to his normal self again.

As they began to eat, the lion suddenly changed his mind. He wanted all the fruit for himself. The lion grabbed Momo's part of the fruit and ate it quickly. Momo's eyes filled with tears as he watched the lion eat his fruit. Now his tummy was still empty and he had nothing to eat.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big sign. The sign says "Quiz". Sara and Ben are curious. They want to know what quiz means.
They go to the sign. There is a man with a funny hat. He smiles at them. He says, "Hello, kids. Do you want to play a quiz? It is a game where I ask you questions and you try to answer them. If you answer right, you get a prize. If you answer wrong, you have to yield your turn to the next player. Do you want to try?"
Sara and Ben nod. They like games. They like prizes. The man asks them the first question. He says, "What color is the sky?" Sara and Ben look up. They see the blue sky. They say, "Blue!" The man claps. He says, "Very good. You are right. You get a sticker." He gives them a sticker with a star. Sara and Ben are happy.
The man asks them the second question. He says, "What animal says 'moo'?" Sara and Ben think. They remember the farm they visited. They say, "Cow!" The man claps again. He says, "Very good. You are right. You get a candy." He gives them a candy with a wrapper. Sara and Ben are happier.
The man asks them the third question. He says, "What is the name of the planet we live on?" Sara and Ben pause. They do not know this word. They look at each other. They shrug. They say, "We do not know." The man says, "That is okay. You do not have to know everything. The answer is Earth. You have to yield your turn to the next player. But you did very well. You can keep your sticker and your candy. Thank you for playing the quiz."
Sara and Ben say, "Thank you, too. The quiz was fun." They wave goodbye to the man. They go to the swings. They share their sticker and their candy. They are proud of themselves. They learned a new word. They had a fun day.

Lucy hugged the witch and said, "Thank you, dependable witch!" The witch smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lucy. Remember, if you ever need help, just come to my house." And from that day on, Lucy and the witch were the best of friends.


One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park. He saw his friend, Sam, playing with a new toy. Tim wanted the toy too. He felt bitter because he did not have a toy like that.
Tim thought of a plan. He would take Sam's toy when Sam was not looking. Tim waited and watched. He observed Sam playing with the toy. When Sam went to get a drink, Tim took the toy and hid it.
Later, Sam found out that Tim took his toy. Sam was very sad. Tim felt bad for making his friend sad. He gave the toy back to Sam and said sorry. Sam forgave Tim, and they played together.
The moral of the story is that taking things from others can hurt their feelings. It is better to be kind and share with our friends.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a gentle cat named Fluffy. Fluffy had a secret. She liked to store her toys under the bed.
One day, a little girl named Lily came to visit Fluffy. Lily loved to play with Fluffy and her toys. But when Lily looked for the toys, she could not find them.
"Fluffy, where are your toys?" Lily asked. Fluffy just looked at her and then at the bed. Lily looked under the bed and saw all the toys. "Oh, you store them here!" Lily said with a big smile.
Fluffy and Lily played with the toys all day. At the end of the day, Fluffy shared her secret with Lily. Lily promised not to tell anyone. They became best friends and played together every day.


Once upon a time, there was a very intelligent bird called Bob. Bob was flying around one day when he saw an impossible triangle in the ground. It looked so strange that he stopped to take a closer look.
"What a wonderful triangle!" he said to himself. "I must complete it."
He flew down and started to work on the triangle. But just then, another bird flew down and said,
"That triangle is mine! I was going to complete it myself."
Bob was a bit surprised but he said,
"I want to help. Let's complete it together."
The other bird smiled and said,
"Okay then! Let's do it."
So Bob and the other bird worked together. After a few seconds, the triangle was complete. They both cheered in delight and thanked each other for the help.
From then on, they were the best of friends. They looked after each other and worked together to complete all their difficult tasks. Bob was so proud of his intelligent friend.


One day, a girl named Lily found a flute in her room. She did not know how to play it. She felt happy to find the flute. She asked her mom, "Can you show me how to play this flute?" Her mom said, "I don't know how to play it, but we can learn together."
Lily and her mom played the flute slowly. They made some fun sounds. They laughed and played more. They did not know that the flute was magic. When they played it slow, it made things move slow too. They did not see the ball that was rolling fast to them.
Just then, the ball came near them. But it was moving very slow. Lily and her mom were surprised. They played the flute fast, and the ball moved fast too. They found out that the flute was magic! They had fun playing with the magic flute and the ball all day.

Joe was sad, he felt it wasn't fair at all. He wanted to catch the star too. So, he asked Sam if they could play a different game and then both be winners.
Sam agreed and they decided to play catch with the star instead. The star was the same for both of them and it was a lot of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. Lucy loved the rain.
One day, the sky started to turn purple, and before long, it was pouring. Lucy put on her raincoat and went outside to play.
In her garden, she saw a big pile of hay. She ran up to it and jumped in, enjoying the feeling of the rain on her face.
When Lucy's mom came out to see where her daughter had gone, she called out, "Lucy! Where are you? What are you doing?"
Lucy poked her head up from the pile of hay and said, "I'm here! I'm playing in the rain!"
Her mom smiled and said, "That sounds like a lot of fun! Just make sure you stay dry!"
Lucy stayed in the hay, enjoying the sound of the rain. When she was done, she said goodbye to the rain, and went back inside.
From then on, every time it rained, Lucy would go out and play in the hay, feeling the purple sky above her.


Anna and Ben are playing with their toys. Anna has a doll and Ben has a car. They like to act like the doll and the car are talking to each other.
"Hello, car. I am a doll. Do you want to be my friend?" Anna says in a high voice.
"Vroom, vroom. Yes, doll. I want to be your friend. Let's go for a ride." Ben says in a low voice.
They make the doll and the car move around the floor. They have fun.
But then, Ben sees another toy. It is a big truck. He likes the truck. He wants to play with it.
"Bye, doll. I am going to play with the truck now." Ben says. He drops the car and grabs the truck.
"Hey, that's not fair!" Anna says. She is sad. She likes the car. She wants to keep playing with it.
"Give me back the car, Ben. You can't take it away. We were playing with it." Anna says.
"No, I want the truck. You can have the doll. The truck is better." Ben says.
They start to argue. They are not happy.
Mom hears them. She comes to see what is wrong.
"What's going on, Anna and Ben? Why are you fighting?" Mom asks.
"Ben took the car away from me. He is not fair." Anna says.
"I want the truck. Anna can have the doll. The truck is mine." Ben says.
Mom looks at them. She thinks for a minute. She has an idea.
"How about this? You can take turns with the toys. Anna, you can play with the car for five minutes. Then, you can give it to Ben. Ben, you can play with the truck for five minutes. Then, you can give it to Anna. That way, you can both enjoy the toys. Is that fair?" Mom says.
Anna and Ben think about it. They nod.
"OK, Mom. That sounds fair. We can take turns." Anna says.
"OK, Mom. That sounds fair. We can share." Ben says.
Mom smiles. She gives them a hug.
"Good. I'm glad you agree. Now, let's set the timer for five minutes. And remember, be nice to each other." Mom says.
Anna and Ben say thank you to Mom. They start to play with the toys again. They act like the doll, the car, and the truck are friends. They have fun. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Lily. She loved to pack her toys in a bag and go on adventures. One day, she decided to go to the moon. She packed her bag with her favorite toys: a ball, a doll, and a toy car.
Lily went outside and looked up at the sky. She saw the moon and wished she could fly there. A friendly bird heard her wish and said, "I can help you fly to the moon, but you must be kind to others on our journey." Lily agreed and climbed onto the bird's back. They flew high up in the sky, past the clouds, and towards the moon.

Lily gave her doll to the cat to keep her warm. Finally, they reached the moon and met a lonely boy. Lily shared her ball with the boy, and they all played together. The bird was proud of Lily for being kind and sharing her toys. The moral of the story is to always be kind and share with others, and you will make new friends and have fun adventures.

But then, the boy noticed something strange. He noticed that he was standing right under the sun and it was very bright. So bright that he couldn't see very well. The boy started to worry and decided to slowly climb down the slide, back to his friends.

Lily loved to play princess with her dolls. She had a pink dress, a shiny crown, and a big castle. She pretended that she was the queen of a fairy land, and her dolls were her friends.
One day, she invited her brother Max to play with her. Max liked to play cars and robots, but he agreed to try princess for a while. He put on a fake beard and a hat, and said he was a king.
"Hello, Queen Lily," he said. "Do you want to see my kingdom?"
"Yes, please, King Max," Lily said. "Can I bring my dolls?"
"Sure, why not?" Max said. He took her hand and led her to his room.
Lily saw many cars and robots on the floor. She thought they looked fun, but not very fairy-like. She picked up a red car and made it zoom.
"Vroom, vroom!" she said.
Max paused. He looked at her and frowned.
"That's not how you play princess," he said. "You have to be polite and graceful and talk about flowers and tea."
Lily paused. She looked at him and smiled.
"That's not how I play princess," she said. "I like to be fast and loud and talk about cars and robots."
They looked at each other for a moment. Then they both laughed.
"Maybe we can play both," Max said.
"Maybe we can," Lily said.
They decided to make a new game, where they were both princesses and kings, and they had cars and robots and dolls and castles. They had a lot of fun, and learned to share and enjoy each other's toys.


Once upon a time, there was a baby shark who liked to behave badly. He played too much and didn't listen to his mommy and daddy shark.
One day, when baby shark was playing in the ocean, he came across an old bottle and started playing with it. "Be careful," warned mommy shark, "it might be dangerous!"
But baby shark ignored her warning and started to act crazy. He swam around and around with the bottle, not realizing how much trouble he was getting into.
Suddenly, the bottle bumped into a group of strong whales. Furious, the whales chased after baby shark.
The mommy and daddy shark saw their little baby getting chased and were very worried. They swam as fast as they could and came to baby shark's rescue.
Using their strength, mommy and daddy shark pushed the whales away and saved baby shark.
The mommy and daddy shark hugged their baby and made sure he was okay. "You need to listen to us and behave," said mommy and daddy shark. "You could have gotten hurt if we hadn't been here."
From that day onwards, baby shark no longer behaved badly and always listened to his mommy and daddy shark.
The moral of the story is that we should always listen to our parents and behave no matter what.

Anna had a big hurt in her tummy. She cried and cried and her mommy took her to the doctor. The doctor looked at her and said she needed an operation. Anna was scared and did not want an operation.
She asked her mommy, "What is an operation?" Her mommy said, "An operation is when the doctor makes a small cut in your tummy and takes out the hurt. Then he puts a bandage on it and you will feel better soon." Anna asked, "Will it hurt?" Her mommy said, "No, the doctor will give you some medicine to make you sleep and you will not feel anything. When you wake up, I will be there with you."
Anna asked, "Can I bring my teddy bear?" Her mommy said, "Yes, of course. Your teddy bear will keep you company and make you brave." Anna hugged her teddy bear and said, "OK, I will do the operation. But I am still scared." Her mommy said, "It is OK to be scared, but you are very wise to do the operation. It will make you healthy and happy again. I love you very much." Anna said, "I love you too, mommy." Then they went to the operation room and the doctor smiled at them.

Tim saw the sticker on Lily's leg and wanted one too. But Lily didn't want to share. She wanted to keep the sticker all to herself.
Tim was sad and went home. Lily felt bad for not sharing. She went to Tim's house to say sorry, but it was too late. Tim's mommy said he was already asleep. The next day, Lily's leg started to hurt. The sticker had given her a rash. She was sad and wished she had shared with Tim.
The moral of the story is to not be spoiled and always share with your friends.


Once upon a time, there was a big, red ball. The ball had a voice. One day, the ball wanted to play with the other balls. But the other balls did not like the big, red ball's voice. They said it was too sour.
The big, red ball was sad. It wanted to have a nice voice like the other balls. So, it went to a wise, old tree for help. The tree told the ball to split its voice into two. The ball did as the tree said.
Now, the big, red ball had two voices. One voice was sweet, and the other voice was sour. The other balls liked the sweet voice and played with the big, red ball. The big, red ball was happy. It learned that it was okay to have a sour voice, but it could also have a sweet voice to make friends.

Once upon a time, there was a compassionate whale. He swam across the ocean. One day, he decided to take a break and stop for a rest. As he arrived at a small island, he noticed a little girl sitting alone on the beach.
The whale swam closer and said, "hello!"
The girl was startled by the whale's unexpected greeting. She smiled and replied, "hello!"
The whale asked, "why are you here all alone?"
The girl looked at the whale with a sad expression and said, "I was on a boat trip with my parents. But then a big storm came and now I can't find them. I'm scared and alone."
The whale felt sad for the little girl. He said in a gentle voice, "I understand how you feel. Don't worry, I'm here with you. You are not alone."
The girl hugged the whale. She smiled and thanked the whale for being so compassionate.
From that day on, the whale became the little girl's best friend. They both lived happily together on the island.

Tom and Lily were playing in the kitchen. They saw a big mop and a bucket of water. They wanted to have fun with them.
"Let's mop the floor!" Tom said. "It will be like a slide!"
"OK!" Lily said. "But don't make too much mess!"
They took the mop and dipped it in the water. Then they dragged it on the floor. The floor became wet and slippery. They laughed and slid on the floor.
But then Mom came in. She saw the water and the mop. She was not happy.
"What are you doing?" Mom asked. "You made a big mess!"
Tom and Lily stopped playing. They felt bad. They regretted mopping the floor.
"We're sorry, Mom," Tom said. "We just wanted to have fun."
"We didn't mean to make a mess," Lily said.
Mom sighed. She was not angry, but she was tired. She had a lot of work to do. She was poor and had no help.
"I know, kids," Mom said. "But you have to be careful. The mop and the water are not toys. They are for cleaning. And the floor is not a slide. It is for walking. You could have hurt yourself or broken something."
Tom and Lily nodded. They understood. They wanted to help Mom.
"Can we help you clean, Mom?" Tom asked.
"Yes, please," Mom said. "That would be very nice."
Tom and Lily took some towels and dried the floor. Then they hugged Mom and said they loved her.
Mom smiled and hugged them back. She said she loved them too. She was glad they were sorry and wanted to help. She was proud of them.

Jim gently took the rock out of Spot's foot. It hurt a little, but Spot was brave. "Thank you, Jim," said Spot. Now, Spot's foot felt better. He was happy to play with Jim again. They played with the ball all day and had lots of fun.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to dig holes and look for bugs. They found a big hole under a tree. They wondered what lived inside.
"Maybe it is a rabbit," said Lily.
"Or a mouse," said Tom.
They decided to peek inside the hole. They saw a small, furry animal with a long nose and tiny eyes. It was a mole.
"Hello, mole," said Lily. "Do you want to play with us?"
The mole was scared. He did not like loud noises or bright light. He wanted to hide in his hole.
"Go away, go away," he said. "You are too noisy and too bright. Leave me alone."
Lily and Tom felt sad. They did not want to hurt the mole. They wanted to be friends.
"Sorry, mole," said Tom. "We did not know you were shy. We will be quiet and gentle."
They backed away from the hole. They saw some flowers and leaves nearby. They picked some and made a wreath. They put it near the hole as a gift for the mole.
"Look, mole," said Lily. "We made this for you. It is pretty and smells nice. We hope you like it."
The mole was curious. He sniffed the wreath. He felt the soft petals and the green stems. He liked it. He felt a warm feeling in his heart.
"Thank you, thank you," he said. "You are kind and sweet. I like your gift. I want to be your friend."
He came out of his hole. He smiled at Lily and Tom. They smiled back. They clapped their hands. They were happy.
They played together in the garden. They learned about each other. They had fun.
The moral of the story is: Be respectful and gentle to others who are different from you. You might make a new friend.

Suddenly, the dog started to dance! Mia and her mom were surprised. The dog wasn't scary at all. It was a dancing dog! Mia laughed and said, "Look, Mommy! The dog is dancing!" They all danced together and had a fun time at the market.

Once upon a time, there was a panda named Pandy. Pandy loved to play with his friends in the big green forest. They would run, jump, and laugh all day long.
One day, Pandy and his friends heard a loud noise. It was a big tree that had fallen down. Pandy and his friends were scared, but they wanted to help. So, they started to strike the tree with their paws to make it smaller and easier to move.
After a lot of hard work, Pandy and his friends moved the tree. They were very happy and proud. They played and had fun for the rest of the day. And from that day on, whenever there was a loud noise, Pandy and his friends knew they could work together to make things better.


Ben and Mia liked to play in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. One day, they saw a big crane near the park. The crane was lifting heavy things and putting them on a truck.
"Wow, look at that crane!" Ben said. "It is so big and strong!"
"I want to see it closer!" Mia said. "Let's go!"
They ran to the fence and looked at the crane. They saw a man sitting in a small box on top of the crane. He was pushing buttons and moving a stick.
"Hello, Mr. Crane!" Mia shouted. "Can you hear us?"
The man looked down and smiled. He waved at them and said, "Hello, kids! Do you like my crane?"
"Yes, we do!" Ben and Mia said. "It is amazing!"
"Thank you!" the man said. "Do you know what I do with my crane?"
"No, what do you do?" Ben asked.
"I help to build new houses and buildings. I lift the bricks, the wood, the metal and the glass. I put them where they need to go. It is a lot of work, but it is fun!"
"That sounds cool!" Mia said. "Can we help you?"
The man laughed. He said, "Well, you are too small to help me now. But maybe when you grow up, you can be crane drivers too. You just need to learn a lot and practice a lot. And you need to be lucky too. Lucky to find a good job and a good crane."
Ben and Mia nodded. They said, "We will do that! We want to be like you!"
The man said, "That's great! I'm sure you can do it. But for now, you should go back to the park and play. Have fun and be safe!"
"Okay, thank you, Mr. Crane!" Ben and Mia said. They waved goodbye and ran back to the park. They were happy and excited. They had seen a big crane and talked to a nice man. They had learned something new and made a new friend. They felt very lucky.


Once upon a time, there was a pretty flower. The flower was sad because it could not bloom. Every day, the flower tried to bloom, but it just could not. The flower was very sad.
One day, a kind bird saw the sad flower. The bird was compassionate and wanted to help. The bird said, "Why are you sad, little flower?" The flower said, "I can't bloom, and I don't know why."
The bird thought about it and said, "Maybe you need some help. Let's ask the sunset." So, the bird and the flower asked the sunset for help. The sunset said, "You need more light, little flower. I will give you more light."
The next day, the flower got more light from the sunset. The flower was happy and finally bloomed. The bird and the sunset were happy too. They all lived happily ever after.


Janie was playing with her dolls when she noticed a pink knot near her foot. She picked it up and showed it to her mom.
"Mommy, what's this?" May asked, holding the knot in her hand.
"That's a knot," Mommy replied. "Now put it back where you found it."
Janie heard her mom, but she didn't want to. The knot was so pretty and colourful, she decided she wanted to keep it.
"No, I won't!" Janie said. "I want to keep it!"
Mommy became cross. She didn't want Janie to have the knot in her room. It wouldn't be safe.
"You must put it back where you found it," Mommy said firmly.
Janie knew that her mom was right. She reluctantly put the pink knot back on the floor. But out of the corner of her eye, she thought she saw it move.

As the wolf mixed, something unexpected happened. The mix in the bowl started to grow and grow! The wolf and the other animals were very surprised. The mix became so big that it turned into a giant ball. The animals all played with the giant ball and had so much fun. The patient wolf was happy that his mix made everyone smile.

One day, Lily's mom said, "Lily, it's time to wash your pebbles. They are very dirty." Lily agreed and took her box of pebbles outside. She filled a big bowl with water and began to wash her pebbles one by one. As she washed them, they became shinier and prettier than before.
As Lily was washing her pebbles, her friend Tom came over. He saw the shiny pebbles and asked, "Lily, can I help you wash the pebbles?" Lily smiled and said, "Yes, Tom! Let's wash them together." So, Lily and Tom washed all the pebbles until they were clean and shiny.
When they were done, Lily and Tom made a big rainbow with the pebbles on the ground. It was the most beautiful rainbow they had ever seen. They were very happy and proud of their work.
From that day on, Lily and Tom would wash their pebbles and make beautiful pictures together. And they lived happily ever after, playing and creating with their shiny, clean pebbles.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Lucy. She was only 3 years old and she loved playing by the river.
One day, Lucy went down to the river to play like she always did. But this time, something strange happened. She saw a fish jump out of the water, right up close to her.
The fish said to Lucy, "Hi there! Do you want to come and play with me?"
Lucy was very surprised and she replied, "Yes, I do!"
But then, the fish said "Not so fast! You must be careful if you want to come and play with me. I'm afraid of people's eyes. So you must not look at me with your eyes, okay?"
Lucy was a little bit scared, but she said to the fish "Okay, I'll be careful."
The fish smiled and jumped back into the water. Lucy followed carefully, being very careful not to look at the fish with her eyes.  They then played happily together in the river.
The end.

They pull and tug on the truck. They are both angry. They do not listen to each other.
Then, Ben pushes Anna. Anna falls on the floor. She cries. She hurts her knee.
Mom hears the noise. She is alert. She runs to the bedroom. She sees Anna and Ben. She is not happy.
She says, "What is going on here? Why are you pushing and crying? You need to share and be kind."
She helps Anna up. She hugs her. She puts a band-aid on her knee. She says, "I'm sorry you got hurt, Anna. Ben, you should not push your sister. That is not nice. You need to say sorry."
Ben feels bad. He says, "I'm sorry, Anna. I was wrong. Do you want to play with the truck?"
Anna says, "It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. Yes, I want to play with the truck. But we can take turns. You can play with the doll, too."
Mom smiles. She says, "That's better. I'm glad you are making up. Now, play nicely and have fun."
She leaves the bedroom. Anna and Ben hug. They play with the truck and the doll. They are happy. They are friends.

On his third birthday, Sammy's mom and dad presented him with a special gift: a robot! He was so excited to see it and quickly opened the box. Inside, the robot was made of plastic and had a big, friendly smile.
Sammy gave the robot a hug and it hugged him back. Its arms were soft and flexible, and Sammy felt very comfortable when it was around. They became good friends and went for long walks together.
At the park, Sammy would stretch with his robot. They both put their arms straight out in the air and challenged each other to see how far they could go. It was always a fun way to end the day.

Bonnie looked at the man and said, "I don't know, let's get out of here." They quickly ran away from the park and back to Bonnie's home.
Tom was still scared and anxiously asked Bonnie, "What happened to him?"
"I don't know," Bonnie said, "but he scared me too. Let's not go to the park for a while."
Bonnie and Tom decided to stay in Bonnie's house and play with their blocks. They laughed and enjoyed playing together so much that they soon forgot about the strange man in the park.

The engine guessed that it was a big monster and they all needed to hide. But, it was not a monster. It was a big snowball that had rolled down the hill and hit the house.

One day, a little girl named Mia and her dog, Max, went on a journey. They walked and walked. The sun was very hot. Mia started to feel tired and thirsty. She saw a big tree and thought, "Maybe there is something to drink there."
As they got closer to the tree, Mia saw a small, sour fruit hanging from a branch. She picked it and took a bite. "Yuck!" she said, making a funny face. Max barked and wagged his tail, as if he knew something good was coming.
Mia and Max continued their journey until they found a small, cold river. They both drank the cold water and felt much better. Mia looked at Max and said, "I'm glad we found this river, Max!" Max barked happily in agreement.
As the sun started to set, the air became cooler. Mia and Max began to shiver. They knew it was time to go home. They walked back, remembering their journey and the sour fruit. When they got home, they were happy to be warm and cozy again.
Mia hugged Max and whispered, "Today was a fun journey, but I'm glad we're home now." Max wagged his tail and snuggled close, happy to be home too.

Tom was nervous. He said, "No, Lily. We don't know what they are. They might be bad for us. Mom said not to eat things we don't know."

Tom shook his head. He said, "Don't do it, Lily. Please. It might make you sick. Let's go home and ask Mom."
But Lily did not listen. She bit the fruit and put it in her mouth. She made a face. It was sour and bitter. She spat it out and threw it away. She said, "Yuck. This is not yummy. This is nasty."
Then she felt a pain in her tummy. She clutched it and cried. She said, "Tom, help me. It hurts. It hurts so much."
Tom was scared. He ran to her and hugged her. He said, "Lily, I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'll get help. Don't worry."
But it was too late. The fruit was poison. Lily fell to the ground and did not move. She did not breathe. She was gone. Tom was alone. He screamed and cried. He wished he could go back and stop Lily. But he could not. He had lost his sister. He was sad. He was sad forever.

"I'm sorry, too," Jen says.

Lily was a curious girl who liked to learn new things. She had a big book with many pictures and words. She wanted to read the book, but some words were hard for her. She asked her mom to help her.
"Mom, what does this word mean?" Lily pointed to a word in the book. It was "weigh".
"Weigh means how heavy something is," Mom said. "For example, this pencil weighs very little, but this book weighs more."
Lily picked up the pencil and the book. She felt the difference in her hands. She nodded. She understood.
"Can I weigh other things?" Lily asked.
"Sure, you can. But be careful not to break anything," Mom said.
Lily ran to her room. She found a toy scale that she got for her birthday. She put the pencil on one side of the scale and a stuffed bear on the other side. The scale tipped to the bear's side.
"The bear weighs more than the pencil," Lily said to herself.
She tried other things. She weighed a ball, a flower, a cookie, and a necklace. She had fun comparing them.
Then she saw her cat sleeping on her bed. She wondered how much the cat weighed. She was very curious. She picked up the cat and put it on the scale. The cat did not like it. It meowed and scratched Lily's arm. It jumped off the scale and ran away.
"Ow!" Lily cried. "That hurt!"
Mom heard Lily and came to her room. She saw the scratch on Lily's arm and the scale on the floor.
"What happened, Lily?" Mom asked.
"I wanted to weigh the cat, but the cat was angry," Lily said.
Mom hugged Lily and cleaned her wound. She explained to Lily that the cat did not like to be weighed. She said that some things are better left alone.
"I'm sorry, Mom. I was just curious," Lily said.
"I know, Lily. Curiosity is good, but you have to be gentle and respectful with living things. They have feelings too," Mom said.
Lily nodded. She learned something new. She said sorry to the cat and gave it a treat. She decided to weigh only things that did not mind. She still liked to be curious, but she also liked to be kind.

Then, the cat's friend, a big dog, came to help. The dog knew where the ball was. He found the ball behind a tree. The cat was so happy! They played with the ball together and had lots of fun.


Once upon a time, there was a lawyer named Tom. Tom was a bit careless. He sometimes forgot to put away his things.
One day, Tom had a big test. He had to go to court and help his friend. But, Tom was in a rush and left his important papers at home. He was very sad.
His friend, Sally, saw that Tom was sad. She said, "Don't worry, Tom! I can help you find your papers." They went back to Tom's house and found the papers. Tom was very happy, and he did a good job on his test. From that day on, Tom tried not to be careless anymore.


Once there was a girl named Mary. Mary was only 3 years old. One day Mary went outside to see the earth and explore. As Mary was walking, she noticed something heavy on the ground. She cautiously walked closer and saw what it was. It was an old chest! Mary was so excited. She opened the chest and found a magical jokes book inside.
"Wow!" exclaimed Mary, "Can I really play with this book?"
The magical book replied, "Yes Mary, I'll teach you how to joke!" Mary couldn't believe it and eagerly accepted the book's offer.
The magical joke book taught Mary all kinds of fun jokes. Soon she had learnt so many that she made her mom, dad and all her friends laugh.
Mary was so happy with the magical joke book, she took it and the chest wherever she went on Earth. Whenever someone was feeling sad, she would tell them a joke and make them laugh and feel better.
Mary was a joke master!


Once upon a time, there was a big, hairy dog named Max. Max lived in a small house with a backyard. He loved to play and run in the backyard. One day, Max saw a small rock in the backyard. He did not know what it was, so he left it alone.
The next day, Max went to the backyard to play again. He saw the rock again, but this time, it was a little bigger. Max thought it was strange, but he still left it alone. He played with his ball and had fun in the backyard.
On the third day, Max went back to the backyard. The rock was now very big! Max was surprised and curious. He went close to the rock and gave it a little push. The rock started to move! It was not a rock, but an egg! The egg cracked open, and out came a baby bird. Max and the baby bird became best friends, and they played together in the backyard every day.

As they walked, Mia tripped and fell on her knee. "Ouch!" she cried. Spot looked at Mia with big, worried eyes. A kind lady saw Mia and came to help. "Are you okay?" she asked. Mia nodded, but her knee still hurt.
The lady helped Mia stand up and gave her a band-aid for her knee. "Thank you," Mia said with a smile. The lady smiled back and waved goodbye. Mia and Spot continued their walk, happy to be together on such a perfect day.


Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big mill near the park. The mill has a big wheel and a big door.
"Let's go and see the mill," Tom says.
"OK, but be careful," Sue says.
They walk to the mill. They hear a loud noise inside. They peek through the door. They see a big machine with many teeth. The machine is making flour from wheat.
"Wow, that is how they make flour for bread and cake," Tom says.
"Yes, flour is tasty," Sue says.
Suddenly, the machine stops. A man comes out of the mill. He sees Tom and Sue.
"Hey, what are you doing here? This is not a place for children. Go away!" the man shouts.
He scares Tom and Sue. They run away from the mill. They go back to the park.
"Sorry, Tom, I did not like the mill. The man was mean and the machine was scary," Sue says.
"It's OK, Sue, I did not like it either. Let's play something else. Do you want to swing or slide?" Tom says.
"I want to swing. Swinging is fun and not scary," Sue says.
They go to the swing. They swing high and low. They laugh and smile. They forget about the mill. They are happy.

My shoulder feels good now!" Bobo smiled, happy to help his friend. They played together in the forest for the rest of the day.

Lily and Ben were playing at the harbor. They liked to watch the boats and the birds and the water. They saw a big boat with pretty flags and people on it. They wanted to go closer and see.
"Can we go on the boat, Mommy?" Lily asked.
"No, sweetie, that boat is not for us. It is for people who go far away. We can look from here," Mommy said.
Lily and Ben nodded. They held Mommy's hand and walked along the harbor. They saw a small boat with a man and a dog on it. The dog was brown and fluffy and had a red collar. Lily and Ben liked dogs. They wanted to pet the dog.
"Can we pet the dog, Mommy?" Ben asked.
"Maybe, honey, but we have to ask the man first. He is the owner of the dog. We have to be polite and careful," Mommy said.
Lily and Ben nodded. They walked up to the small boat and said hello to the man. The man smiled and said hello back. He said his name was Sam and his dog's name was Max. He said they could pet Max if they were gentle and nice.
Lily and Ben were happy. They reached out their hands and touched Max's fur. Max wagged his tail and licked their faces. Lily and Ben giggled. They said Max was a good dog.
But then, something bad happened. Ben felt a sharp pain in his finger. He looked and saw a small crab had pinched him. He cried out and pulled his hand back. The crab fell into the water.
"Ow, ow, ow! Mommy, it hurts!" Ben said.
"Oh, no, Ben, I'm sorry. Let me see your finger. It's okay, it's just a little pinch. It will get better soon. Here, let me kiss it," Mommy said.
She kissed Ben's finger and hugged him. She said he was brave and strong. She said the crab was scared and didn't mean to hurt him. She said they should be careful with the animals at the harbor. They might bite or pinch or sting.
Lily and Ben nodded. They said they were sorry for the crab. They said they still liked the harbor and the boats and the birds and the water. They said they still liked Max and Sam. They said thank you and goodbye to them. They said they wanted to go home and have a snack.
Mommy smiled and said okay. She held their hands and walked with them. She said they had a fun and exciting day at the harbor. She said she loved them very much. Lily and Ben smiled and said they loved her too. They were happy.


Once upon a time, in a big jungle, there lived a messy gorilla named Gogo. Gogo loved to play in the mud and get dirty. All the other animals in the jungle would laugh and say, "Look at Gogo, he is so messy!"
One day, a little bird named Peep flew to Gogo and said, "Gogo, can you help me? My nest is broken, and I cannot fix it." Gogo wanted to help, so he said, "Okay, Peep, I will help you. Let's go fix your nest!" Gogo and Peep went to the tree where Peep's nest was.
Gogo looked at the broken nest and thought about how to fix it. He requested, "Peep, can you find some sticks and leaves? I will use them to fix your nest." Peep flew around and brought Gogo some sticks and leaves. Gogo used his big hands and fixed Peep's nest. Peep was very happy and thanked Gogo.
From that day on, the animals in the jungle stopped laughing at Gogo. They saw that even though he was messy, he was kind and helpful. Gogo and Peep became the best of friends, and they played together every day. And sometimes, Peep would even join Gogo and play in the mud!


Once upon a time, there lived a nosy mouse. The mouse was always searching. One day, he was searching in an old barn.
Suddenly, the mouse spotted something! He passed it once and then quickly passed it again. It was a yummy piece of cheese!
The mouse was so excited. He scratched and scratched, but the cheese was stuck inside a box.
The mouse squeaked and squeaked, asking a nearby caterpillar for help.
The caterpillar was very nosy. He wanted to take the cheese for himself!
The caterpillar said: "You can pass the cheese to me, and then I will try to find a way to open it for you."
The mouse was so excited to pass the cheese, but it was all a trick. The caterpillar never opened the box, he just took it away.
The mouse was sad. He never got to enjoy his yummy cheese.

"James, you should be careful," she said.
James just kept jumping. He absolutely loved it!
Suddenly, the bed collapsed with a loud thump. James tumbled out from the mess and burst out into tears.
His mom came running and quickly picked him up.
"It's okay, I was expecting something like this," she said.
James stopped crying and looked up.
"You were?"
His mom nodded and gave him a hug.
"Yes, I knew if I kept on reading the newspaper and didn't tell you to stop jumping, something like this could happen."
James smiled and hugged his mom back tight.
"That's okay! We can just buy a new bed," he said.
His mom nodded and laughed.
The next day, they went to the store and bought an enormous new bed.
James couldn't help but jump on it straight away.
His mom laughed, "Hey, don't forget our lesson!"
James just smiled and kept on jumping.

The cat started playing with the squirrel, and within moments, the squirrel was nothing but a pile of fur. The squirrel was gone, and his nut was still sitting there, dirty and forgotten. The cat licked its lips and crossed its way, leaving the poor squirrel behind.

Then, something unexpected happened. The comet turned into a big, friendly bird! The bird took Tim back home and said, "Thank you for playing with me, Tim." Tim woke up and looked at the smooth rock. He smiled and knew that the rock was special.

So Max and the banana marched with the ants. They went up and down hills and around trees. At last, they found a big ant hill. The ants were taking food inside. Max and the banana were happy to see where the ants lived.
Max said, "Thank you, ants, for letting us march with you!" The ants said, "You're welcome, Max and banana! Come back and visit us soon." Max and the banana went back to their tree, and they had a fun day.

Lila and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is brown and has a long tail. The dog runs to them and wags his tail.
"Hello, dog!" Lila says. "Do you want to play with us?"
The dog barks and licks Lila's face. He is happy. Ben is scared. He thinks the dog will bite him.
"Go away, dog!" Ben says. "You are big and scary!"
The dog does not go away. He sniffs Ben's pocket. He smells something good. Ben has a sandwich with meat in his pocket. The dog wants the meat.
"Hey, that's mine!" Ben says. He tries to pull his sandwich away from the dog. The dog growls and pulls harder.
Lila sees that Ben and the dog are fighting. She does not like fighting. She wants them to be peaceful.
"Stop, stop!" Lila says. "Ben, share your sandwich with the dog. He is hungry. He is not scary. He is friendly. He wants to be your friend."
Ben listens to Lila. He thinks for a moment. He does not want to be mean to the dog. He breaks his sandwich in half and gives one half to the dog.
"Here, dog. You can have this. But you have to be nice to me. And you have to play with us."
The dog takes the meat and eats it. He is happy. He wags his tail again. He licks Ben's face. He is thankful.
"Thank you, Ben. You are kind. You are my friend. Can I play with you and Lila?"
Ben smiles. He is not scared anymore. He likes the dog. He pets the dog.
"Sure, dog. You can play with us. What is your name?"
The dog barks. He does not have a name.
"Can we give you a name?" Lila asks.
The dog nods. He likes that idea.
"How about Brownie?" Lila suggests.
The dog barks. He likes that name.
"OK, Brownie. Welcome to our park. Welcome to our game. Welcome to our friendship."
Lila, Ben and Brownie play together. They have fun. They are peaceful. They are happy.

The girl asked the man if she could join in. He smiled and handed her the flute. She started to climb the tree, higher and higher until she almost reached the top. The man clapped for her as she came down with the flute held tight in her hands.

Max arrived at Lily's house with the copper penny in his mouth. He barked and wagged his tail to show her the penny. Lily was so happy to see the shiny penny. She clapped her hands and said, "Wow, Max! You found a pretty penny!"
Together, Max and Lily played with the copper penny all day. They took turns hiding it and finding it again. They laughed and had so much fun. When it was time for Max to go home, he gave the penny to Lily as a gift. She hugged Max and said, "Thank you, Max! You are the best friend ever!"


One day, Sarah went for a walk with her mom. As they walked, Sarah stopped and said, "Mommy, I see a statue!" Her mom said, "Yes, that is a statue!"
Sarah stared at the statue. Its head was bowed and its eyes were closed, and it looked very sad. She asked her mom, "Why is the statue so sad?".
Her mom said, "Maybe it is sad because no one is visiting."
Sarah was very sad. She waved to the statue and said, "Hi! I am here!"
Suddenly, the statue opened its eyes and smiled.
Sarah was so happy and said, "See, Mommy? The statue isn't sad anymore!"


One day, a little girl named Lily found an umbrella. It was an incredible umbrella with many colors. Lily loved her umbrella and took it everywhere she went. She knew it would help her if it rained.
One day, Lily saw a sad boy named Tim. He was wet from the rain. Lily wanted to improve his day, so she shared her incredible umbrella with him. They both stayed dry and happy under the umbrella.
The next day, the sun was shining bright. Lily and Tim went to the park with the umbrella. They opened it and something unexpected happened. The incredible umbrella turned into a big, colorful kite! They laughed and played with the kite all day, and the umbrella made their days even better than before.


Tom and Lily were bored. They had no toys to play with and no books to read. Their mom was busy in the kitchen and their dad was at work. They looked out the window and saw a big slide in the park. They wanted to go there and have fun.
"Mom, can we go to the park and slide?" Tom asked.
"Not now, dear. I have to finish cooking. Maybe later," Mom said.
Tom and Lily did not listen. They put on their coats and shoes and ran out of the door. They did not tell Mom where they were going. They crossed the street and ran to the park. They saw the big slide and smiled.
"Let's go, Lily. I'll go first and you follow me," Tom said.
He climbed up the ladder and sat on the top of the slide. He pushed himself down and felt the wind in his hair. He laughed and shouted, "Whee!"
Lily climbed up the ladder and sat on the top of the slide. She saw Tom waiting for her at the bottom. She pushed herself down and felt the wind in her hair. She laughed and shouted, "Whee!"
But then something bad happened. The slide was broken and had a sharp edge. Lily did not see it and slid over it. It cut her leg and made her bleed. She screamed and cried, "Ow! Ow! Ow!"
Tom heard her scream and ran to her. He saw her leg and felt scared. He did not know what to do. He shouted, "Help! Help! Help!"
Mom heard the shouts and looked out of the window. She saw Tom and Lily in the park and felt angry. She also saw Lily's leg and felt worried. She grabbed her phone and ran to the park. She called Dad and the doctor. She hugged Lily and Tom and said, "Why did you go to the park without telling me? You could have been hurt or lost. You were very naughty and made a big mistake."
Tom and Lily felt sorry and sad. They said, "We're sorry, Mom. We were bored and wanted to slide. We didn't mean to make you angry or worried. We didn't know the slide was broken. Please don't be mad at us."
Mom said, "I'm not mad at you, but I'm very disappointed. You have to listen to me and follow the rules. You have to be careful and safe. You have to ask me before you go anywhere. Do you understand?"
Tom and Lily nodded and said, "We understand, Mom. We won't do it again. We love you, Mom."
Mom said, "I love you too, but you have to learn from your mistake. Now let's go to the hospital and get Lily's leg fixed. And no more sliding for a while."
Tom and Lily followed Mom to the car and went to the hospital. They felt dull and sore. They wished they had stayed at home and played with their toys and books. They learned a hard lesson that day.

"Let's go on the slide!" Lily said.
"OK!" Ben said.

"Maybe we can find a way to climb up," Lily said.
They searched for a ladder, a box, or a stool. They did not find anything.

"Maybe he has something we can use," Ben said.
"Let's ask him," Lily said.
They ran after the man. They did not see where they were going. They did not see the car.
The car was fast. It hit them. They fell down. They were hurt.
The man heard the noise. He turned around. He saw Lily and Ben on the ground. He was scared. He dropped his bag and ran away.
The bag was full of money. He had stolen it from a bank. He was a bad man.
Some people saw what happened. They called for help. They tried to help Lily and Ben. But it was too late. Lily and Ben were gone.
The people were sad. They wished Lily and Ben had not chased the man. They wished Lily and Ben had stayed in the park.
The moral of the story is: Do not talk to strangers. Do not leave the place where you are safe. Be careful when you cross the street.

Anna and Ben like to play in the garden. They see many bugs and flowers. They also see a cricket. It is green and jumps fast.
"Look, a cricket!" Anna says. "Let's catch it and keep it as a pet."
Ben nods. He runs after the cricket with a jar. But the cricket is too quick. It jumps over the jar and hides under a leaf.
"Come on, cricket, don't be shy," Ben says. "We will be nice to you."
But the cricket refuses to come out. It likes to be free and hop around. It does not want to live in a jar.
Anna and Ben are sad. They want a pet. They look around for another bug. They see a snail. It is slow and slimy.
"Maybe we can keep the snail as a pet," Anna says. "It won't run away."
Ben shakes his head. He does not like the snail. He thinks it is boring and icky.
"No, thank you," he says. "I want a pet that is fun and reliable. Like a dog or a cat."
Anna and Ben decide to leave the bugs alone. They go back to the house and ask their mom for a real pet. Maybe she will say yes.

One day, while Fin was swimming, he met a new friend. The new friend was a frog named Fred. "Hi, I'm Fin!" said Fin. "Hi, I'm Fred!" said Fred. "Let's swim together!" So, Fin and Fred swam in patterns, making big circles and little circles together.
As they swam, something unexpected happened. A big bird swooped down and tried to catch Fred! But Fin was quick. He jumped out of the water and pushed Fred away. The big bird missed them both. Fin and Fred were safe! They swam back to their friends, happy to be together. And from that day on, they were best friends forever.

Sam and Anna were best friends. They liked to play together every day. Sometimes they played with dolls, sometimes they played with cars, and sometimes they played pretend.
One day, they decided to play pretend with a big box. They cut out a door and a window in the box and made it their house. They used a thread to make a curtain for the window and a blanket to make a roof.
"Let's imagine we are a family," said Sam. "I will be the dad and you will be the mom."
"OK," said Anna. "And this is our baby." She held a stuffed bear in her arms.
They had fun pretending to cook, clean, and take care of the baby. They also pretended to go to work, to the park, and to the store.
But then, Sam had an idea. He wanted to pretend to be a superhero. He took a towel and tied it around his neck like a cape. He said, "I will be Super Sam. I can fly and save the world."
Anna wanted to play along, but she also liked their house. She said, "But what about our baby? Who will take care of him?"
Sam said, "You can be Super Anna. You can fly with me and help me fight the bad guys."
Anna said, "But I like our house. It is cozy and nice. And our baby needs us. He might get lonely or scared."
Sam said, "Don't worry. He will be fine. He has the thread curtain and the blanket roof. Come on, let's go."
Anna felt sad. She wanted to be a good mom and a good friend. She didn't want to leave the baby or the house. But she also didn't want to make Sam unhappy. She didn't know what to do.
She thought for a moment. Then she said, "How about this? We can take turns. First, you can be Super Sam and I will be the mom. Then, I can be Super Anna and you will be the dad. That way, we can both have fun and be dependable."

Sometimes, when Mama or Daddy was putting the clothes away, they would remind the little girl how important it is to keep the laundry basket full. That way, when it was time for the laundry to go away and get washed, the little girl would already have plenty of clothes ready to go.
The little girl nodded and smiled. She knew it was important to listen to Mama and Daddy, so she made sure to keep the laundry basket full. She especially liked putting her special blue shirt in it; it would remind her of her Mama and Daddy.


Once upon a time, in a small house, a boy named Tim lived with his mom. They had a big tree in their yard. The tree had many pears. The pears were big, round, and green. Tim liked to eat pears. But, Tim was small, and he could not reach the pears on the tree.
One cold day, Tim saw a pear on the ground. He picked it up and showed it to his mom. "Look, Mom! I found a pear!" he said. His mom smiled and said, "Good job, Tim! Let's eat it together."
Tim and his mom sat down to eat the pear. They cut it into pieces. The pear was sweet and juicy. Tim was happy. He wanted to reach more pears from the tree. So, he asked his mom, "Can you help me reach the pears on the tree?"
His mom said, "Yes, Tim. I will help you." She picked up Tim and lifted him high. Tim reached for the pears. He got a big, green pear from the tree. Tim and his mom ate more pears. They were very happy. And from that day on, they always reached for pears together.


Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play basketball in the park. They have a big orange basketball that bounces high. They take turns to throw the basketball into the hoop.
One day, a nosy boy comes to the park. He sees Lily and Ben playing basketball. He wants to play too, but he does not ask nicely. He says, "Give me the basketball. I am better than you. You are too small and slow."
Lily and Ben do not like the nosy boy. He is rude and mean. They say, "No, you cannot have our basketball. It is ours. We are playing nicely. You are not. Go away."
The nosy boy gets angry. He tries to grab the basketball from Lily and Ben. He pushes and pulls and shouts. Lily and Ben hold on to the basketball. They do not let go.
A lady sees the nosy boy. She is the park keeper. She comes to Lily and Ben. She says, "What is going on here? Why are you fighting over the basketball?"
Lily and Ben tell the lady what happened. They tell her that the nosy boy was rude and mean. They tell her that he did not ask nicely. They tell her that he tried to take their basketball.
The lady nods. She says, "I see. That is not nice at all. The nosy boy should say sorry. He should learn to share and be polite. He should not bother you when you are playing nicely."
The lady takes the nosy boy by the hand. She says, "Come with me. We need to talk. You need to learn some manners. You need to say sorry to Lily and Ben."
The nosy boy hangs his head. He says, "Sorry, Lily and Ben. Sorry, lady. I was wrong. I will not do it again."
Lily and Ben smile. They say, "Thank you, lady. Thank you, nosy boy. We forgive you. Maybe you can play with us next time. But you have to ask nicely and be kind."
The lady smiles too. She says, "That is very nice of you, Lily and Ben. You are good friends. You are good at playing basketball. Have fun and be safe."
Lily and Ben wave to the lady and the nosy boy. They go back to playing basketball. They have fun and are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Tim. He had a cup that he loved very much. Every day, he would fill the cup with water and drink from it. One day, Tim saw a rock near his house. He thought it would be fun to talk to the rock.
"Hi, rock," said Tim. "Do you want to be my friend?" To his surprise, the rock answered, "Yes, Tim, I would like to be your friend!"
Tim was so happy to have a new friend. He played with the rock all day. They had fun running, jumping, and laughing. Then, Tim had an idea. He ran inside and got his cup. He filled it with water and brought it to the rock.
"Here, rock, have some water," Tim said, pouring the water on the rock. Suddenly, the rock began to shake and change. It grew bigger and bigger until it turned into a big, friendly dog!
The dog wagged its tail and licked Tim's face. "Thank you, Tim," said the dog. "I was a dog turned into a rock by a mean witch. You saved me with your kindness and your cup of water!"
From that day on, Tim and the dog were the best of friends. They played together every day and had lots of fun. And Tim learned that even the smallest act of kindness could make a big difference.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in the garden. They enjoyed digging, watering and picking flowers. One day, they saw a bright red berry on a bush. It looked yummy and juicy.
"Can we eat it?" Lily asked Ben.
"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe it is poison. Poison is bad. It makes you sick or sleepy."
"Let's ask Mom," Lily said. "She is dependable. She knows everything."
They ran to the house and showed Mom the berry. Mom looked at it and shook her head.
"No, no, no," she said. "This is not a berry. This is a cherry tomato. It is not poison. It is good. You can eat it, but only after you wash it."
She took them to the sink and helped them wash the cherry tomato. Then she cut it in half and gave one piece to each twin.
"Mmm, this is delicious," Lily said.
"Thank you, Mom," Ben said.
They smiled and hugged Mom. They were happy and safe. They enjoyed their snack.

Soon, Anna could feel her stomach struggle to hold all the food. Her stomach hurt and Anna had to stop eating.
Anna felt so sad that she couldn't keep eating the amazing treats. She wished she listened to her parents earlier and stopped eating sooner.
The next time Anna went on a picnic, she remembered to listen to her parents' advice. She ate only until her stomach felt full and felt so happy that she made the right choice.
Anna learned that it's ok to eat amazing treats, but to only eat until her tummy is full. That way, she can enjoy the treats without making her stomach struggle!

"Don't worry, Bob," said Sam. "You will grow a new tooth soon."
Bob felt better and they kept playing. Then, something unexpected happened. A fairy appeared and picked up Bob's tooth. She smiled and gave Bob a big, shiny nut.

"That's cool, Tom, but I can go faster than you," Lily said, as she zoomed her car around the carpet. "I can race you to the other side of the room. Ready, set, go!"
Tom and Lily started to drive their toys as fast as they could, but they did not see that their mom had left her purse on the floor. Lily's car bumped into the purse and made it fall over. Some things came out of the purse, including a shiny badge and a whistle.
"Wow, what's this?" Lily asked, as she picked up the badge. "It looks like a star."
"That's mom's badge, Lily. She is a police," Tom said. "She helps people and catches bad guys. She wears the badge on her shirt and the whistle on her neck."
"Can I try it?" Lily asked, as she put the badge on her shirt and the whistle in her mouth. She blew the whistle and made a loud sound. "Wee-woo, wee-woo, I'm a police too!"
Tom and Lily laughed and played with the badge and the whistle, pretending they were police. They did not hear their mom coming back from the kitchen. She saw them with her things and smiled.
"Hey, you two, what are you doing with my stuff?" she asked, as she picked up her purse and put the things back in. "Are you having fun?"
"Yes, mom, we are playing police," Tom said. "You are a good police, mom. We want to be like you."
"Thank you, Tom. That's very sweet of you," mom said. "But you know, being a police is not always easy. Sometimes it can be hard and scary. That's why I need you and Lily to be good and safe when I'm not home."
"We will, mom. We love you," Lily said. "Can we give you a hug?"
"Of course, you can," mom said, as she hugged them both. "You are my best helpers and my favorite people. You make me feel comfortable and happy."

Once upon a time there was a shy little lamb named Lucy. She lived on a green farm with her family, but she was always too scared to explore. One day, as Lucy watched other animals walk though the farm gate, she decided to be brave and follow. But when she put her hoof on the gate, she was too scared to move it again.
Suddenly, a friendly goat appeared by her side.
"Hi there, Lucy. What's the matter?" The goat asked.
"I want to go through the gate, but I'm too shy" said Lucy.
The goat smiled and said "Come, let's go together. I'll show you the way." He then opened the gate and they both walked out of the farm.
Together they explored the fields, looking for food. They ate grass, leaves and delicious berries. Lucy was having so much fun with her new friend and she soon felt less shy.
At the end of a wonderful day, Lucy returned back to the gate with a big smile on her face. She couldn't wait to explore more of the farm with her new friend.

Anna loved to look at the big book of animals. She liked to point at the pictures and say their names. She knew many animals, like dog, cat, fish, and cow. But her favorite animal was the owl. She liked how the owl had big eyes, a round head, and soft feathers. She wished she could see a real owl someday.
One night, Anna heard a strange sound outside her window. It was like a soft hoo-hoo. She got out of her bed and looked out. She saw a dark shape on a branch. It was an owl! Anna was so happy and excited. She opened the window and said, "Hello, owl! I like you. You are charming. Do you want to be my friend?"
The owl looked at Anna and tilted its head. It seemed curious and friendly. It hoo-hooed back at Anna. Anna smiled and asked, "What is your name, owl? Can you talk to me?" The owl blinked and hoo-hooed again. Anna thought the owl was trying to talk to her. She said, "My name is Anna. I have a big book of animals. Do you want to see it?"
The owl nodded and flew to Anna's window. Anna was very careful and gentle. She picked up the owl and brought it to her bed. She showed the owl her book of animals. She pointed at the pictures and said their names. The owl looked at the book and listened to Anna. It seemed to like the book. It hoo-hooed when Anna said the names of the animals.
Anna and the owl had a lot of fun. They looked at the book, played with Anna's toys, and cuddled on the bed. Anna felt very happy and sleepy. She said, "Owl, you are my best friend. I love you. Can you stay with me?" The owl nuzzled Anna and hoo-hooed softly. It seemed to say yes. Anna hugged the owl and closed her eyes. She fell asleep with the owl in her arms.
The next morning, Anna woke up and looked for the owl. But the owl was gone. Anna felt sad and confused. She wondered where the owl went. She looked out the window and saw a note on the branch. It was written in big letters. It said, "Thank you, Anna. You are a charming friend. I had to go back to my home. But I will come back to visit you. Love, Owl." Anna smiled and felt happy again. She knew the owl was her friend. She said, "Bye, owl. See you soon. I love you too." She put the note in her book of animals. She hoped to see the owl again. She knew the owl would come back. It was a test of their friendship. And they passed.

"Okay, here's my joke. Why is a slide heavy?" Lily asked.

"I don't know. Why is a slide heavy?" he asked.

"That was a good joke!" the boy said. "And a good slide!"
They got up and introduced themselves. The boy's name was Ben. They decided to play together and tell more jokes. They had a lot of fun at the park. Lily and Ben became good friends.
