Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with toys. One day, Tom brings a new toy to Mia's house. It is a tank. It can move and make noise.
"Look at my tank!" Tom says. "It is big and strong. I own it. It is mine."
Mia likes the tank. She wants to play with it too. She asks Tom, "Can I try your tank? Please?"
Tom shakes his head. "No, you can't. It is my tank. You have your own toys. Go play with them."
Mia feels sad and frustrated. She thinks Tom is not nice. She says, "That is not fair. You are not sharing. Sharing is good. You are being mean."
Tom does not listen. He keeps playing with his tank. He makes it go forward and backward. He makes it shoot and roar.
Mia gets angry. She grabs the tank from Tom. She says, "Give me the tank! It is my turn!"
Tom gets angry too. He pulls the tank back. He says, "No, it is not! It is my tank! Let go!"
They both tug and pull. They both yell and cry. The tank breaks. It stops moving and making noise.
Tom and Mia look at the broken tank. They feel sorry and ashamed. They wish they had shared. They say, "We are sorry. We are sorry."

Jimmy couldn't contain his excitement. It was his birthday and his parents had bought him a shiny new book. As he opened the first page, he felt a jolly feeling of joy. He blinked and looked around to show his parents how much he was enjoying his present.
Suddenly, there was a loud bang outside his house. Everyone was running away, shouting and screaming. Jimmy's parents quickly gathered him up and darted for safety. Jimmy stroked his book before leaving.
Jimmy's parents kept Jimmy safe during the danger, but when they returned home, he saw the sad sight of his ruined bedroom. His book was gone - the page where he had blinked was gone too.
Jimmy couldn't believe it. His jolly feeling had gone away and he was feeling so sad. Even worse, the danger was still lurking outside. Jimmy buried his head in his mother's chest and stayed there for a long time. His birthday had taken a bad turn.

Once there was a mighty dragon called Anna. She was so brave that everyone around believed in her. One day Anna saw a box of sugar and she was very excited. She opened it right away, not knowing the danger it could bring.
Suddenly the box started talking. "Please, don't take the sugar," it said. "Doing so will bring you terrible trouble". But Anna didn't believe it. "No no, I'm mighty," she thought. So Anna kept taking the sugar and continued eating it.
Soon there were loud screams from other dragons in the distance. Anna was so curious that she flew towards them. But what she saw was horrifying. There were all the other dragons, rotten and burned. "What happened?" Anna asked. The answer came from the box of sugar: "I warned you not to take the sugar. It was cursed, and now a terrible doom awaits those who took it. I'm sorry."
Anna was heartbroken. She knew this was her fault, for not believing the box. She wished she could turn back time, but it was too late. The mighty dragon was doomed to suffer the same fate.

Suddenly, a bee came out of the flower. It buzzed and flew around Lily's head. Lily was scared. She screamed and ran away.
Ben laughed. He thought it was funny. He said, "I told you the flower was fake. The bee was fake too. It was a toy. I put it there to trick you. It was a joke."
Lily was angry. She did not like Ben's joke. She said, "That was not a joke. That was mean. You made me feel bad. You are not a good friend."
Ben felt sorry. He realized he was wrong. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I did not mean to hurt you. I was just having fun. Please forgive me. I will not do it again."
Lily looked at Ben. She saw he was sincere. She said, "OK, Ben. I forgive you. But next time, be nice. Do not play tricks on me. Or on anyone else."
Ben nodded. He said, "You are right, Lily. I will be nice. I will not play tricks. I will be a good friend."
Lily smiled. She said, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. Do you want to play with me?"
Ben smiled too. He said, "Yes, Lily. I want to play with you. What do you want to play?"
Lily said, "How about we play with the slide? It is fun and real."
Ben agreed. He said, "OK, let's play with the slide. It is fun and real. And no more fake flowers or bees."
They held hands and ran to the slide. They played and laughed. They were happy.
The moral of the story is: Do not play tricks on your friends. It is not nice. It can hurt their feelings. Be honest and kind. That is how you make good friends.

Tim and Lily were playing in the garden. They saw a big vine that grew on the wall. It had many green leaves and purple flowers.
"Let's climb the vine!" Tim said. "It looks like fun!"
Lily was not sure. "But what if we fall? Or what if Mom and Dad get angry?"
Tim shrugged. "Don't be scared. They won't see us. And the vine is tough. It can hold us."
He grabbed the vine and started to pull himself up. Lily followed him, but she felt nervous. The vine was high and wobbly.
They reached the top of the wall and looked around. They saw the neighbor's dog, a big and black one. It barked at them and ran towards the wall.
"Uh-oh!" Tim said. "The dog is mad at us! We have to go down!"
They tried to slide down the vine, but it was not easy. The vine was rough and scratchy. It hurt their hands and legs. The dog jumped and snapped at them.
"Help!" Lily cried. "Mom! Dad!"
Mom and Dad heard them and came outside. They saw Tim and Lily on the vine and the dog on the ground. They were shocked and worried.
"Tim! Lily! What are you doing?" Mom shouted. "Get down from there!"
Dad grabbed a stick and scared the dog away. He helped Tim and Lily down from the vine. They were dirty and bleeding.
Mom hugged them and checked their wounds. She was angry and sad.
"Why did you climb the vine?" she asked. "You could have been hurt badly! Or bitten by the dog! You know you are not allowed to do that!"
Tim and Lily looked down. They felt sorry and ashamed.
"We wanted to have fun," Tim said. "We thought the vine was tough."
"But it was not safe," Lily said. "We were wrong."
Mom and Dad took them inside and cleaned their wounds. They gave them a hug and a kiss.
"We love you, Tim and Lily," they said. "But you have to be careful and listen to us. We only want you to be safe and happy."
Tim and Lily nodded. They learned their lesson. They never climbed the vine again.

Tom liked to whistle. He whistled when he walked, when he played, and when he was happy. He learned to whistle from his dad, who whistled a lot too. Tom wanted to whistle like his dad, who could make different sounds and tunes with his mouth.
One day, Tom and his dad went to the park. They saw a big, modern building with glass and metal. Tom thought it looked shiny and cool. He asked his dad what it was.
"That's a museum, Tom. It's a place where people can see old and new things, like paintings and statues and machines. Do you want to go inside and look?" his dad said.
"Yes, please!" Tom said. He was curious and excited.
They went inside the museum and saw many things. Tom liked the colorful paintings and the funny statues. He also liked the machines that moved and made noises. He whistled along with some of them. His dad smiled and whistled with him.
They came to a room that had a sign that said "Rocks and Minerals". Tom saw many stones of different shapes and colors. Some were shiny, some were dull, some were smooth, some were rough. He wanted to touch them and feel them.
"Can I touch the stones, dad?" he asked.
"Sure, but be careful. Some of them are very old and fragile. And don't take any of them with you, okay? They belong to the museum," his dad said.
"Okay, dad," Tom said. He touched some of the stones gently. He liked how they felt in his hand. He saw one stone that was round and white. It had a hole in the middle. It looked like a donut. He thought it was funny and cute. He picked it up and put it in his pocket. He forgot what his dad said.
They left the museum and went back to the park. Tom and his dad played catch with a ball. Tom was happy and whistled. He felt the stone in his pocket. He wanted to show it to his dad.
"Dad, look what I found in the museum!" he said. He took out the stone and showed it to his dad.
"Tom, that's not yours. That's a fossil. It's a very old stone that has the shape of an animal that lived a long time ago. It's very rare and valuable. You can't take it from the museum. That's stealing. You have to give it back," his dad said. He was angry and disappointed.
Tom felt bad. He didn't know it was a fossil. He didn't mean to steal. He liked the stone, but he didn't want to make his dad mad. He wanted to do the right thing.
"I'm sorry, dad. I didn't know. I'll give it back. Please don't be mad at me," he said. He started to cry.
His dad hugged him and said, "It's okay, Tom. I'm not mad at you. I'm glad you told me the truth. You made a mistake, but you can fix it. Let's go back to the museum and return the fossil. Maybe they'll let you whistle with the machines again."
Tom nodded and smiled. He wiped his tears and whistled. He held his dad's hand and walked back to the museum. He hoped they would forgive him. He learned a lesson. He would never take anything that wasn't his again. He would only whistle.

When they got to the air show, they saw many jets parked on the ground. Some were shiny and new, and some were old and rusty. Sara and Ben ran to look at them and touch them. Dad told them to be careful and not to climb on them.
"Look, Dad, this jet has a star on it!" Sara said, pointing to a red and white plane.
"That's a Soviet jet, Sara. It was used by our enemies in the big war. But now we are friends with them," Dad explained.
"Wow, that's cool. And look, this jet has a cross on it!" Ben said, pointing to a black and yellow plane.
"That's a German jet, Ben. It was also used by our enemies in the big war. But now we are friends with them, too," Dad said.
Sara and Ben nodded. They wondered how the jets could be friends after fighting in the big war. They wanted to see them fly and make peace signs.
Soon, the air show started. The jets took off and flew in the sky. They made loops and twists and turns. They flew very fast and very high. Sara and Ben clapped and cheered. They loved the jets.
Then, the old planes came out. They were smaller and slower than the jets. They had propellers and wings. They looked like toys. Sara and Ben were not very impressed.
But then, something amazing happened. The old planes started to shoot at each other. They made loud bangs and smoke. They pretended to be in the big war. Sara and Ben gasped. They were scared.
"Dad, why are they shooting at each other? I thought they were friends!" Sara cried.
"Don't worry, Sara. It's just a display. They are not really shooting. They are just showing us how they fought in the big war. It's like a game," Dad said.
"But it's not a fun game, Dad. It's a scary game. I don't like it," Ben said.
"I know, Ben. It's not a fun game. It's a sad game. That's why we don't want to have another big war. We want to have peace and friendship," Dad said.
Sara and Ben hugged their dad. They understood. They hoped the old planes would stop shooting and be friends.

Mom hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She sees their animals and smiles. She says, "You both made very nice animals with blocks. But you know what? You can make even better animals if you work together. Why don't you try to add some blocks from each other's animals and see what happens?"

Tom and Lily were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make food with the pots and pans. They also liked to open and close the cabinet doors and see what was inside.
One day, they found a big jar of yellow powder in one of the cabinets. They did not know what it was, but it looked like sand. They decided to use it for their food. They poured some of it into a bowl and mixed it with water. Then they tasted it.
"Yuck!" Tom spat out the yellow paste. "This is bitter! It is not good for food!"
"Let me try!" Lily said. She took a spoonful of the paste and put it in her mouth. She made a face and spit it out too. "You are right, Tom. This is bitter and yucky!"
They did not want to play with the yellow powder anymore. They wanted to get rid of it. They looked around the kitchen and saw the trash can. They thought that was a good place to put the yellow powder. They carried the bowl to the trash can and dumped the paste inside.
But they did not see that the trash can was full of paper and cardboard. The yellow powder was not sand. It was fire powder. It made a big boom and a big fire. The fire spread to the paper and the cardboard and the trash can. It also spread to the cabinet and the wall and the curtains.
"Help! Help!" Tom and Lily screamed. "Fire! Fire!"
Mom and Dad heard their screams and ran to the kitchen. They saw the fire and grabbed the fire extinguisher. They sprayed the fire with the white foam and put it out. They were very angry and scared.
"Tom! Lily! What did you do?" Mom shouted. "You could have burned the house down! You could have hurt yourselves!"
"We are sorry, Mom!" Tom and Lily cried. "We did not know it was fire powder! We thought it was sand! We wanted to make food!"
Mom and Dad hugged them and checked them for injuries. They were glad they were not hurt. But they were also very sad. The fire had destroyed the cabinet and the wall and the curtains. They had to call the firemen and the repairmen to fix the damage.
They also had to explain to Tom and Lily what fire powder was and why it was dangerous. They told them to never play with things they did not know and to always ask before they touched anything. They also told them to never taste anything that was not food.
Tom and Lily learned their lesson. They said they were sorry again and again. They also helped Mom and Dad clean up the mess. They never played with fire powder again. They only played with safe things. And they always asked before they opened any cabinet.

Sam and Mia like to play in the park. They like to swing on the swings, slide on the slide, and run on the grass. One day, they see a new thing in the park. It is a pitch. It has a big net and a small ball.
"Look, Mia, a pitch!" Sam says. "Let's play with the ball!"
"OK, Sam, but how do we play?" Mia asks.
Sam picks up the ball and throws it to Mia. Mia catches it and throws it back. They do this for a while, and then Sam has an idea.
"Let's swing the ball!" he says. "I will swing it to you, and you will swing it to me!"
"OK, Sam, but how do we swing the ball?" Mia asks.
Sam shows Mia how to swing the ball. He holds the ball in one hand, and swings his arm back and forth. Then he lets go of the ball, and it flies to Mia.
"Wow, Sam, you swing the ball so well!" Mia says. She tries to swing the ball back to Sam, but she swings too hard, and the ball goes over the net.
"Oh no, Mia, the ball is gone!" Sam says. "How will we get it back?"
They run to the net, and see that the ball is on the other side. There is a gate, but it is closed.
"Maybe we can open the gate," Mia says. She pushes the gate, but it does not move.
"Maybe we can climb the net," Sam says. He tries to climb the net, but it is too high.
They are sad, and do not know what to do. Then they hear a voice.
"Hello, kids, do you need some help?" the voice says.
They look up, and see a man. He is wearing a hat and a shirt with a logo. He is holding a big bag.
"Who are you?" Sam asks.
"I am the coach," the man says. "I work here at the pitch. I teach people how to play with the ball."
"Can you help us get our ball back?" Mia asks.
"Sure, I can," the coach says. "The gate is locked, but I have the key. Follow me."
The coach opens the gate, and walks to the other side. He picks up the ball, and gives it to Sam and Mia.
"Here you go, kids, your ball," he says. "Do you like to play with the ball?"
"Yes, we do," Sam and Mia say. "We like to swing the ball."
"That's great," the coach says. "Do you want to learn more about how to swing the ball?"
"Yes, we do," Sam and Mia say.
"OK, then, come with me," the coach says. "I will show you some tips and tricks. And maybe you can join my team someday."
Sam and Mia are happy, and follow the coach. They learn how to swing the ball better, and have fun. They make a new friend, and find a new game. They like the pitch.

Lily loved to draw. She drew many things: flowers, animals, stars, and people. She used many colors and made her pictures bright and happy. She wanted to show her drawings to everyone.
One day, her teacher said they would have a drawing contest. The children could display their drawings on the wall and a judge would pick the best one. Lily was very enthusiastic. She thought she could win the contest. She worked hard on her drawing and made it very big and beautiful.
The next day, the children brought their drawings to school. Lily saw that the other children had different kinds of drawings. Some were small and simple, some were dark and scary, some were funny and silly. Lily thought her drawing was the best. She put it on the wall and waited for the judge.
The judge came and looked at all the drawings. He smiled and nodded and said nice things. He said he liked all the drawings because they showed the children's imagination and feelings. He said there was no best drawing, because every drawing was special and unique. He gave every child a sticker and a hug.
Lily felt confused. She thought her drawing was better than the others. She wanted to win the contest. She wanted the judge to say her drawing was the best. She felt angry and sad.
Her teacher saw her face and came to talk to her. She said, "Lily, why are you unhappy? You have a wonderful drawing and a sticker and a hug. You should be proud of yourself."
Lily said, "But I wanted to win. I wanted to have the best drawing. I worked so hard on it."
Her teacher said, "Lily, drawing is not a competition. Drawing is a way to express yourself and have fun. It doesn't matter if your drawing is big or small, bright or dark, happy or scary. What matters is that you enjoy drawing and share it with others. Everyone has a different style and a different story to tell. You can learn from other people's drawings and appreciate their creativity. You can also be happy for them and celebrate their achievements. That is the true meaning of drawing."
Lily thought about what her teacher said. She looked at the other children's drawings and saw that they were all different and interesting. She realized that she had been selfish and rude. She felt sorry and ashamed.
She said, "Teacher, I'm sorry. You are right. Drawing is not a competition. I was wrong to think that my drawing was the best. I should have been more respectful and kind to the other children. I want to apologize to them and tell them that I like their drawings."
Her teacher said, "That's very brave and mature of you, Lily. I'm proud of you. I'm sure the other children will forgive you and be your friends. Go ahead and talk to them. They are waiting for you."
Lily smiled and thanked her teacher. She went to the wall and looked at the other children's drawings. She found something nice to say about each one. She said sorry and gave them hugs. The other children smiled and thanked her. They said they liked her drawing too. They said they were happy to be her friends.
Lily felt happy and relieved. She learned a valuable lesson. She learned that drawing is not a competition, but a way to express yourself and have fun. She learned that everyone has a different style and a different story to tell. She learned that she should respect and appreciate other people's creativity. She learned that she should be happy for them and celebrate their achievements. She learned that drawing is a way to make friends and share joy. She learned that drawing is a wonderful thing.

The banana fell from the tree. Bobo and Toto were very happy. They laughed and ate the yummy banana together.

Tim and Liz were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with a hole in it. They wanted to see what was inside.
"Let's enter the tree!" Tim said.
"OK, but be careful!" Liz said.
They crawled into the hole and found a dark and cozy space. They saw a trunk with a lock on it.
"Wow, what is in the trunk?" Liz wondered.
"Maybe it is a treasure!" Tim guessed.
They tried to open the trunk, but it was too hard. They pushed and pulled, but nothing happened.
Suddenly, they heard a voice.
"Who is there? What are you doing in my tree?" The voice was angry and loud.
Tim and Liz were scared. They saw a man with a beard and a hat. He was the owner of the tree and the trunk.
"We are sorry, sir. We were just playing. We did not mean to bother you." Tim said.
"You should not enter other people's homes without permission. That is rude and wrong. And you should not touch other people's things. That is stealing and bad." The man said.
Tim and Liz felt ashamed. They knew they had made a mistake.
"We are very sorry, sir. We will not do it again. Please forgive us." Liz said.
The man looked at them. He saw they were young and curious. He decided to be kind.
"OK, I forgive you. But you have to promise me to respect other people's property and privacy. And you have to leave now. This is my home, not a playground." The man said.
Tim and Liz nodded. They thanked the man and crawled out of the hole. They ran back to their parents and told them what happened. They learned a lesson that day. They never entered the tree again.

Lily and Sam are scared. They run to the house. They slam the door. They take off their costumes. They hug each other.
They hear a knock on the door. They hear a voice. It is their dad. He says, "Sorry, kids. I forgot to tell you. I brought home a tiger from the zoo. He is my new friend. He is very nice. He just wanted to play with you. Can you come out and say hello?"
Lily and Sam look at each other. They shake their heads. They say, "No, thank you. We do not want to play with a tiger. We do not want to wear tiger costumes. We want to be safe and warm and hidden."

"Wow!" Lily and Ben said.

Charlie was walking in a meadow when he noticed a strange insect. He bent down on one knee and tried to get closer but it hopped away. He followed it, slowly and carefully and it eventually stopped on a rock.
"Hello strange insect," Charlie said. "Where do you live?" The strange insect just stepped away from the rock and onto the grass.
Charlie followed it, taking small steps and admiring its shiny antennae. Eventually, they reached an icy river. The river was so dark and cold that Charlie could not remember ever seeing an insect so close to it.
The strange insect stepped onto the icy water and for the first time Charlie noticed the reflection of his own face. He smiled and waved to the insect, and the insect waved back with it's little leg, and then hopped away into the woods.

Anna was a thoughtful girl who liked to help others. She often visited her grandma, who was old and used a cane to walk. Anna liked to talk to her grandma and listen to her stories.
One day, Anna saw a big bag of apples at the market. She thought they would make a nice gift for her grandma, who loved apples. She asked the seller how much they cost. The seller said they cost one coin for each apple.
Anna counted her coins. She had five coins. She could buy five apples, but the bag had more than five apples. She wanted to buy the whole bag for her grandma. She had an idea. She asked the seller if he had a scale to weigh the apples.
The seller nodded and brought out a scale. He put the bag of apples on one side and a weight on the other side. The scale balanced. He said the bag of apples weighed the same as the weight.
Anna looked at the weight. It had a number on it. The number was ten. Anna thought hard. She remembered that her grandma's cane also had a number on it. The number was ten. She wondered if her grandma's cane weighed the same as the bag of apples.
She asked the seller if he would trade the bag of apples for her grandma's cane. The seller was surprised, but he agreed. He gave Anna the bag of apples and took her grandma's cane.
Anna was happy. She ran to her grandma's house with the bag of apples. She knocked on the door and gave her grandma the bag of apples. She said she traded her grandma's cane for the apples.
Her grandma was shocked. She asked Anna why she did that. She said she needed her cane to walk. She said she could not walk without her cane.
Anna felt sad. She did not think of that. She wanted to make her grandma happy, but she made her unhappy. She said she was sorry. She said she would get her cane back.
She ran back to the market with the bag of apples. She looked for the seller, but he was gone. He had left with her grandma's cane. Anna cried. She did not know what to do.
A kind man saw Anna crying. He asked her what was wrong. Anna told him what happened. The kind man felt sorry for Anna. He said he had a spare cane at home. He said he would give it to Anna if she gave him the bag of apples.
Anna was grateful. She thanked the kind man and gave him the bag of apples. He gave her the spare cane. He said it was a good trade. He said he liked apples and he did not need two canes.
Anna smiled. She ran back to her grandma's house with the spare cane. She knocked on the door and gave her grandma the spare cane. She said she got it from a kind man who traded it for the bag of apples.
Her grandma was relieved. She hugged Anna and thanked her. She said she was proud of her. She said she was a thoughtful girl who learned from her mistake. She said she loved her.
Anna was happy. She hugged her grandma and said she loved her too. She said she learned a lesson. She said she would never trade something important for something less important. She said she would always think of the consequences of her actions.
The end.

As they played, Lily forgot about her screen. She realized that playing outside was more fun than watching her screen all day. She learned that it is important to try new things and enjoy the world around her.


Tom and Mia are playing with their toys in the living room. Tom has a big truck and Mia has a doll. Tom likes to make loud noises with his truck and pretend to crash into things. Mia likes to dress up her doll and talk to her.
"Tom, stop being so rude!" Mia says. "You are making too much noise and you are hurting my doll!"
Tom does not listen to Mia. He thinks his truck is more fun than her doll. He drives his truck closer to Mia and bumps into her doll. Mia's doll falls on the floor and her dress gets dirty.
"Tom, you are mean!" Mia cries. "You made my doll fall and you ruined her dress!"
Tom laughs and picks up Mia's doll. He sees that the doll has a rubber band around her hair. He pulls the rubber band and snaps it on the doll's head. The doll's hair gets messy and Mia gets more upset.
"Tom, give me back my doll!" Mia shouts. "You are hurting her!"
Tom runs away with the doll and heads to the door. He wants to hide the doll in his room and make Mia chase him. He thinks it is a funny game. He opens the door and runs outside. But he forgets to close the door behind him.
Mia sees the door open and runs after Tom. She wants to get her doll back and tell him to say sorry. She catches up with Tom in the garden and grabs the doll from his hands. Tom tries to hold on to the doll, but Mia is stronger. She pulls the doll away and hugs her.
"Tom, you are a bad boy!" Mia says. "You need to say sorry to me and to my doll!"
Tom does not want to say sorry. He thinks Mia is boring and he does not like her doll. He sticks out his tongue and makes a face at Mia. He turns around and runs back to the door. He wants to go to his room and play with his truck. He reaches the door and tries to open it. But he cannot. The door is locked.
Tom is confused and scared. He does not know why the door is locked. He does not have a key. He bangs on the door and calls for his mom. He hopes she will hear him and open the door.
But his mom does not hear him. She is in the kitchen, making lunch. She does not know that Tom and Mia are outside. She thinks they are still playing in the living room. She locked the door to keep them safe and to keep the bugs out.
Tom and Mia are stuck outside. They do not know what to do. They are hungry and thirsty and hot. They wish they had not been so rude to each other. They wish they had shared their toys and played nicely. They wish they could go back inside and say sorry to their mom. They wish they had a key.


Once upon a time there were two friends called John and Lucy. They had a big garden with lots of flowers and trees. One day, they were playing hide and seek. Suddenly, they heard a loud trumpet sound! They were very alert and they knew they had to find out where it was coming from.
John said, "Let's go and find out who is playing such a loud trumpet!" Lucy said, "OK!". So they followed the noise.
When they arrived at a big hill, they found an old man playing a trumpet. The man said, "Hello children! Can you help me find my glasses?" John and Lucy said, "Yes!" But, they didn't see the glasses anywhere.
The man said, "Let's look together!" So, John and Lucy looked for the glasses and eventually found them behind a nearby bush.
The man was so happy to have his glasses back, he said, "Thank you children! I am so grateful. Here, please have this trumpet as a gift!"
John and Lucy were overjoyed with their special gift and they kept it forever.
The end!


Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jane. She searched everywhere to find her favourite teddy bear.
Jane's mum said: "Go and search for it, Jane. I'm sure you will find it soon."
So Jane looked out of the window, around the chairs and under the sofa. She even looked outside the house but still found nothing.
Suddenly, Jane saw a shoulder in the corner and ran over to check it out. She looked closer and could not believe her eyes - there was her teddy bear! Jane was so happy she ran over to hug it.
But then, a little puppy appeared around the corner! Jane was angry that the puppy had taken her teddy bear and the puppy did not look very happy either.
Jane stuck out her hand and said: "Give me back my teddy bear." But the puppy didn't want to let go and growled.
But Jane was too determined to give up. She said: "Please give it back," and looked the puppy in the eyes with a determined smile.
And the little puppy finally let go of the teddy bear and ran away.
The end.


Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pink dress that she loved very much. One day, she went to the park with her mom. Lily's mom had a wallet with her to buy ice cream later.
At the park, Lily played with her friends. They ran, jumped, and laughed. Lily's mom sat on a bench and watched them play. She put her wallet next to her. Lily saw her mom's wallet and thought, "I should keep it safe."
Lily took the wallet and hid it in a secret place. She then went back to play with her friends. After a while, it was time to go home. Lily's mom looked for her wallet but could not find it. She asked Lily if she saw it. Lily said, "I hid it to keep it safe!"
Lily's mom asked her to get the wallet. Lily tried to remember where she hid it, but she could not. She insisted that she could find it if she looked more. They looked and looked, and finally, they found the wallet under a bush.
Lily and her mom were happy to find the wallet. They went to get ice cream, and Lily learned to always ask before taking something. From that day on, Lily never hid her mom's wallet again.


One day, a little fish named Fin was very hungry. He wanted to find some food to eat. He swam around the big blue sea, looking for something yummy. As he swam, he saw a big building in the water. Fin was curious and decided to swim closer.
As he got near the building, he saw a little crab named Carl. Carl was also hungry. Fin said, "Hi, I'm Fin. I'm looking for food. Are you hungry too?" Carl said, "Yes, I am. Let's look for food together!" So, Fin and Carl swam around the building, searching for something to eat.
As they swam, they found a hidden door in the building. They went inside and saw a big room full of food! They couldn't believe their eyes. Fin and Carl ate and ate until they were not hungry anymore. They were so happy they found the secret food room. From that day on, Fin and Carl were best friends and always swam together in the big blue sea.

Max ran to the pond and shouted, "Hello, ducks! Let's play!" The ducks looked confused. They did not know what Max wanted to do. One duck said, "Why do you shout, Max? We are scared."
Max felt sad. He did not want to scare the ducks. He said, "I am sorry, ducks. I just want to be friends." The ducks smiled and said, "Okay, Max. We can be friends, but please do not shout." Max and the ducks played together and had a lot of fun.


Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a strong bear named Ben. Ben loved to nap under his favorite tree. He had a pattern of napping every day after eating his lunch.
One day, while Ben was taking his nap, a little bird saw him. The bird thought, "I want to be friends with this strong bear." So, the bird sat on a branch above Ben and started to sing a pretty song.
Ben woke up from his nap, surprised by the song. He looked up and saw the little bird. Ben smiled and said, "Thank you for your song, little bird. Let's be friends." The bird and Ben became best friends, and they learned that even the smallest act of kindness can make someone's day.


Once upon a time, there was a wise old dog named Spot. Spot lived in a small house with a big yard. Every day, Spot would run and play in the yard. He loved to chase birds and dig holes.
One day, a little boy named Tim came to the yard. He saw Spot and said, "Hi, Spot! Can I play with you?" Spot was happy to have a friend and they played together all day. They ran and jumped and had lots of fun.
As the day went on, it was time for Tim to go home. Spot didn't want Tim to leave, so he didn't close the gate to the yard. When Tim left, Spot went to sleep. In the night, a big mean dog came into the yard. The big dog saw the open gate and went in. The big dog chased Spot and hurt him. Spot was very sad and wished he had closed the gate.


Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play together. One day, they found a big bottle of milk in the fridge. They wanted to drink some, but they did not know how old it was.
"Let's try it," Ben said. He opened the bottle and smelled it. He made a face. "It smells funny."
"Maybe it's good," Sara said. She wanted to encourage Ben. "Maybe it's a new kind of milk. Maybe it's sweet and yummy."
Ben was not sure, but he liked to try new things. He poured some milk into a cup and took a sip. He spat it out right away. "Blech! It's sour! It's bad! It hurts my mouth!"
Sara saw Ben's reaction and felt sorry for him. She did not want to drink the milk anymore. She gave him a hug and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I was wrong. It's not a new kind of milk. It's old milk. It's spoiled. We should throw it away."
They ran to the sink and poured the milk down the drain. They rinsed their cups and mouths with water. They decided to have some juice instead. They learned to check the date on the bottle before they drink milk. They also learned to trust their noses more than their ears.


One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. They saw a man with a big leather bag. The man said, "Hi! I provide tasty treats for kids. Would you like one?" Tim's mom said yes, and the man gave Tim a tasty cookie.
Tim and his mom walked around the park. They saw a big tree with a hole in it. Tim put his hand in the hole and felt something soft. He pulled it out, and it was a small leather bag! It looked just like the big leather bag the man had.
Tim opened the small leather bag and found more tasty cookies inside. He shared them with his mom and said, "Now I can provide tasty treats too!" Just then, a squirrel came out of the tree hole. The squirrel looked at Tim and said, "Thank you for finding my tasty treats!" Tim and his mom were surprised to hear the squirrel talk, but they were happy to share the cookies with their new friend.


Once upon a time, a little girl named Madison was playing in her garage. She saw a cookie on the ground and was so excited to eat it.
"Yummy! I love cookies," she exclaimed.
She took a bite and tried to chew it, but it was too hard. Madison wrinkled her nose and said, "This cookie is too hard."
Suddenly, Madison heard a voice from behind her. It was her mom. "Madison, why don't you try putting the cookie in your mouth, taking a sip of your drink and then try to chew it again?"
Madison followed her mom's advice. She put the cookie in her mouth, took a sip of water and then she was able to chew it more easily.
Madison smiled brightly. "Yay! I can eat the cookie now!" And so Madison happily finished her delicious cookie.


Once upon a time, there was a beautiful school in a small town. In this school, many little kids came to learn new things. One day, a new girl named Lily joined the school. She was shy and scared to talk to the other kids.
At playtime, a boy named Tom saw Lily sitting alone. He walked up to her and said, "Hi, I am Tom. Do you want to play with me?" Lily looked up and smiled. She said, "Yes, I would like that." They played together and had a lot of fun.
As the days went by, Lily and Tom learned many things together in the beautiful school. They learned to share their toys and help each other. The other kids saw them and started to do the same. Everyone in the school became kind and helpful. The moral of the story is that when we are kind and help others, we can make the world a beautiful place.


Lila and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to look for things in the grass and the trees. They found some stones, some leaves, and some twigs. Lila picked up a twig and tried to whistle with it. She put it in her mouth and blew hard, but nothing happened.
"Look, Tom, I have a whistle!" she said.
Tom looked at her and laughed. "That is not a whistle, Lila. That is a twig. You cannot whistle with a twig. You need a hole in it, like this." He showed her his whistle, which was a small plastic tube with a hole in the middle.
"Wow, can I try?" Lila asked.
"Sure, here you go." Tom gave her his whistle and took her twig. He blew on the twig, but nothing happened. He smiled and said, "See? It does not work."
Lila put the whistle in her mouth and blew hard. She made a loud sound that scared some birds. She was very happy and said, "Look, Tom, I can whistle!"
Tom clapped and said, "Good job, Lila! You are very smart. Can I have my whistle back?"
Lila nodded and gave him his whistle. They took turns whistling and laughing. They did not see a hidden squirrel that was watching them from a tree. The squirrel was curious and wanted to try the whistle too. It waited until Lila and Tom were busy with something else, and then it jumped down and grabbed the whistle. It ran away with it, making a funny noise.
Lila and Tom heard the noise and looked around. They saw the squirrel with the whistle in its mouth. They were surprised and said, "Hey, that is our whistle! Give it back, squirrel!"
They chased the squirrel, but it was too fast and too clever. It climbed up another tree and hid the whistle in a hole. Lila and Tom could not reach it. They were sad and said, "Oh, no, we lost our whistle. How will we whistle now?"
They looked at each other and had an idea. They put their lips together and blew. They made a sound that was like a whistle, but softer and sweeter. They smiled and said, "Look, Tom, look, Lila, we can whistle with our mouths!"
They whistled with their mouths and forgot about the whistle and the squirrel. They were happy and had fun. The squirrel watched them and felt sorry. It took the whistle out of the hole and dropped it on the ground. It hoped that Lila and Tom would find it and forgive it. It whistled with its mouth and ran away.

"Look, Ben, I have a hammer!" she said.
Ben saw the hammer and felt scared. He did not like loud noises or hard things. He urged Lily to put the hammer down.
"Please, Lily, no hammer. Hammer is bad. Hammer makes noise. Hammer hurts box. Put hammer back," he said.
Lily did not listen to Ben. She liked the hammer. She thought it was fun to hit the box. She hit the box harder and harder. The box made a loud bang. Ben covered his ears and cried.
"Stop, Lily, stop! You are mean. You make me sad. You make box sad. Hammer is not fun. Hammer is mean," he said.
Lily heard Ben cry and felt sorry. She did not want to make Ben or the box sad. She stopped hitting the box and put the hammer back. She hugged Ben and said sorry.
"I'm sorry, Ben. I did not know you did not like hammer. I did not know hammer was mean. I will be gentle. I will not hit box. I will play with you. Do you want to play with me?" she said.
Ben nodded and smiled. He forgave Lily. He was glad she was gentle. He wanted to play with her. They looked for something else to play with in the box. They found a ball and a teddy bear. They played with the ball and the teddy bear. They had fun. They were happy.

Once upon a time, in a village far away, lived a little bunny called Lucy. One day, Lucy wanted to travel and she hopped off into the wood. She hopped and hopped and saw many things, as she stopped to smell the flowers.
But then, Lucy came across a wreck - a broken-down old car! Lucy hopped up to take a closer look and was amazed at how fast it was. She spoke out loud, "I wonder how it got here!".
A wise owl heard her and said, "It's a lesson for you, Lucy. Things that go too fast end up slowing down or stopping completely. If you want to travel, you must go at a steady and safe speed".
Lucy thanked the wise owl and hopped off, hopping at the steady and safe speed she should. Lucy's travels were more enjoyable now and she learned a valuable lesson. The moral of the story is that we must learn to take care of our things and not go too fast, so we don't wreck them!

"Wow, a camera!" Sara says. "Let's go outside and take pictures of the flowers and the birds."
"Okay!" Ben says. "And we can take pictures of Spot, too. He is very funny."
They run outside with the camera and Spot. They see many pretty things. They take turns to hold the camera and press the button. They hear a click sound when they take a picture.
"Look, a butterfly!" Sara says. She points to a yellow and black butterfly on a pink flower. She gives the camera to Ben. "You take a picture of it."
Ben holds the camera and tries to aim at the butterfly. He presses the button. But the butterfly flies away.
"Oh no!" Ben says. "I missed it."
Sara hugs him. "It's okay. Maybe we can find another butterfly. Or we can take a picture of something else."
They look around and see Spot. He is chasing his own tail. He is spinning and spinning. He looks very silly.
"Let's take a picture of Spot!" Sara says. She takes the camera from Ben. She aims at Spot and presses the button. She hears a click sound.
But Spot stops spinning. He looks at the camera. He blinks. He thinks the camera is a toy. He runs towards Sara and Ben. He jumps on them. He licks their faces.
"Spot, no!" Sara says. "You are making us wet."
"Spot, stop!" Ben says. "You are messing up the camera."
They laugh and push Spot away. They look at the camera. They see a picture of Spot on the screen. He is blinking and smiling.
"Wow, what a lucky picture!" Sara says. "Spot looks very cute."
"Yes, he does!" Ben says. "We have a lucky camera. And a lucky dog."
They hug Spot and the camera. They are very happy.

Lily liked to help her mom in the kitchen. She liked to mix things in a big bowl. Mom said mixing was fun and good for making yummy food.
One day, mom gave Lily a banana. She said, "Do you want to make banana bread with me?" Lily nodded and smiled. She loved banana bread. It was sweet and soft and warm.
Mom peeled the banana and broke it into small pieces. She put them in the bowl with some flour and sugar and eggs and milk. She gave Lily a big spoon and said, "Now you can mix everything together. Mix, mix, mix!"
Lily stirred the bowl with the spoon. She watched the banana and the other things become a smooth batter. She liked the sound of the spoon scraping the bowl. She liked the smell of the banana. She said, "Mix, mix, mix!"
Mom smiled and said, "You are a great helper, Lily. You are very friendly and kind. I love you very much." She gave Lily a hug and a kiss. Then she poured the batter into a pan and put it in the oven. She said, "Soon we will have delicious banana bread to share. Do you want to help me set the table?"
Lily nodded and smiled. She liked to help her mom in the kitchen. She liked to mix things in a big bowl. She liked to make banana bread with mom. She was happy.

Tom and Lily were hungry. They wanted to eat something delicious. They saw some potatoes in the kitchen. They asked their mom if they could cook them.
"Sure, you can cook the potatoes. But you need to be careful and follow my instructions. Do you want to make mashed potatoes?" Mom said.
"Yes, we love mashed potatoes!" Tom and Lily said.
"Okay, then you need to wash the potatoes, peel them, and cut them into small pieces. Then you need to put them in a big pot with some water and salt. I will help you turn on the stove and watch the pot. When the potatoes are soft, we will drain the water and mash them with a fork. Then we will add some butter and milk and mix them well. Do you understand?" Mom said.
"Yes, we understand. Thank you, Mom!" Tom and Lily said.
They did what Mom told them. They washed, peeled, and cut the potatoes. They put them in the pot with water and salt. Mom turned on the stove and watched the pot. When the potatoes were soft, she drained the water and gave them a fork. They mashed the potatoes with the fork. They added some butter and milk and mixed them well.
"Wow, the mashed potatoes look so good and creamy!" Tom said.
"They smell so good and yummy!" Lily said.
They put some mashed potatoes on their plates and tasted them.
"Mmm, they are so delicious!" Tom and Lily said.
"Good job, you made delicious mashed potatoes! I'm proud of you!" Mom said.
They ate their mashed potatoes and enjoyed them. They were happy and full. They thanked Mom and helped her clean the kitchen. They hugged and kissed her.
"We love you, Mom!" Tom and Lily said.
"I love you too, my sweet potatoes!" Mom said.

Lily and Sam were best friends. They liked to play with dolls, cars and books. One day, they heard a loud noise outside. They ran to the window and saw a parade. There were people with drums, flags and costumes. There were also animals, like horses, dogs and elephants.
"Wow, look at the parade!" Lily said. "It is so pretty and fun!"
"I want to go and see it!" Sam said. "Can we go, please?"
Lily and Sam asked their moms if they could go to the parade. Their moms said yes, but they had to be careful and stay together. They also had to come back soon, because it was almost lunch time.
"OK, we promise!" Lily and Sam said. They put on their coats and hats and ran outside. They held hands and followed the parade.
They saw many things that made them happy and curious. They saw clowns, dancers, balloons and cars. They saw a fire truck, a police car and an ambulance. They waved and smiled at the people in the parade. They also saw some people who were sad and cold. They had no coats, hats or shoes. They had no food, toys or books.
"Who are they?" Lily asked.
"They are people who need help," Sam said. "They have no home, no family, no money."
"That is very sad," Lily said. "Can we help them?"
Sam thought for a moment. He remembered that he had a sandwich, a cookie and a juice box in his backpack. He also remembered that he had a compassionate heart.
"Yes, we can help them," Sam said. He opened his backpack and took out his lunch. He gave half of his sandwich, his cookie and his juice box to a man who looked hungry. He gave the other half of his sandwich, his hat and his scarf to a woman who looked cold. He gave his book, his car and his doll to a boy and a girl who looked bored.
"Thank you, thank you, thank you!" the people said. They hugged and kissed Sam. They smiled and thanked Lily too.
Lily and Sam felt very happy and proud. They had helped some people who needed help. They had shared their things and their love. They had kept their promise and came back soon. They had seen a parade and made some friends. They had had a wonderful day.


Sara was sick. She had a fever and a cough. She felt hot and wet. Her mom took her to the doctor. The doctor was nice. He gave her some medicine and a sticker.
"Take this medicine three times a day," the doctor said. "And drink lots of water. You will feel better soon."
Sara and her mom went home. Sara lay on the couch. She drank some water. She took her medicine. She watched some cartoons. She felt a little better.
The next day, Sara's mom had to go to work. She called a nurse to come and take care of Sara. The nurse was not nice. She was ignorant. She did not know how to make Sara feel better.
She did not give Sara her medicine. She did not give Sara water. She did not let Sara watch cartoons. She made Sara eat dry toast. She said it was good for her cough.
Sara did not like the dry toast. It hurt her throat. She wanted water. She wanted her mom. She wanted the nice doctor. She cried.
"Why are you crying?" the nurse asked. "Stop being a baby. You are not that sick. Eat your toast and be quiet."
Sara felt angry. She felt sad. She felt sick. She threw the dry toast at the nurse. The nurse got mad. She yelled at Sara. She grabbed Sara's arm. She hurt Sara.
Sara screamed. She screamed loud. She screamed for her mom. She screamed for the nice doctor. She screamed for help.
Her mom heard her scream. She came back from work. She saw the nurse. She saw the dry toast. She saw Sara's arm. She saw Sara's tears.
She fired the nurse. She hugged Sara. She gave Sara water. She gave Sara medicine. She gave Sara a kiss.
"I'm sorry, Sara," her mom said. "I did not know the nurse was ignorant. I will never leave you with her again. You are my brave girl. I love you."
Sara smiled. She felt loved. She felt better. She said, "I love you too, mom."

Thinking quickly, Mama told Sammy that they could make squash soup out of the squash. Sammy's face lit up and he helped Mama make the soup. After a few hours, the soup was ready. Sammy took a sip and said that it was delicious. Daddy praised Sammy for turning a rotten squash into something as wonderful as soup. From then on, Sammy knew that it was always important to make the best out of a bad situation.


Once upon a time, in a big garden, there lived a selfish bird named Blue. Blue did not like to share his food with anyone. One sunny day, Blue found a tasty insect to eat. He was very happy and did not want to share it with his friends.
As Blue was about to eat the insect, he saw that it was stuck in a spider's web. The insect was very scared and needed help. Blue thought about being selfish but then decided to rescue the insect. He used his strong beak to break the web and set the insect free.
The insect was very thankful and became friends with Blue. They played together in the garden every day. Blue learned that sharing and helping others was more fun than being selfish. He became a kind and happy bird, loved by all his friends in the garden.

Her mom smiled and told Sue, "Stretching is important. It will help you play better. Plus it's a great way to get started."
So Sue listened to her mom and stretched for a few minutes. When she was done stretching, she felt ready to play. She ran around the park, chasing her friends and having a great time.
At the end of the day, Sue realized that stretching before she started playing really did help. From then on, she always stretched before she started playing, and she had lots of fun!

Lily and Ben were playing with blocks. They wanted to make a big stack of blocks, as high as they could. Lily put one block on top of another, and then another, and another. She was happy with her stack.
Ben wanted to make his own stack, but he did not have enough blocks. He looked at Lily's stack and felt angry. He wanted to have the same stack as Lily. He did not ask Lily if he could use some of her blocks. He just grabbed one block from her stack and put it on his own.
Lily saw what Ben did and shouted, "No, Ben, that is my block! Give it back!" She tried to take the block from Ben, but he held it tight. They both pulled the block and started to fight.
The block slipped from their hands and fell to the floor. It made a loud noise. The noise made their stack of blocks shake and wobble. Then, all the blocks fell down and scattered everywhere. Lily and Ben were shocked. They looked at their mess and felt sad.
They heard their mom coming. She saw the blocks and asked, "What happened here? Why are you fighting?" Lily and Ben did not know what to say. They felt ashamed. They knew they did something wrong.
Mom said, "You should not fight over blocks. You should share and play nicely. Fighting does not solve anything. It only makes things worse. Look, you ruined your stack of blocks. How do you feel now?"
Lily and Ben said, "We feel sorry, mom. We feel frustrated. We wanted to make a big stack of blocks, but we were selfish and greedy. We did not listen to each other. We did not respect each other. We slapped each other and made a mess."
Mom said, "I'm glad you realize your mistake. You should apologize to each other and help each other clean up. Then, you can try to make a new stack of blocks, together. Maybe you can make it even bigger and better, if you cooperate and have fun."
Lily and Ben said, "We are sorry, mom. We are sorry, each other. We will help each other clean up. We will try to make a new stack of blocks, together. We will share and play nicely. We will listen and respect each other. We will not slap each other and make a mess."
Mom said, "That's good, my children. I'm proud of you. You learned a valuable lesson today. Fighting is bad. Sharing is good. Cooperation is better. Love is best." She hugged them and kissed them. Then, she helped them pick up the blocks and start a new stack. They smiled and laughed. They were happy with their stack.

Sara liked to gather flowers in the park. She had a big basket and she filled it with red, yellow and pink flowers. She liked to give them to her friends and family.
On Tuesday, she went to the park with her mom. She saw a boy with a kite. The kite was blue and green and it flew high in the sky. Sara wanted to play with the kite. She was envious of the boy.
She asked her mom, "Can I have a kite too?"
Her mom said, "Maybe for your birthday, Sara. Kites are not cheap. You have to save money for them."
Sara was sad. She did not want to wait for her birthday. She wanted a kite now.
She saw the boy put down his kite and run to the swings. She had an idea. She left her basket of flowers and ran to the kite. She picked it up and tried to fly it.
But the boy saw her. He was angry. He shouted, "Hey, that's my kite! Give it back!"
Sara was scared. She dropped the kite and ran back to her mom. She cried, "I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I just wanted to try it."
Her mom hugged her and said, "Sara, you can't take things that are not yours. That's not nice. You have to ask first. And you have to be happy with what you have. You have beautiful flowers. They are a gift from nature. You should share them with others."
Sara felt ashamed. She nodded and said, "You're right, mom. I'm sorry. I will share my flowers."
She went to the boy and said, "I'm sorry I took your kite. It was wrong. Can I give you some flowers to say sorry?"
The boy was surprised. He said, "Really? You want to give me flowers?"
Sara said, "Yes, I do. They are pretty and they smell good. And they are for you."
The boy smiled and said, "Thank you, Sara. That's very kind of you. Do you want to fly my kite with me?"
Sara smiled too and said, "Yes, I do. Thank you, too."
They became friends and played with the kite and the flowers. Sara learned to be happy with what she had and to be generous with others. She was not envious anymore. She was glad.

They ran out of the maze and hugged each other. They also saw their mom and dad waiting for them. They were worried and angry.

He went to the drawer and found Timmy's scissors. He gave them to Timmy and said, "Here are your scissors, Timmy. They are good for paper. They are not good for fabric. Do you want to try again?"
Timmy nodded and smiled. He took his scissors and cut the paper. He made a beautiful paper flower for his mom. He was happy. He thanked his dad and gave him a hug. He said, "I love you, Dad. And I love my scissors."

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside with his ball. One day, he kicked his ball very hard and it flew far away. Tim felt sorry because he did not want to lose his ball.
Tim went to look for his ball. He saw a big tree and thought his ball might be there. He walked to the tree and saw a girl named Sara. Sara was kneeling by the tree, looking at something. Tim asked Sara if she saw his ball.
Sara said, "Yes, I found your ball. But first, let's look at this cool thing I found!" Tim and Sara looked at a big rock. On the rock, there was a word: "oxygen." They did not know what it meant, but they liked how it sounded. Tim and Sara laughed and played with the ball and the rock. They became good friends and always remembered the word "oxygen" as their special secret word.


Once upon a time, there was a little kitten named Kitty. She lived in a small house with her best friend, a boy named Tim. They loved to play together all day long. Kitty liked to chase her tail and Tim liked to run with her.
One day, they found a big, scary rock in their yard. Tim and Kitty were curious about the rock. They wanted to see what was inside. So, they decided to split the rock open. Tim used a stick to hit the rock, while Kitty watched.
When the rock split open, they found a shiny, pretty stone inside. Tim and Kitty were very happy. They took the stone inside their house and put it in a special box. They knew they had found something very special. From that day on, they were no longer scared of the big, scary rock. Instead, they were happy that they had found a new treasure together.


One day, a little girl named Mia went for a walk. She saw a modest house. It was not big or small, just nice. She went near the house and saw a little door. Mia was curious.
Mia opened the door and it was dark inside. She heard a voice say, "Hello! Who are you?" Mia said, "I am Mia. Who are you?" The voice said, "I am Tom. I seem to be lost. Can you help me?" Mia wanted to help Tom.
Mia took Tom's hand and they looked for a way out. They saw a light and followed it. It was another door! They opened the door and found a big party with cake and games. Tom was not lost, it was a surprise party for him! Mia and Tom had lots of fun at the party.

Lucy and the colorful boot had so much fun together. They played in the sun and danced in the rain. They never wanted to leave each other. And they became the best of friends.


Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a big statue. The statue was very important to the people. They loved it and took care of it every day.
One day, a mean man came to the town. He saw the statue and wanted to destroy it. He said, "I will destroy this statue and take its place!" The people were scared and did not want the man to destroy their statue.
A brave little boy talked to the man. He said, "Please don't destroy our statue. We love it and it makes us happy!" The man listened to the boy and decided not to destroy the statue. The town was successful in saving their statue and they were very happy. The mean man learned to be nice and became friends with the little boy.


Once upon a time, there was a little horse named Daisy. Daisy lived in a stable. The stable was her cozy home. One day, Daisy's friend, a wise bird named Mr. Blue, came to visit her.
Mr. Blue wanted to explain something to Daisy. He told her to be alert and look out for a big cat. Daisy listened carefully to Mr. Blue. She wanted to be a good friend and stay safe.
Daisy was now alert and watched for the big cat. She stayed close to her stable, so she would be safe. Daisy and Mr. Blue played and had fun together. They were happy and safe, thanks to Mr. Blue's help.


Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They had a small house made of wood and a big box of toys. They liked to pretend they were animals and make noises.
"Let's be lions today," said Tom. "We can roar and hunt and feed on other animals."
"Okay," said Lily. "But I want to be a nice lion, not a mean one."
They put on their lion masks and ran around the garden. They saw a bird on a tree and tried to catch it, but it flew away. They saw a cat on the fence and tried to scare it, but it hissed and scratched them. They saw a dog on the street and tried to chase it, but it barked and ran away.
They were hungry and tired. They went back to their small house and looked for something to eat. They found a bowl of soup that Mom had left for them. It smelled good and looked yummy.
"Let's feed on this soup," said Tom. "It will make us strong and happy."
They took a spoon each and dipped it in the soup. They put it in their mouths and made a face. The soup was very hot and spicy. It burned their tongues and made them cough.
"Ow, ow, ow!" they cried. "This soup is not good for lions. It is too spicy. It hurts."
They spit out the soup and ran to the tap. They drank some water and felt better. They looked at the bowl of soup and had an idea.
"Let's escape from this soup," said Lily. "We can give it to someone else who likes spicy food."
They picked up the bowl and carried it to the fence. They saw the cat that had scratched them before. It was licking its paws and looking bored.
"Hey, cat," said Tom. "Do you want some soup? It is very tasty and good for you."
The cat looked at the bowl and sniffed it. It smelled the spices and licked its lips. It liked spicy food. It jumped off the fence and took the bowl.
"Thank you, lions," said the cat. "This soup is perfect for me. It is not too spicy. It is just right."
The cat ate the soup and purred. Lily and Tom smiled and waved. They were glad they had found a friend who liked spicy food. They went back to their small house and played some more. They decided to be different animals tomorrow.


There was a fisherman named Sam. He liked to read books by the sea. One day, he sat in his boat and read a book. He felt safe and happy.
A little fish swam up to Sam's boat. "Hello, fisherman," said the fish. "Can you read me a story, please?" Sam was very surprised. He never heard a fish talk before! But he said, "Okay, little fish. I will read you a story."
As Sam read the story, more and more fish came to listen. They all liked the story. When the story was over, the fish said, "Thank you, fisherman." Then, they swam away. Sam felt happy and safe, knowing he had new friends in the sea.

Once upon a time there lived a mum and her little girl. Every day they would spend time together and have fun. Today, mum was looking through a magazine and the little girl was watching. Suddenly the magazine caught the girl's eye and she smiled. She found a picture of a charming princess and wanted to take it out of the magazine.
Mum said, "No, you have to leave the magazine alone."
The little girl was sad. She tried to explain to her mum why she wanted the picture, but mum was not convinced.
"Maybe another day you can have it," said mum.
The little girl sadly nodded. But then mum smiled brightly and winked at her. The little girl smiled too. Mum understood and she felt happy again.
The end.


Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. Mia loved her bottle very much. She took it everywhere she went. One day, Mia went to the park with her mom and her bottle.
At the park, she met a boy named Tim. Tim saw Mia's bottle and wanted it. He said, "Can I have your bottle?" Mia felt sad and said, "No, it's my bottle." They both found it difficult to share the bottle.
Mia's mom saw them and said, "Why don't you both take turns with the bottle?" Mia and Tim agreed. They took turns and played together. In the end, they both learned to share and became good friends. The moral of the story is that sharing can make new friends and solve problems.


Once upon a time there was a little child. She was so small she could barely go anywhere with her tiny legs. One day she decided to go and explore her garden. As she opened the back door, she saw a big dog and she was scared. But the dog was very kind and said, "Don't be scared little one, I won't hurt you".
The child relaxed a bit and went further into the garden. She saw lots of flowers, birds and bees. She was so curious that she wanted to pick up a flower, which was very big and beautiful. Suddenly, the flower moved and she got a bit scared again. When she looked closer she realised that the flower was a bee.
The bee wasn't happy that the child was trying to pick it up and he got angry. He started to sting the child's hand and it really hurt. The little child started crying and the dog rushed over and told her, "You must be careful and listen before you do something. Not everything was meant for you to touch".
The little child learnt a valuable lesson that day. She learnt to respect nature and also to be careful around it. The moral of the story is that we should always be careful and listen before we do something so that we don't get hurt!


Once upon a time, there was a big room with a bookcase. The bookcase was full of books. In the room, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to read books. She was a good girl who always listened to her mom and dad.
One day, Lily saw a book on the top shelf of the bookcase. She wanted to read that book. Lily tried to reach the book, but she was too small. She had an idea. She would push a chair to the bookcase and climb on it. Lily pushed the chair and climbed up. Just as she was about to grab the book, the bookcase started to shake.
Lily got scared and jumped off the chair. The bookcase fell down, but something unexpected happened. All the books flew out and made a big pile on the floor. Lily's mom and dad came running to see what happened. They were happy that Lily was safe, but they told her she should ask for help next time. The moral of the story is to always ask for help when you need it.

Ben and Mia were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. They saw a big dog with black fur and a long tail. The dog was barking and running towards them.
"Look, Mia, a dog!" Ben said. He liked dogs and wanted to pet it.
"No, Ben, don't!" Mia said. She was scared of dogs and hid behind a tree. "The dog is big and loud. It might bite us!"
Ben did not listen to Mia. He ran to the dog and tried to touch it. The dog did not like that. It growled and showed its teeth. It jumped on Ben and knocked him down.
"Help, Mia, help!" Ben cried. He was scared and hurt. He wished he had listened to Mia.
Mia saw Ben in trouble. She was scared too, but she wanted to help her friend. She picked up a stick and waved it at the dog. She made a loud noise and motioned for the dog to go away.
"Go away, bad dog! Leave Ben alone!" Mia shouted.
The dog was surprised by Mia. It did not like the stick and the noise. It ran away from Ben and Mia. It went to find another place to play.
Ben got up and ran to Mia. He hugged her and thanked her.
"Thank you, Mia, you saved me!" Ben said. He was sorry he did not listen to Mia.
"You're welcome, Ben, I'm glad you're okay!" Mia said. She was happy she helped Ben.
They decided to play somewhere else. They did not want to see the dog again. They learned to be careful and listen to each other. They were good friends.


Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved holidays. He liked to play with his friends, eat good food, and have fun. But there was one holiday that seemed very distant. It was called "Kindness Day." On this day, people would do nice things for others.

Tim climbed the tree and got Sue's toy back. Sue was so happy. Tim felt good too. On Kindness Day, Tim learned that helping others can make you feel good. From that day on, Tim was always kind to others. The moral of the story is that being kind to others can make you feel happy too.


One day, a girl named Lily was playing in her room. She had a big box of stamps. Lily liked to put stamps on paper to make pretty pictures. Today, she found a dull stamp in the box. It was not shiny like the others. It was a stamp of a tree with no leaves.
Lily took the dull stamp and put it on a paper. As she did, she heard a voice say, "Hello!" Lily looked around and saw a small, talking tree. It was the tree from the stamp! Lily was very surprised.
"Hi there," said Lily. "Why did you fall from the stamp?" The tree said, "I was lonely in the box. I want to be with you and your pretty stamps." Lily smiled and said, "Okay, let's play together." From that day on, Lily and the tree played together, and the tree was never lonely again.

Zoomy saw his friend, a red truck named Truckie, and they started to talk. "Hi Truckie!" said Zoomy. "Do you want to race?" Truckie said, "Yes, let's race to the big tree over there!" They got ready, and then they started to race. Zoomy was going so fast, and Truckie was trying to catch up.
Suddenly, Zoomy saw a big gray rock in the road. He had to stop very fast, or he would hit the rock! Truckie saw the rock too, and they both stopped just in time. They were scared, but they were also happy that they did not hit the rock. Zoomy and Truckie learned that it is important to be careful when they zoom around the landscape.


One day, a girl named Sue found a big crystal. It was shiny and pretty. She took it home and showed it to her mom. "Look, Mom! I found a crystal!" said Sue. Her mom smiled and said, "That's so pretty, Sue! Let's cover it with a tight cloth to keep it safe."
At night, Sue heard a noise from the crystal. She took off the tight cloth and saw that the crystal was glowing. The light was so bright that it filled her room. Sue was scared, but then she heard a tiny voice. "Don't be scared," said the voice. "I am a fairy, and I live in the crystal."
The fairy told Sue that she was lost and needed help to find her way home. Sue and the fairy became good friends, and they searched for the fairy's home together. After many days, they found the fairy's home in a big tree. The fairy was so happy that she gave Sue a big hug and a magic seed. Sue planted the seed in her yard, and it grew into a beautiful tree with shiny leaves. Sue and the fairy played together every day, and they were always happy.

The little girl had a green hand. She wanted to fly it around, but her mom said no. She was mad, and refused to surrender. She made her tiny hand into a fist and refused to let go of it.
But then, the sun came out. It was so warm and inviting, so the little girl decided to surrender. She opened her hand, and the green hand started to rise. The little girl smiled and laughed.
She flew her hand around in the sky, up and down and all around. The little girl felt free and happy. She had surrendered, and now she could enjoy the freedom of the open sky.
But all of a sudden, a gust of wind came and blew the green hand away from her. She panicked and searched everywhere, but it was nowhere to be found. The little girl was so sad and angry. But then, she had an idea: if she surrendered and opened her heart, then maybe the green hand would come back to her.
So, the little girl chose to surrender. She let go of her anger and sadness, and opened her heart. A moment later, the green hand arrived and flew right into her hand. She rejoiced and hugged her hand tightly. She had finally surrendered and won her battle.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they find an old kite in a sack. The kite is red and blue and has a long tail.
"Look, a kite!" Tim says. "Let's fly it!"
"OK!" Sam says. "But we need some wind."
They run to the hill with the kite and the sack. They wait for the wind to blow. They see some clouds in the sky.
"Maybe it will rain," Tim says.
"No, it will not," Sam says. "The wind will come soon."
They wait and wait. Then they feel a breeze. The kite moves in the sack.
"Quick, quick!" Tim says. "Let's fly the kite!"
They take the kite out of the sack. They hold the string. They run with the kite. The kite goes up in the air. It flies high and fast. It looks like a bird.
"Wow, look at the kite!" Sam says.
"It's so fun!" Tim says.
They laugh and smile. They fly the kite until the sun sets. They are happy. They put the kite back in the sack. They go home with the sack. They say goodbye to each other.
"See you tomorrow!" Tim says.
"See you tomorrow!" Sam says.
They are good friends. They love the old kite.

One day, he had an idea. He thought it would make everyone happy if he could organize a picnic in the park. He ran to get his spade and then carefully he started to plan out the perfect picnic in the park.

He then ran to ask his parents for help. His parents happily came with more spades and soon they all started to work together to make the picnic even better. Dale and his parents worked hard for the whole day.
Finally, when the picnic was finished, Dale looked around him - it was beautiful! He was so pleased to see that his idea had come true. Everyone was having fun and smiling.
Dale was very proud that he was able to be so thoughtful and organize this picnic in the park. He will always remember this day.


Lila and Sam were friends who liked to play in the jungle. They liked to climb trees, swing on vines and look for animals. One day, they saw a big lion sleeping under a bush. Lila wanted to get closer and see his teeth and fur. Sam was scared and said, "No, Lila, don't go. The lion might wake up and be angry. He might hurt us. We should mind him and leave him alone."
But Lila did not listen to Sam. She said, "Don't be silly, Sam. The lion is sleeping. He won't mind us. I just want to look at him. He is so beautiful and strong." She walked slowly towards the lion, trying not to make any noise. Sam followed her, but he was very nervous.
When Lila was very close to the lion, she reached out her hand to touch his mane. But the lion was not sleeping. He was just resting his eyes. He felt Lila's hand and opened his eyes. He saw Lila and Sam and roared loudly. He was not happy to see them. He thought they were trying to steal his food or his spot. He jumped up and chased them.
Lila and Sam were very scared. They ran as fast as they could, but the lion was faster. He was almost catching them. They saw a big tree and climbed up. The lion could not climb the tree. He stayed at the bottom and growled. He was very hungry and angry.
Lila and Sam hugged each other and cried. They were sorry for not minding the lion. They wished they had listened to Sam. They hoped the lion would go away soon. They learned that the jungle was harsh and they had to be careful. They promised to never bother the lion again.

The little girl was excited. She had been waiting all day for the big surprise her mom had promised. Finally, the doorbell rang. She jumped off the couch and ran to the door.

The little girl squealed with joy and hugged her mom. She couldn't wait to ride the bike.
"First let's show you how it works," her mom said, helping her sit on the bike. She showed her how to pedal and turn the handlebars.
The little girl wobbled at first, but soon found her way. She rode up and down the driveway, feeling as happy as could be.
But, in her excitement, the little girl didn't realize her mom hadn't shown her how to break. As she rode faster and faster, she realized too late that she couldn't stop.
The little girl screamed as she flew off the bike, crashing into a nearby tree. Her mom ran out to help, and she was rushed to the hospital.
The doctor said it was a bad accident, ending the little girl's excitement for the day.

Lizzy thought and thought about what she could do on the stage. She wanted to make her friends happy. She had an idea! She would dance and sing for them. Lizzy practiced her dance and song all day and all night. She wanted to be the best she could be.
The next day, all of Lizzy's friends came to watch her perform. When Lizzy danced and sang on the stage, her friends were so happy. They clapped their hands and wings. They all cheered for her. They all said, "Good job, Lizzy! We love your dance and song!" Lizzy felt so proud and happy. She knew that she had made her friends smile. And from that day on, Lizzy and her friends always had fun together in the big, empty garden.


Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She had a pet cat named Fluffy. Fluffy was a jealous cat. She did not like it when Lucy played with other animals.
One day, Lucy saw a wild bird in the garden. She wanted to be friends with the bird. Fluffy did not like this. She wanted Lucy to trust her and only play with her. But Lucy trusted the wild bird too.
Lucy, Fluffy, and the wild bird played together. Fluffy learned to trust the wild bird. She was not jealous anymore. They all became good friends and played together every day. And they lived happily ever after.


Once upon a time, in a small humble hut, there lived a kind old man named Tom. He had a pet bird named Blue. They were very good friends. Every day, they played and talked together.
One sunny day, Tom said to Blue, "I am going to the store. Stay home and be good." Blue nodded his head. When Tom left, Blue sat by the window to watch the world outside.
Suddenly, a big wind came and blew the window open. Blue was scared and flew out of the hut. He looked around and saw that he was lost. He didn't know what to do. Just then, another bird came and said, "I can help you find your home." Blue was very happy.
Together, they flew around until they found the humble hut. Blue said, "Thank you for helping me." The other bird smiled and said, "You're welcome. We can be friends too." And from that day on, Blue had two friends to play with, and they all lived happily ever after.


Once there was a little boy who wanted to play, so he asked his mother if he could. His mother said no, but the little boy was persistent. He kept asking and asking, but his mother would not yield.
The little boy then started to throw a tantrum. He shouted and pouted, and eventually his mother gave in. She said he could play, but only for a little while.
The little boy was so happy he didn't listen to his mother. He kept playing and playing until dark. But then something weird happened - he heard a spooky noise and started to feel scared.
The little boy ran to his mother for help, but she was angry. "I told you to only play for a short time," she said sternly. The little boy said sorry and sadly went back outside.
But it was too late. The spooky noises were getting louder and he was so scared he couldn't move. He was so frightened that he just lay there until morning came. Sadly, the little boy never played outside again.
