Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play in the garden. They have a hose that sprays water. They also have a big box of clothes. They like to wear different clothes and pretend to be someone else.
One day, Sara finds a dress in the box. It is pink and shiny. It has many beads and flowers. Sara thinks it is very pretty. She wants to wear it. She puts it on and looks at herself in the mirror. She feels like a princess.
"Look, Ben, look at me!" she says. "I am a princess. Do you like my dress?"
Ben looks at Sara. He sees the dress. He thinks it is very expensive. He remembers that it belongs to their mom. Their mom only wears it for special occasions. She told them not to touch it.
"Uh-oh, Sara, that is mom's dress!" he says. "You should not wear it. It is expensive. You might get it dirty or tear it. Mom will be angry."
Sara does not listen to Ben. She likes the dress too much. She wants to play with it. She runs outside with the dress. She sees the hose. She has an idea. She thinks it will be fun to spray water on the dress. She thinks it will make it sparkle more.
"Come on, Ben, come and play with me!" she says. "Let's spray water on the dress. It will be fun."
Ben follows Sara outside. He sees her holding the hose. He feels scared. He knows that water will ruin the dress. He tries to stop her.
"No, Sara, no, don't do that!" he says. "You will spoil the dress. It will get wet and stained. Mom will be very angry. Please, take it off. Put it back in the box."
But Sara does not listen to Ben. She turns on the hose. She sprays water on the dress. She laughs and twirls. She thinks it is fun. She does not see the dress getting wet and stained. She does not hear Ben shouting. She does not notice mom coming home. She only sees the water and the dress.
The end.

The end.
Moral value: Be careful on the slide. Be kind to your siblings. Share the lemonade.

From that day on, Tim and the little bird were best friends. They played together in the park every day. The bird was glad that Tim's hat did not fit on his head. Tim did not mind, because he was happy to have a new friend. And they lived happily ever after.


Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. Mia loved to measure things. She measured her toys, her bed, and even her dog. One day, she found a map in her room.
Mia showed the map to her mom. "Mom, what is this?" she asked. Her mom looked at the map and said, "This is a treasure map, Mia! It will lead you to a special surprise!"
Mia was excited. She took her ruler and measured the map. She followed the map to a big tree in her yard. Under the tree, she found a box. Mia opened the box and saw a big cake inside. But the cake was spoiled! It was green and smelled bad.
Mia was sad. She went back to her mom and told her about the spoiled cake. Her mom smiled and said, "I put that cake there a long time ago as a surprise. I forgot about it! Let's make a new cake together."
So Mia and her mom baked a new cake. They measured the ingredients and made the best cake ever. Mia learned that sometimes, the best surprises are the ones you make yourself.

Her mum said, "That is a rainbow. It's very lucky to see one." Clara smiled again and said, "Let's have some of the fruit for lunch."
They went back inside and ate the warm oranges with honey. Clara was so happy and ate two of them. She kept smiling and said, "Yummy!"
At the end of the day, Clara looked up at the rainbow and said, "Thank you for a very lucky day." Then she waved goodbye to the rainbow and went back inside to dream of more happy days.

"Look, Sam, we made a snowman!" Lily says. "The penny is his nose. He is white and cute and has a smile."
"Look, Lily, we made a snowman!" Sam says. "The paper is his body. He is white and happy and has a face."
They are very proud of their snowman. They put him on the table and show him to their mom. Mom smiles and hugs them.
"You are very creative, Lily and Sam!" Mom says. "You made a snowman with a penny. He is white and beautiful and has a sparkle."

He said, "I'm sorry, Anna and Ben. I was grumpy. I did not see your building. It is pretty. You had fun. You can keep your building. But can you help me find another box?"
Anna and Ben smiled. They said, "Yes, dad. We can help you find another box. Thank you for letting us keep our building."
They hugged their dad and went to look for another box. They were happy. Their dad was happy. Their building was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. Tom was very curious about the world and liked to explore. One day, he saw a beautiful shadow on the wall. He wanted to borrow it.
Tom asked his mom if he could borrow the shadow. His mom said no. She said, "No Tom, you cannot borrow the shadow, be careful, shadows cannot be moved".
Tom ignored his mom and took the shadow anyway. He thought it would be very impressive to take the shadow with him.
He waited until his mom was not around and then grabbed the shadow. When he tried to take it away, he noticed that the shadow was stuck to the wall.
Tom tugged and pulled and tried very hard to borrow the shadow, but he couldn't move it at all.
Tom was very upset and sad. He learnt a lesson that day and never tried to borrow something that was not his again.

Mimi said, "I want to play with the ball first!" Fifi said, "No, I want to play with it first!" They couldn't agree, so they decided to search for a way to share the ball.
They asked a big, friendly bear for help. The bear said, "Why don't you both play with the ball together? You can roll it, kick it, and even throw it to each other!" Mimi and Fifi thought that was a great idea. They played with the ball together, and they had so much fun!
From that day on, Mimi and Fifi always shared their toys and played together. They learned that sharing is caring, and it made their friendship even stronger. And they lived happily ever after in their little cave.


Once upon a time, there was a bald man named Jeff. He was a very wise man and he wanted to keep his brain sharp.
Every day he would sit down under a big oak tree and prepare himself. He would meditate and think of all kinds of ideas.
One day, a small three year old boy named Tim noticed him and asked, "What are you doing?"
"I'm preparing myself," said Jeff.
"Why are you doing that?" asked Tim curiously.
"Well, I'm preparing my brain so that I can remember all kinds of things," Jeff explained.
Tim asked, "Can I do that too?"
Smiling, Jeff said, "Of course! All you have to do is take time to prepare and you can become smarter just like I am."
The moral of the story is that everyone can use their brain and become smarter, no matter their age. All they have to do is take the time to prepare their brain.

Once upon a time, there was a big ugly storm coming. Two sisters, one old and one young, were stuck at home.

The little sister watched her sister with curiosity as she tested the door. She asked, "What are you doing?"
"I am making sure our door is strong so that the storm can't blow it open," the older sister replied.
The younger sister thought for a moment and then said, "I'm glad we tested it so it's safe."
The older sister smiled and said, "Me too."
The sisters wrapped themselves up in blankets and watched the storm through the window. In the end, their door was strong enough to resist the ugly storm.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had a lot of toys, but their favorite was a big, furry sheep. The sheep was soft and white, and it had a lot of wool on its back. Lily and Ben liked to hug the sheep and pretend it was their friend.
One day, they decided to play a game with the sheep. They took some scissors and cut some of the wool from the sheep. They wanted to make a hat and a scarf for themselves. They thought the sheep would not mind, because it had so much wool.
But the sheep did mind. It did not like to lose its wool. It felt cold and angry. It wanted to get its wool back. It waited for Lily and Ben to finish their game and go to sleep. Then it sneaked into their room and looked for the hat and the scarf.
It found them on a chair near the bed. It grabbed them with its teeth and pulled them hard. It tried to put them back on its back. But they did not fit. They were too small and too tight. The sheep felt even more cold and angry.
It saw Lily and Ben sleeping in their bed. They looked warm and cozy. They had taken some of the sheep's wool and made themselves happy. The sheep felt jealous and mean. It decided to get revenge. It raised its head and struck the bed with its horns. It made a loud noise and woke up Lily and Ben.
Lily and Ben opened their eyes and saw the sheep. They saw the hat and the scarf in its mouth. They saw the holes in its back. They realized what they had done. They felt sorry and scared. They said to the sheep:
"Please, sheep, don't be mad. We are sorry we took your wool. We did not know you would be cold and angry. We wanted to play with you and make you happy. Please, sheep, forgive us. We love you, sheep."
The sheep heard their words and saw their faces. It felt a little bit of warmth and kindness. It dropped the hat and the scarf and walked to the bed. It licked Lily and Ben's cheeks and snuggled with them. It felt a little bit of love and happiness. It said to Lily and Ben:
"It's okay, Lily and Ben. I forgive you. I know you did not mean to hurt me. I love you, too. But please, don't take my wool again. It is mine and it keeps me warm. You can hug me and play with me, but don't cut my wool. Okay?"
Lily and Ben nodded and hugged the sheep. They said:
"Okay, sheep. We promise. We won't take your wool again. We will take care of you and keep you warm. You are our friend, sheep. The best friend ever."
The sheep smiled and closed its eyes. It felt warm and cozy. It fell asleep with Lily and Ben. They all dreamed of happy things.

Max's mom watched the two play from the window. She had never seen such an amazing sight before. She was glad her son was so thoughtful and kind to the elephant.

Anna and Ben like to play golf with their dad. Dad has a big bag with many sticks. He lets Anna and Ben choose one stick each. Anna picks a short stick and Ben picks a long stick. Dad says they can hit the small ball with the stick and try to make it go in the hole.
They go to a big field with many holes. Dad shows them how to hold the stick and swing it. He hits the ball very far and it goes in the hole. Anna and Ben clap and say, "Wow, dad, you are good at golf!"
Then it is Anna's turn. She holds the stick and swings it. But the ball does not go far. It rolls on the grass and stops. Anna says, "Oh, no, I am bad at golf!"
Dad says, "No, Anna, you are not bad. You just need to practice more. And maybe you need a taller stick. Do you want to try Ben's stick?"
Anna says, "Yes, please, dad. Can I try Ben's stick?" Ben says, "OK, Anna, you can try my stick. But you have to guess how tall it is."
Anna looks at Ben's stick. It is much taller than her. She says, "Hmm, I guess it is as tall as a tree. Or maybe as tall as a house. Or maybe as tall as a giraffe."
Ben laughs and says, "No, Anna, it is not that tall. It is as tall as me. See, it reaches my head. Can you guess how tall I am?"
Anna says, "Yes, I can guess. You are as tall as a chair. Or maybe as tall as a table. Or maybe as tall as a dog."
Ben says, "No, Anna, I am not that tall. I am as tall as four books. See, I can stack four books on the ground and they reach my head. Can you do that?"
Anna says, "Yes, I can do that. I can stack four books on the ground and they reach my head too. Look, we are the same tall!"
Ben says, "Yes, we are the same tall. And we are both good at guessing. And we are both good at golf. Let's try to hit the ball with my stick and see how far it goes."
Anna says, "OK, let's try. Maybe it will go in the hole. Maybe we will be as good as dad."
They take turns to hit the ball with Ben's stick. The ball goes farther than before. They run after it and try to find the hole. They have fun playing golf with Ben's stick. They are happy. Dad is happy too. He says, "You are both good at golf. And you are both good at guessing. And you are both good at being my kids. I love you."

Lily reached the top of the hill. She felt proud and happy. She looked around and saw the park and the trees and the sky. She shouted, "Look at me, Ben, I'm on the hill!"
But Ben did not hear her. He was busy playing with a new friend. He met a boy named Sam, who liked to swing and slide and run. They were having fun together.
Lily felt lonely. She wanted to share her joy with Ben, but he was not there. She wished he would look at her and smile. She started to climb down the hill.
But the hill was steep and slippery. Lily lost her balance and fell. She rolled and rolled and bumped and scraped. She cried out, "Help, help, I'm falling!"
Ben heard her. He looked up and saw Lily falling. He was scared and sorry. He ran to help her. He said, "Lily, Lily, are you okay?"
Lily stopped falling. She was hurt and sad. She said, "Ben, Ben, I'm sorry. I was mean to you. I should have played with you."
Ben hugged her. He said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm sorry too. I should have gone with you. I'm glad you're not hurt too much."
They said sorry and hugged and made up. They went back to the park and played with Sam. They learned to be brave and kind and share. They were not lonely anymore. They were happy.

"No, dear, we can't buy a swan. Swans are wild animals. They belong to the pond. They would not be happy in our house," Mom said.
"But they are so pretty and soft," Lily said. She reached out her hand to touch a swan that came close to the shore.
"Careful, Lily, swans can be rough. They might bite you if you bother them," Mom said.
Just then, the swan hissed and snapped at Lily's hand. Lily pulled back and cried. Ben laughed and said, "See, Lily, swans are not nice. Ducks are better. They are friendly and quack."
Mom hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, Lily, the swan didn't hurt you. It was just scared of you. Swans are not toys, they are living creatures. We can admire them from a distance, but we can't touch them or buy them."
Lily nodded and wiped her tears. She looked at the swan and said, "Sorry, swan, I didn't mean to make you angry. You are very beautiful, but I will leave you alone."
The swan swam away and joined the other swans. Lily and Ben watched them for a while, then they fed some bread to the ducks. The ducks were happy and quacked. Lily and Ben smiled and had fun. Mom took a picture of them and said, "What a lovely day at the park!"

"Lily, it's time for bed. You have to sleep, or you will be tired tomorrow," her mom said.
"No, I don't want to go to bed. I want to stay up," Lily said.
Her dad came and lifted her from under the table. He carried her to her room. He tucked her in and gave her a kiss.
"Good night, Lily. We love you. You have to sleep, or you will miss the fun things tomorrow," he said.
Lily pouted and turned away. She did not say good night. She closed her eyes, but she did not sleep. She was angry and sad.
She heard a noise outside her window. She opened her eyes and saw a big moon. It was bright and round. She saw stars, too. They were shiny and small. She felt curious and happy. She wanted to see more.
She got out of her bed and went to the window. She looked at the moon and the stars. She smiled and waved at them. She felt like they were her friends.
She heard a voice in her ear. It was the moon.
"Hello, Lily. Do you like me and the stars?" the moon said.
"Yes, I do. You are beautiful and nice," Lily said.
"Thank you, Lily. We like you, too. But you know what? We have to go soon. We only come out at night. When the sun comes, we have to sleep. That's how we stay ready for the next night," the moon said.
"Really? You have to sleep, too?" Lily said.
"Yes, we do. Everyone has to sleep, Lily. Even you. Sleep is good for you. It makes you grow and learn and dream. It makes you happy and healthy. If you don't sleep, you will miss the fun things tomorrow. You will be tired and grumpy. You will not enjoy the sun and the flowers and the birds. You will not play well with your toys and your friends. You will not listen to your mom and dad. You will not be a good girl," the moon said.
Lily thought about what the moon said. She realized that the moon was right. She needed to sleep. She wanted to be ready for the next day. She wanted to be happy and healthy. She wanted to be a good girl.
She said goodbye to the moon and the stars. She thanked them for talking to her. She went back to her bed. She snuggled with her teddy bear. She said good night to her mom and dad in her heart. She closed her eyes and fell asleep.
She had a nice dream. She dreamed that she was flying with the moon and the stars. They showed her many wonderful things. They told her stories and jokes. They made her laugh and sing. They were her friends.
She woke up in the morning. She felt refreshed and cheerful. She saw the sun shining through her window. She heard the birds chirping outside. She smelled the pancakes that her mom was making in the kitchen. She jumped out of her bed and ran to the bathroom. She brushed her teeth and put on her clothes. She was ready for the day.
She hugged her mom and dad and said good morning. She ate her pancakes and drank her milk. She played with her toys and watched TV. She had fun with her friends. She listened to her mom and dad. She was a good girl.
She learned that bed was not bad. She learned that sleep was good. She learned that the moon and the stars were her friends. She learned that she could be ready for the day. She did not hate bed anymore. She loved bed.

Once upon a time there was a tan fox named Frank. Frank was a happy fox who liked to play in the field but one day there was a problem. It was a big stormy rain. Frank hid under a bush in the field, but he was feeling sad.

Frank lied and said he was okay. But inside he was scared of the rain.
The rabbit hopped a bit closer to Frank. "It's okay to tell the truth," the rabbit said. "I know you are scared of the rain. I get scared too. Why don't we journey together to the end of the field to escape from the storm?"
Frank thought about it for a moment and decided it was a good idea. He hopped out from under the bush and followed the rabbit.
The two friends eventually made it to the far end of the field, safe and warm.  When the storm passed, the bright sunlight shone down and made the field come alive again.
The moral of this story is that it is always better to tell the truth. Lying can cause you to feel scared and lonely. An honest friend is a dead friend and one honest word can be worth more than a thousand false ones.

Sara nodded. She took the book to the librarian. The librarian scanned the book and told Sara how much money she had to pay. Sara gave the librarian some coins from her piggy bank. The librarian gave her a receipt and a date. She said Sara had to return the book by that date, or she would have to pay a fine.
Sara thanked the librarian and hugged the book. She was so happy. She went home with her mom and read the book. She loved the story and the pictures. She read the book every day until the date came. Then she remembered what her mom and the librarian had said. She had to bring the book back, or she had to pay more money.
Sara did not want to pay more money. She also did not want to keep the book from other children who might want to read it. She decided to do the right thing. She put the book in her backpack and went to the library with her mom. She gave the book to the librarian and said goodbye to the dragon. The librarian smiled and said Sara was a good girl. She did not have to pay any fine. She also gave Sara a sticker and a new book to borrow.
Sara was proud of herself. She learned that paying was fair and that returning was kind. She also learned that there were many brilliant books in the library. She could not wait to read them all.

Suddenly, the little boy felt a sharp pain in his finger. It was so sharp he began to cry. When he looked at his finger, he saw that there was a bee on it.
The bee had stung him. Soon the pain spread all over his arm and he was in agony. He was so sad, he had to go home.
The little boy learnt a very important lesson that day. Never poke something that looks empty - you never know what comes next!

"Tom, it's my turn to be the pilot now," Lily said. "You have been the pilot for a long time."
"No, I want to be the pilot more," Tom said. "You can be the co-pilot again."
"But that's not fair," Lily said. "We have to share the box. And the co-pilot seat is uncomfortable. It has a hole in it."
Tom did not listen to Lily. He stayed in the pilot seat and made spaceship noises. Lily was angry. She got out of the box and walked away.
"Fine, then I will play something else," she said.
She saw a ball on the grass. She picked it up and threw it at the box. The ball hit the box hard and made a loud sound. Tom was scared. He jumped out of the box and looked at Lily.
"Why did you do that?" he asked. "You broke our spaceship."
"I didn't break it," Lily said. "I just wanted to pay you back for being mean to me. You didn't share the box with me."
Tom felt sorry. He realized he was wrong. He went to Lily and gave her a hug.
"I'm sorry, Lily," he said. "You are right. We have to share the box. Do you want to be the pilot now?"
Lily smiled. She forgave Tom. She took his hand and they went back to the box.
"OK, I will be the pilot now," she said. "But you can be the pilot again later. And we can fix the hole in the co-pilot seat."
They got into the box and resumed their spaceship adventure. They were happy and had fun. They learned to share and be nice to each other.

Sam wants to look at the book too. He likes to see the pictures. He tries to grab the book from Tim. He says: "Give me the book! It is my turn!"
Tim does not want to give the book. He says: "No, it is not your turn! I found the book first! Go away!"
Sam does not go away. He pulls the book harder. Tim pulls the book harder too. They both shout and cry.

She takes the book from them. She says: "This book is too old and fragile for you. You might break it or tear it. It is an ancient book. It belongs to Grandpa. He gave it to me when I was little. He loves this book very much."
She shuts the book and puts it on a high shelf. She says: "You can look at the book later, but only if you promise to be careful and respectful. And only if you promise to play nicely with each other. Do you understand?"
Tim and Sam nod. They say: "Yes, Mom. We are sorry. We understand."
Mom hugs them and says: "That's good. I love you both. Now, why don't you go and play with your other toys? I have a surprise for you. I made some cookies for you. They are in the kitchen. Do you want some?"
Tim and Sam smile. They say: "Yes, Mom. We want some. Thank you, Mom."
They run to the kitchen. They forget about the book. They eat the cookies and play with their other toys. They share and take turns. They are happy.

Max went to the wise old owl. The owl told Max a secret: "Give Ella a big hug. Hugs make everyone feel better." Max went back to Ella and hugged her tight. Suddenly, Ella's tummy felt better! Ella was so happy, she did her tricks again. Ella and Max learned that hugs can be magic. They hugged each other and laughed, knowing they would always be there to help each other.


Once there was a strong frog who was very brave. Everyone was scared of him, even the shadows. One day he decided to part from his friends and go on a journey.
As he walked through the forest the shadow seemed to follow him everywhere he went. He looked back, but he could not see it. He stopped to rest and the shadow appeared quietly behind him. He was not scared, instead he was very brave. He said, "Are you coming with me?"
The shadow was silent, but strange growls could be heard deep in the forest. The frog continued to walk, but the shadow still followed him. He thought he could make it home before dark, but it was getting darker quicker than he thought.
The growls were getting closer and the frog started to get scared. He turned to the shadow and said, "Come on, let's get out of here!" But the shadow wouldn't move. The frog was very scared, but he tried to be brave and he kept walking, but the growls were closer and closer.
Suddenly he heard something big, he turned around and saw a big bear. He shouted, "Run!" But it was too late, the bear caught him and he was never seen again.


Once upon a time, in a tiny town, there was a popular cat named Peek. Peek was very good at playing hide and seek. All the kids loved to play with Peek.
One day, Peek and his friend, a little girl named Lily, were playing hide and seek. Peek said, "Lily, I will go hide first. You count to ten, then come find me!" Lily started counting, "One, two, three..."
Peek ran to the east, where he found a big tree. He climbed up and hid in the branches. Lily finished counting and went to look for Peek. She looked everywhere but could not find him. Finally, she looked up and saw a little bird in the tree. The bird said, "Lily, look up here! Peek is hiding in the branches!" Lily found Peek, and they laughed and played all day.

Mia showed her toy to Ben and said, "Look, I made this for you!" Ben smiled and hugged the toy. "Thank you, Mia!" he said. They played with the toy all day, and Mia felt proud of her creative work.

A man at the station heard the bird sing. He said, "Wow, what a nice song!" The bird felt proud and sang even louder. Everyone at the station heard the bird's song and smiled.
But then, a hurt cat heard the bird sing too. The cat was very hungry. It saw the bird and wanted to eat it. The cat jumped high into the air and caught the bird. The people at the station yelled, "No, stop!" But it was too late. The cat ate the bird, and the station was quiet again.


One day, a playful cat named Kitty was walking in the woods. She saw a little mouse in a trap. The mouse was sad and scared. Kitty felt bad for the mouse.
Kitty said, "Don't worry, little mouse. I will help you." She used her paw to release the mouse from the trap. The mouse was very happy and said, "Thank you, Kitty!"
They became good friends and played together every day. One day, Kitty got stuck in a big trap. The little mouse saw Kitty and quickly helped her get out. Kitty said, "Thank you, little mouse. You are a good friend."
The moral of the story is: always be kind and help others, as they may help you when you need it too. And sometimes, the smallest friends can make the biggest difference.

Once upon a time, there was a man who wanted to sell a toy gun. The toy gun was very big and made a loud sound when you played with it. The man went to the park to find kids who would like to buy his toy gun.
At the park, he met a little boy who liked the toy gun a lot. The little boy tried to play with the toy gun, but it did not make a loud sound. Instead, the toy gun squirted out a bitter juice! The little boy did not like the bitter taste and started to cry.
The man felt bad for the little boy and decided to fix the toy gun. He opened the toy gun and found a lemon inside! The lemon was making the bitter juice. The man took out the lemon, and the toy gun made a loud sound again. The little boy was happy and bought the toy gun. The man learned that sometimes, unexpected things can happen, but we can always fix them.


Once there was a little girl who was very clumsy. She was playing in her garden when she found a long piece of string. She thought it was really cool and decided to tie it into a knot. The knot kept getting bigger and bigger so the girl kept tying it tighter and tighter.
Before long, the knot was so tight that the little girl couldn't get it undone. Knowing she needed some help, she ran to her mom who was inside the house.
"Mommy, I can't get the knot out of the string!", said the little girl. Her mom smiled and said, "That's okay. Let me show you how all knots can be untied". She tied an extra piece of string around the big knot the little girl had created, looping it around and around until the knot had been undone.
"Remember this, my little one," said her mom. "No matter how tight a knot may become, it can always be undone if you take the time to think of a solution".
The little girl thanked her mom and ran off to play, much wiser than before. She had learned that no matter how clumsy she was or how difficult a situation might seem, she could find a way to untie the knot.

John and Bill were so sad that their measuring didn't turn out the way they wanted. They had to clean up the scattered boxes and their measuring stick won't be of use anymore.

Ben does not want to share the car. He thinks it is the best car. He puts it on the table and plays with it. He forgets to watch out for the cat. The cat jumps on the table and knocks over the car. The car falls on the floor and breaks. Ben is shocked and sad. He cries and shouts at the cat.
Anna hears Ben cry. She runs to see what is wrong. She sees the broken car on the floor and the cat on the table. She feels sorry for Ben. She forgets the fight. She hugs Ben and says, "It's okay. We can fix the car. Or we can play with something else. We are still friends." Ben hugs Anna and says, "Thank you. I'm sorry I was mean. You can play with the pink car. We are still friends." They smile and wipe their tears. They pick up the broken car and the cat. They go to find some glue and some other toys. They are happy again.


Once upon a time, there was a big, thick tree. It was so big that it could wrap its arms around all the other trees. One day, a little, red bird came to sit on the tree. The bird was sad because it could not find a match to play with.
Then, a small, green bug came to the tree. The bug said, "I will play with you, little bird." The bird was happy, and they played all day long. But the big, thick tree was not happy. The tree wanted to play, too. So, the tree shook and shook, trying to join in the fun.
The little bird and the bug were scared of the tree's shaking. They did not know why the tree was shaking. They thought the tree did not like them. But then, the big, thick tree stopped shaking and said, "I just want to play, too!" The little bird and the bug were surprised. They did not know trees could talk! They all became friends and played together every day. And they all lived happily ever after.


Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with cars and trucks. Today is Tom's birthday. He has a big cake and many balloons. He invites Mia to his house to celebrate.
"Happy birthday, Tom!" Mia says. She gives him a present. It is a new truck. It is red and shiny. Tom likes it very much. He says, "Thank you, Mia! This is a great truck. Let's play with it outside."
They go to the backyard. There is a hill of dirt. Tom and Mia put their trucks on the hill. They make them go down fast. They make loud noises. "Vroom, vroom!" They have fun.
But then, something bad happens. Tom's truck goes too fast. It hits a rock. It flies in the air. It lands on the fence. It breaks into pieces. It is a wreck.
"Oh no!" Tom cries. He runs to his truck. He picks up the pieces. He is sad. His new truck is ruined.
Mia feels sorry for Tom. She runs to him. She hugs him. She says, "I'm sorry, Tom. It was an accident. Your truck was very high. It was too high for the fence. Don't be sad. I have an idea."
She takes him to her house. She has a box of tools. She says, "We can fix your truck. We can use these tools. We can make it new again. It will be fun."
Tom smiles. He says, "Really? You can do that? Thank you, Mia. You are a good friend. Let's fix my truck."
They work together. They use the tools. They put the pieces back. They make the truck whole again. It is not as shiny as before. But it still works. It can still go fast.
They go back to the hill. They put their trucks on the hill. They make them go down fast. They make loud noises. "Vroom, vroom!" They have fun.
They celebrate Tom's birthday. They eat cake and balloons. They are happy. They are friends.


Once upon a time, there were two friends named Bob and Kay.
Bob said to Kay: "I want a result!"
Kay asked him: "What kind of result?"
Bob replied: "I want a generous result!"
Kay thought for a moment and said: "I know how to help you! Let's go to the park, and then we can play a game together. We will take turns, and at the end, the winner will get the result!"
So Bob and Kay went to the park and played the game, and Bob won. Then, Kay gave the generous result to Bob and everyone was happy.
The end.


Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot was restless. He liked to run and play all day long. One day, Spot found a shield. The shield was big and round. Spot wanted to play with the shield.
Spot tried to pick up the shield with his mouth, but it was too big. He tried to push it with his nose, but it was too heavy. Then, Spot had an idea. He would sneeze at the shield to make it move. Spot took a big breath and sneezed very hard.
The shield moved a little bit. Spot was happy. He sneezed again and again. The shield moved more and more. Finally, the shield rolled all the way to his dog house. Spot was tired, but he had so much fun playing with the shield. Now, Spot had a new toy to play with every day.


Ben and Lily were playing in the backyard with their toy cars. They liked to make noises and pretend they were driving fast. Sometimes they would crash into each other and laugh.
But then they saw a big bird on the roof of their house. It was black and white and had a long yellow beak. It was making loud noises too.
"What is that?" Lily asked.
Ben shrugged. "I don't know. Maybe a duck?"
Lily shook her head. "No, ducks are not black and white. And they don't go on roofs. They go in ponds."
Ben frowned. "Well, maybe it's a penguin?"
Lily rolled her eyes. "No, penguins are not noisy. And they don't go on roofs. They go in snow."
Ben thought hard. He wanted to explain what the bird was, but he didn't know. He wished his mom or dad were here. They would know.
Then the bird flew down from the roof and landed near them. It looked at them with its shiny eyes and opened its beak.
"Hello, children," it said. "Do you want to play with me?"
Ben and Lily gasped. They had never heard a bird talk before. They were scared and amazed.
"Who are you?" Ben asked.
"I'm a magpie," the bird said. "I like shiny things and I like to talk. I saw your toy cars and I wanted to see them. They are very shiny and pretty."
Ben and Lily looked at their toy cars. They were shiny and pretty. They liked them too.
But they didn't like the magpie. He was crazy and rude. He had no right to take their toy cars.
"Go away," Lily said. "These are our toy cars. You can't have them."
The magpie tilted his head. "Why not? I like them. And I'm bigger than you. I can take them if I want."
He reached his beak to grab one of the toy cars. Ben and Lily shouted and tried to stop him. They were angry and scared. They wanted their toy cars back.
"Help!" they cried. "Mom! Dad! There's a crazy bird on our toy cars!"

Once there was a grasshopper who lived in a patch of grass. He liked to hop around and sing all day. He was very happy in his patch.
One day, the grasshopper decided to go for a hop around outside his patch. He hopped slowly towards the sun. He stopped to rest in the shade of a tree.
Suddenly, the grasshopper heard a loud noise. It was the noise of a truck coming down the road. The grasshopper was scared, so he quickly hopped back to his patch.
He hopped in a big circle around his patch, pausing to rest every few jumps. As he jumped, he noticed that the grass was getting dry and patchy. The grasshopper was sad. He wanted to help his patch get green again.
With a slow hop, the grasshopper took some of the dry patches and put them together, like a patchwork quilt. He watered the patch with a few drops of dew.
Soon, the grasshopper's patch of grass was green and lush again. The grasshopper was so happy. He hopped around, singing and playing for the rest of the day.

The orange cloud still does not say anything. It just moves away from Lily and Ben. It goes to another part of the sky. Lily and Ben feel very sad. They do not understand why the cloud does not want to be their friend.
"Maybe the cloud is shy," Lily says. "Maybe it does not know how to talk. Maybe it is lonely."
"Maybe we can try again tomorrow," Ben says. "Maybe the cloud will be happier then. Maybe it will say hello to us."
Lily and Ben hug each other. They are still friends. They go back to their house. They hope the orange cloud will come back. They hope it will be their friend too.

With a big push, they opened the door and Tim flew out. Tim was so happy to be free and thanked his family for saving him. From that day on, Tim learned to be careful and stay away from strange boxes.

Once upon a time there was a prince who wore a shiny crown on his head. But one day, he suddenly felt so tired. He was so tired that he wished he could just close his eyes and fall asleep.
But his crown kept getting in the way. No matter how he moved his head, he couldn't get comfortable with it on. He thought for a moment, and finally had an idea.
He quickly opened the clasp at the back of his crown. He carefully took it off his head and placed it on a table. Immediately, the prince sighed in relief; he was much more comfortable now!
But before he could drift off to sleep, his crown suddenly began to glow. Out of the crown came a beautiful fairy! She said that the prince must not take off his crown, for it was where his power came from. Without it, he could not be the ruler of his kingdom.
The prince was so sad. He asked the fairy if there was any way he could be comfortable with his crown, and she said yes! She taught the prince how to close the clasp of his crown so he could still wear it, but keep it comfortable on his head.
The prince thanked the fairy and quickly closed the clasp. He was now able to wear his crown without feeling uncomfortable. And the kingdom was happy, because their prince was able to rule with his crown on. The end.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is brown and has a long tail. The dog runs to them and barks.
Anna is fearful. She hides behind Ben. She says, "Ben, I don't like the dog. The dog is scary. Can we go away?"
Ben is not fearful. He likes dogs. He says, "Anna, don't be scared. The dog is nice. He wants to play with us. Look, he is wagging his tail. That means he is happy."
Ben reaches out his hand to the dog. The dog sniffs his hand and licks it. Ben laughs. He says, "See, Anna? The dog is friendly. He tastes my hand. He says hello."
Anna comes out from behind Ben. She sees the dog licking Ben's hand. She says, "Really? The dog is not mean?"
Ben says, "No, Anna. The dog is not mean. He is a good dog. Do you want to pet him?"
Anna nods. She is curious. She touches the dog's fur. The dog wags his tail more. He licks Anna's hand too. Anna smiles. She says, "The dog is soft and warm. He tastes my hand too. He says welcome."
Anna and Ben pet the dog. The dog barks happily. He plays with them. They have fun. They are not fearful anymore. They are friends with the dog.

They used a big sheet of paper and drew twelve boxes. In each box, they drew something that happened in that month. For example, in January they drew snowmen, in April they drew flowers, and in December they drew a Christmas tree.
They showed their calendar to their dad, who was very proud of them. He said, "That's a wonderful gift for your mom. She will love it. Do you want to sell some calendars to our neighbors? Maybe they will like them too."
Ben and Lily thought that was a good idea. They made more calendars with different pictures. They put them in a bag and went outside. They knocked on the doors of the houses near their own. They said, "Hello, we are Ben and Lily. We made some calendars. Do you want to buy one? They are only one dollar."
Some of the neighbors said yes, and some said no. Ben and Lily were happy when they sold a calendar, and they said thank you. They were not sad when they did not sell a calendar, and they said goodbye. They were calm and polite.
After they sold all their calendars, they counted their money. They had ten dollars. They decided to buy a gift for their mom with some of the money, and save the rest for later. They went to the store and bought a pretty scarf for their mom. They wrapped it in a nice paper and put it under the tree. They also put their calendar under the tree. They could not wait to see their mom's face when she opened her gifts. They knew she would be very happy.

Lily was sad. Her doll had a big cut on her arm. She did not know how to heal it. She asked her mom for help.
"Mom, can you heal my doll? She is hurt and I love her very much."
Mom smiled and hugged Lily. She said, "Of course, sweetie. We can heal your doll together. We need some water, some soap, some cloth and some glue. Come with me to the kitchen."
They went to the kitchen and mom filled a pot with water. She put it on the stove and turned it on. She said, "We have to wait for the water to get hot. Then we can wash your doll's arm and make it clean."
Lily nodded and held her doll. She saw a smelly cheese on the table. She wrinkled her nose and said, "Mom, what is that? It smells bad."
Mom laughed and said, "That is cheese, honey. Some people like to eat it, but I agree, it is smelly. We can put it in the fridge later."
The water in the pot started to bubble. Mom turned off the stove and said, "The water is ready. Let's go to the sink and wash your doll's arm."
They went to the sink and mom poured some water and soap on a cloth. She gently rubbed the cloth on the doll's arm. She said, "See, we are making it clean. Does it hurt, doll?"
Lily pretended that the doll said, "No, it does not hurt. Thank you, mom and Lily. You are very kind."
Mom smiled and said, "You are welcome, doll. Now we need to dry your arm and put some glue on the cut. Then we can wrap it with another cloth and make a bandage."
They did as mom said and soon the doll's arm was healed. Lily hugged her doll and said, "You are all better now, doll. I am so happy. You are my best friend."
Mom hugged Lily and said, "I am happy too, sweetie. You are a good doctor and a good friend. I love you and your doll very much."

Sara and Tom were twins who liked to help their mom in the kitchen. One day, mom was making soup on the stove. She told Sara and Tom to stay away from the stove, because it was hot and could hurt them.
But Sara and Tom were curious and wanted to see the soup. They waited until mom went to the living room to answer the phone. Then they tiptoed to the stove and peeked inside the large pot. The soup smelled good and looked yummy.
"Can we taste it?" Sara asked Tom.
"Maybe just a little bit," Tom said. He reached for a spoon and dipped it in the soup. He blew on it and offered it to Sara. "Here, you try first."
Sara opened her mouth and took a sip. But the soup was too hot and burned her tongue. She cried out loud and dropped the spoon. The spoon splashed some soup on Tom's hand and he cried too.
Mom heard their cries and ran to the kitchen. She saw Sara and Tom crying and the soup on the floor. She was angry and worried. She turned off the stove and took Sara and Tom to the sink. She ran cold water over their tongues and hands. She hugged them and said, "I told you to stay away from the stove. Why did you not listen to me?"
Sara and Tom felt sorry and ashamed. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We wanted to taste the soup. We did not mean to make a mess or hurt ourselves."
Mom said, "I know you were curious, but you have to obey me. The stove is dangerous and the soup is hot. You could have burned yourself badly. You have to be careful and patient. Next time, wait until I say it is ready and safe. Then I will share the soup with you."
Sara and Tom nodded and said, "We understand, mom. We will wait and listen to you. We love you and the soup."
Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, my sweet twins. Now let's clean up the kitchen and then we can have some soup together."
The moral of the story is: Obey your parents and be careful around hot things.

Once there was a spider named Sam. Sam supported his family by spinning webs. But one day, as he was spinning, he felt uncomfortable.
Sam wondered why he felt so strange. He asked his Mom, ''Mom, why do I feel uncomfortable?''
His Mom answered, ''Sam, life can be difficult at times. But you are strong and must support your family.''
Sam tried his best to spin, but the uncomfortable feeling stayed. As he looked up at the sky, he saw thunderclouds rolling in.
''Uh oh,'' he thought, ''It looks like a storm is coming!''
He felt even more uncomfortable as the storm grew closer. Soon, a huge gust of wind blew through and knocked down Sam's web!
The uncomfortable feeling suddenly made sense. His Mom was helping him prepare for the storm by making sure he was strong enough to support his family during tough times.
Sam smiled, for he now knew the reason for the uncomfortable feeling. He spun a new web, this one even stronger than before, and the spider family was able to stay safe during the storm.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play with cars and trucks. One day, they find a big toy bus in the park. It is red and yellow and has many seats.
"Wow, look at this bus!" Sara says. "It is so cute!"
"Can we play with it?" Tom asks.
"Yes, let's play!" Sara says. "I will be the driver and you will be the passenger."
They climb on the bus and pretend to drive around the park. Sara makes honking noises and Tom waves to the birds and the flowers. They have a lot of fun.
But then, they hear a loud voice.
"Hey, kids, that's my bus!" the voice says. "Give it back to me!"
They look and see a man running towards them. He is wearing a blue uniform and a hat. He is the real driver of the bus.
"Oh, no, we are sorry!" Sara says. "We did not know it was your bus. We just wanted to play."
The driver reaches the bus and looks at them. He is angry at first, but then he sees their scared faces. He softens a bit and smiles.
"It's okay, kids, I understand," he says. "But this bus is not a toy. It is my job to drive people around the city. You can't play with it. It is dangerous."
He helps them get off the bus and gives them each a sticker. The sticker has a picture of a bus and says "I love buses".
"Here, take these stickers," he says. "They are cute, too. And next time, if you want to ride on a bus, you can ask me. I will let you sit in the front and see everything. But only if you promise to be good and listen to me. Deal?"
Sara and Tom nod and say "Deal". They thank the driver and apologize again. They stick the stickers on their shirts and wave goodbye to him. They run back to their parents, who are waiting for them.
They tell them what happened and show them the stickers. Their parents are glad that they are safe and that they learned a lesson. They hug them and say "We love you".
Sara and Tom are happy. They learned something new and made a new friend. They still like to play with cars and trucks, but they also like to ride on buses. They think buses are cute, too.

Sara climbed on a chair and reached for the machine. She touched a button. The machine started to beep and flash. Sara was scared. She tried to turn it off, but she did not know how. She heard her dad running to the garage. He saw Sara and the machine. He was angry and worried.
He grabbed Sara and took her away from the machine. He turned it off and hugged Sara. He said he was glad she was not hurt. He said he was sorry he yelled at her. He said he loved her. He said he did not permit her to play with the machine because it was not a toy. He said it was a tool for his work. He said it could be harmful if she did not know how to use it.
Sara said she was sorry too. She said she did not mean to make the machine beep and flash. She said she was curious and wanted to see what it did. She said she loved her dad. She said she would not touch the machine again. She said she would play with her toys instead. Her dad smiled and kissed her. He said he was proud of her. He said he would show her the machine when she was older and teach her how to use it safely. He said they could play with it together. Sara nodded and smiled. She was happy. She and her dad went to the house and played with her toys.

Finally, Remy found a big bird named Benny. Benny said, "I saw Ava. She fell into a deeper hole." Remy was scared but he knew he had to save his friend. Remy and Benny went to the deeper hole. They saw Ava and helped her out.
Ava said, "Thank you, Remy and Benny!" Remy joked, "You are a deep avocado now!" They all laughed and played together, happy to be with their friends again.

Tom and Lily were playing with blocks. They wanted to build a big wall with their blocks. They had many blocks of different colors and shapes.
"Look, I have a red block. It is square. It can fit here," Tom said. He put his block on the wall.
"I have a blue block. It is round. It can fit here," Lily said. She put her block on the wall.
They kept adding blocks to the wall. They were happy.
But then, they ran out of blocks. The wall was not finished. There was a big gap in the middle.
"Oh no, we need more blocks. How can we finish the wall?" Tom asked.
Lily looked around. She saw Sam, their friend, playing with his blocks. He had many blocks of different colors and shapes.
"Hey, Sam, can we use some of your blocks? We want to finish our wall," Lily asked.
Sam looked at Tom and Lily. He looked at their wall. He looked at his blocks.
"No, you can't. These are my blocks. I don't want to share. Go away," Sam said. He hugged his blocks.
Tom and Lily felt sad. They wanted to finish their wall. They wanted to play with Sam.
"Why is Sam so mean? He has so many blocks. He can share some with us," Tom said.
"Maybe he is afraid. Maybe he thinks we will take all his blocks. Maybe he doesn't know how to play with others," Lily said.
They thought for a while. They had an idea.
"Sam, we are sorry. We don't want to take your blocks. We want to include you. We want to play with you. You can help us finish our wall. You can choose where to put your blocks. You can make the wall more beautiful. You can be our friend," Lily said.
Tom and Lily smiled at Sam. They showed him their wall. They showed him the gap.
Sam looked at Tom and Lily. He looked at their wall. He looked at his blocks.
He felt sorry. He felt lonely. He felt curious.
He put down his blocks. He walked to Tom and Lily. He smiled at them.
"Okay, I will share my blocks. I will help you finish your wall. I will play with you. You can be my friends," Sam said.
They hugged each other. They picked up some blocks. They finished the wall. They made the wall more beautiful. They played together.
They were happy.
The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. It is better to include others than to exclude them. Friendship is more fun than selfishness.

Ben likes to play with his blocks. He has many blocks of different shapes and colors. He can make towers, houses, cars and animals with his blocks. He is very happy when he plays with his blocks.
One day, he meets a new boy in the park. The boy is called Sam. Sam also likes to play with blocks. He has a big bag of blocks with him. He says to Ben, "Do you want to play with me?"
Ben says, "Yes, I want to play with you. What do you want to make?"
Sam says, "I want to make a big square. A square is a shape with four sides that are all the same. Like this." He shows Ben a block that is a square.
Ben says, "I know what a square is. I have many squares too. Look." He shows Sam his blocks that are squares.
Sam says, "Your squares are bad. They are too small and too colorful. My squares are good. They are big and white. You have to use my squares to make a big square."
Ben says, "No, I don't have to use your squares. I like my squares. They are not bad. They are fun and pretty. You are bad. You are mean and bossy."
Sam says, "No, you are bad. You are silly and stupid. Give me your squares. I need them to make a big square."
Sam tries to grab Ben's blocks. Ben does not let him. He holds his blocks tight. He says, "No, these are my blocks. You can't have them. Go away."
Sam and Ben start to fight. They push and pull and shout. They are not happy. They are not friends.
A lady sees them. She is Ben's mom. She comes to them. She says, "Stop, stop, stop. What are you doing? Why are you fighting?"
Ben and Sam stop fighting. They look at the lady. They are scared. They say, "Sorry, sorry, sorry."
The lady says, "You should not fight. You should share and be nice. You can play with both your blocks. You can make different shapes. You can have fun together. Do you understand?"
Ben and Sam nod. They say, "Yes, we understand."
The lady says, "Good. Now, say sorry to each other and shake hands."
Ben and Sam say sorry to each other and shake hands. They are not mad anymore. They are sorry.
The lady says, "Good. Now, you can play with your blocks. But be careful and gentle. Don't break them or hurt each other. OK?"
Ben and Sam say, "OK."
The lady smiles. She says, "Good. Have fun."
Ben and Sam start to play with their blocks. They make different shapes. They make a big square, a big circle, a big triangle and a big star. They use both their blocks. They are happy. They are friends.

The thin cat ate the piece of bread. It was very happy. Sue and her mom played with the cat. They had a fun day at the park. Sue learned that it was nice to help others.


Once upon a time, there was a big red ball. The ball had a little spot on it. One day, the ball met a small blue ball. The blue ball said, "Hello! Can we play together?" The red ball said, "No! I am too big and you are too small. Go away!"
The blue ball felt sad and went away. It met a little green ball. The green ball was very nice. They played together and had fun. The red ball saw them and felt a pinch in its heart. It wanted to play too, but it was too selfish to share with others.
In the end, the red ball stayed alone with its spot. The blue and green balls played together and had lots of fun. The red ball wished it could join, but it was too late. It had learned that being selfish only brings a bad ending.


One day, a hairy dog named Spot went for a walk. Spot liked to be quiet when he walked. He saw a cat named Fluffy. Fluffy was not quiet. Fluffy was loud.
Spot said, "Fluffy, can you be quiet? I want to record the sounds of the birds." Fluffy said, "No, I like to be loud! I like to chase the birds." Spot was sad. He wanted to enjoy the quiet and record the sounds.
Then, Spot had an idea. He said, "Fluffy, if you are quiet, we can play a game after I record the sounds." Fluffy thought about it and said, "Okay, I will be quiet." Spot was happy. He recorded the sounds of the birds. After that, Spot and Fluffy played a fun game together. They both had a great day.

Once upon a time, in an enormous universe, there was a little star named Twinkle. Twinkle loved to travel and see new things. One day, Twinkle saw a big, dark cloud in the sky.
"Hello, big cloud," said Twinkle. "I want to travel past you to see the other stars."
"No," said the big cloud. "You can't go past me. I am too big and dark."
Twinkle was sad. But then, she had an idea. She asked all her star friends to come and help her. They all came together and shined their light very bright.
The big cloud saw all the bright light from Twinkle and her friends. The cloud started to go away. "Okay, you can go past me," said the big cloud.
Twinkle and her friends were happy. They all traveled through the enormous universe and saw many new things. And they all lived happily ever after.

One day, Lily went to the park with her mom. She brought her passport with her. At the park, she put her passport on a bench and went to play. When she came back, she saw a big dog. The dog was trying to cover her passport with dirt.
Lily was scared, but she wanted her passport back. She asked the dog, "Can I have my passport, please?" To her surprise, the dog talked! He said, "I'm sorry, I thought it was a toy. Here you go!" The dog gave Lily her passport back. Now, Lily had a new friend, and they played together at the park.


Anna and Ben are friends. They like to walk and play outside. One day, they see a big mountain far away. They want to go there and see what is on top.
"Can we walk to the mountain, Mom?" Anna asks.
"It is too far, Anna. You will get tired and hungry," Mom says.
"But we want to see the mountain, Mom. Please, please, please," Ben says.
Mom thinks for a moment. She smiles and says, "OK, but we need to take a bus first. The bus will take us closer to the mountain. Then we can walk a little bit and have a picnic."
Anna and Ben are happy. They say, "Thank you, Mom. You are the best."
They get ready and go to the bus stop. They wait for the bus. They see many cars and people and dogs and birds. They talk and laugh and sing.
Soon, the bus comes. They get on the bus and find a seat. They look out the window and see the mountain getting bigger and bigger. They are excited.
The bus stops near the mountain. They get off the bus and follow Mom. They walk on a path that goes up and up. They see trees and flowers and rocks and animals. They say hello to a rabbit and a squirrel and a bird. They take pictures and collect stones and leaves.
They reach a nice spot with a view of the mountain. They sit down and open their backpacks. They have sandwiches and fruits and cookies and juice. They eat and drink and enjoy the view.
They are happy. They are lucky. They have a good day. They love the mountain. They love Mom. They love each other.

One day, a small girl named Amy went to the park with her mom. They saw a big tree with roots coming out of the ground. Amy wanted to sit on the root, but it was dirty. Her mom said, "Let's polish the root to make it clean."
Amy and her mom polished the root until it was shiny and clean. Then, they sat on it and ate their lunch. They had tasty sandwiches and shared them with a squirrel. The squirrel said, "Thank you for the tasty food!"
As they were eating, a big wind came and blew their bag of food away. Amy was sad, but the squirrel had an idea. He ran to his tree and brought back nuts and berries for Amy and her mom. They all shared the food and had a great day. The moral of the story is to always be kind and share with others, because you never know when you might need help too.


Once upon a time, in a big park, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was very adventurous. He loved to play and have fun. One day, Tim saw a big slide in the park. He wanted to play on the slide.
Before Tim went on the slide, he decided to study it. He looked at the slide from top to bottom. He saw that it was very tall and very fast. But Tim was not scared. He wanted to try the slide.
Tim climbed up the slide and sat at the top. He was ready to go down. But when he slid down the slide, he went too fast. Tim fell off the slide and got hurt. He cried, and his mom came to help him. Tim learned that sometimes being adventurous can lead to a bad ending.


Once upon a time there were two best friends, Daisy and Daisy Duck. Daisy was the lazy one, lying in the sun all day, while Daisy Duck was always on the hunt for adventure. One day, Daisy Duck saw something very mysterious. It was a tiny inch worm, slowly crawling along the grass. Suddenly, the inch worm vanished into thin air!
Daisy Duck looked around with her big eyes, trying to find the creature. She called out, "Yoo-hoo, where have you gone?"
Just then, a loud voice came from behind them. "Did you call for me?" asked the inch worm.
Daisy and Daisy Duck were so surprised. How did the inch worm reappear? Daisy asked her lazy friend, "How did it vanish and then come back again?"
The inch worm replied, "As all inch worms can, I can vanish and reappear wherever and whenever I please. I am in full control of my magic. Now, if you'll excuse me, I must be on my way." With that, the inch worm vanished again.
Daisy and Daisy Duck stayed still, trying to take in what just happened. Daisy smiled at her best friend, and they both agreed that today had been a very exciting but lazy day.

As Jane cleaned, she found a toy she had lost a long time ago. She was so happy! Jane realized that cleaning her room was not so bad after all. When she was done, her mom was proud of her. Now, Jane could play with her toys in a clean room.


Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to play outside in the mud. One day, she played so much that her feet got very dirty. Sue knew it was important to have clean feet, so she went inside her house to clean them.
Sue filled a big bowl with warm water and put her dirty feet in it. She used soap and a soft cloth to clean her feet. The water turned brown from all the mud! Sue was happy to see her feet becoming clean again.
After her feet were clean, Sue put on her favorite socks and shoes. She felt good knowing her feet were clean and healthy. Sue promised herself that she would always remember how important it was to clean her feet after playing outside. And from that day on, she always did.


Once, a big elephant with a long trunk lived in a forest. He had many friends. One day, he saw a small hole in a tree. He wanted to see what was inside the hole. He tried to put his trunk in the hole, but it did not fit. His trunk was too big for the small hole.
The elephant asked his friend, the bird, to help him. The bird could see inside the hole because she was small. She flew near the hole and looked inside. She saw a small, shiny stone. The bird picked up the stone with her beak and gave it to the elephant.
The elephant was happy to see the shiny stone. He thanked his friend, the bird. The bird was happy to help her friend. They played together in the forest, and the elephant kept the shiny stone with him always.


Once upon a time, Aaron and his mommy took a walk in the park.
Aaron saw something far away. He pointed to it and asked his mommy, "What's that?"
His mommy smiled and said, "That's a fence. Let's go see it!"
So, Aaron and his mommy went to the fence. It was so long that Aaron had to stretch his neck to see the top.
Aaron thought the fence looked strange. He asked his mommy, "Why is the fence so tall?"
His mommy said, "It's to keep something hidden away from peoples' eyes."
Aaron asked, "What is hidden?"
His mommy smiled and said, "You'll see soon enough."
And they did! Behind the fence was a beautiful garden with colorful flowers. Aaron's eyes went big with delight!
He asked, "Can I go in?"
His mommy grinned and said, "Of course!"
So, Aaron went inside the garden and found that it was full of wonders. He explored it for hours, and he never wanted to leave.
The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He liked to play and find things in his big house. One day, Tim went to the old room upstairs to look for something new to play with.
In the old room, he saw a big, old box. Tim opened the box and found an ancient uniform. It was very old and had many colors. Tim put on the uniform and felt very happy. He played in the old room all day, pretending to be a brave hero.
But then, something unexpected happened. Tim's toy bear, Mr. Cuddles, began to talk! "Tim," said Mr. Cuddles, "that uniform is magic. It makes your toys come to life!" Tim was very surprised, but he loved his new talking friend. They played and talked all day, and Tim's life was never the same again.


Tom and Lily liked to play hide and seek in the big park. They took turns to count and hide behind trees, bushes and benches. They laughed and shouted when they found each other.
One day, they saw a new place to hide. It was a small house made of wood and stone. It had a door and a window, but no one lived there. Tom and Lily ran to the house and opened the door. It was dark and dusty inside.
"Wow, this is a great place to hide!" Tom said. "Let's go in and explore!"
"OK, but be careful. It might be scary," Lily said.
They went in and looked around. They saw a table, a chair, a bed and a shelf. On the shelf, there was a box. It was old and rusty, and had a lock on it.
"What's in the box?" Tom asked.
"I don't know. Maybe a treasure, or a toy, or a secret," Lily said.
"Let's open it and see!" Tom said. He tried to break the lock with a stick, but it was too strong.
"Stop, Tom! You might break something!" Lily said.
But Tom did not listen. He hit the lock harder and harder, until it snapped. He opened the box and looked inside.
There was nothing in the box, except a small ball of light. It floated out of the box and flew around the room. It made a soft sound, like a whisper.
"Wow, what is that?" Tom asked.
"I don't know. It looks like a spirit," Lily said.
"A spirit? What is a spirit?" Tom asked.
"A spirit is a thing that has no body, but has feelings and thoughts. Sometimes, spirits are nice and friendly, and sometimes, they are mean and scary," Lily said.
"Is this spirit nice or mean?" Tom asked.
"I don't know. Let's say hello and find out," Lily said.
They said hello to the spirit, and the spirit said hello back. It had a cheerful voice, and it smiled.
"Hello, children. I'm glad you found me. I've been lonely for a long time," the spirit said.
"Who are you? Where did you come from?" Tom asked.
"I'm a fairy. I used to live in the forest, with my friends and family. But one day, a bad man came and caught me. He put me in this box and locked me up. He wanted to use my magic for his own selfish purposes. He was very cruel and greedy," the spirit said.
"That's terrible! How long have you been in the box?" Lily asked.
"I don't know. A very long time. I lost track of the days and the seasons. I missed the sun and the moon, the flowers and the birds, the wind and the rain. I missed my home and my people. I was sad and lonely," the spirit said.
"I'm sorry. That's very sad," Lily said.
"Can we help you? Can we set you free?" Tom asked.
"Yes, you can. You already did. By opening the box, you broke the spell that kept me trapped. Now I can go back to the forest, and find my friends and family. You are very kind and brave, children. Thank you very much," the spirit said.
"You're welcome. We're happy to help you. We're your friends, too," Tom said.
"Can we go with you? Can we see the forest and the fairies?" Lily asked.
"Of course. I would love to show you my home and my people. They will be happy to meet you, too. Come, follow me. Let's go," the spirit said.
The spirit took Tom and Lily by the hand, and led them out of the house. They flew in the air, with the spirit's magic. They saw the park, the town, the river and the hills. They saw the forest, green and bright. They saw the fairies, colorful and cheerful. They played and danced and sang with them. They had a lot of fun.
Tom and Lily never forgot that day. They never forgot the spirit, their friend. They never forgot the forest, their adventure. They never forgot the magic, their gift. They always remembered to be kind and brave, and to help those in need. They always remembered to be happy and grateful, and to enjoy life. They always remembered to play hide and seek, and to laugh and shout. They always remembered to be children, and to dream.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. She was very excited to explore her grandmother's old attic. She used the rickety stairs to climb up the attic. Excitedly she opened the door, but she stumbled when she saw what was inside it.
"What could be in here?" she asked herself.
Lucy slowly turned the light on and she realized it was full of boxes and dusty old toys! She carefully looked around and found a box filled with some treasures.
Curiously, she opened the box and carefully took out an old doll. As she touched the doll, the doll started to move. Lucy was quite surprised and stepped back.
The doll said softly, "Hello, Lucy. I'm so happy to see you. Have you been patient while waiting to play with me?"
Lucy, who was scared and confused, slowly nodded her head and said, "Yes."
The doll said cheerfully, "Let's go and explore the attic, together!"
Lucy eagerly nodded and ran with the doll throughout the attic. They stumbled upon some other hidden treasures, too!
Eventually, Lucy went back home but she kept the doll and those precious treasures forever.
The end!

Once upon a time, there was a mighty chair that could talk. It had big legs and a soft seat. The chair lived in a house with a little boy named Tim.
One sunny day, Tim and the chair decided to race. They went outside and stood at the start line. Tim said, "Ready, set, go!" And off they went! Tim ran fast, but the chair was faster. The chair's big legs made it go really quick.
As they raced, Tim's friend Sam came outside and saw them. Sam laughed and said, "Wow, a chair that can race! That's so fun!" Tim and the chair finished their race, and they all played together. The mighty chair had a great day with its new friends.


Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a boy named Tom. Tom had a special gift. He could understand the language of animals. This was very unusual, but Tom loved it.
One sunny day, Tom went to the park to play. He saw a bird on a tree. The bird was singing a pretty song. Tom said, "Hello, bird! I like your song." The bird was surprised and replied, "Hello, Tom! You can understand my language!"
Tom and the bird became friends. They played in the park every day. One day, the bird pointed at a shiny thing on the ground. "Look, Tom! It's a shiny stone!" Tom picked it up and showed it to his mom. She was very happy and said, "This is a special stone, Tom. Keep it safe."
Tom and the bird continued to play and talk every day. They had many fun adventures together. And that is how Tom learned that his unusual gift of understanding the language of animals could bring happiness and friendship.


Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. But they did not like the big dog that lived next to the park. The dog was mean and loud. It always barked and chased them.
One day, the dog got out of its fence. It ran towards Lily and Tom. They were scared and ran away. But the dog was faster. It caught up with Tom and bit his leg. Tom cried out in pain.
Lily saw what happened. She was brave. She picked up a stick and hit the dog. The dog let go of Tom and ran away. Lily helped Tom get up. She hugged him and said, "It's okay, Tom. You are brave too. Let's go home and tell mom."
Mom was at home. She saw Tom's leg. It was bleeding and had teeth marks. She was angry and worried. She cleaned and bandaged Tom's leg. She gave him a kiss and said, "You are very brave, Tom. I'm proud of you. But you should not play near the dog. It is dangerous."
She called the dog's owner. She told him what happened. She said, "You should punish your dog. It hurt my son. It is not nice. You should keep your dog in your fence. Or I will call the police."
The dog's owner was sorry. He said, "I'm sorry, mom. I did not know my dog got out. I will punish him. I will give him no treats and no toys. I will keep him in my fence. I hope your son is okay."
Mom said, "Thank you, sir. I hope your dog learns to be nice. Goodbye."
Mom hung up the phone. She smiled at Lily and Tom. She said, "You are both brave and good. I love you. How about we have some ice cream?" Lily and Tom smiled too. They said, "Yes, please!" They forgot about the dog. They were happy.


One day, a little girl named Mia went to a farm with her mom. They saw many animals like cows, pigs, and chickens. Mia was very happy to see them all.
Mia noticed a hurt bunny near the hay. She said, "Mom, look at the bunny! It is hurt!" Her mom looked and said, "Oh, poor bunny. Let's help it feel better."
Mia and her mom got some hay and made a soft bed for the hurt bunny. They also gave it some food and water. Soon, the bunny started to feel better. It hopped around and played with Mia. They had a fun day at the farm, and Mia made a new friend.


Once upon a time, there was a sad book. The book was a novel. It felt sad because no one wanted to read it. The novel sat on the shelf all alone. It wanted to be with the other books and be read by kids.
One day, a little girl came to the shelf. She saw the sad novel and picked it up. She started to read it. The novel was so happy that someone was finally reading it. But then, something bad happened.
The little girl took the novel outside to read. It started to rain. The novel began to soak in the rain. The girl ran home and left the novel behind. The novel was sad and wet. It thought no one would want to read it now.
But the little girl came back. She found the sad and soaked novel. She took it home and dried it with a towel. The novel was happy again. The girl read the novel every day, and they became the best of friends. The novel was never sad or alone again.

One day, a little boy named Tom got a new scooter. He loved to ride it up and down the street. It was red and shiny, and he felt very happy when he rode it.
One day, Tom saw a girl named Sue sitting on the sidewalk. She looked very sad. Tom stopped his scooter and asked, "Why are you sad, Sue?" Sue looked down and said, "I fell off my bike and hurt my knee. I suffer and feel ashamed because I can't ride like before."
Tom wanted to help Sue feel better. He thought for a moment and then said, "You don't have to be ashamed. I can help you learn to ride again. We can practice together!" Sue smiled and said, "Thank you, Tom." They became friends and had lots of fun riding their bikes and scooters together.


Sam and Mia were playing with their toy cars on the floor. They liked to make them zoom and crash and honk. But then Sam saw something on the window. It was a big bird with black feathers and a yellow beak. It looked angry and hungry.
"Look, Mia, a bird!" Sam said, pointing at the window.
Mia looked up and gasped. She was scared of the bird. She thought it might break the window and hurt them.
"Let's hide, Sam!" Mia said, grabbing her car and running to the couch.
Sam followed her, but he did not want to hide. He wanted to see the bird. He thought it was cool and brave. He left his car on the floor and crawled to the window. He wanted to touch the bird.
"Sam, come back!" Mia whispered, but Sam did not listen.
He reached the window and put his hand on the glass. The bird saw him and squawked. It pecked at the glass, trying to get to Sam. Sam was not scared. He laughed and wiped the glass with his hand, making the bird more angry.
"Go away, bird!" Sam said, wiping harder.
But the bird did not go away. It pecked harder and harder, until the glass cracked. Sam was surprised and stopped wiping. He saw the crack and felt the wind. He heard the bird flap its wings and fly inside. He was in trouble.
"Help, Mia, help!" Sam screamed, as the bird chased him around the room.
Mia heard Sam and got up from the couch. She saw the bird and the broken window. She felt helpless. She did not know what to do. She wanted to help Sam, but she was too scared of the bird.
She looked around and saw Sam's car on the floor. She had an idea. She picked up the car and threw it at the bird. The car hit the bird on the head and made it fall. The bird was stunned and stopped moving.
"Sam, run!" Mia shouted, as she ran to the door.
Sam saw Mia and the car and the bird. He realized what Mia did. He was proud of her. He ran to the door and joined her. They opened the door and ran outside. They were safe.
They hugged each other and thanked each other. They looked at the window and the bird. They felt sorry for the bird. It was hurt and lost. It did not belong in their land. They hoped it would fly away and find its home.
They decided to never play with the window again. They learned their lesson. They went back inside and played with their cars on the floor. They were happy and careful. They were friends.


Lila and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to swing and slide and run. They saw a big bird in the sky. It was black and white and had a long neck. It was a swan.
"Look, Tom, a swan!" Lila said. "It can soar high and low. It is so pretty!"
Tom nodded. He liked the swan too. He wanted to touch it. He ran to the pond where the swan was landing. He reached out his hand.
"Tom, no!" Lila shouted. "The swan can bite you. It is not nice. Come back!"
But Tom did not listen. He got closer to the swan. The swan saw him and hissed. It opened its beak and snapped at Tom. Tom screamed and ran away. He was scared and hurt.
Lila ran to him and hugged him. She was sorry for him. She saw a piece of wood on the ground. It was weird. It had a shape like a swan. It had a head and a neck and a body and wings. It was a toy.
"Look, Tom, a toy!" Lila said. "It is a swan too. But it can not bite you. It can only soar in your hand. Do you want it?"
Tom nodded. He liked the toy. He took it and smiled. He forgot the bad swan. He waved the toy in the air. He made it soar high and low. He was happy.
Lila and Tom played with the toy. They had fun. They liked the weird wood swan. It was so pretty.


Once upon a time, there was a small beetle named Pat. Pat was always busy examining the world. He had never seen anyone like him before so he felt quite alone. One day, Pat was examining a tiny, brown leaf. Suddenly he saw something moving. It was a small worm named Liz.
Pat smiled and shouted "hi". Liz looked up and said "Hello Pat". Pat was so happy that he had found someone like him that he ran over to Liz, and rubbed her back with his tiny antennae.
Liz was delighted. She said to Pat, "You know, sometimes it's helpful to have a friend to examine the world with. We can learn so much together!" Pat agreed and they vowed to explore the world together. Pat gave Liz a big hug and they flew off to explore their next big adventure.
The moral of this story is to always be helpful and kind to your friends. You never know what kind of adventure you might have together if you lend a helping hand.

Tom and Jen moved to a new house with Mom and Dad. They had many boxes to unpack. Tom and Jen wanted to help. They looked for their toys and books.
They found a big box in the corner of their room. It had a label that said "Tom and Jen's stuff". They opened the box and saw many things they liked. They saw dolls, cars, puzzles, and crayons.
"Look, Jen, our old teddy bears!" Tom said. He took out two brown bears with red bows. He gave one to Jen and hugged the other. "I missed them so much!"
"Me too, Tom!" Jen said. She hugged her bear and smiled. "Let's put them on our beds. They will be happy here."
They carried their bears to their beds. They saw something on the wall. It was gray and dusty and had many thin strings. It looked like a spider's home.
"Yuck, what is that?" Tom asked. He pointed at the wall.
"That is a cobweb," Jen said. She remembered what Mom told her. "It means a spider lived here before. But it is gone now. We can clean it with a cloth."
"Let's do that," Tom said. He found a cloth in the box. He climbed on his bed and reached for the cobweb. He wiped it off the wall. It was easy.
"Good job, Tom!" Jen said. She climbed on her bed and did the same. She wiped off another cobweb. It was easy too.
"Thank you, Jen!" Tom said. They looked at their clean wall. They felt proud. They put their bears on their pillows. They looked at each other and smiled.
"We did it, Jen!" Tom said.
"We did it, Tom!" Jen said.
They hugged their bears and each other. They liked their new room. They liked their new house. They were happy.
