While they were playing, a little bird came to Ellie and said, "Ellie, I need your help to weigh these fruits. I am too small to do it alone." Ellie agreed to help the little bird. She used her big, strong trunk to weigh the fruits. The little bird was very happy and thanked Ellie for her help.
Later that day, Ellie and her friends were playing near the river again. Suddenly, one of her friends fell into the water and couldn't swim. Ben says, "Maybe. Let's leave it here. Maybe they will like it."

The end.

Soon, other kids came to see Tom's castle. They thought it was great! They asked Tom if they could help him build more castles. Tom said yes, and they all played together. Tom's troubled heart was filled with joy, and he made many new friends that day.

The train and the car started to race down the track. The train went very fast, and the car tried to keep up. In the end, the busy little train won the race. The car smiled and said, "Good job, train! You are very fast!" And they both went on their way, happy to have had a fun race.

Whiskers, the speaking cat, told Amy, "We should not eat the dessert. It is not ours." Amy knew Whiskers was right. She was an honest girl and did not want to make her mom sad. Once upon a time, there was a little pink bunny named Daisy. Daisy loved to hop and play in the big green field. One day, she saw a big tree with a hole in it. "I wonder what is in there?" Daisy thought.
Daisy hopped closer to the tree and heard a small voice from inside the hole. "Hello," said the voice. "I am a little bird. Can you help me? I am stuck." Daisy thought for a moment. She knew she needed to trust the little bird.
"I will help you," Daisy said. She reached into the hole and carefully pulled the little bird out. The bird was so happy to be free. "Thank you, Daisy," said the bird. "You are a good friend."
From that day on, Daisy and the little bird were best friends. They played together in the big green field every day. And Daisy learned that trusting her new friend was the best thing she could have done.

Once upon a time there was a happy frog called Jeff. Jeff was always looking out for his friends and enjoyed nothing more than playing with them.
One day Jeff and his friends were playing in the pond, when they heard a loud noise. They all looked around, but they could not see anything.
Suddenly, a big crack split open in the middle of the pond and Jeff was very scared.
His friend Hazel said "Don't worry Jeff, I know just what to do. Follow me!"
She led Jeff and his friends over to a lily pad and said "Put your hands together like this and rub them round and round. It'll make the crack go away!"
So they did, and sure enough, the crack began to slowly close. Jeff was so relieved and he was so happy that he hugged Hazel.
They all jumped back into the pond, happy to be playing together again.

Joe and Sam stopped playing and looked at one another. Joe said, "That was not nice of me. I should not have poked the fly." Sam nodded and said, "Yes, it would have been better to leave the fly alone."
So the two friends learned a lesson: it is important to be kind to all creatures, even a small fly. It is better to use our words instead of poking to get what we want.

John and his mom were walking in the park. "Mommy, can I count the trees?" asked John. His mom smiled and said, "Sure, go ahead!"
John began counting the trees out loud. "One, two, three..." he counted. Soon he had counted all the way to twelve.
But then something strange happened. A white veil suddenly appeared and blocked his view of the trees. John couldn't count anymore. He looked up at his mom and asked, "What's that veil doing there?"
His mom frowned and said, "That's a selfish veil. It's keeping us from counting the trees. We have to find a way to get it away." Just then, they heard a loud noise in the sky and looked up. It was a giant number 20! "That number will get rid of the veil," said John's mom. Sure enough, the number flew straight down and knocked the veil away.
John and his mom cheered. John was able to finish counting all the way to twenty. His mom smiled and said, "See, John, numbers can be very helpful!"

But there was a problem. The honey was up high in the tree, and Bobo was scared to climb. He thought he might get hurt. Buzzy said, "Don't worry, Bobo. I will help you."
With Buzzy's help, Bobo climbed the tree and got the honey. They both shared the honey and were very happy. From that day on, Bobo and Buzzy were best friends, and they always helped each other.

But the baby was determined to get the smelly shoe, and so the mommy said "Okay, I'll keep it safe until you remember why you wanted it".
The baby couldn't remember why it wanted the smelly shoe, so the mommy and the baby kept going to the park every day. The baby kept asking for the smelly shoe, but the mommy said no.
Eventually, one day when the baby was playing at the park, a bird dropped a seed and the seed got stuck in the smelly shoe. The baby smiled and said "Oh yeah! That's why I wanted it!"
The mommy and baby laughed, and from then on the smelly shoe was the baby's favorite toy.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They saw a small hive on a tree. They wanted to examine it.
"Look, bees!" Lily said. "They make honey. Yum!"
"Can we go closer?" Ben asked. "I want to see them."
Lily nodded. They walked slowly to the tree. They were careful not to make noise.
They saw many bees flying in and out of the hive. They heard a buzzing sound. They saw some honey dripping from the hive.
"Wow, so cool!" Ben said. "Can we touch it?"
Lily shook her head. "No, no, no. Bees can sting. It hurts. We have to be nice to them."
Ben frowned. He wanted to touch the honey. He reached out his hand.
"Ben, no!" Lily shouted. "Stop!"
But it was too late. A bee saw Ben's hand and flew to him. It stung him on his finger.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cried. He pulled his hand back. He saw a red bump on his finger. He felt pain.
Lily ran to him. She hugged him. She said sorry.
"I'm sorry, Ben. I'm sorry. Are you okay?"
Ben sobbed. He showed her his finger.
"It hurts, Lily. It hurts."
Lily felt sad. She said sorry again.
"I'm sorry, Ben. I'm sorry. Let's go to mom. She can help you."
They ran to the house. They found mom. They told her what happened.
Mom looked at Ben's finger. She said it was not bad. She put some ice on it. She gave him a kiss. She said it would be better soon.
Ben felt better. He smiled. He thanked mom.
He looked at Lily. He said sorry.
"I'm sorry, Lily. I'm sorry. I was silly. I should have listened to you."
Lily smiled. She hugged him. She said it was okay.
"It's okay, Ben. It's okay. You are not silly. You are curious. But you have to be careful. Bees are good, but they can sting."
Ben nodded. He said he understood.
They said they loved each other. They said they loved mom. They said they loved bees.
They went back to the garden. They played with other things. They did not touch the hive. They were happy.

Once there was a little girl named Sophie who loved wearing her favourite shirt. It was her favourite because it had an ocean blue colour her parents had bought for her birthday. She wore it every day and always felt very special in it.
One day, Sophie went to the park with her friends. Everyone was playing happily together and having a lot of fun. Later, the group was joined by a wealthy girl who had a very pretty dress on. When the wealthy girl saw Sophie's shirt, she started to laugh and said, "You must be so embarrassed wearing something like that!"
Sophie was confused. She looked down at her shirt and was suddenly ashamed. But then she reminded herself that everyone has different kinds of clothes and surely no one should be made to feel bad about what they wear.
She replied to the wealthy girl, "My shirt may be old and simple, but I love it because it makes me feel special. I'm not embarrassed about my shirt and I think it's much better for everyone to accept the way we all dress differently."
The wealthy girl smiled and thanked Sophie for the words. From that day on, she always chose to be kind and mindful of how she made others feel.
The moral of this story is that we should never judge someone based on their clothing or style as it is a reflection of their personality. Instead, we should choose to be kind, accepting and understanding of differences

Ben and Mia were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they decided to have a picnic. They brought some bread, cheese, fruit and juice. They found a nice spot under a big tree and spread a blanket on the grass.
"Let's eat!" Ben said. He took a piece of bread and put some cheese on it.
"Wait!" Mia said. "We have to say thank you first. Thank you for the food and the sun and the park."
"Okay, okay," Ben said. He put his bread down and folded his hands. "Thank you for the food and the sun and the park."
They ate their picnic and drank their juice. They were happy and full.
"Let's play now!" Mia said. She picked up a ball and threw it to Ben.
"Okay!" Ben said. He caught the ball and threw it back.
They played catch for a while. Then, they saw a big dog running towards them. The dog was black and brown and had sharp teeth. It looked fierce.
"Look out!" Ben shouted. He dropped the ball and ran behind the tree.
"Help!" Mia cried. She grabbed the blanket and wrapped it around her.
The dog reached the picnic spot and sniffed the food. It liked the smell of cheese. It took a bite of Ben's bread and cheese. Then, it saw the ball. It liked the ball too. It picked up the ball and ran away.
"Hey!" Ben said. "That's my ball! Give it back!"
He came out from behind the tree and chased the dog.
"Ben, no!" Mia said. "The dog is fierce! It might bite you!"
She followed Ben and tried to stop him.
The dog ran faster and faster. Ben and Mia ran after it. They ran across the park and out of the gate. They ran into the street and saw a car coming.
"Stop!" Mia screamed. "The car!"
Ben and Mia stopped and jumped back. The car honked and passed by. The dog kept running and disappeared.
Ben and Mia looked at each other. They were scared and sad. They had lost their ball and their picnic.
They hugged each other and cried.
A lady saw them and came over. She was kind and gentle.
"What's wrong, children?" she asked.
"A dog took our ball and our picnic," Ben said.
"It was a fierce dog," Mia said.
"Oh, I'm sorry," the lady said. "That's not nice. Do you want to come with me? I have some cookies and milk at home. And I have a ball too. You can play with it if you want."
"Really?" Ben asked.
"Really," the lady said. "I don't own the ball. It belongs to my son. But he's at school now. He won't mind if you play with it. He likes to share."
"Thank you," Mia said.
"Thank you," Ben said.
They took the lady's hand and walked with her. They felt better. They had found a new friend. And they still had each other.

Andy and Bee went to Wise Owl's tree. They told him about the hot sun and their fear of it burning their homes. Wise Owl listened and said, "Do not worry, little ones. The sun is far away and will not burn your homes. It gives us light and warmth. Be happy and enjoy the sunshine."
Andy and Bee felt better after talking to Wise Owl. They went back to their homes and told their families what Wise Owl had said. From that day on, they were not worried about the sun burning their homes. They played in the sunshine and were very happy.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly man who lived at the foot of a volcano. Every morning, the man would get up and drink from the clear spring at the top of the mountain. One day, he decided to take the risk and climb to the peak of the volcano.
When he arrived, he saw a beautiful pool of bubbling water. He was so amazed that he decided to take a drink from it. "This water is so refreshing," the elderly man said.
Just then, he heard a deep rumble coming from within the volcano. The man quickly jumped into the pool and watched as molten lava began to fill the volcano's crater. He swam to the top of the pool and looked around.
Just then, an elderly lady appeared. "These waters are magical," she said. "Come, drink from them and be blessed with eternal youth."
The man was hesitant at first, but then he took a sip and was filled with strength and joy. The elderly lady smiled and vanished, leaving the man to enjoy the beauty of the volcano forever.


Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play games. They were very competitive and always wanted to win. One day, they decided to play a game of hide and seek in the house.
Lily was the seeker and Ben was the hider. Lily counted to ten and then looked for Ben. She checked under the bed, behind the sofa, in the closet, but she could not find him. She sighed and thought, where could he be?
Ben was hiding in the kitchen, inside the refrigerator. He had opened the door quietly and climbed in. He thought it was a good hiding spot, because Lily would never look there. He smiled and waited for Lily to give up.
But Lily did not give up. She searched every room in the house, except the kitchen. She was getting tired and hungry. She decided to go to the kitchen and get a snack. She walked to the refrigerator and opened the door.
She saw Ben sitting inside, holding a carton of juice. She was surprised and angry. She said, "Ben, you cheated! You can't hide in the refrigerator! That's not fair!"
Ben said, "I didn't cheat! I just found a clever spot! I win!"
Lily said, "No, you don't! You broke the rules! I win!"
They started to argue and shout. They did not notice that their mom came into the kitchen. She heard them and said, "What are you two doing? Why are you in the refrigerator? You could get sick or hurt!"
Lily and Ben stopped arguing and looked at their mom. They felt ashamed and sorry. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We were playing hide and seek and we got too competitive."
Mom said, "I'm glad you like to play games, but you have to be safe and respectful. Hiding in the refrigerator is not a good idea. And you don't have to fight over who wins or loses. The most important thing is to have fun and be kind to each other."
Lily and Ben nodded and hugged their mom. They said, "We love you, mom. And we love each other, too. Can we have some juice, please?"
Mom smiled and said, "Of course you can. But first, let's close the refrigerator and clean up the mess."

"Thank you, Mommy," Lily said.

Sam is glad. He hops with the fish, he swims with the fish, he plays with the fish. He is happy when he hops. He is happy when he has a friend.

One day, Sara sees a big duck with a red hat and a shiny medal. He looks different from the other ducks. He walks in front of them and makes loud noises. The other ducks follow him and make noises too. Sara thinks they are having a march.
Sara asks her mom who the big duck is. Her mom says he is a famous duck. He is the leader of the ducks. He helps them find food and water and keeps them safe. He is brave and smart and kind. He won the medal for saving a baby duck from a fox.
Sara thinks the famous duck is very cool. She wants to feed him some bread and corn. She calls his name and waves her hand. The famous duck sees her and swims to the shore. He takes the food from her and thanks her. He says she is a nice girl and a good friend. He gives her a feather as a gift.
Sara is very happy. She puts the feather in her hair and smiles. She says goodbye to the famous duck and the other ducks. She tells her mom she had a lot of fun. She says she wants to come back and feed the ducks again. Her mom says they can do that tomorrow. Sara hugs her mom and says she loves her.


Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy rod that he loved to play with. He would use the rod to catch pretend fish in his yard. One day, the rod broke and Tim was very sad.
Tim's mom saw him crying and asked, "Why are you sad, Tim?" Tim showed her the broken rod and said, "My rod is broken, and I can't play anymore." His mom hugged him and said, "Don't worry, we will replace it with a new one."
The next day, Tim and his mom went to the toy store. They found a new rod that was mild and easy for Tim to use. Tim was very happy and said, "Thank you, Mom!" They went back home, and Tim played with his new rod all day long, catching lots of pretend fish. And they all lived happily ever after.

"Lucy come here," her mother called.
But the lake was very inviting. She felt too relaxed to move.
"Please baby, don't stay there. That lake can be harsh," warned her mother.
That awoke Lucy from her trance. Gathering her strength, she started walking toward her mother. When she got there, her mother hugged her tightly.
"Thank goodness you listened to me," said her mother with a sigh of relief.
Lucy smiled and yawned once again. She was feeling sleepy now. Together, they headed home and Lucy had a peaceful nap.

Lily liked to collect magazines. She had many magazines in her room. She liked to look at the pictures and the words. She wanted to learn more words.
One day, she saw a new magazine at the store. It had a big picture of a dog on the cover. Lily loved dogs. She asked her mom if she could buy the magazine.
"Sorry, Lily, we don't have enough money for that today," her mom said. "Maybe next time."
Lily felt sad. She really wanted the magazine. She looked at the dog again. It had brown fur and black spots. It looked friendly and soft.
She had an idea. She waited until her mom was busy. Then she took the magazine and hid it under her coat. She walked out of the store with her mom. She thought she was very clever.
But when she got home, she found out that the magazine was not what she expected. It was not a magazine about dogs. It was a magazine about gardening. The dog was only on the cover. The rest of the pages had pictures of plants and flowers and tools. Lily did not like plants and flowers and tools. She liked dogs.
And the magazine was not friendly and soft. It was rough and scratchy. It hurt her skin when she touched it. It made her itch and sneeze.
Lily felt bad. She had taken something that was not hers. She had lied to her mom. She had wasted her time. She did not like the magazine at all.
She decided to tell her mom the truth. She hoped her mom would not be angry. She hoped her mom would forgive her. She hoped she could find a real magazine about dogs someday.

Once upon a time, there were two boys, Joe and Bob. Joe was playing on the playground and he noticed something very round. He shouted to Bob saying. "Look! I can see something round!"
Bob hopped off the swing to come look. "Let's go see, Joe!"
When they got close to the round thing they couldn't believe it, it was a big red ball! Joe said, "Let's play!"
But Bob said, "No, that's a stupid thing to do."
Joe was so surprised at what Bob said, he replied, "Why is it stupid?"
Bob said, "Because if we play with it, it could roll away and we won't be able to find it."
Joe thought about it, and he agreed that it was a good idea to observe the ball and not play with it.
So they both sat back and observed the round ball from a distance, until eventually it got dark and they had to go home.


Tom and Lily liked to play in the park. They liked to run, jump and slide. But they did not like the big statue in the park. The statue was of a mean man who looked angry. He had a big stick in his hand and a big hat on his head.
One day, Tom and Lily decided to throw stones at the statue. They thought it was fun to make the statue look dirty and broken. They threw and threw until the statue had many holes and cracks. They laughed and laughed.
But then, a loud voice shouted at them. It was the park keeper. He was very angry. He saw what Tom and Lily had done to the statue. He ran towards them and grabbed them by their arms.
"What have you done, you naughty children?" he yelled. "You have ruined the statue of the great hero. He saved our town from the bad people long ago. He was brave and strong, not like you, you lazy and wicked children. You will have to pay for this. You will have to work hard to heal the statue. And you will have to say sorry to the hero every day."
Tom and Lily were very scared. They cried and begged for mercy. But the park keeper did not listen. He dragged them to his hut and locked them inside. He said he would come back later with tools and glue. He said they would have to work all day and all night until the statue was healed.
Tom and Lily looked at each other. They wished they had never thrown stones at the statue. They wished they had played nicely in the park. They wished they could go home. But it was too late. They had made a big mistake. And they had to pay for it.

Sam said, "I like to climb trees. It is fun!" As they talked, they saw a screw hanging from a branch. Sam and Tim were surprised. "Who put that there?" asked Tim.
As they looked at the screw, a big wind came. The wind blew the screw off the branch. It fell down and hit a big red button on the ground. The button made a loud noise, and a big door opened. Sam and Tim found a secret room with many toys inside. They played together all day and became best friends.

One sunny day, Fred met a new friend, a baby bird named Bella. Fred was excited to tell Bella his best joke. He told her the joke, and Bella laughed so hard. But then, Fred told the joke again. Bella was a little frustrated. She asked Fred, "Why did you repeat the joke?"
Fred didn't know why he always repeated his jokes. He felt sad and wanted to change. He asked Bella for help. Bella had an idea. She told Fred to think of a new joke every day.
The next day, Fred tried to think of a new joke. He thought and thought. Then, he had a funny idea! He hopped over to Bella and told her the new joke. Bella laughed so hard she fell into the pond! All the friends laughed, and Fred was so happy. From that day on, Fred never repeated his jokes again, and he became the best joke-teller in the pond.

Once upon a time, in an icy land, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the snow all day. One day, while playing, she found a small seed under the white snow. Lily was so excited and decided to grow the seed.
Lily ran to her mom and said, "Mommy, look what I found! Can we grow it, please?" Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, sweetie. Let's plant it and see what happens." They went inside their warm house and planted the seed in a pot.
Every minute, Lily would look at the pot and wait for the seed to grow. She was very patient. One day, a tiny green plant started to grow from the seed. Lily was so happy! She took care of the plant every day, giving it water and love.
Soon, the plant grew bigger and bigger. It had beautiful green leaves and bright flowers. Lily's mom said, "Lily, you did a great job! You helped the seed grow into a lovely plant." Lily smiled and hugged her mom, happy that she could grow something so pretty.

Lily was a little girl who liked to do many things. She liked to draw, to sing, to play with her toys and to read books. But she did not like to sleep in her crib at night. She thought her crib was too small, too dark and too boring.
One night, she heard a mysterious sound from her crib. It was like a soft whisper, but she could not understand what it said. She was curious and scared at the same time. She got out of her bed and tiptoed to her crib. She peeked inside and saw a tiny fairy sitting on her pillow.
"Hello, Lily," the fairy said. "I am Faye, and I am here to be your friend. I can show you many wonderful things in your dreams, if you sleep in your crib."
Lily was surprised and happy. She had never seen a fairy before. She wanted to see the wonderful things the fairy could show her. She asked, "What kind of things can you show me, Faye?"
Faye smiled and said, "I can show you the stars, the moon, the flowers, the animals, the rainbows and more. I can also tell you stories and sing you songs. But you have to sleep in your crib, or I will disappear."
Lily thought for a moment. She still did not like her crib very much, but she liked Faye a lot. She decided to give it a try. She said, "OK, Faye, I will sleep in my crib tonight. But you have to promise to stay with me and not leave me alone."
Faye nodded and said, "I promise, Lily. I will stay with you and not leave you alone. Now, let's go to sleep and have some fun."
Lily climbed into her crib and snuggled with Faye. She felt warm and safe. She closed her eyes and waited for Faye to show her the wonderful things in her dreams. "Let's go to the tower," Tom said. He wanted to be brave.
"No, it's too high and wobbly," Lily said. She was afraid.
"Come on, it will be fun," Tom said. He took Lily's hand and pulled her to the tower.
They climbed up the steps and reached the rope bridge. It was long and shaky. Tom went first and crossed the bridge. He waved at Lily.
"Your turn," he said.
Lily looked down and saw the ground far below. She felt dizzy and scared. She wanted to go back.
"No, I can't," she said. She started to cry.
Tom saw that Lily was sad and scared. He felt sorry for her. He crossed the bridge again and hugged her.
"It's okay, Lily. You don't have to do it. Let's go back," he said.
They climbed down the steps and ran to the slide. They slid down together and laughed.
They played on the other equipment until it was time to go home.
They had fun, but they never went to the tower again.
The end.

"I'm sorry, Tom," Lily said. "The bean was not that important. You can have it next time."
"I'm sorry, too, Lily," Tom said. "The bean was not that yummy. You are my friend and I don't want to fight with you."
They hugged and made up. They decided to play something else in the garden. They learned that fighting over a bean was a terrible idea.

Lia and Sam were playing in the park. They liked to pretend they were hunters in the jungle. They had sticks that they used as spears. They threw them at the trees and the bushes.
"Look, Sam, I found a big bird!" Lia said. She pointed at a gray and white creature with a long neck and legs. It was eating some grass near the fence.
"That's not a bird, Lia, that's a giraffe!" Sam said. He had seen one in a book. "It's very unusual. It has spots and horns and a long tongue."
"Can we catch it?" Lia asked. She wanted to touch it and see how it felt.
"I don't know. It's very tall and fast. Maybe it will run away or kick us." Sam said. He was a little scared of the giraffe.
They decided to try anyway. They crept closer to the fence, holding their spears. They waited for the right moment to throw them.
But the giraffe saw them. It lifted its head and looked at them with big brown eyes. It made a funny sound, like a whistle.
"Hello, children," it said. "What are you doing with those sticks?"
Lia and Sam dropped their spears. They were very surprised. They did not know that giraffes could talk.
"Uh, we were playing," Lia said. "We're sorry, we didn't mean to hurt you."
"That's all right," the giraffe said. "I'm not hurt. I'm just curious. Why do you want to catch me?"
"We wanted to see you up close," Sam said. "You're very unusual. We've never seen a giraffe before."
"Well, you can see me now," the giraffe said. "But you don't need to throw sticks at me. You can just ask me nicely. I'm very friendly."
"Can we touch you?" Lia asked.
"Sure, you can touch me," the giraffe said. "But be gentle. And don't pull my tail."
Lia and Sam smiled. They walked up to the fence and reached out their hands. The giraffe bent down and let them stroke its fur and horns. It felt soft and warm.
They liked the giraffe. It was unusual, but nice. They decided to be friends with it. They asked it many questions and learned many things. They had a lot of fun.
The end.

Tim was sad. He should have listened to his mom. Now, his toy car was gone, and the power from the box made everything in his room messy. Tim learned that sometimes, it's better to listen to others and not open things that have too much power.

Tim and Sue are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see a big mountain far away. They want to go there and see what is on top.
"Can we go to the mountain, Mom?" Tim asks his mom.
"No, Tim, it is too far and too high. You are too small to climb the mountain. Maybe when you are older, you can go there," Mom says.
"But Mom, we want to see the mountain. It looks so fun and pretty. Please, Mom, please," Sue says.
"I'm sorry, Sue, but it is not safe for you to go to the mountain. You can play in the park or in the backyard. There are many things you can do there," Mom says.
Tim and Sue are sad. They really want to go to the mountain. They think it is not normal to stay at home when there is a big mountain to explore. They look at the mountain and wish they could go there.
Then, they see a bird. The bird is flying near the mountain. The bird is colorful and loud. It looks happy and free.
"Hello, bird," Tim says. "Do you like the mountain?"
"Yes, I do," the bird says. "The mountain is my home. I fly there every day. There are many trees and flowers and animals on the mountain. It is beautiful and fun."
"Wow, that sounds amazing," Sue says. "Can you take us to the mountain, bird? Can you show us your home?"
The bird thinks for a moment. Then, it says, "I can offer you a ride, but only for a little while. You have to hold on tight and listen to me. The mountain is not easy to fly to. There are many winds and rocks and clouds. You have to be brave and careful."
Tim and Sue are excited. They want to see the mountain with the bird. They say yes to the bird. They hold on to the bird's wings and feathers. The bird flies up in the sky with them. They see the mountain getting closer and closer. They see the trees and flowers and animals on the mountain. They feel the wind and the sun and the rain. They hear the bird's song and the mountain's voice. They are happy and amazed.
They thank the bird for the ride. The bird says, "You are welcome. I hope you enjoyed the mountain. But now, you have to go back to your mom. She will be worried about you. You can come back another day, if you want."
Tim and Sue say goodbye to the bird. They hold on to the bird's wings and feathers again. The bird flies down in the sky with them. They see the park and the backyard and their mom. They are glad to be back. They hug their mom and tell her about the mountain and the bird. Mom is surprised and happy. She says, "You are very lucky to have such a friend. The bird is very kind and generous. But next time, please ask me before you go anywhere. I love you and I want you to be safe."
Tim and Sue say, "We love you too, Mom. And we love the bird and the mountain. They are our friends too. Can we go there again, Mom?"
Mom smiles and says, "Maybe, someday, we can all go there together. But for now, let's have some lunch. You must be hungry after your adventure."
Tim and Sue nod and smile. They are hungry and tired. They have lunch with their mom. They eat and drink and talk. They are happy and normal. They dream of the mountain and the bird. They dream of flying and exploring. They dream of being friends.

"Why does it have dirt on it?" Sara asked.

Sara nodded. She understood. She pulled out the carrot and saw the long root. She ran to the hose and washed the dirt off. Then she took a big bite.
"Mmm, this is a good carrot. Thank you, mom," she said.
"You're welcome, sweetie. I'm glad you like it. Do you want to see if there are more carrots in the garden?" her mom asked.
"Yes, please. Let's go find them," Sara said.

She decided that she liked gardening with her mom. It was a fun and tasty way to learn new things.

After they ate, Sue decided to play with Spot. She was very organized and had all her toys in a big box. Spot admired how clean and tidy Sue's room was. They played all day, and when it was time for bed, Spot and Sue were very happy. They knew they had a special friendship and looked forward to more fun days together.


One day, a duck went to the pond. The duck was tired. The duck saw a frog. The frog was wearing a hat. The duck said, "I like your hat."
The frog said, "Thank you, I found it in the pond. Do you want to wear a hat too?" The duck said, "Yes, I want to wear a hat." So, the frog and the duck looked for a hat in the pond for the duck to wear.
Then, something unexpected happened. A fish jumped out of the pond with a hat on its head. The fish said, "I found a hat too! Now we can all wear hats." The duck, frog, and fish were happy. They all wore hats and played in the pond together.

Tim felt proud that he could help the man, even with his hurt wing. As the days passed, Tim's wing healed. He could fly again and play with his friends in the sky. Tim was happy and never forgot the time he helped the man with the message.

"Help! The snake is out!" Sara screams.
"Run, run, run!" Ben shouts.
Sara and Ben run away from the snake. They are scared. The snake chases them. It is fast. It wants to bite them.
But then, a man sees the snake. He is the zookeeper. He has a net. He throws the net over the snake. He catches the snake.
"Got you, you naughty snake!" the zookeeper says.
He puts the snake back in the truck. He closes the door. He locks it.
"Are you okay, kids?" the zookeeper asks Sara and Ben.
"Yes, we are okay. Thank you, mister," Sara says.
"That was a close one. You should not go near the truck. The animals are not for playing. They are for the zoo. They can be dangerous," the zookeeper says.
"Sorry, mister. We were curious. We wanted to see the animals," Ben says.
"I understand. But you have to be careful. The animals are not like your toys. They have their own feelings and needs. They can be weird sometimes. They can gain or lose their temper. They can escape or attack. You have to respect them," the zookeeper says.
"We will, mister. We will respect the animals. We will not go near the truck again," Sara and Ben say.
"Good. Now, go back to your parents. They must be worried. And have fun in the park. But stay safe," the zookeeper says.
Sara and Ben nod. They run back to their parents. They hug them. They tell them what happened. Their parents are glad they are okay. They are also proud of them. They learned a lesson. They learned to respect the animals. They learned to be careful. They learned to be brave.

Lily went to find Tim, and they both sat down to eat the prunes. They were so excited to eat them, but then something unexpected happened. When they opened the box, there were no prunes inside! Instead, there were lots of colorful balls to play with.
Lily and Tim were surprised, but they laughed and played with the balls all day. They forgot about the prunes and had lots of fun together. In the end, Lily was not shy anymore, and she made a new friend in Tim.


Once upon a time, there was a cauliflower. It was tight and round. It lived in a big garden with other vegetables. They all liked to play together.
One day, the cauliflower wanted to complete a race. It asked its friends to join. The carrot, the tomato, and the pea said yes. They were all very excited.
The race began. The cauliflower rolled very fast. The carrot jumped high. The tomato rolled too, but not as fast. The pea hopped along. In the end, the cauliflower won the race. It was very happy to complete the race and have fun with its friends.


Once upon a time there was a tiny girl named Sun. Sun lived in a village with her family. Sun loved animals and every day she went to the meadow to ride her pony. Sun's pony was gentle and always listened to her.
One sunny day, Sun went to the meadow to see her pony. But when she arrived she saw something strange - a white veil was covering the pony! Sun was scared and she said, "Hello? Who's there?"
Suddenly, a witch suddenly appeared from behind the veil. She said she wanted to take Sun's pony away with her. Sun and the witch had a heated argument because Sun wanted to keep her pony. The witch was very firm and insisted on taking the pony, but Sun refused to let her.
The witch was getting angry and she was about to cast an evil spell on Sun. But then, Sun's family suddenly appeared and they scared the witch away. Sun was so relieved and hugged her family, thanking them for rescuing her.
Sun and her family took the veil off her pony and Sun was finally able to take a gentle ride with her pony, just like she had always done.

One sunny day, a new girl named Sue came to town. Tom saw Sue and wanted her to join him in playing chess. He said, "Hi, Sue! Do you want to join me and play chess?" Sue was happy and said, "Yes, Tom! I would love to join you and play chess."
Tom and Sue played chess together. They had lots of fun. The sun was shining, and the birds were singing. Tom and Sue became good friends. They played chess every day and had a great time.


Once upon a time there were two friends, Al and Jake, who were very brave. They were travelling through the forest and when they came upon a beautiful clear lake they decided to camp there.
The boys set up a very impressive tent and as they admired it, they heard a loud noise coming from behind them. It sounded like someone was surrendering!
Al and Jake cautiously turned around and sure enough there was a band of fierce warriors standing in the clearing. Al and Jake put up their hands in surrender and one of the warriors approached them. She motioned for them to follow her, so they obediently followed.
The warriors led them to a place that was filled with tents, even more impressive than the one they had set up. After showing them around, the warriors made it clear that all were welcome in their camp. Al and Jake stayed in the camp for a few days and had a great time learning about the different cultures that made up the camp.
When it was time for them to leave, the warriors gifted them with a tent of their own so that they could safely camp anywhere in the forest. Al and Jake were so grateful and thanked their new friends for their kindness. They carefully packed their new tent and set off on their way, feeling very impressed by their generous hosts.


Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in the living room. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big, soft armchair. They pretended it was a castle, a spaceship, or a dragon. Sometimes they climbed on it, sometimes they hid behind it, and sometimes they cuddled on it.
One day, they found a new toy on the armchair. It was a beautiful doll with long, yellow hair and a pink dress. Lily and Ben were very happy and wanted to play with it.
"Can I hold her first?" Lily asked.
"No, I want to hold her first!" Ben said.
They both reached for the doll and pulled her in different directions. The doll's hair and dress got tangled and torn. The doll's face looked sad.
"Stop it, you are hurting her!" Lily said.
"No, you stop it, you are breaking her!" Ben said.
They pulled harder and harder, until the doll's arm came off. They both gasped and let go of the doll. The doll's arm fell on the floor, and their dog, Spot, ran to it. He sniffed it, then started to chew it.
"Spot, no!" Lily and Ben shouted.
They ran to the dog and tried to get the arm back. But Spot was faster and ran away with it. He jumped on the armchair and wagged his tail.
Lily and Ben looked at each other. They felt sorry for the doll and for each other. They hugged and said, "I'm sorry, I love you."
They picked up the doll and put her on the armchair. They tried to fix her hair and dress. They looked for her arm, but Spot had hidden it somewhere.
"Maybe we can find her a new arm," Lily said.
"Or maybe we can make her one," Ben said.
They smiled and decided to work together. They looked for some materials and tools. They were going to make the doll a beautiful new arm.

Sue took Tom to a nice cow named Bess. Bess was happy to share her milk with Tom. Tom mixed the milk with the oats and shared the yummy snack with Sue and Bess. They all had a fun time eating together.
The moral of the story is that when we help each other and share, we can all be happy and enjoy good things together.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play in the woods. They knew they had to listen to their mom and dad, who told them to stay close to the house and not go too far. But one day, they saw a big, shiny rock that sparkled in the sun. They wanted to touch it and see what it was.
They ran to the rock, forgetting to listen to their mom and dad. They did not see the pale wolf that was hiding behind a tree. The wolf was hungry and saw the twins as a tasty snack. He waited for them to get closer, then he jumped out and growled.
Lily and Tom were very scared. They screamed and tried to run away, but the wolf was faster. He caught Tom by his leg and dragged him to the ground. Lily did not know what to do. She wished she had listened to her mom and dad.
Then she saw a big stick on the ground. She picked it up and hit the wolf on the head. The wolf let go of Tom and yelped. He ran away, afraid of the stick. Lily helped Tom get up and they hugged each other. They were hurt and dirty, but they were alive.
They ran back to the house, where their mom and dad were waiting for them. They were very angry and worried. They scolded the twins for not listening to them and going too far. They also hugged them and thanked them for being brave and smart. They took them to the doctor, who gave them medicine and bandages.
Lily and Tom learned their lesson. They never went to the woods again without listening to their mom and dad. They also learned to be careful of the pale wolf, who was still out there, looking for food. They knew that listening was important and could save their lives.

Once upon a time there was a curious seal who wanted to go on an adventure. He swam from one side of the ocean to the other, looking for excitement.
One day he stopped by a beach and saw a little girl picking up shells. The seal was so curious about the shells, he wanted to know what the girl was doing.
So, he slid up the shore and asked, "What are you adding?"
The little girl was surprised to see the seal and she said, "I am adding the shells to my collection!" She then showed him what she had found, a pink conch shell, a mother of pearl shell, and an ivory shell.
The seal was so amazed by all the shells. He asked if he could join in and add shells too. The little girl smiled and said, "Yes you can! Come join me and we can search together."
The seal happily followed the little girl around the beach, adding shells to her collection. When they finally were finished they said goodbye and the seal swam off, but happy and curious to explore more of the ocean.


Once upon a time, there was a young baby rabbit who lived in a soft meadow. The baby rabbit often explored the meadow taking in all the sights and sounds. One day, the baby rabbit was hopping around when she saw an interesting plant with vivid purple flowers! She hopped closer and snapped off one of the petals.
Suddenly, a small, soft hand appeared and pet the rabbit's head. Startled, the rabbit looked up to see who it was. It was a young girl, no bigger than the rabbit herself!
"Hi there!" said the girl with a smile. "What are you doing?"
The rabbit quickly explained what she was doing. The girl smiled and bent down until she was eye-level with the rabbit. "Would you like to explore together?" the girl wondered.
The rabbit happily hopped and the little girl followed. Together, they explored the meadow, snapping petals and shells along the way.
As the day grew dimmer, the girl waved goodbye and disappeared. But the rabbit never forgot their special adventure.
The End.

She picks up the picture and looks at it. She sees the dog. She knows the dog.

They look at Mom and say, "We are sorry, Mom. We did not know. We were fighting over the frame. We both liked the dog. We wanted to keep it."
Mom sighs and hugs them. She says, "I know you did not know. I know you liked the dog. But you should not fight over things. You should share and be nice to each other. You are twins. You are lucky to have each other."
Anna and Ben nod and hug Mom. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We love you. We love each other. We will share and be nice."
Mom smiles and says, "That's good. I love you too. Now, let's clean up this mess. And maybe we can find another frame and picture for you to keep. How about that?"
Anna and Ben smile and say, "Yes, Mom. Thank you, Mom."
They decide to help Mom clean up. They decide to be good twins. They decide to love the dog, even if he was old and smelly.

Lily took a piece of bread and walked to the edge of the pond. She saw a swan that looked weird. It had a black spot on its neck and a limp wing. It looked sad and lonely.
"Hello, swan. Do you want some bread?" Lily said.
The swan nodded and swam closer to Lily. Lily threw the bread to the swan. The swan ate it and made a soft noise.
"Thank you, little girl. You are very kind," the swan said.
Lily was surprised. She did not know swans could talk.
"How can you talk?" Lily asked.
"I can talk because I am a magic swan. I used to be a prince, but a witch turned me into a swan. She said I have to suffer until someone breaks the spell," the swan said.
"That's not fair. How can someone break the spell?" Lily asked.
The swan sighed.
"I don't know. The witch said only true love can break the spell. But who would love a weird swan like me?" the swan said.
Lily felt sorry for the swan. She wanted to help him.
"I love you, swan. You are not weird. You are beautiful and brave. Maybe I can break the spell," Lily said.
She hugged the swan gently. The swan felt a warm feeling in his heart. He felt something change in his body. He looked at his reflection in the water. He was not a swan anymore. He was a boy.

Lily smiled. She liked the boy. He had brown hair and blue eyes. He looked like a prince.
"You're welcome, boy. What is your name?" Lily asked.
"My name is Leo. What is yours?" the boy asked.
"My name is Lily. Do you want to play with me and Ben?" Lily asked.

Lily nodded. Leo kissed her on the cheek. Lily giggled.
Mom saw Lily and Leo. She was shocked.
"Lily, who is that boy? Where did he come from?" Mom asked.
Lily and Leo ran to Mom. They told her the story of the magic swan and the witch.
Mom did not believe them at first. She thought they were making it up. But then she saw the black spot on Leo's neck. It was the same as the swan's.
Mom realized it was true. She was amazed and happy.
She hugged Lily and Leo.
"I'm glad you found each other. You are both very special. Now, let's go home and have some cake," Mom said.
Lily and Leo agreed. They held hands and followed Mom. Ben joined them too. He liked Leo. He wanted to be his friend.

The spell was broken. She had lost her power. She had to suffer. She flew away on her broom. She never bothered them again.

Once upon a time there was a small boy named Steven who went to the park with his dad. Whilst running around, he felt an itch on his arm. He rubbed his arm and his dad asked him what was wrong. Steven replied "I have an itch". With a smile, his dad replied "Maybe a friendly caterpillar is visiting you". Steven was curious and started to search around, but he couldn't find any caterpillar.
Suddenly, he noticed a small furry caterpillar on his arm. He investigated and realised that the caterpillar was what had made him itch. He looked up to his dad and showed him the caterpillar. His dad smiled and then Steven noticed the small caterpillar had become bigger, it was now a butterfly! Steven was amazed; he didn't realise that caterpillars could turn into butterflies. He gently butterfly flew away into the sky.
Steven watched it fly away and realised that life can bring so many surprises. He held his dad's hand and smiled as they walked away from the park.

Mia and Leo were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with many leaves. They wanted to climb the tree and see what was on top.
"Let's go, Mia!" Leo said. "Maybe we can find a prize in the tree."
"OK, Leo!" Mia said. "But be careful. The tree is very old and ancient. It might break."
They climbed the tree slowly and carefully. They reached the top and looked around. They saw many birds and squirrels. They also saw a shiny thing hanging from a branch.
"Look, Mia! A prize!" Leo said. He reached for the shiny thing. It was a necklace with a blue stone.
"Wow, Leo! It's so pretty!" Mia said. "Where did it come from?"
"I don't know, Mia. Maybe someone left it here long ago. Maybe it's magic." Leo said. He put the necklace around his neck. He felt happy and proud.
Suddenly, they heard a loud crack. The branch they were sitting on broke. They started to fall.
"Help, Mia!" Leo said. "We're going to drop!"
"Help, Leo!" Mia said. "Hold on to me!"
They grabbed each other and screamed. They dropped to the ground. They landed on a pile of leaves. They were not hurt, but they were scared.
They looked at each other and hugged. They were glad they were OK.
"Are you OK, Mia?" Leo said.
"I'm OK, Leo." Mia said. "Are you OK?"
"I'm OK, Mia." Leo said. "But look, I lost the prize."
They looked at the tree. The necklace was gone. It had fallen off Leo's neck when they dropped. They could not see it anywhere.
"Maybe it was not a prize, Leo." Mia said. "Maybe it was a curse. Maybe the tree did not like us taking it."
"Maybe you're right, Mia." Leo said. "Maybe we should leave it alone. Maybe it belongs to the tree."
They got up and dusted themselves off. They decided to go back to their parents. They learned a lesson. They would not climb the ancient tree again. They would not take things that were not theirs. They would be happy with what they had.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a doll that she loved very much. She called her doll Anna. Ben had a car that he liked to zoom around. He called his car Zoomy.
One day, Ben wanted to play with Anna. He asked Lily, "Can I have Anna for a little bit?" Lily said, "No, she is mine. You have Zoomy." Ben felt angry. He wanted to have both toys. He grabbed Anna from Lily's arms and ran away. Lily cried, "Give her back! You are mean!"
Ben ran to his room and slammed the door. He looked at Anna. She had a pretty dress and long hair. He pulled her hair and ripped her dress. He felt happy. He thought, "Now Lily will be sad. She will not want Anna anymore. I can have her."
But then he heard Lily knock on his door. She said, "Ben, please open the door. I want to talk to you." Ben felt scared. He hid Anna under his bed. He opened the door and saw Lily. She had tears in her eyes. She said, "Ben, why did you take Anna? She is my best friend. I miss her. Please give her back."
Ben felt guilty. He saw that Lily was hurt. He did not want to hurt her. He liked Lily. She was his sister. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was angry. I wanted to have Anna too. But I was wrong. I did something bad. I hurt Anna. Look." He took Anna from under his bed and showed her to Lily.
Lily gasped. She saw that Anna's hair was pulled and her dress was ripped. She felt sad. She said, "Ben, how could you do this? Anna is broken. She needs to heal. She needs love. You don't love her. You are mean."
Ben felt sorry. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I do love her. I love you too. I don't want to be mean. I want to be nice. Can you forgive me? Can we heal Anna together?"
Lily looked at Ben. She saw that he was sorry. She felt sorry too. She said, "I forgive you, Ben. I love you too. We can heal Anna together. We can fix her hair and her dress. We can give her a hug. We can say a nice word to her. We can be her friends."
Ben smiled. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good sister. You are kind. You have a nice word. What is your word?"
Lily thought for a moment. She said, "My word is love. Love is a good word. Love can heal. Love can make us happy. Do you have a word, Ben?"
Ben thought for a moment. He said, "My word is sorry. Sorry is a good word. Sorry can heal. Sorry can make us friends. Can we say our words to Anna?"
Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, we can. Let's say our words to Anna. Let's heal her. Let's play with her. Let's share her."
They hugged Anna and said their words. They said, "We love you, Anna. We are sorry, Anna. We are your friends, Anna." Anna smiled. She felt healed. She felt loved. She felt happy. She said, "I love you, Lily. I love you, Ben. I am your friend, Anna." They played with Anna and Zoomy. They shared their toys. They were happy. They learned a lesson. They learned that words can heal. They learned that words can hurt. They learned to be careful with their words. They learned to be kind with their words. They learned to use good words.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly man named Bob. He had a red car with four big tires. Bob loved to drive his car around the town. One day, he saw a little girl named Sue sitting on the side of the road. She looked sad.
Bob stopped his car and asked Sue, "Why are you sad?" Sue looked at him and said, "I am tired and my legs hurt. I can't walk home." Bob thought for a moment and said, "I can help you. Please seat in my car, and I will take you home."
Sue smiled and said, "Thank you!" She sat in the car on the soft seat. As they drove, Bob told Sue stories about when he was young. Sue listened and laughed. The big tires on the car went round and round, taking them closer to Sue's home.
When they arrived at Sue's house, she said, "Thank you, Bob, for the ride and the stories." Bob smiled and said, "You're welcome. I'm glad I could help you." Sue waved goodbye as Bob drove away, his big tires taking him on more adventures.
From that day on, whenever Sue saw Bob's red car with the big tires, she would wave and smile. Bob would always wave back, happy that he had helped a friend. And they both knew that sometimes, all it takes is a soft seat and a kind heart to make someone's day better.


Once upon a time there was a duck named Quack. Quack lived near a pond which was always very warm and inviting. One day Quack's best friend, a little frog called Hop, came to visit.
"Hi Quack, I've been invited to a special party tonight. Would you like to come?" said Hop.
"Sure! I would love to go," said Quack.
So the two friends set off and they had a wonderful night at the party. Quack and Hop danced, laughed, and ate some delicious food.
After the party, Quack noticed that one of Hop's friends had left a pile of waste in the pond. That didn't seem very inviting!
"Hey Hop, why did your friend leave all that waste in the warm pond? That's not very nice," said Quack.
"I'm sorry Quack," said Hop. "My friend must have forgotten to take it away with him. Let's get rid of it and make the pond inviting again."
So the two friends worked together to take out the waste and throw it away in a bin. Soon, the pond was clean and warm again, just as inviting as before!

As Tom rubbed the sink, he heard a sound. Out of the sink came water! Tom was so happy to find water in the yard. He drank the water and played with it. From that day on, Tom always rubbed the sink when he was thirsty. And he stayed a healthy and happy cat.


Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lily. She loved running around outside in the sunshine. Today was an especially beautiful day, so Lily decided to go on an adventure. She ran around in circles and rolled in the grass before coming to a stop at the foot of a hill.
Lily looked up the hill and wondered what was at the top. She decided to find out. She started to climb up the hill, a smile spreading across her face. She went faster and faster until she reached the top.
At the top, Lily was surprised to find a pile of colorful yarn. There must have been a hundred pieces, all tangled up in a big, colorful mess. Lily didn't know what to do, so she sat down and thought about it.
Suddenly, a voice from behind her said, "Do you want some help?" Lily turned around to see a nice lady standing there. "It looks like you need a hand," said the lady. Lily nodded yes and the lady smiled back. She started untangling the yarn, a thoughtful look on her face.
The lady was so nice and helpful that Lily was sad to say goodbye. But when the lady finished helping, she said, "Here, this one is for you," and handed Lily a piece of yarn. Lily hugged the yarn close and waved goodbye, a big smile on her face. She was so thankful for the thoughtful gift!

Once upon a time, there was a poor girl. She was always kind and caring to everyone around her, but no one seemed to care much in return. One day, she got into a fight with a friend over a magazine. She tried to stay calm and explain her side, but her friend kept shouting. The poor girl began to feel sad.
Her mother saw that she was feeling low, so she took her daughter aside and said, "My sweet child, why did you get into a fight? Fighting won't help solve a problem but talking kindly can."
The poor girl thought about her mother's wise words. She decided that next time, she wouldn't fight but rather talk kindly and explain herself. The poor girl went back to her friend and apologized for her part in the fight and explained her feelings. Her friend apologized too and the two of resolved the argument without a fight.
The moral of the story is that it is important to talk kindly and not fight when we have disagreements.

The other kids in the park see them. They clap their hands. They applaud Tom and Lily. They say, "Well done, Tom and Lily, you are brave!"
Tom and Lily smile. They thank the other kids. They play together. They have a good day.

Tim and Sam were playing with their toy cars in the backyard. They liked to pretend they were cops and robbers, chasing each other around the grass. Tim had a blue car that made a siren sound when he pushed a button. Sam had a red car that could glow in the dark.
"Stop, robber! You are under arrest!" Tim shouted, as he drove his blue car towards Sam's red car.
"No way, cop! You can't catch me!" Sam said, as he drove his red car away from Tim's blue car.
They zoomed around the yard, dodging the flowers and the rocks. They were having a lot of fun, until they saw something disgusting on the ground. It was a big pile of dog poop, and Sam's red car drove right into it.
"Yuck! Gross! My car is dirty!" Sam cried, as he picked up his red car and saw the brown stuff on it.
"Ha ha! You got poop on your car! That's what you get for being a robber!" Tim laughed, as he drove his blue car near Sam.
"That's not funny, Tim! That's mean! You made me drive into the poop!" Sam said, as he threw his red car at Tim.
"Ow! That hurt! You hit me with your car!" Tim said, as he dropped his blue car and rubbed his head.
They both started to cry, and their mom heard them from the house. She came out to see what was wrong.
"What's going on here? Why are you crying? And why is there poop on your car?" she asked, as she looked at the mess.
"Tim and Sam, you need to say sorry to each other. And you need to clean up your cars. And you need to stay away from the poop. That's disgusting and dangerous. Do you understand?" she said, as she gave them a hug.
"Yes, mom. We're sorry. We'll clean up. We'll be nice. We won't play with the poop." they said, as they sniffled and nodded.
They took their cars to the hose and washed them off. Then they dried them with a towel and put them away. They decided to play something else, something that didn't involve poop. They learned their lesson, and they were friends again.

Once upon a time, there was a tough auto. People all around town marveled at how strong it was. But the auto had one problem - it was too noisy!
The auto's owners warned it sternly not to make such loud noises. They said if it disobeyed again then it would be punished. But the auto didn't listen. It blared its horn and revved its engine without a care.
The auto's owners were so angry they decided to punish it. They drove the auto out to a distant, quiet spot. When they got there, the owners opened the hood and let out a loud surprise.

Lila and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park near their home. One day, they see a big dog with black fur and brown eyes. The dog is friendly and wags his tail. He has a tag on his collar that says his name is West.
"Hi, West!" Lila says. She pets his head and ears. "You are a good dog. Do you want to play with us?"
West barks and licks her face. He follows Lila and Ben to the slide and the swings. He runs and jumps and chases a ball. He makes Lila and Ben laugh.
But West does not hear when other people call him. He does not hear when a car honks or a bird sings. He does not hear when Lila and Ben say goodbye. West is deaf. He can only see and smell and feel.
Lila and Ben do not know that West is deaf. They think he is just busy or shy. They go home and tell their mom about their new friend. They ask if they can see him again.
"Maybe," their mom says. "But you have to be careful. West is deaf. He cannot hear you or anything else. You have to use your hands and eyes to talk to him. And you have to watch out for dangers that he might not notice."
Lila and Ben are surprised. They do not know what deaf means. They ask their mom to explain.
"Deaf means you cannot hear," their mom says. "Some people and animals are born deaf. Some become deaf because of an illness or an accident. It is not their fault. They are still smart and kind and brave. They just need some help to communicate and stay safe."
Lila and Ben nod. They want to learn how to help West. They want to be his friends. They ask their mom to teach them some signs that West can understand.
Their mom smiles. She shows them how to say hello, goodbye, play, and good dog with their hands. She tells them to look at West's eyes and body to see how he feels. She tells them to always be gentle and respectful with him.
Lila and Ben practice the signs. They hope to see West again soon. They dream of playing with him in the park. They wake up happy and excited. They love West. And West loves them.

He banged his head and started to cry. Suddenly, an old man appeared from behind the wall.
He said: "Don't worry, Tom. That juice is called chili juice. It is much too spicy for little boys like you to drink. Give it to me and I'll keep it safe."
Tom smiled and handed the juice to the old man. From then on, Tom was careful to not speed too quickly or he might slip over again!

"What should we do?" they ask.

"Let's drink some water," Ben says. "They will make us wet and cool."

"Let's try again," they say. "We can do it."
They stand up and hold hands. They walk up the hill with new energy and hope. They want to see what is on the other side. They want to have fun in the sun. They are friends. They try.

"Sure, you can see them. But don't touch them. They are very heavy and dangerous. We only use them when we need to," the fireman said.

The bear ate the berries and felt very happy. He was not so scary anymore. The little girl smiled at the bear, and they became friends. From that day on, they played together in the woods and shared their berries. And the bear was never scary again.

Lila and Ben were playing in the sandbox. They liked to make castles and roads with the sand and their toys. But then a big dog came and jumped into the sandbox. The dog was filthy. He had mud and dirt all over his fur. He shook his body and made the sand fly everywhere.
"Hey, go away!" Lila shouted at the dog. "You are ruining our game!"
The dog did not listen. He barked and wagged his tail. He thought the sandbox was fun. He dug holes and knocked down the castles and roads. He grabbed some of the toys in his mouth and ran away.
Ben was very angry. He frowns and stomps his feet. He liked his toys. He wanted them back.
"Bad dog! Bad dog!" Ben yelled. "Give me back my toys!"
Lila and Ben chased the dog. They ran out of the sandbox and into the grass. The dog was faster than them. He ran and ran until he reached a fence. He dropped the toys and jumped over the fence.
Lila and Ben stopped. They could not go over the fence. They looked at their toys. They were filthy too. They had mud and dirt and dog spit on them.
Lila and Ben were sad. They did not want to play with their filthy toys. They did not want to play in the filthy sandbox. They wanted to go home and take a bath.
They walked back to the sandbox. They picked up their filthy toys. They carried them to their mom.
"Mom, look what the dog did!" Lila said.
"Mom, can we have a bath?" Ben asked.
Mom looked at them. She saw their filthy clothes and faces and hands. She saw their filthy toys and the filthy sandbox. She shook her head and sighed.
"Of course you can have a bath," she said. "But first, let me take a picture of you. You look like you had a very adventurous day."

"No, it is not!" Lily says. She is happy. She likes her part of the net.
"Yes, it is!" Tom says. He is angry. He pulls the net to make his part bigger.
"Stop it!" Lily says. She is sad. She pulls the net back to make her part the same.
The net breaks. The ball rolls away. Lily and Tom have no sport to play. They have no net and no ball. They have no fun.
They look at each other. They feel sorry. They say sorry.
"I am sorry, Lily. I was mean. I don't need a bigger part of the net. I just want to play with you." Tom says.
"I am sorry, Tom. I was mean too. I don't care about the net. I just want to play with you too." Lily says.
They hug. They are friends again. They find the ball. They play a new sport. They kick the ball to each other. They laugh. They have fun. They are happy.

On their way back home, Will barked loud and happy. He knew he did a good job helping Lily mail the letter. They played and laughed together for the rest of the day. And they lived happily ever after.


One day, a boy named Tim had a chicken. The chicken was his best friend. They played together every day. Tim loved his chicken very much.
One day, a girl named Sue came to Tim. She said, "Can you lend me your chicken? I want to play with it too." Tim thought and said, "Okay, but be very nice to my chicken. I will get it back later."
Sue took the chicken and played with it. But something unexpected happened. The chicken got very sick and soon it was dead. Sue was very sad and scared to tell Tim.
Sue went to Tim and said, "I am so sorry. Your chicken is dead." Tim was very sad and angry. He said, "You were not nice to my chicken. I will never lend you anything again."
From that day on, Tim and Sue were not friends. Tim missed his chicken very much and never forgot what happened.


Once upon a time, there was a loyal dog named Max. Max lived in a big lab with his friend, a kind man who wore a white coat. They played and worked together every day.
One day, Max and the kind man were playing with a big red ball in the lab. Max was very happy. But then, the kind man had to go away for a while. He told Max, "Stay here, Max. I will be back soon." Max sat down and the kind man shut the door.
Max waited and waited. He heard a strange noise outside the lab. Max was scared, but he wanted to see what it was. He pushed the door with his nose and it opened! Max saw a big, green frog. The frog said, "Hello, Max! You found me! I can talk!" Max was very surprised. The kind man came back and saw Max with the talking frog. They all became good friends and had more fun in the big lab together.


Once upon a time, there was a class of obedient little animals. They lived in a big, green forest. The animals liked to play, laugh, and learn new things.
One day, while they were playing, they found a magic button. The button had the word "reverse" on it. The animals did not know what it meant, but they were curious. So, they pushed the button.
Suddenly, everything started to go backward! The animals walked backward, talked backward, and even played backward. It was very funny and strange. They did not know how to make it stop, but they liked this new game.
The animals played with the magic button for a long time. They laughed and enjoyed the twist in their day. But soon, they started to miss their normal way of playing. So, they decided to push the button one more time.
When they pushed the button, everything went back to normal. The animals were happy to play, laugh, and learn like before. They knew their adventure was unexpected, but it made their day very special. And they never forgot the magic button that made them reverse.


One day, a kind cat and a fast dog had a race. They wanted to see who was the fastest. The cat was very good at running, and the dog was very good at running too. They were both very excited to race each other. Before the race, they put a big tray of treats at the end of the race path. The winner would get to eat the treats first.
The cat and the dog got ready to start the race. They both stood at the starting line, waiting for the signal to go. The cat looked at the dog and the dog looked at the cat. They both knew that this race would be very fun and exciting.
The race began, and the cat and the dog ran as fast as they could. They raced past trees, bushes, and flowers. The cat was very fast, but the dog was faster. The dog crossed the finish line first and won the race. The dog was very happy and proud.
The dog went to the tray of treats and started to eat them. The cat was sad that she lost the race, but the dog was kind. The dog shared the treats with the cat, and they both enjoyed them together.
From that day on, the cat and the dog were best friends. They learned that racing was fun, but being kind to each other was even better.

Amy wanted to show her mom the tube, so she ran to her mom as fast as she could. But, Amy ran so fast that she started to feel dizzy. Her head went round and round, and she fell down on the soft grass.
Amy's mom came over to help her. She gave Amy a big hug and asked her if she was okay. Amy showed her mom the tube and they both looked inside. They saw the pretty colors and smiled. Amy felt better, and they played at the park all day long.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park to play. She saw a perfect tree with big branches. Lily thought it would be fun to climb the tree. She started to climb up, up, up.
As she climbed, she found a big sheet stuck in the tree. She tried to pull it down, but it was stuck very tight. "Oh no!" Lily said. "I need help!" A boy named Tim heard her and came over to help. He climbed the tree too, and together they pulled and pulled on the sheet.
Suddenly, the sheet came loose, and Lily and Tim started to fall. They held onto the sheet, and it acted like a parachute. They floated safely down to the ground. They laughed and smiled, happy that they had worked together to solve the problem.


Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toy gun. He would run around and shoot it in the air. He felt proud when he shot it, just like a big hero. Tim also liked to watch his favorite show on the television.
One day, Tim was playing with his toy gun while watching television. He thought it would be fun to shoot at the television, just like the heroes on his favorite show. So, he aimed and shot his toy gun at the television. But something unexpected happened.
Instead of just making a fun noise, the toy gun broke the television! Tim was shocked and scared. He didn't know that his toy could break something. His mom came in and saw what happened. She was not happy, but she knew it was an accident. Tim learned to be more careful with his toys, and his mom got a new television. They watched their favorite show together, and Tim felt proud to be a good boy.


Once upon a time there was a little boy called Ben. Ben loved to explore and was always curious about everything. One day, he stumbled upon history books in his grandparents house.
Ben held one of the books and asked his Grandpa, "What's this?"
Grandpa smiled. "This is a book about history," he said.
Ben looked confused and asked, "What is history?"
Grandpa looked up and said, "History is something we can lift up to become better. It teaches us lessons and makes us smart. It's full of stories."
Ben didn't understand and he said, "It looks so dull."
Grandpa lifted Ben up onto his chair and said, "It's not dull. It's a part of your identity. It's your past, present and future."
Ben smiled and he suddenly understood the importance of learning history.
The moral of this story is that history can teach us valuable lessons. We can lift it up to become better and to avoid mistakes from the past.


Once upon a time, there was a little insect. The insect was light and could fly high in the sky. It had many friends who lived in the big green tree.
One day, the insect and its friends were playing near the tree. They were flying high and low, laughing and talking. The insect said, "Let's play hide and seek!" Its friends agreed, and they all hid in the tree.
While they were playing, the insect saw a big boy coming. The boy was not nice. He liked to punish insects for fun. The insect was scared and told its friends, "Quick, hide and be quiet!"
The friends listened and hid. The boy looked for insects but could not find any. He went away, and the insects were safe. They were happy that they could play again, and they promised to always watch out for each other.


Lily and Sam were on a big boat with their mom and dad. They liked to look at the sea and the fish and the birds. Sometimes they saw other boats and waved hello.
One night, Lily and Sam could not sleep. They heard a loud noise from the sea. They got out of their bed and went to the window. They saw a big whale jumping out of the water and making a splash.
"Wow!" Lily said. "Look at the whale, Sam! It is so big and strong!"
"Shh!" Sam said. "Don't wake up mom and dad. They are sleeping. Let's watch the whale quietly."
They watched the whale for a long time. It jumped and played and sang. It was happy and free. Lily and Sam smiled and clapped.
Soon, the whale got tired. It swam away slowly. It said goodbye to Lily and Sam with a loud blow.
"Goodbye, whale!" Lily and Sam said. "Thank you for showing us your tricks. We hope to see you again."
They went back to their bed and snuggled under the blanket. They closed their eyes and dreamed of the whale and the sea. They slept well and peacefully.
