Once there was a little boy who loved to look at the stars in the night sky. He often wished he could touch one of the stars. One night he wished even harder. Then, all of a sudden, a star came down from the sky and and started to talk to the little boy. The star asked the boy if he wanted to go on a special adventure. The boy said yes!
So the star picked up the little boy and flew very high into the night sky. It was a beautiful journey, and the sleepy little boy was very happy.
But then, the star started to cry. It said it was very sorry and needed forgiveness. The little boy was very sad. He asked the star why it was so sorry. But the star only said it was too late for forgiveness.
The little boy was very sad. He knew there was nothing he could do to help the star. He watched as the star flew away.


Anna and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park, draw pictures and read books. One day, they found a big letter on the ground. It was red and shiny and had a star on it.
"Wow, what an amazing letter!" Anna said. "I wonder what it says."
"Let's open it and see," Ben said. He tore the letter and looked inside. There was a piece of paper with some words on it.
"What does it say?" Anna asked.
Ben tried to read the words, but they were too hard. He only knew some of them. He read: "This is a magic letter. If you say the word 'disappear', you will go to a wonderful place. But be careful, you can only come back if you say the word 'appear'."
"Wow, that sounds fun!" Anna said. "Let's try it. Maybe we will go to a place with candy and toys and animals."
"OK, but we have to remember the word 'appear'," Ben said. "Or we will be stuck there forever."
They held hands and said together: "Disappear!"
Suddenly, everything went dark. They felt a strange wind and heard a loud noise. They opened their eyes and saw a new place. It was not wonderful at all. It was scary and ugly and cold. There were no candy and toys and animals. There were only rocks and thorns and monsters.
"Help!" Anna cried. "This is a bad place. I want to go home."
"Me too," Ben said. "Let's say the word 'appear' and go back."
They held hands and said together: "Appear!"
But nothing happened. They said it again and again, but nothing changed. They were still in the bad place. They looked at the piece of paper, but it was gone. They had lost it when they tore the letter.
They realized they had made a big mistake. They had opened a bad letter that lied to them. They had said a bad word that trapped them. They had forgotten a good word that could save them.
They started to cry. They wished they had never found the letter. They wished they had never said 'disappear'. They wished they could see their home and their parents and their friends again.
But they couldn't. They were stuck in the bad place forever. The end.


Once upon a time, there was a charming little bunny. The bunny loved to hop and play. One day, the bunny decided to go on an adventure. He wanted to find the big mountain he had heard about.
As the bunny hopped and hopped, he saw the mountain. It was very big! The bunny was so happy. He hopped faster and faster to get to the mountain. When he got there, he saw something he did not expect. There was a big frog on the mountain.
The frog was sad. The bunny asked the frog, "Why are you sad?" The frog said, "I miss my mommy. She is far away." The bunny wanted to help the frog. He had an idea. He said, "I will give you a kiss. Maybe it will help you feel better."
The bunny kissed the frog. Then, something unexpected happened! The frog turned into a beautiful bird. The bird said, "Thank you, bunny! Your kiss broke the spell. Now, I can fly to my mommy." The bird flew away, and the bunny was happy. He hopped back home, knowing he had done a good thing.


Once upon a time there was a little girl. Her name was Kay. Kay had many friends, but her favorite friend was the dancer. The dancer could move like no other. Kay loved to watch him twirl and tap around the room.
One day, Kay decided to try to be like the dancer. She jumped and twirled around the room, just like her friend. But then, she started to complain. She was very confused.
"Why can't I twirl like you?" asked Kay with a frown.
The dancer smiled and said, "It takes lots of practice and hard work. Keep at it, and soon you will be twirling like me!"
Kay wasn't so sure, but the dancer's words gave her hope. That night she practiced twirling and tapping until she was exhausted. But later, Kay twirled around the room with a giant smile on her face.
Kay's amazing twirling only got better with practice, and soon she was just as good as the dancer.


Once upon a time, there was a small town where people were very patient. They waited for good things to come. One day, a big earthquake came and shook the town. The houses wobbled, and the people were scared.
A little boy named Timmy went to his mom and asked, "Mom, why is the ground shaking? What is happening?" His mom replied, "It's an earthquake, Timmy. We must be patient and wait for it to stop."
Timmy wanted to help, so he took a ruler to measure the cracks in the ground. He saw one crack that was very big. He told his mom, "This crack is too big! What can we do?" His mom said, "We must wait and be patient. The town will fix it."
But the people in the town were not able to fix the big crack. The ground kept shaking, and the houses started to fall. The people were very sad. They had been patient, but the earthquake was too strong. The town was not safe anymore, and the people had to leave their homes.


One day, a little boy named Tim went for a walk. He saw an enormous alligator by the river. The alligator was green and had big teeth. Tim was scared, but the alligator said, "Don't be scared. I am a nice alligator."
Tim asked, "What are you doing here?" The alligator said, "I like to count the fish that swim by." Tim thought that was fun. So, he sat down next to the alligator and they started to count the fish together. One, two, three, four, five fish swam by.
After they counted the fish, the alligator said, "Thank you for counting with me." Tim smiled and said, "You're welcome. I had fun." Then, Tim went back home and told his mom about the enormous alligator who liked to count fish.


Once upon a time there was a lamb with bright white wool. His wool was so soft and bright, it made all the other animals very jealous.
The other animals wanted her wool too, so they tried to take it away. They tried to replace it with inferior material like hay and leaves, but it didn't work.
The lamb knew she could never replace something so special and beautiful. She kept her wool and kept it safe, because she knew it was special.
The moral of the story is that if you have something that is special and unique, you should never replace it with something ordinary. You should always treasure it - no matter what!


Sara was a little girl who liked to rise early. She wanted to see the sun come up and make the sky bright. She would get out of her bed, put on her slippers, and go to the window. She would watch the sun rise over the hills and smile.
One morning, Sara saw something different. There was a big balloon in the sky. It was red and yellow and blue. It had a basket with people in it. Sara was very curious. She wanted to know what the balloon was and where it was going.
She ran to her mom and dad's room and woke them up. She said, "Mom, dad, look! There is a balloon in the sky! Can we go see it?" Mom and dad rubbed their eyes and got up. They looked out the window and saw the balloon too. They said, "Wow, that is a hot air balloon. It is a special way to fly. Maybe they are going on an adventure."
Sara asked, "Can we go on an adventure too?" Mom and dad smiled and said, "Maybe someday, Sara. But today is an ordinary day. We have to get ready for school and work. But we can wave to the balloon and say hello." Sara nodded and said, "OK. But I hope they have fun." She waved to the balloon and said, "Hello, balloon! Have a good day!"
The balloon waved back with its bright colors. It flew higher and higher until it was a small dot in the sky. Sara felt happy. She had seen something new and exciting. She wondered what else she would see today. She went to get dressed and have breakfast. She was ready for her ordinary day.

One day, Susie and her mom were going on an adventure. They decided to go to the village store. As Susie and her mom walked up to the porch, Susie noticed something strange. She could hear a little squeak coming from the porch.
"Mom, what is that noise?", Susie asked.
"I'm not sure, why don't you go and take a look?", Mom replied.
Susie carefully stepped onto the porch and looked around. There, in the corner, was a tiny mouse recording a song. It was the strangest thing she had ever seen. It made her feel a bit uncomfortable.
"Mom! Look!", Susie exclaimed.
Her mom gasped. "That is so cute!", she said.
The little mouse kept on recording its song, unaware of its audience. Susie and her mom just watched in amazement.
Finally, Susie and her mom said goodbye to the singing mouse, and continued on their way to the village store. Susie had never seen something so special before. She knew she would always remember the singing mouse on the porch.

Tom didn't listen to the squirrel. He stayed under the cherry tree, even though he was cold and wet. The rain got stronger and stronger. Suddenly, a big wind came and blew the cherry tree down. Tom was hurt and cried. He should have listened to the squirrel and gone home.


Once upon a time, there was a big cabinet in a room. It was full of toys. In the room, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was a selfish boy. He did not like to share his toys with anyone.
One day, Tim's friend, Max, came to play with him. Max wanted to play with the toys in the cabinet, but Tim did not let him. Max was sad and sat in a corner. Tim continued to play alone.
Suddenly, a magic fairy appeared in the room. She saw Max sitting sad and Tim being selfish. The fairy waved her wand, and the cabinet disappeared! Tim looked around and gazed at the empty space where the cabinet was. He realized that he had been selfish and should have shared his toys with Max. Tim said sorry to Max and promised to be a better friend. The fairy saw this and brought back the cabinet. From that day on, Tim shared his toys and played happily with Max.


The sun was setting and the sky was getting gloomy. Carlos was walking home when he heard a rustling noise in a nearby bush. He went closer to take a look and saw a note next to a small box. He opened the box and found a small bird inside. The bird was scared and Carlos tried to calm it down.
"Don't be scared, little bird. I won't hurt you," he whispered. The bird calmed down a bit and Carlos read the note. It said that the bird's owner was going away for a long time and couldn't take him along. Carlos felt sad for the bird and decided to keep him.
He took the bird home and made a small nest for him. He closed the window so the bird wouldn't fly away and fed him his favorite snacks. He also wrote a note of his own explaining that he had taken the bird in.
The little bird was very grateful and they became the best of friends. Living with him made Carlos forget all his worries and sadness, even on the gloomiest of days.

Sara was very cold. She wanted to go outside and play with her friends, but she did not have a warm jacket. She looked in her closet and saw a big jacket that was her brother's. She thought maybe she could wear it and be warm.
She put on the jacket and zipped it up. It was very big and heavy. She felt something in the pocket. She put her hand inside and felt something soft and wet. She pulled it out and saw it was a half-eaten sandwich. It was green and smelly. It was disgusting!
Sara screamed and threw the sandwich on the floor. She took off the jacket and ran to her mom. She told her what happened and showed her the sandwich. Her mom was angry and said, "That's your brother's jacket. He always fills his pockets with food and forgets about it. He is very messy and wasteful. He needs to learn to clean up after himself."
She gave Sara a hug and said, "Don't worry, sweetie. I have a jacket for you. It's clean and warm and fits you well. You can wear it and go outside and have fun." She took Sara to her room and gave her a pink jacket with flowers on it. Sara liked it very much. She thanked her mom and put on the jacket. She felt cozy and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big blackboard in a small room. One day, a boy named Tom came into the room. Tom saw the blackboard and wanted to draw on it. He picked up a piece of chalk and started to draw a big sun.
Suddenly, Tom's friend, Sally, came into the room. She saw Tom drawing on the blackboard and said, "Tom, you should not draw on that blackboard. It is not yours." Tom felt guilty and stopped drawing. He looked at Sally and said, "I am sorry, I did not know."
Just then, they heard a noise coming from the corner of the room. They went to see what it was. They found a big, old apple that was starting to rot. Tom and Sally looked at each other, surprised. They did not expect to find a rotting apple in the room.
Sally had an idea. She picked up the apple and said, "Let's go outside and throw this away. Then we can play together." Tom agreed, and they left the room, forgetting all about the blackboard.
From that day on, Tom and Sally always played together and never felt guilty again. They learned that it is important to share and take care of things, even if they are not yours.


Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a little girl named Mia. Mia loved to play outside. One day, it started to rain. Mia did not like the rain because she could not play outside. She felt sad.
Then, Mia saw a small bird who was wet from the rain. She wanted to help the bird. Mia gave the bird a warm welcome and brought it inside her house. The bird was grateful for Mia's help.
Mia and the bird became good friends. They played inside the house while it rained outside. But one day, the bird flew away and never came back. Mia was very sad and missed her friend. The rain stopped, but Mia's heart was still full of sadness.


One day, a cat was walking through the hot summer day. As it walked along, the cat stopped to take a rest under a tree. Suddenly, the cat heard a funny noise coming from a bush nearby. The cat was curious and crept towards it.
In the bush, the cat saw a little rabbit. The rabbit was shivering and looked very scared.
"Why are you shaking?" asked the cat.
The rabbit looked up. "I'm scared of the loud thunder," it said.
The cat said, "Just close your eyes and listen. The thunder won't hurt you."
The rabbit listened and the thunder slowly faded away. The rabbit was so relieved that it hopped out of the bush and thanked the cat.
The cat smiled, then said, "You must now be careful when it is hot outside. Thunder may come again from far away."
The rabbit nodded and hopped away. The cat watched it go and smiled knowingly.


Once upon a time, there was an ancient statue in a small town. The statue was big and old. People in the town liked the statue. They would say "Welcome" to the statue every day.
One day, a little boy named Tim went to the statue. He looked up at the statue and said, "Hello, Mr. Statue! Welcome to our town!" The statue did not say anything back. Tim felt sad.
Suddenly, a loud noise came from the sky. A big storm was coming! The wind blew very hard. The ancient statue fell down and broke into many pieces. Tim and the people in the town were very sad. They could not say "Welcome" to the statue anymore.


Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy named Match. Match was a small car. Tim and Match liked to play together. They had lots of fun.
One day, Tim saw a big rock. He thought it would be fun to make Match speak. So, Tim put Match on the rock and said, "Speak, Match!" But Match did not speak. Tim tried again and again, but Match was still quiet.
Tim felt sad and thought playing with Match was boring now. He went to his mom and told her about Match. His mom said, "Match is just a toy, it can't speak." Tim understood and decided to find new ways to play with Match. Soon, they were having fun again.


One day, a big orange cat named Sam saw an envelope on the floor. He wanted to see what was inside. Sam tried to stretch his paw to reach it, but it was too far away. He called his friend, a little mouse named Tim, to help him.
"Tim, can you help me get the envelope?" Sam asked. Tim nodded and ran to the envelope. He pushed it closer to Sam. Together, they opened the envelope and found a note inside.
The note said, "Surprise! You both get a big cake!" Sam and Tim were so happy. They did not expect to get a cake. They shared the cake and had a fun day.


Once upon a time, there was a big cow. The cow was very careless. She would walk and run all over the farm without looking where she was going. One day, the cow saw a big pile of hay. The cow wanted to carry the hay to her friends, the horses.
The cow tried to pick up the hay with her mouth, but she was still being careless. She dropped the hay all over the ground. The cow felt sad because she could not carry the hay to her friends.
A little boy saw the cow and wanted to help. The boy was not careless like the cow. He picked up the hay and put it in a big bag. Then, the boy and the cow carried the hay to the horses together. The horses were happy, and the cow learned to be more careful.


It was a sunny day. Little Jack was full of joy as he ran around in the garden. He felt the warm sun on his face, and the light breeze against his skin. He wanted to stay outside forever, but his mom called him in for dinner.
"Come in now, Jack." She smiled.
Jack sighed, but he followed his mom inside. He was sad to leave the sun and the garden, but he put on a brave face. He knew that dinner was a part of his nightly routine.
Soon, Jack was sitting at the dinner table. His mom put down a heavy plate in front of him. She had made one of Jack's favorite meals - pancakes. Jack beamed, his sadness forgotten.
Little did Jack know, his mom had a surprise planned for him. After dinner, she opened the back door and let Jack return to the garden. Jack let out a sigh of relief; his day was not over yet. He ran off to explore the garden in the late afternoon sun with a heavy heart, full of joy.


Once upon a time there was an orange bird who lived in the hay. The bird was very happy there, tweeting away each day. But one day something disturbed the bird's peace. A fox came near the hay, and the bird had to flee!
The bird flapped its wings and flew away to the other side of the meadow. It was scared, but also relieved. The fox didn't find it.
The bird sat on a branch and looked back on the hay. It was sad to leave the place it called home, but then it saw something orange in the hay. It was an orange butterfly!
The bird flew down and the butterfly welcomed it with a beautiful song. The orange butterfly seemed to know the bird, as if they were old friends. The bird was no longer disturbed, for the butterfly had brought back its peace.


Once upon a time, there was a lazy octopus. He lived in the sea and loved to sleep all day. He had many legs and was very big. One day, he met a little fish who was very sad.
"Hi, little fish," said the lazy octopus. "Why are you sad?"
"I can't number my friends," said the little fish. "I want to play with them, but they are too many."
The lazy octopus wanted to help the little fish. He used his big legs to count the fish's friends. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight. There were eight friends.
"Little fish, you have eight friends," said the lazy octopus. "Now you can play with them."
The little fish was very happy. He played with his friends all day. The lazy octopus watched them play and felt happy too. From that day, the lazy octopus was not lazy anymore. He helped his friends in the sea and had many fun days.

One day, the sailor saw a little fish struggling in the water. The fish said, "Help, I am stuck!" The sailor wanted to help the fish. He pulled up the anchor and moved his boat closer to the fish.
The sailor picked up the fish and put it back in the water. The fish was happy and said, "Thank you, sailor!" They both smiled and the sailor went back to his boat. Now, the fish and the sailor were friends forever.


Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Penny. She had a friendly family who lived on a farm. One day, Penny and her family decided to go outside and perform some activities.
Penny held her arms up high and started twirling around. Her white dress spun around and around in circles. With an impish grin she shouted, 'look at me!'. Suddenly a big white bird flew up and landed on one of Penny's arms.
"Wow!" said Penny.
Her father smiled and said, "Penny, you are so talented! You can even perform for the birds."
Penny giggled and started playing with the bird. She fed it some of the food crumbs from her pocket and watched it fly away.
Penny was very proud of herself. She had performed such a wonderful trick!


One day, a girl named Sue went to a stable. She saw a big horse. The big horse was sad. Sue wanted to make the big horse glad. Sue said, "Can I sit on you, big horse?"
The big horse said, "Yes, you can." So, Sue sat on the big horse. The big horse started to feel glad. They went for a walk around the stable. They saw a small cat. The small cat was in a tree.
But then, something unexpected happened! The big horse turned into a small horse. The small cat jumped down from the tree. The small cat turned into a big cat! The big cat said, "Thank you for making the big horse glad. Now, I am a big cat and the horse is small."
Sue was very surprised, but she was still glad. She said, "I am happy to help. I like making friends glad." The big cat, the small horse, and Sue all played together. They were all very glad.

They could not play with the ball anymore. The brown ball stayed in the mud, and Max and the bird were stuck in the jail.

Bill called the bug, and the bug came to help. The bug was strong and could carry Zip. Zip held on to the bug, and they flew in the sky. Zip, Bill, and the bug had a fun day playing together. The clever cat, Zip, was happy he made new friends.

Once upon a time, in a big oak tree, there lived a little squirrel named Sam. Sam was very impatient. He loved to chew on nuts all day long. One day, he found a big shiny nut under the oak tree. He was so happy, he could not wait to chew it.
Sam took the nut to his friend, a wise old owl. The owl told Sam, "Wait until tomorrow, and you will find something very good." But Sam was too impatient. He wanted to chew the nut right away. So, he went back to the oak tree and started to chew the nut.
As Sam chewed the nut, something unexpected happened. The nut cracked open, and out came a beautiful butterfly! The butterfly flew around Sam and the oak tree, making everything look so pretty. Sam was surprised and happy. He learned that sometimes, waiting can bring something even better.


Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to play with her toys. One day, Sue lost her favorite toy, a small red car. She looked everywhere, but she could not find it. Sue was very sad.
Sue's mom saw her crying and asked, "Sue, why are you crying?" Sue replied, "I lost my red car and I can't find it." Her mom said, "Don't worry, we will find it together. But first, let's have a little talk about taking care of our things." Sue listened to her mom's talk, which was like a small lecture.
Sue's mom told her that it's important to put things away when we are done playing with them. That way, we won't lose them and we can find them easily next time. Sue thought her mom was right and promised to be more careful.
Together, they searched for the red car. They found it under Sue's bed. Sue was so happy! She gave her mom a big hug and said, "Thank you, Mom! I promise to put my toys away when I'm done playing."
From that day on, Sue always put her toys away after playing. She never lost anything again. The moral of the story is to always take care of our things and put them away when we are done, so we don't go crazy looking for them later.

One day, a big bear and a little rabbit were in the woods. They wanted to build a house together. The big bear was very strong and dependable. The little rabbit was fast and smart. They thought they would make a great team.
As they started to build, the big bear said to the little rabbit, "You pass me the wood, and I will put it up." The little rabbit agreed and passed the wood to the big bear. They worked very hard all day and were very happy with their new house.
But then, something unexpected happened. A big wind came and blew their house down! The big bear and the little rabbit were sad. They talked and decided to build their house again, but this time they would make it stronger.
The big bear and the little rabbit worked together again. They built a new house that was strong and safe from the wind. They learned that working together and never giving up made their house better than before. And they lived happily ever after.
The moral of the story is that when friends work together and are dependable, they can overcome any problem, even when something unexpected happens.

"Look, Tom, this book has a big red car on the cover. I like cars. Can we read this one?" Lisa asks.
"OK, Lisa, but be careful. The book is high up. You need to reach for it," Tom says.
Lisa nods. She stands on her toes and stretches her arm. She tries to grab the book. But the book is too far. Lisa slips and falls. She bumps her head on the floor. She starts to cry.
"Ow, ow, ow! That hurts!" Lisa says.
Tom is scared. He runs to Lisa and hugs her. He says sorry. He calls the teacher. The teacher comes and helps Lisa. She puts a band-aid on her head. She gives her a hug and a kiss.
"Lisa, are you OK? You were brave. But next time, please ask for help when you want to pick a book that is high up. You could get hurt," the teacher says.
Lisa nods. She says thank you. She feels better. She smiles at Tom. Tom smiles back. They pick another book that is low down. They sit on the carpet and read together. They are still friends. They are happy.

Once there was a group of friends who liked to count. Every day they would meet up to count things like leaves, stones, cats, and cars. They loved counting and even made it into a game. They grew more and more competitive as time went on.
One day, the friends decided to have a counting contest. They wanted to see who could count the most things in one day. They started counting and counting and counting. Every time someone counted more than the other, they grew more angry.
Finally, one of the friends became so mad that he said he was going to win no matter what! He started defending counting faster and faster but soon he was too tired and he fell asleep.
The other friends continued counting but no one ever had a chance to win. In the end, the competition went on with no winner and the friends stopped counting altogether.


Ben and Lily went to the museum with their mom. They saw many things that were old and strange. They saw bones of big animals, shiny rocks, and paintings of people and places.
Mom said they had to be quiet in the museum, because other people wanted to look and learn. But Ben and Lily wanted to talk and ask questions. They tried to whisper, but sometimes they forgot.
"Look, Lily, a dinosaur!" Ben whispered loudly, pointing at a skeleton.
"Shh, Ben, you are too loud!" Lily whispered back, pulling his arm.
"Sorry, sorry," Ben whispered, but he was too excited.
A man who worked at the museum heard them. He had a harsh voice and a frown. He came over and said, "You two, stop making noise! This is a museum, not a playground! If you can't be quiet, you have to leave!"
Ben and Lily felt scared and sad. They did not mean to be bad. They looked at their mom, who was also unhappy.

Sara climbs up the ladder and sits on the slide. She smiles at Ben and says, "Ready, set, go!" She pushes herself down the slide. She feels the wind in her hair and the sun on her face. She is happy.
But then, she sees something at the end of the slide. It is a big dog. It is barking and jumping. It wants to catch Sara. Sara is scared. She screams, "Help, Ben, help!"
Ben hears Sara and runs to the slide. He sees the dog and the sight makes him brave. He picks up a stick and waves it at the dog. He shouts, "Go away, dog, go away!"
The dog is scared of Ben and the stick. It runs away. Sara slides down and hugs Ben. She says, "Thank you, Ben, thank you. You saved me. You are not scared. You are brave."
Ben smiles and says, "You are welcome, Sara, you are welcome. You are brave too. You tried the slide. Maybe I will try it too. But first, let's play catch." They run and catch each other. They are happy.

Lily was sad and surprised. Tom saw her and said, "Don't worry, Lily. You look pretty even without makeup. Let's keep dancing!" They danced and danced until the party was over. Lily learned that she didn't need makeup to have fun and feel pretty.

Tim was surprised but happy. He and the magic bird became best friends. They had many fun adventures together in the red jeep.

Anna and Ben were twins who loved to play music. They had a drum, a flute, a guitar and a piano. They liked to make loud and lively sounds with their instruments. Sometimes they played together, and sometimes they played alone.
One day, Anna wanted to play the drum, but Ben was already playing it. Anna said, "Ben, give me the drum. I want to play it too."
Ben said, "No, Anna, I was playing it first. You can play the flute or the guitar."
Anna said, "But I don't want to play the flute or the guitar. I want to play the drum. It is the most fun."
Ben said, "Well, I want to play the drum too. It is the most fun."
They started to argue and tug at the drum. They made a lot of noise and their mom heard them. She came to their room and said, "Anna and Ben, what are you doing? You are making too much noise and you are not sharing. You need to settle down and take turns."
Anna and Ben looked at their mom and felt sorry. They said, "Sorry, mom. We were fighting over the drum. We both like it a lot."
Mom said, "I know you both like the drum, but you can't play it at the same time. You have to share and be fair. How about you play the drum for five minutes, and then you switch with your sister or brother? That way, you can both enjoy the drum and the other instruments."
Anna and Ben thought that was a good idea. They said, "Okay, mom. We will do that. Thank you for helping us."
Mom smiled and said, "You're welcome. I'm glad you settled your problem. Now, you can play music nicely and have fun."

The moral of this story is that even brave mice can get into trouble if they explore unknown, scary places. Always be careful and stay away from dangerous places.

Lily liked to paint. She had many colors to paint with. She liked red and yellow and blue and green. She wanted to paint a rose for her mom. She found a picture of a rose in a book and looked at it.
She took her red paint and made a big circle. Then she made smaller circles inside the big circle. She painted some green for the leaves. She was happy with her rose. She showed it to her mom.
"Look, mom, I painted a rose for you!" Lily said.
Mom smiled and hugged Lily. "Thank you, Lily, it's very pretty. I love it."
Lily was happy. She wanted to paint more roses. She looked for more colors. She saw a black paint. She wondered how a black rose would look like. She took the black paint and made another big circle. Then she made smaller circles inside the black circle. She painted some green for the leaves. She was curious about her black rose. She showed it to her mom.
"Look, mom, I painted another rose for you!" Lily said.
Mom frowned and shook her head. "No, Lily, that's not a rose. That's a black spot. Roses are not black. Black is not a pretty color for roses. You should use other colors."
Lily was sad. She liked her black rose. She thought it was different and cool. She did not understand why mom did not like it. She felt angry and hurt. She did not want to paint anymore. She threw her black paint on the floor.
"Mom, you are mean! I like my black rose! It's my rose! I can paint it any color I want!" Lily shouted.
Mom was shocked and upset. She did not mean to hurt Lily's feelings. She wanted to help Lily learn about colors and flowers. She did not like to see Lily angry and crying. She tried to calm Lily down.
"Lily, I'm sorry. I didn't mean to be mean. I know you like to paint. I know you are creative. But black is not a good color for roses. It makes them look sad and sick. Roses are beautiful and bright. They have many colors, like red and pink and white and yellow. You can paint roses with any of these colors. They will look much better than black. Please, don't be mad at me. I love you and your paintings." Mom said.
Lily looked at mom. She saw mom's eyes were wet. She felt sorry for mom. She did not want to make mom cry. She realized mom was trying to teach her something. She decided to listen to mom. She picked up her black paint and put it back in the box. She took a tissue and wiped mom's eyes.
"Mom, I'm sorry too. I didn't mean to shout at you. I know you love me and my paintings. I was just curious about black. I wanted to try something new. But I see you are right. Black is not a good color for roses. It does make them look sad and sick. I will use other colors. I will paint roses with red and pink and white and yellow. They will look beautiful and bright. Please, don't be sad. I love you and your hugs." Lily said.
Mom smiled and hugged Lily. "Thank you, Lily. You are very sweet and smart. I'm glad you are willing to learn and try new things. I'm proud of you and your paintings. You can paint anything you want, as long as you use good colors. I'm happy to see you happy."
Lily smiled and hugged mom. She felt happy again. She wanted to paint more roses. She took her red paint and made another big circle. Then she made smaller circles inside the big circle. She painted some green for the leaves. She showed it to mom.
"Look, mom, I painted another rose for you!" Lily said.
Mom smiled and hugged Lily. "Thank you, Lily, it's very pretty. I love it."

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. They took a big bottle of juice to drink when they got thirsty. They played on the swings and the slide, and Tim had lots of fun.
Tim saw a little girl named Sue playing with a toy. He wanted to play with it too, but Sue didn't want to share. Tim got mad and pinched Sue's arm. Sue started to cry, and Tim's mom came over to see what happened.
"Tim, why did you pinch Sue?" his mom asked. Tim said, "She wouldn't share her toy with me." His mom said, "That's not nice, Tim. You should say sorry to Sue." Tim felt bad and said sorry to Sue. Sue stopped crying and they both shared the toy.
Later, Tim and Sue got thirsty, so they went to drink the juice. But Tim's mom said, "This juice is disgusting! I think it's old." They threw the juice away and drank water instead.
The moral of the story is to always be nice and share with others. Also, check if the juice is good before you drink it.

Tim liked to play hockey with his friends. He had a stick and a puck and he wore a helmet and gloves. He was good at hitting the puck and scoring goals. He was proud of his hockey skills.
One day, he went to the park with his friends to play hockey. There was a big ice rink where they could skate and play. Tim was excited and he wanted to show off his skills. He skated fast and tried to hit the puck hard. But he was careless and he did not look where he was going.
He bumped into a girl who was also skating on the ice. She fell down and dropped her hat and scarf. She was not happy. She looked at Tim and said, "Hey, watch where you are going! You are so careless! You made me fall and you messed up my hat and scarf!"
Tim felt bad. He did not mean to bump into the girl. He said, "I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I did not see you. Are you okay? Here, let me help you." He picked up her hat and scarf and gave them to her. He helped her get up and asked if she was hurt.
The girl was not hurt, but she was still angry. She said, "You should be more careful. You could have hurt me or yourself. You should not play hockey here. This is not a hockey rink. This is a skating rink. Go play hockey somewhere else!"
Tim felt embarrassed. He did not know that this was not a hockey rink. He thought he could play hockey anywhere. He looked around and saw that everyone was staring at him. He felt his face turn red. He said, "I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I did not know. I will go play hockey somewhere else." He took his stick and puck and skated away. He felt sad and ashamed. He wished he had been more careful. He learned a lesson that day. He learned to be more careful and to respect other people's space. He hoped the girl would forgive him. He hoped his friends would not laugh at him. He hoped he could still play hockey and have fun.

Tom and Lily are twins. They like to play in their big house. They have many toys and books and games. But their favorite thing is to rush up and down the stair. The stair is long and has many steps. They pretend they are climbing a mountain or flying a plane or chasing a monster.
One day, they hear a loud noise from the kitchen. It sounds like a crash and a bang. They wonder what it is. They rush to the stair and start to go down. But they are too fast and they slip and fall. They bump their heads and knees and elbows. They cry and shout.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom says. "That hurts!"
"Mom, mom, mom!" Lily says. "Help us!"
Mom hears them and comes to the stair. She sees them lying on the floor. She is worried and scared. She runs to them and hugs them. She checks if they are hurt. She kisses their boo-boos and wipes their tears.
"Are you okay, my loves?" Mom says. "What happened?"
"We heard a noise and we rushed to the stair and we fell and we hurt ourselves," Tom says.
"We wanted to see what it was and we were too fast and we slipped and we bumped and we cried," Lily says.
Mom smiles and says, "I'm sorry, my loves. The noise was me. I dropped a pot and a pan. It was an accident. I'm glad you are not badly hurt. But you have to be careful on the stair. It is long and steep and slippery. You have to go slow and hold the rail. Do you understand?"
Tom and Lily nod and say, "Yes, mom. We understand. We are sorry. We love you."
Mom says, "I love you too, my loves. Now, let's go to the kitchen and have some cookies and milk. How does that sound?"
Tom and Lily smile and say, "That sounds good, mom. Thank you."
They hold Mom's hand and go to the kitchen. They are happy and safe. They eat their cookies and drink their milk. They forget their pain and their fear. They laugh and talk and play. They are good twins. They are good children. They are Mom's loves.

Timmy loved his bicycle. It was red and shiny and had a bell that went ding-ding. He got it for his birthday from his mom and dad. They said it was his original bicycle, because it was the first one he ever had.
One day, Timmy wanted to ride his bicycle to the park. He asked his mom if he could go. She said yes, but he had to wear his helmet and be careful. She also said he had to remind her when he came back, because she had a surprise for him. Timmy wondered what the surprise was. He said okay and put on his helmet.
He rode his bicycle to the park and had a lot of fun. He saw his friends and played with them. He went on the swings and the slide and the seesaw. He forgot about the time and the surprise. He was having too much fun.
Then he heard a loud noise. It was a big truck that was driving by the park. It was very noisy and scary. Timmy looked at the truck and saw something that made him gasp. It was his bicycle! The truck had his bicycle on the back, along with other things. Timmy realized that he had left his bicycle outside the park gate, and someone had taken it and put it on the truck.
Timmy ran after the truck, but it was too fast. He shouted and cried, but no one heard him. He lost his bicycle, his original bicycle, and he didn't know what to do. He felt very sad and angry.
He walked back to his house, with tears in his eyes. He didn't want to see his mom or his surprise. He just wanted his bicycle back. He opened the door and saw his mom waiting for him. She smiled and said, "Timmy, I have a surprise for you. Look what I found on the street. It's your bicycle!"
Timmy couldn't believe his eyes. It was his bicycle, his red and shiny and ding-ding bicycle. His mom had seen the truck and followed it. She had seen the driver stop and unload some things. She had seen his bicycle and recognized it. She had taken it back and brought it home.
Timmy was so happy and relieved. He hugged his mom and thanked her. He said he was sorry for forgetting to remind her. He said he loved her and his bicycle. He said it was the best surprise ever. His mom said she loved him too and was glad he was safe. She said he had learned a lesson. He had to be careful with his things and not leave them unattended. She said he had to be more responsible with his original bicycle. Timmy said he understood and he would. He said he wanted to ride his bicycle again. His mom said he could, but he had to wear his helmet and be careful. Timmy said okay and put on his helmet. He rode his bicycle to the park and had a lot of fun. He didn't forget about the time or the surprise. He was happy and grateful. He had his bicycle, his original bicycle, and he loved it.

Once upon a time there was a boy who loved to explore. He wanted to find a secret cave. So he went on a journey.
The boy came to a deep dark forest. He looked for a cave for a long time. But he couldn't find one. Then he heard a funny sound! It was a reverse sound!
The boy looked around and saw a big tree with a hole in it. He ran inside and it was very dark. But then he heard the reverse sound again! Suddenly, the cave lit up!
In the dim light, the boy saw a deep pool of water. It had blocks of wood in it! He was sure it was the secret cave! He reversed the wood blocks and the water disappeared!
The boy found a secret passageway! It was full of incredible things! He smiled and thought he would be back soon to explore more.

Once there was a cactus named Sue. Sue was a very excited cactus as she finally had lots of friends. She loved to have picnics with her friends and play games.
One day, Sue's friends decided to play hide and seek. "We will hide and one of you has to find us!" They shouted. Sue was so excited that she quickly said she would do it.
The friends went to hide and Sue kept looking around for them. But, she could not find any of her friends. Suddenly she noticed something strange behind a big sack on the ground. She carefully pulled the sack away and there were her friends, hiding!
"You tricked me!" she cried. Sue was so mad that she did not want to be friends with them anymore and ran away.
The moral of this story is that it is wrong to trick your friends. Even though it can seem fun, it usually hurts their feelings and can make them never want to be friends with you again.


Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they found a big sack in the shed. They opened it and saw many fireworks inside. They were shiny and colorful and had funny names.
"Wow, look at these!" Tom said. "Let's take some and play with them."
"No, Tom, we can't!" Lily said. "Mum and Dad said fireworks are dangerous. They can hurt us and make loud noises. We have to wait for them to light them for us on Bonfire Night."
But Tom did not listen. He was naughty and wanted to have fun. He took some fireworks and hid them in his pocket. He told Lily to follow him to the park.
At the park, Tom found a stick and a match. He lit the match and touched it to the stick. Then he put the stick in a firework and threw it in the air.
"Look, Lily, look!" he shouted. "It's going to make a big bang!"
But the firework did not go up. It fell down and landed on a pile of dry leaves. The leaves caught fire and made a lot of smoke. The smoke made Lily and Tom cough and cry.
"Help, help!" they screamed. "Fire, fire!"
Some people saw the fire and called the firemen. The firemen came with a big red truck and a loud siren. They used a hose to put out the fire. They also found the sack of fireworks and took it away.
The firemen were angry and asked Lily and Tom who did it. Lily told them the truth. She said Tom was naughty and took the fireworks without asking. Tom felt sorry and ashamed. He said he was sorry and he would never do it again.
The firemen told Lily and Tom to go home and tell their parents what they did. They said fireworks are not toys and they should never play with them. They said they were lucky they did not get hurt or burn the park.
Lily and Tom nodded and ran home. They were scared and sad. They knew Mum and Dad would be very cross with them. They wished they had listened to Lily and left the fireworks alone. They learned a hard lesson that day.


Once upon a time, there was a smart cat named Tim. Tim loved to play with his ball. One day, while playing, his ball vanished. Tim looked everywhere but could not find his ball. He felt sad and missed his ball.
Tim asked his friend, a dog named Sam, "Have you seen my ball?" Sam shook his head and said, "No, but I will help you look for it." They looked under the trees and behind the bushes, but the ball was still not there.
Finally, they asked a wise old owl named Mr. Wise. He listened to their question and said, "I saw your ball roll into the big hole by the tree." Tim and Sam went to the big hole and found the ball. They were so happy! From that day on, they always played together and never let the ball vanish again.

The dog said to the cat, "I want to sit on the sack!" The cat said, "No! I got here first!" The dog was very sad and felt bitter. He wanted to find a way to sit on the sack too.
Then, the dog had an idea. He said to the cat, "Let's share the sack! You can sit on one side, and I can sit on the other side." The cat thought about it and said, "Okay, we can share the sack." So, the cat and the dog both sat on the sack, and they were both happy in the warm sun.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a little mouse. The mouse was worried because he was very dirty. He wanted to be clean and nice, but he did not know how to wash himself.
One day, the mouse saw a big cat. The cat was washing her face with her paw. The mouse said, "Hello, cat! Can you help me? I am worried because I am dirty. How do you wash yourself?" The cat looked at the mouse and said, "Of course, little mouse! I can help you. Just use your paws like me. Wet them and rub them on your face and body."
The mouse did what the cat said. He wet his paws and rubbed them on his face and body. Soon, the mouse was clean and not worried anymore. He thanked the cat and they became good friends. From that day on, the mouse always knew how to wash himself and was never worried about being dirty again.

Once upon a time, there was a sailor called Nelly. She loved the seas and was always wishing to go far and explore new reefs. One day, Nelly set sail with the wind in her sails and the sun bright in the sky. Her boat was filled with happiness and joy.
Just as Nelly was getting close to a distant reef, however, a storm began! Rain started to pour and waves started to crash against her boat. Nelly was terrified and quickly began to close the sails, trying to find shelter within the reef.
Suddenly, she heard a voice:
"Surrender and turn your boat around!" Nelly turned to find an old sailor. He had a stern expression on his face, demanding that she stop.
"No, I can't surrender!" she exclaimed. She was determined to cross the difficult reef.
The old sailor warned her of the approaching storm, but Nelly was brave and assumed the challenge. With all her might, she managed to lead her boat successfully across the reef.
Nelly had learnt a new lesson. Even when faced with something as difficult as a storm, don't surrender and keep fighting on!

Once upon a time, there was a mighty butterfly named Bob. Bob loved to fly high in the sky. He had many friends, but his best friend was a little girl named Sue. Sue and Bob would play all day in the sun.
One day, Sue said to Bob, "Let's have a race! I want to see who is the fastest." Bob liked the idea and said, "Okay, let's race to the big tree and back." They both got ready and started to run. Sue was fast, but Bob was faster. He flapped his wings as fast as he could.
As they got close to the finish line, Bob and Sue were neck and neck. They both pushed as hard as they could. In the end, Bob won the race by just a little bit. Sue was a little sad, but she was happy for her friend. She said, "Good job, Bob, you are very fast!"

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in the living room. But today, they have a problem. There is only one bathroom in their house, and they both need to go.
"Mom, I need to go to the bathroom!" Anna says.
"Me too, me too!" Ben says.
"OK, OK, calm down. You can take turns. Anna, you go first. Ben, you wait here." Mom says.
Anna runs to the bathroom and closes the door. Ben waits outside. He is grumpy. He does not like to wait. He wants to go to the bathroom now.
He knocks on the door. "Anna, hurry up! I need to go!"
"Go away, Ben! I'm not done!" Anna says.
Ben knocks harder. "Anna, come on! You're taking too long!"
"Stop it, Ben! You're being mean!" Anna says.
Ben gets angry. He shakes the door. He tries to open it. He yells. "Anna, let me in! Let me in!"
Anna gets scared. She screams. "Ben, stop! Stop! You're hurting the door!"
Mom hears the noise. She comes to the bathroom. She sees Ben shaking the door. She sees Anna crying inside.
She is not happy. She grabs Ben by the arm. She pulls him away from the door.
"Ben, what are you doing? You're being very naughty! You can't shake the door like that! You have to wait your turn!" Mom says.
"But Mom, I need to go to the bathroom!" Ben says.
"Well, you have to be patient. And you have to be nice to your sister. She needs to go to the bathroom too. You have to share." Mom says.
She opens the door. She lets Anna out. She hugs her. "Are you OK, Anna? I'm sorry Ben scared you. He was being very rude."
"I'm OK, Mom. Thank you." Anna says.
She looks at Ben. She is still mad at him. But she is also sorry for him. She knows he needs to go to the bathroom too.
She says to him. "Ben, I'm sorry I took so long. You can go to the bathroom now. But please don't shake the door again. It's not nice."
Ben looks at Anna. He is still grumpy. But he is also sorry for her. He knows he scared her.
He says to her. "Anna, I'm sorry I shook the door. I was being very mean. Thank you for letting me go to the bathroom now. But please don't take so long again. It's not fair."
Mom smiles. She is glad they are sorry. She hopes they will be nicer to each other.
She says to them. "OK, kids, I'm proud of you for saying sorry. Now, Ben, you go to the bathroom. Anna, you come with me. We'll find something else to play with. And remember, you have to share. And you have to be kind. OK?"
"OK, Mom." Anna and Ben say.
They hug Mom. They hug each other. They go to the bathroom and to the living room. They play with their toys. They are not grumpy anymore. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a busy ant named Tim. Tim was always working hard, carrying steel to build his ant home. One day, he met a lazy bug named Max. Max did not like to work at all.
"Tim, why don't you quit working so hard?" Max asked. "Come play with me instead!" Tim thought about it, but he knew he had to help his ant friends build the home.
"No, Max," Tim said. "I can't quit. I have to help my friends." Max was sad, but he went away to play by himself.

"No, Ben, you can't!" Lily said. "If you take one of mine, then I will have four and you will have six. That is not fair."

Mom hugged Lily and said, "I'm sorry, honey, but you can't touch the seals. They are wild animals, not pets. They don't like to be touched by strangers. You have to be careful and listen to me."
Lily nodded and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I won't touch the seals again."
Mom took Lily to a nurse, who cleaned and bandaged her finger. Tom followed them, feeling nervous.
"Are you okay, Lily?" Tom asked.
Lily smiled and said, "I'm okay, Tom. Thank you. The seal didn't mean to hurt me. It was just scared."
Tom hugged Lily and said, "I'm glad you're okay, Lily. I love you."
"I love you too, Tom," Lily said.
Mom smiled and said, "I love you both, kids. Now, let's go see some other animals, okay?"
Tom and Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom."
They left the seal pool and went to see some other animals. They had fun, but they never touched the seals again.

"Roar!" Tom said, jumping on the couch. "I am the king of the jungle!"
"Tweet!" Anna said, flying around the room. "I am the fastest bird in the sky!"
They laughed and chased each other until they heard their mom call them.
"Tom! Anna! It's time for dinner!" Mom said from the kitchen.
Tom and Anna ran to the table and sat down. They saw their mom had made their favorite food: spaghetti and meatballs. They smiled and said thank you.
"Mom, this is yummy!" Tom said, twirling his fork.
"Mom, this is delicious!" Anna said, taking a big bite.
Mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you like it. And guess what? I have a surprise for you after dinner."
"What is it?" Tom and Anna asked, curious.
Mom winked and said, "You'll see. But you have to finish your plates first."
Tom and Anna ate quickly, eager to find out the surprise. They wondered what it could be. A new toy? A book? A game?
When they were done, mom brought out a big tray with four bowls. In each bowl, there was a scoop of ice cream, some whipped cream, and a cherry on top.
"Dessert!" Tom and Anna exclaimed, clapping their hands.
Mom nodded and said, "Yes, dessert. I made it for you because you have been such good kids today. You can choose your flavor: chocolate, vanilla, strawberry, or mint."
Tom and Anna looked at the bowls and thought hard. They both liked all the flavors, but they had different favorites.
"I want chocolate!" Tom said, reaching for a bowl.
"I want strawberry!" Anna said, grabbing another bowl.
But then they realized they had both taken the same bowls. They looked at each other and frowned.
"Hey, that's mine!" Tom said, pulling the bowl.
"No, that's mine!" Anna said, tugging the bowl.
They started to fight over the bowl, spilling some ice cream on the table. They were upset and angry.
"Stop it!" Mom said, raising her voice. "You can't have the same bowl. There are two more flavors. Why don't you trade?"
Tom and Anna looked at the other bowls. They saw vanilla and mint. They didn't like them as much as chocolate and strawberry, but they knew they had to share.
"Fine," Tom said, letting go of the bowl. "I'll take vanilla."
"Fine," Anna said, pushing the bowl. "I'll take mint."
They swapped the bowls and started to eat. They were still upset, but they didn't want to waste their dessert.
They ate in silence, until they heard a knock on the door.
"Who is it?" Mom asked, getting up.
She opened the door and saw their dad standing there. He had a big smile and a bag in his hand.
"Hi, everyone!" Dad said, coming in. "I'm home from work. And I have a surprise for you!"
He opened the bag and took out two boxes. He gave one to Tom and one to Anna.
"What is it?" Tom and Anna asked, excited.
They opened the boxes and saw two cupcakes. One was chocolate and one was strawberry. They had frosting and sprinkles and candles on top.
"Cupcakes!" Tom and Anna shouted, jumping up.
Dad nodded and said, "Yes, cupcakes. I bought them for you because I love you. And because today is a special day. Do you know what day it is?"
Tom and Anna thought for a moment. Then they remembered.
"It's our birthday!" Tom and Anna said, smiling.
Dad hugged them and said, "That's right. It's your birthday. You are four years old today. Happy birthday, my twins!"
Mom joined them and said, "Happy birthday, my sweeties!"
They lit the candles and sang happy birthday. Then they blew them out and made a wish.
Tom and Anna wished for the same thing: to be happy and to have more dessert.


Tommy was a dog who loved to run and play. He had a red collar that his owner gave him. He was very proud of his collar and liked to show it to other dogs. One day, he saw a big park with many trees and flowers. He wanted to explore it and have fun.

His owner said, "Yes, you can, but be careful. Don't go too far and come back when I call you."
Tommy was very excited and ran to the park. He saw many things that he liked: a pond, a bridge, a slide, a swing. He chased a butterfly, jumped over a log, slid down the slide, and swung on the swing. He was having a great time.

After a while, his owner called him, "Tommy, come here. It's time to go home."
Tommy heard his owner and ran back to him. But when he got there, his owner looked worried.
"Tommy, where is your collar?" his owner asked.
Tommy felt his neck and realized that his collar was gone. He felt sad and scared. He did not know where his collar was. He said, "I'm sorry, I lost my collar. I was playing and I did not see it."
His owner said, "Oh, Tommy, you should have been more careful. Your collar is important. It has your name and my phone number on it. If you lose it, someone might not know who you are or where you live. You could get lost or in trouble. You have to be more responsible and pay attention to your things."
Tommy felt sorry and ashamed. He said, "I'm sorry, I was too excited and I forgot. Can we find my collar, please?"
His owner said, "We can try, but it might be hard. The park is big and there are many people and dogs. Someone might have taken it or thrown it away. But we can look for it together. Maybe we will succeed."
They went back to the park and searched for the collar. They asked other people and dogs if they had seen it. They looked under the slide, behind the log, near the pond, and on the bridge. They did not give up.
Finally, they found the collar. It was on a bench, next to a lady who was reading a book. She had seen the collar and picked it up, hoping to find the owner. She was happy to see Tommy and his owner.
She said, "Is this your collar? I found it on the ground. It's a nice collar. It has your name and your owner's phone number on it. You are a lucky dog."
Tommy and his owner thanked the lady and took the collar. Tommy was very happy and relieved. He put the collar back on his neck and felt safe and proud again.
He said, "Thank you, thank you, thank you. I'm so glad we found my collar. I'm sorry I lost it. I will be more careful next time. I will not forget."
His owner said, "You're welcome, you're welcome, you're welcome. I'm glad too. I'm proud of you for looking for it and not giving up. You learned a good lesson today. You have to be responsible and pay attention to your things. They are part of who you are and what you love. You have to respect them and take care of them."
Tommy nodded and hugged his owner. He learned a good lesson and he was happy. He still loved to run and play, but he also loved his collar and his owner. He did not want to lose them again. He was a good dog.

Andy's friends saw how hard he was working. They came to help Andy. Together, they all pushed the food to their home. They were very happy that they succeed. The other ants learned from Andy that if you are persistent and never give up, you can do anything.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to play outside. He saw a big rock and wanted to climb it. As he climbed, he saw a pretty bird in the sky. Tim wanted to say "hi" to the bird, so he tried to climb higher. But then, he started to slip. He was scared and called out for help.
A compassionate dog named Max heard Tim's call. Max ran to the rock and said, "Don't worry, Tim! I will help you!" Max jumped up and caught Tim just as he was about to fall. They both landed on the soft grass. Tim hugged Max and said, "Thank you, Max! You saved me!"
After that day, Tim and Max became best friends. They played together every day and always looked out for each other. Tim learned to be careful when climbing and Max was always there to help. They had lots of fun and were happy to have each other.

Jill was a three-year-old girl who spent her summer days playing in the park. Today she decided to go on a hunt for a special tree. She looked high and low, and found a tall, strong tree that was full of beautiful leaves. It was just what she was looking for.
Jill wanted to take a break underneath its shade, but when she reached the tree she found that it was too far away from the sun to provide any shade.
Jill sat down in disappointment and looked up at the tree. She said, "Tree, why won't you help me? I need some shade!"
The tree remained still and stubbornly refused Jill's request. Jill thought a moment and then remembered something her mom had told her. She said, "Tree, if you move one step closer to the sun, I will give you lots of hugs and kisses."
The tree hesitated, but then slowly shuffled closer to the sun. It was now providing the perfect amount of shade for Jill.
Jill smiled and hugged the tree. She said, "Thank you for helping me, tree!"


Tommy loved horses. He liked to look at pictures of horses, to play with toy horses, and to pretend he was a horse. He wished he could see a real horse someday.
One day, his mom said, "Tommy, I have a surprise for you. We are going to the farm. Do you know what you will see there?" Tommy was very excited. He guessed, "Horses?"
"Yes, horses!" his mom said. "And cows, and pigs, and chickens. Are you ready to go?" Tommy nodded and ran to get his coat and hat.
They drove to the farm and parked the car. Tommy saw a big barn and a fence. He heard some noises. He said, "Mom, can we go see the horses now?" His mom smiled and said, "Sure, let's go."
They walked to the fence and looked inside. Tommy saw a lot of animals. He saw cows, and pigs, and chickens. But he did not see any horses. He felt sad. He asked, "Mom, where are the horses?"
His mom looked around and said, "Oh, I'm sorry, Tommy. It looks like the horses are not here today. Maybe they are in another field, or maybe they are sick, or maybe they are gone. I don't know."
Tommy felt miserable. He wanted to see the horses so much. He did not care about the other animals. He started to cry. He said, "Mom, I want to see the horses. I want to see the horses."
His mom hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Tommy. I know you love horses. But we can't see them today. Maybe we can come back another day, or maybe we can find another farm, or maybe we can watch a movie about horses. Would that make you feel better?"
Tommy shook his head and said, "No, no, no. I want to see the horses. I want to see the horses." He cried louder and louder. He did not stop crying. He did not have a good day. He did not have a good surprise. He did not see the horses.

The shark swam close to the little boy, but thankfully it swam by without attacking him. The little boy swam back to shore, but even though he was safe, he was still scared.
The next day he decided to swim out farther once again. Despite the warnings of his parents, he was determined. This time he was more careful and the sea was so easy.
But then disaster struck when the shark reappeared! He had been there all along waiting and watching, and now it was mad. It was angry and shouted at the little boy before attacking him, ending the story in a bad way.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play together. One day, they went to the park with their mom and dad. They saw many things: swings, slides, flowers, birds, and dogs. They had a lot of fun.
After playing, they went to a cafe with their mom and dad. They saw many desserts: cakes, pies, cookies, and ice cream. They wanted to try them all. But their mom and dad said they could only have one dessert each. They had to choose.
Tom saw a big white cake with strawberries on top. He liked strawberries. He said, "I want this cake!" Lily saw a small brown pie with cream on top. She liked cream. She said, "I want this pie!" But then they saw a problem. There was only one cake and one pie left. And they both wanted them.
They started to argue. "I saw the cake first!" Tom said. "No, I saw the pie first!" Lily said. They did not want to share. They did not want to choose another dessert. They did not listen to their mom and dad. They made a lot of noise.
The people in the cafe were not happy. They looked at Tom and Lily with angry faces. They said, "Shh! Be quiet! Be nice!" But Tom and Lily did not care. They kept arguing.
Then, something bad happened. A big dog came into the cafe. He saw the cake and the pie. He liked them too. He ran to the table where Tom and Lily were. He jumped on the table. He ate the cake and the pie. He made a big mess.
Tom and Lily were shocked. They saw their desserts gone. They saw the dog licking his lips. They saw their mom and dad shaking their heads. They felt sad and sorry.
They learned a lesson. They learned that being greedy and selfish is not good. They learned that sharing and caring is better. They learned that desserts are not as important as family and friends. They said sorry to each other and to their mom and dad. They hugged and smiled.
The end.


Ben and Lily are twins. They like to play and laugh. They are jolly children. One day, they go to the park with Mom and Dad. They see a big slide and a swing. They run to the slide and take turns to slide down. Whee!
"Look, Ben, a clown!" Lily says. She points to a man with a red nose and a funny hat. He is making jokes and balloons for the children. Ben and Lily go to see him. He gives them each a balloon. Lily gets a pink flower and Ben gets a green frog.
"Hello, little ones. Do you like jokes?" the clown asks. He smiles and winks.
"Yes, we do!" Ben and Lily say.
"OK, then. Here is a joke for you. What do you get when you cross a frog and a flower?" the clown says.
Ben and Lily think hard. They shake their heads.
"I don't know," Lily says.
"Me neither," Ben says.
The clown laughs. "You get a hoppy bouquet!" he says. He makes a sound like a frog. "Ribbit, ribbit!"
Ben and Lily giggle. They think the joke is funny. They clap their hands.
"That's a good joke!" Ben says.
"Thank you, clown!" Lily says.
"You're welcome, little ones. Enjoy your balloons. And remember, always be jolly!" the clown says. He waves and walks away.
Ben and Lily hug their balloons. They are happy. They go back to Mom and Dad. They tell them about the joke and the clown. Mom and Dad smile and hug them.
"Are you hungry, Ben and Lily?" Mom asks.
"Yes, we are!" Ben and Lily say.
"Good. Let's go and eat some sandwiches and cookies. Then we can play some more," Dad says.
Ben and Lily nod. They follow Mom and Dad. They hold their balloons. They are jolly children. They like to play and laugh. They like jokes and clowns. They like to eat sandwiches and cookies. They like the park. They like Mom and Dad. They like each other. They are happy. The end.


Lily and Max were playing in the park. They saw a man with a big bag of lollipops. He was giving them to the children who answered his questions.
"Can I have a lollipop, please?" Lily asked the man.
"Sure, but you have to answer a question first. What is the name of this animal?" The man showed Lily a picture of a dog.
"That's easy. It's a dog!" Lily said.
"Very good. Here is your lollipop." The man gave Lily a red lollipop.
Max wanted a lollipop too. He ran to the man and said, "Me too, me too!"
"Okay, what is the name of this animal?" The man showed Max a picture of a cat.
Max did not know. He did not like cats. He said, "I don't know. I don't care. Just give me a lollipop!"
The man shook his head. "No, you have to answer the question. If you don't know, you can guess."
Max was angry. He did not want to guess. He wanted a lollipop now. He tried to grab the bag from the man.
"Hey, stop that! That's not nice!" The man said.
Lily saw Max being rude. She felt sorry for the man. She said, "Max, don't do that. That's not how you get a lollipop. You have to answer the question. It's a cat. See, it has whiskers and a tail."
Max did not listen. He pulled harder on the bag. The bag ripped open. Lollipops fell on the ground.
"Oh no! Look what you did!" The man said.
Lily and Max looked at the lollipops. They were dirty and sticky. They could not eat them.
They felt bad. They said, "We're sorry, mister. We're sorry we broke your bag and wasted your lollipops."
The man was sad. He said, "It's okay. I forgive you. But you have to learn to be polite and patient. Lollipops are not more important than being kind."
Lily and Max nodded. They said, "We understand. We will be better next time."
The man smiled. He said, "That's good. Here, I have one more lollipop left. You can share it."
He gave them a blue lollipop. Lily and Max broke it in half. They said, "Thank you, mister. Thank you for being nice to us."
They ate their lollipop together. They learned their lesson. They were happy.


Ben and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big cake on a table. It looks tasty.
"Wow, look at that cake!" Ben says. "Can we have some?"
"I don't know," Mia says. "Maybe it is for someone's birthday."
They go closer to the table. They see a sign that says: "Happy Birthday, Lily!"
"Who is Lily?" Ben asks.
"I don't know," Mia says. "Maybe she is a girl who plays here."
They look around. They do not see any girl or anyone else. They see the cake. It has pink frosting and sprinkles.
"It looks so tasty," Ben says. "I want to try it."
"Me too," Mia says. "But we should not take it. It is not ours."
They think for a moment. Then they have an idea.
"Maybe we can just have a little bit," Ben says. "We can use our toes."
"Our toes?" Mia asks.
"Yes, our toes," Ben says. "We can take off our shoes and socks. We can dip our toes in the cake. No one will notice."
Mia thinks it is a funny idea. She agrees.
They take off their shoes and socks. They sneak to the table. They dip their toes in the cake. It feels soft and sticky. They lick their toes. It tastes sweet and yummy.
They giggle and smile. They dip their toes again. They lick their toes again.
They do not see the woman who comes to the table. She is Lily's mom. She is angry.
"Hey, what are you doing?" she yells. "That is my daughter's cake! You are ruining it with your toes!"
Ben and Mia are scared. They drop their toes. They put on their shoes and socks. They run away.
They do not talk to each other. They feel bad. They know they did something wrong. They wish they did not touch the cake. They wish they said sorry to Lily's mom. They wish they had a tasty cake of their own.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Kelly. She was playing bow and arrow with her best friend, Todd. Todd had a great big arrow that went very far and Kelly was very impressed. She asked if she could try it.
Todd handed the arrow to Kelly, but then he forgot to tell her how to use it. Kelly was embarrassed and put the arrow down on the ground.
Todd saw Kelly feeling silly and said, "I'm sorry! I forgot to tell you how it works. Here, let me show you how to do it. Put the arrow on your bow like this, then pull back and let go."
Kelly tried it and was amazed by how far the arrow flew. She smiled and said, "Thanks for teaching me how to use it Todd! Let's play again!"


Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a bird with a broken wing. The bird could not fly. It was sad. One day, a kind rabbit saw the bird and said, "I will help you."
The rabbit went to find help. It met an unknown bug who could perform magic. The bug said, "I can help the bird, but I need something in return." The rabbit agreed to the deal.
The unknown bug performed magic on the bird's wing. The bird could fly again. But the rabbit had to give the bug all its food. The rabbit was hungry and sad. The bird flew away, and the rabbit was left with nothing.


Sara and Ben like to play in the park. They have a big box of toys. They have cars, dolls, balls, and books. But their favorite toy is a dragon. The dragon is green and soft. It has wings, horns, and a long tail.
One day, a new boy comes to the park. His name is Max. He sees Sara and Ben playing with the dragon. He wants to play too. He runs to them and grabs the dragon.
"Hey, that's mine!" Sara says. She tries to pull the dragon back.
"No, it's mine now!" Max says. He holds the dragon tight.
"Stop it, you're hurting him!" Ben says. He stares at Max with angry eyes.
Max stares back. He does not care. He likes the dragon. He thinks it is cool.
Sara and Ben are sad and mad. They want their dragon back. They do not like Max. They think he is mean.
Then, they hear a voice. It is the dragon. He speaks in a low and gentle voice.
"Please, let me go. I do not like to be squeezed. I am delicate. I want to be with Sara and Ben. They are my friends. They take good care of me."
Max is surprised. He did not know the dragon can talk. He feels sorry. He realizes he was wrong. He lets go of the dragon.
"I'm sorry, dragon. I'm sorry, Sara and Ben. I was rude. Can I play with you?" Max says.
Sara and Ben look at the dragon. The dragon nods. He smiles.
"Okay, you can play with us. But you have to be nice. And you have to share. The dragon is not only yours. He is ours." Sara says.
Max agrees. He says he will be nice and share. He apologizes again. Sara and Ben forgive him. They all play together. They have fun. The dragon is happy. He has more friends.


The sun was hot and bright as Bob walked up the stairs to reach the attic. He was feeling excited, as he had never been there before. He looked around and saw so many delicious looking things.
Bob saw a sign that said "Do not eat any of these things", so he knew he had to be careful. Bob heard a noise and saw his dad standing in the corner of the attic.
"Dad, what are all of these delicious things? Can I have some?" Bob asked.
His dad smiled and said, "No Bob, you cannot. Nothing in this attic is for you."
Bob was disappointed, but he still smiled. His dad patted his head and said, "It's OK, I'll encourage you with something else. How about a cool glass of juice? That's much better!"
Bob smiled and hugged his Dad. But as soon as Bob hugged his Dad, he noticed his Dad's smile fading away. Bob looked down and saw that the delicious things in the attic were all over the floor.
Bob's dad was mad and he scolded him for not listening. Bob was sad, but he knew he deserved it. He realized that he should have listened to Dad and not been tempted by the delicious food in the attic.

When it was Lily's turn, she went inside with her mom. The doctor was very nice. He asked Lily to count her fingers and toes. Lily counted, "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!" The doctor was happy. Lily was a smart girl. She knew how to count, even at the patient place with noisy kids around.

One day, as Tim was walking down the street, he saw a cat. The cat was so cute and fluffy. Tim wanted to say hi, but he started to tremble. He was scared the cat would not like him.
Tim took a deep breath and said, "Hi, I am Tim the potato. Will you be my friend?" The cat looked at Tim and smiled. "Of course, Tim! I am Cat. I like you, even if you tremble." They became best friends and played all day long. From that day on, Tim learned that it was okay to tremble, because true friends will like you just the way you are.


Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tree with many green needles. Lily says, "What is this tree?"
Tom says, "This is a pine tree. My dad told me. He knows a lot of things."
Lily says, "Can we touch it?"
Tom says, "Yes, but be careful. The needles are sharp. They can hurt you."
They go closer to the pine tree. They touch the needles gently. They smell the pine tree. It smells good. They see a brown cone hanging from a branch. Lily says, "What is this?"
Tom says, "This is a pine cone. It has seeds inside. The birds and squirrels like to eat them."
Lily says, "Can we take it?"
Tom says, "No, we should leave it for the animals. They need it more than we do."
They hear a loud noise. They turn around. They see a man running and shouting. He has a red hat and a yellow coat. He looks crazy. He says, "I am the king of the pine trees! Bow to me!"
Tom and Lily are scared. They run away from the man. They find their moms. They tell them what they saw. Their moms hug them. They say, "Don't worry. He is just a silly man. He is not the king of anything. You are safe with us."
Tom and Lily are glad. They say, "We like pine trees. But we don't like crazy men."

Ben and Lily liked to play in the garden. They had a small house made of wood and a swing and a slide. They also had a big dog named Max who liked to run and bark.
One day, they saw a hole in the wall of their house. They were sad because they liked their house very much. They decided to repair it with some sticks and mud.
"Let's fix our house, Lily," Ben said. "We can use these sticks and this mud."
"OK, Ben," Lily said. "But we have to be careful. Max might knock it down again."
They worked hard to fill the hole with sticks and mud. They were happy when they finished. They went inside their house and pretended to have tea and cookies.
But they did not see that someone was watching them. It was Mrs. Jones, their nosy neighbor. She did not like children or dogs. She thought they were noisy and messy. She always complained to their parents.
She saw the hole in the wall and the sticks and mud. She was angry. She thought they had ruined the garden. She decided to tell their parents.
She walked to their house and knocked on the door. She waited for their parents to come out.
But before they did, Max saw her. He did not like her either. He ran out of the garden and barked at her. He jumped on her and licked her face.
She screamed and tried to push him away. She dropped her purse and her glasses. She fell on the ground and got mud on her dress.
Ben and Lily heard the noise and came out of their house. They saw Mrs. Jones and Max. They were scared. They did not want her to be mad at them.
They ran to her and tried to help her. They said they were sorry.
"Sorry, Mrs. Jones," Ben said. "We did not mean to make you angry. We were just repairing our house."
"Sorry, Mrs. Jones," Lily said. "We did not mean to make you dirty. We were just playing in the garden."
Mrs. Jones looked at them. She saw their innocent faces and their dirty hands. She felt a little sorry for them. She realized they were just children having fun.
She sighed and smiled. She said she was not angry. She said she was sorry too.
"Sorry, Ben and Lily," Mrs. Jones said. "I was too nosy. I should have let you play in peace. Your house is very nice. And your dog is very friendly."
She got up and dusted herself off. She picked up her purse and her glasses. She said goodbye to them and walked away.
Ben and Lily waved at her. They were happy. They hugged Max and thanked him. They went back to their house and played some more.
