Once upon a time, there was a little duckling named Dilly. Dilly loved to explore the pond and the meadow nearby. Just as Dilly finished exploring the meadow, he found a shiny, round wheel. He was curious to know what it was, so he decided to take it with him.
When Dilly returned to the pond, he saw his elder duck, Mr. Quack. He asked him what the wheel was. Mr. Quack said, "Young duckling, this wheel is harmless. It can help turn many things."
Dilly asked, "But why can't I keep this wheel?"
Mr. Quack replied, "Young one, it does not belong to you. It is important to always return things that do not belong to us."
Dilly felt a little sad, but he remembered the advice given by Mr. Quack and returned the wheel to where he had found it. Whenever Dilly found something that did not belong to him, he would do the same. He learned a valuable lesson: to be honest and always respect other people's belongings.

Her mom replied, "They are going to get food for their babies."
Jane was curious and questioned, "What do they eat?"
Her mom answered, "They eat little insects and seeds. Now go get dressed, it's a new day."
Jane smiled and quickly put on her clothes. She skipped outside and picked a bright flower.
She admired the light color and asked her mom, "What kind of flower is this?"
Her mom smiled and answered, "That is a daffodil."
Jane was happy and cheered. She twirled around in the morning light and shouted, "Today is a beautiful day!"

Lily heard Tim and ran to him. She hugged him and comforted him. She was glad and relieved.
"Are you okay?" she asked.
"Yes, I'm okay," Tim said. "But I was wrong. You were right. The hole was dangerous. There was a rat. It was scary and mean."
"I'm sorry you saw a rat," Lily said. "But I'm happy you are safe. Next time, let's stay away from holes. They are not fun. They are trouble."
Tim nodded and agreed. He learned his lesson. He thanked Lily for being his friend. They decided to play somewhere else. They found a sandbox and a ball. They had fun and forgot about the rat.

One day, a lion was very hungry. He saw a zebra near a lake and wanted to eat it. He ran fast and jumped on the zebra. But the zebra was not weak. He kicked the lion with his legs and ran away. The lion was hurt and angry.
He saw a monkey on a tree and wanted to eat it. He climbed the tree and tried to catch the monkey. But the monkey was not weak. He threw a banana at the lion and swung to another tree. The lion fell down and was more hurt and angry.
He saw a turtle on the grass and wanted to eat it. He walked slowly and bit the turtle. But the turtle was not weak. He hid in his shell and the lion could not open it. The lion was very hurt and very angry.
He saw a mouse on a rock and wanted to eat it. He crawled to the mouse and opened his mouth. But the mouse was not afraid. He said to the lion, "Why are you so mean? You are big and strong, but you are not happy. You should be kind and share with others. Then you will have friends and be happy."
The lion was surprised. He said, "But I am hungry and you are small and weak. I can eat you easily."
The mouse said, "Maybe you can, but you should not. You should accept what you have and be grateful. Look, there is a staff of honey on that bush. You can eat that and be sweet. And I can help you with your wounds and be your friend."
The lion thought for a moment. He said, "You are right. I have been greedy and rude. I am sorry. I will accept the staff of honey and be sweet. And I will be your friend and be kind."
The mouse smiled and said, "That is good. Come, I will show you the staff of honey and help you with your wounds."
The lion and the mouse walked together to the bush. They ate the staff of honey and licked each other's wounds. They became friends and were happy.
The moral of the story is: You should accept what you have and be grateful. You should be kind and share with others. Then you will have friends and be happy.

One day, a wise cat named Wednesday went for a walk. She saw a big tree and wanted to climb it. Up she went, higher and higher, until she reached the top. She looked around and saw her friend, a little bird, sitting on a branch.
"Hi, bird!" said Wednesday. "What are you doing up here?" The bird looked at her and said, "I am looking for water to drink. I am very thirsty." Wednesday thought for a moment and said, "I can help you find water."
Just then, something unexpected happened. A big cloud came and started to spray water on them. They were both surprised, but happy because the bird could now drink the water. They laughed and played in the rain, enjoying the cool water.
Soon, the rain stopped, and they climbed down the tree. They were both very wet but very happy. "Thank you, Wednesday," said the bird. "You are a very wise and good friend." Wednesday smiled and said, "You're welcome, bird. I am always here to help you." And they both went on their way, knowing they would always be friends.


One day, a large cat put on a costume. The costume was very funny. The cat looked like a big, big bird. The cat went for a walk in the park. The cat saw a little girl and wanted to play with her.
The little girl saw the cat and did not know it was a cat. She thought it was a big bird. The girl was happy to play with the big bird. They played and laughed together. The cat blinked its eyes and the girl blinked back.
Then, something unexpected happened. The costume fell off the cat. The little girl was surprised. She did not know it was a cat all this time. The cat was happy too. Now, they could play together without the costume. They played and laughed more, and the cat and the girl became best friends.


Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play together. But sometimes they also liked to poke each other and make each other angry. One Sunday, they were playing with their blocks in the living room. Anna wanted to build a tall tower, but Ben wanted to knock it down.
"Stop it, Ben!" Anna said. "I want to make a tower!"
"No, I want to make a crash!" Ben said. He poked Anna's tower with his finger and it fell down.
Anna was frustrated. She poked Ben back and he cried. "Mommy, Anna poked me!" he shouted.
Mommy came from the kitchen and saw the mess. She was not happy. She picked up Ben and hugged him. Then she looked at Anna and said, "Anna, why did you poke your brother?"
"Because he poked my tower!" Anna said.
Mommy sighed. She put Ben down and said, "Both of you, listen to me. Poking is not nice. It hurts and it makes people sad. You need to share your toys and play nicely. Do you understand?"
Anna and Ben nodded. They said they were sorry to each other and hugged. Then they decided to build a tower together, without poking. Mommy smiled and gave them a kiss. She was glad they were friends again.


Once upon a time, there was an intelligent dog named Max. Max lived in a small house with his friend, a girl named Lily. They loved to play and have fun together. Max was very good at finding things, and Lily liked to measure things with her ruler.
One day, Max and Lily went to the park to play. They played catch with a ball and had lots of fun. But as the day went on, it started to get dark. Max and Lily knew it was time to go home, but they couldn't find their way back.
Max used his intelligent nose to sniff the ground and find their way. Lily used her ruler to measure how far they had walked. Together, they found their way back home, just before it got too dark. Max and Lily were so happy to be safe and sound in their small house.
The moral of the story is that working together can help us find our way through difficult situations.

"Hi, Ella!" said Bob. "Why are you so confused?"
"I can't find my home," said Ella. "Will you help me?"
Bob thought for a moment and then said, "Yes, I will help you find your home."
Bob and Ella walked and walked. They saw a big tree. "Is that your home?" asked Bob.
"No," said Ella. "Let's keep looking."
They walked some more and found a big lake. "Is that your home?" asked Bob.
"No," said Ella. "But thank you for helping me."
Finally, they found a big field with other elephants. Ella was so happy! "This is my home!" she said. "Thank you, Bob!"
Ella and Bob became best friends. They played together every day. And Ella was never confused again.

"What do you need, little ones?" the man says.

"Sure, I can try. But you have to be careful. The balloon might pop," he says.
He puts his ladder under the balloon. He climbs up. He reaches for the balloon. He grabs it. He comes down.
"Here you go, kids. The blue balloon is yours," he says.
He gives the balloon to Anna and Ben. They are very happy. They thank the man.
"Thank you, sir, you are very nice!" Anna says.
"Yes, thank you, sir, you are very kind!" Ben says.
They hug the balloon. They play with it. They are very careful. They do not want the balloon to pop. They have a lot of fun. They are glad that the blue balloon happened to be in the sky. It is very pretty.

Sara and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to gather flowers and leaves and make pretend spells. They had a big pot and a wooden spoon. They put the flowers and leaves in the pot and stirred them with the spoon. They said funny words like "abracadabra" and "hocus pocus".
But Tom, the boy next door, did not like their game. He thought it was dull and silly. He wanted to play with his ball and his bike. He came over to the fence and shouted at Sara and Ben.
"Stop playing with that rubbish! You are not real witches or wizards. You are just babies. Come and play with me. I have a cool ball and a fast bike. They are much more fun than your stupid pot and spoon."
Sara and Ben felt sad and angry. They liked their game. They did not want to play with Tom's ball and bike. They thought they were boring and loud. They told Tom to go away and leave them alone.
But Tom did not listen. He climbed over the fence and ran to their pot. He kicked it over and spilled their flowers and leaves. He laughed and said, "There, I broke your spell. Now you have to play with me."
Sara and Ben cried. They were very upset. They had worked hard to gather their flowers and leaves. They had made a beautiful spell. They did not like Tom. He was mean and rude. They wished he would disappear.

Sara and Ben stopped crying. They looked at each other and smiled. They realized that their spell had worked after all. They had turned Tom into a frog. They felt happy and proud. They picked up their pot and spoon and went to find more flowers and leaves. They decided to make more spells and have more fun. They did not care about Tom's ball and bike. They left him in the garden, hopping and croaking. They hoped he would learn his lesson.

One day, a big alligator was in a pond. He was calm and liked to swim. He had many friends in the pond, like fish and frogs. They all played together and had fun.
A little duck got stuck in the pond. The duck was scared and called for help. "Help me, please!" said the little duck. The alligator heard the duck and wanted to rescue him.
The calm alligator swam to the duck. "Don't be scared. I will help you," said the alligator. The alligator used his strong tail to push the duck out of the pond. The duck was happy and thanked the alligator.
The alligator and the duck became good friends. They played in the pond with the fish and frogs. Everyone was happy and safe. The calm alligator was a hero to all his friends.


Once upon a time, a hungry cat named Tom saw a big tree. In the tree, he saw a bird. Tom wanted to catch the bird. He saw a ladder near the tree. Tom was happy and thought he could use the ladder to get the bird.
Tom put the ladder on the tree and climbed up. The bird saw Tom coming and flew away. Tom was sad. He looked around and saw another bird. Tom tried to catch it, but the bird flew away too.
Tom did not recognize that the ladder was not safe. It started to shake. Tom was scared. The ladder fell down with Tom. Tom fell on the ground and got hurt. He did not catch any bird and was still hungry.


John was hiking in the mountains when he came across a giant fire. He looked around and noticed that the fire was very tight, as if somebody had made it that way on purpose.
John thought it was strange, so he decided to test it to see what would happen. He reached for a rock and threw it into the fire. The rock quickly disappeared under the flames and the fire danced higher.
John was very surprised and stepped closer to the fire. He heard a voice from behind him. It was a gentle voice.
"Don't be scared, John," the voice said. "I made the fire tight so it doesn't get out of hand. I'm testing it to make sure it's doing its job."
John looked around, but he couldn't find the voice's owner. He thanked the voice for being friendly and continued on his hike.

As Mia played, she saw something in the water. It seemed to be moving in a funny way. Mia looked closer and saw a mysterious dolphin. The dolphin was jumping in and out of the water, making big splashes. Mia thought the dolphin was playing a game with her.
Mia waved at the mysterious dolphin and it waved back with its tail. They played together all day, splashing in the water and having fun. When it was time to go home, Mia said goodbye to her new dolphin friend. She knew she would always remember the fun day she had at the beach with the mysterious dolphin.


Once upon a time, there was a big, clumsy bear named Bobo. Bobo lived in a small cave near the woods. He loved to play with his friends, the birds and the rabbits.
One day, Bobo saw some smoke coming from the woods. He was scared and wanted to help. He ran to the woods and saw a little fire. Bobo's friend, a small bird named Chirpy, was flying around the fire. "Help me, Bobo!" Chirpy said. "I can't put out the fire!"
Bobo knew what to do. He found a big rock near the fire. He pushed the rock with all his strength, and it rolled over the fire. The fire went out, and the smoke disappeared. Chirpy was so happy and said, "Thank you, Bobo! You saved the woods!"
From that day on, Bobo and Chirpy became the best of friends. They played together every day, and the other animals in the woods knew that Bobo was not just a clumsy bear, but a hero too.

Mommy and her son looked at the sculpture every day and remembered their visit to the park. They also said a special prayer for all the junk and for all the happy times.

Lucy ran to her mommy and told her what happened. Mommy said, "It's okay, Lucy. We can fix it." They went to the living room and saw the wrap had a small cut. Mommy took out some tape and fixed the cut on the wrap. Lucy said, "Thank you, mommy! I won't be naughty again."
From that day on, Lucy played with her ball outside and never broke anything in the house again. And when she saw a pretty wrap, she remembered to be a good girl.

Once upon a time there was a tall tiger. One day, it had a big problem to solve. So it started walking around looking for help.
It came across a small mouse and asked him, "Mouse, can you help me solve my problem?"
The mouse said, "I'm very small, I don't know if I can help."
The tiger said, "Please try, it's very important!"
So the mouse thought and thought and finally said, "I think I have the answer! You can go to the top of the tall hill, and look down. Then you can see the answer!"
The tiger thanked the mouse and said, "you are very smart!"
So the tiger climbed the tall hill and, sure enough, he solved the problem. After that, the tiger and the mouse became good friends.


Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big white dog. The dog is friendly. He wags his tail and licks their faces.
"Can we pet him?" Sara asks.
"Yes, he is nice. His name is Spot," a man says. He is the dog's owner.
Sara and Tom pet Spot. They rub his ears and his belly. Spot is happy. He barks and jumps.
"Can we play with him?" Tom asks.
"Sure, you can. He likes to fetch and run," the man says. He gives them a ball.
Sara and Tom throw the ball. Spot runs and catches it. He brings it back. They do this many times.
But then, Spot sees a squirrel. He drops the ball and chases the squirrel. He runs very fast.
"Spot, come back!" the man calls.
But Spot does not listen. He wants to catch the squirrel.
"Spot, stop!" Sara and Tom shout.
But Spot does not stop. He runs out of the park. He crosses the street.
"Spot, no!" the man yells.
But Spot does not hear. He is too busy.
A car is coming. It is big and loud. It honks its horn.
"Spot, look out!" Sara and Tom scream.
But Spot does not look. He is too excited.
The car brakes. It skids. It stops.
Spot is safe. He is not hurt. He is lucky.
The man runs to Spot. He hugs him. He scolds him.
"Spot, you are a bad dog. You could have been hit by the car. You could have died. You must never run away like that. You must listen to me. Do you understand?" the man says.
Spot looks at the man. He looks sorry. He wags his tail. He licks his face.
"I'm sorry, Spot. I love you. But you have to be careful. You have to obey me. OK?" the man says.
Spot nods. He barks. He agrees.
Sara and Tom run to Spot. They hug him. They are glad he is OK.
"Spot, you are a good dog. But you are also a silly dog. You scared us. You made us worry. You have to be smart. You have to stay with us. OK?" Sara and Tom say.
Spot nods. He barks. He agrees.
They all go back to the park. They play with the ball. They have fun.
Spot does not chase squirrels. He does not run away. He does not refuse to listen.
He stays with his friends. He is a happy dog.

At home, the little boy read a book to the smooth rock. The smooth rock liked the story. It felt happy to listen to the little boy.
The next day, the little boy took the smooth rock back to its group. The smooth rock told the other rocks about the story. They all wanted to hear it too. So, the little boy read the story to the group of rocks. They all had fun together.


Once upon a time, there was a little horse named Max. Max lived on a farm with many animals. Max loved to play and run in the fields. He was a very calm horse and liked to make friends with everyone.
One day, Max saw a big rock in the field. He wanted to jump over it. Max took a few steps back and then sprang high into the air. He jumped over the rock and landed safely on the other side. All the animals clapped and cheered for Max.
Max felt so happy that he could help his friends. He learned that being calm and trying new things can make everyone happy. And from that day on, Max and his friends played together all the time, and they all lived happily ever after. The moral of the story is to always be calm and try new things, because it can bring happiness to you and others around you.


Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a little monkey named Momo. Momo loved to play and swing on the flexible vines all day. He had many friends, like the birds, the bugs, and the other animals in the forest.
One sunny day, Momo saw a big bird send a little bird away. The little bird was sad and could not play with the others. Momo felt bad and wanted to help the little bird. He thought of a plan to make the little bird happy again.
Momo climbed up the tree and found a long, flexible vine. He held the vine and swung to the little bird. Momo said, "Come, little bird! Swing with me on this vine, and we will have fun together!" The little bird was so happy and joined Momo. They played and laughed all day long.
The big bird saw Momo and the little bird having fun. The big bird felt sorry for sending the little bird away. The big bird flew down and said, "I am sorry, little bird. I want to play with you too." The little bird forgave the big bird, and they all played together.
The moral of the story is to be kind and include everyone in our play. When we are nice to others, we can have more fun and make more friends.


One day, a happy leaf fell from a tree. The wind blew it far away. The leaf met a small bug. The bug said, "Hi, I am Bug. You look nice."
The happy leaf said, "Thank you, Bug. I like the wind. It makes me dance."
Bug and the leaf played all day. They had lots of fun. But then, the leaf started to rot. It turned brown and soft. Bug was sad.
The leaf said, "Don't be sad, Bug. It is okay. I will turn into food for the ground."
Bug smiled and said, "You are a good friend, Leaf. I will miss you." The wind blew the leaf away and Bug waved goodbye.

Once upon a time, there was a clever dog named Spot. Spot loved to play in the mud. One day, he played in the mud all day long. When he got home, he was very dirty.
Spot's mom said, "Spot, you need to bathe. You are too dirty!" Spot did not like to bathe, but he knew his mom was right. So, he went to the bathroom and started the water. The warm water felt nice on his fur.
As Spot washed, he made a fun motion with his paws to make the water splash. He laughed and said, "Look, Mom! I am making a big splash!" Spot's mom smiled and said, "Good job, Spot! Now you are clean and clever again." And they lived happily ever after.


One day, a little boy named Tim found a magazine on the floor. He picked it up and saw a picture of a man whistling. Tim wanted to whistle too, so he tried to make the same sound. He blew air out of his mouth, but no sound came out. Tim felt sad that he couldn't whistle.
Tim's big sister, Lily, saw him looking sad and asked what was wrong. Tim showed her the magazine and told her he wanted to whistle like the man in the picture. Lily smiled and said she could teach him how to whistle. Tim felt happy and excited to learn.
Lily showed Tim how to put his lips together and blow air gently. Tim tried again and this time, he made a small whistling sound. He felt so happy and proud of himself. He looked at Lily and said, "Thank you for helping me." Lily felt a little guilty because she knew she should have helped him sooner, but she was happy that Tim could now whistle. They both laughed and whistled together, making music with their new skill.


Once upon a time, there was a big red bus. The bus was very uncomfortable. People did not like to sit on the bus. One day, the bus wanted to make people laugh. The bus thought, "If I make people laugh, they will not feel uncomfortable."
The bus tried to be funny. It made funny noises and danced. The bus was very good at dancing. The people laughed and laughed. They forgot about the uncomfortable seats. They were happy on the bus.
But then, the bus danced too much. It danced so hard that it broke. The people stopped laughing. They were sad because the bus could not take them home. The bus was also sad. It just wanted to make people happy, but now it could not help the people at all.


Tom was a tall boy who liked to play with his ball. He would throw it high in the air and catch it in his palm. He was very good at it and he was proud of himself. He did not like to share his ball with anyone. He would say, "This is my ball, go away!"
One day, he went to the park with his ball. He saw a little girl who was sitting on a bench. She had no toys and she looked sad. Tom thought she was boring and he did not want to play with her. He threw his ball high in the air and said, "Look at me, I am so good!"
The little girl looked at him and smiled. She said, "Can I play with you? Your ball looks fun." Tom did not like her smile. He said, "No, you can't. This is my ball, go away!" He threw his ball again, but this time, he threw it too far. It went over the fence and into the street.
Tom ran after his ball. He did not look both ways. He did not see the big car that was coming fast. The car hit him and he fell down. He was hurt and he cried. He dropped his ball and it rolled away. The little girl saw what happened and she ran to help him. She called for help and she held his hand. She said, "I am sorry, I hope you are okay."
Tom felt sorry too. He wished he had been nice to the little girl. He wished he had shared his ball with her. He learned that being selfish and rude is not good. He learned that being kind and friendly is better. He said, "Thank you, you are a good friend. Can I play with you?" The little girl said, "Yes, you can. But first, we have to go to the doctor. Come on, let's go."
The end.
Moral value: Sharing is caring. Be kind to others. Look both ways before crossing the street.


Once there was a bunny named Benny. He was very small, but he had very big ideas. He wanted to explore the world, so one day he hopped off into the forest.
As he hopped, he saw lots of things. He saw flowers, trees, and other animals. He saw a big, heavy diary lying by the side of the path. It was so heavy that he couldn't lift it, but he opened it and wrote down all the things he had seen.
When he finished, he kept hopping. He saw more and more things, wrote them down in the diary, and hopped some more. He kept exploring and hopping, until he reached the far side of the forest. He closed the diary, tucked it beneath his arm, and hopped back home.
When he arrived, he showed his diary to all his friends. He was so proud of all he had seen and written down. He had explored the world, and he knew he could go anywhere. Because his little hops had taken him everywhere he wanted to go.


Once there was a little girl named Lucy who always wanted to escape the house. She was very jealous of her brother who seemed to be able to do anything. She saw her brother playing outside and so she asked her mom if she could join him.
"No, Lucy," said her mom, "It's too dangerous for you outside." Lucy's stomach sank, as she had wanted to escape so badly.
Later, Lucy was playing in her bedroom when she saw a switch on the wall. She pressed the switch and suddenly the wall opened wide. To her surprise, a secret passageway was revealed!
Lucy excitedly ran down the passageway and came out in the backyard. While she was playing with her brother, she saw her mom watching them from the window, and noticed a smile on her face.
Lucy knew then that her mom had wanted her to escape the house all along. She felt so happy and proud!

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a rare, beautiful sunset. Everyone loved to see it. A little boy named Tim wanted to see it too. He asked his mom, "Can I see the rare sunset?" His mom said, "Yes, but you must be home before dark."

Mira and Ravi were friends who liked to play in the garden. One day, they found a big melon on a vine. It was green and round and smelled sweet.
"Let's take it home and eat it!" Mira said.
"But how will we carry it?" Ravi asked. "It is too big for our hands."
Mira had an idea. She ran to the shed and brought a wheelbarrow. She put the melon in the wheelbarrow and pushed it. Ravi helped her.
They were very happy and proud of their melon. They met a lady on the way. She smiled and said, "What a nice melon you have! Where did you get it?"
"We found it in the garden," Mira said. "It is ours."
The lady nodded. She said, "It is a very big melon. Do you think it will fit in your house?"
Mira and Ravi looked at each other. They had not thought of that. They wondered if the melon would fit through the door or the window. They felt a little worried.
The lady saw their faces. She said, "Don't worry, children. I have a knife and a bowl. I can help you cut the melon and share it with me. Then you can take some pieces home and eat them."
Mira and Ravi liked the idea. They thanked the lady and followed her to her house. She cut the melon and gave them each a big slice. It was juicy and sweet. They ate it and felt happy.
The lady said, "You are very humble and kind, children. You are willing to share your melon with me. I am glad to have met you."
Mira and Ravi smiled. They said, "You are very nice and helpful, lady. You are our friend."
They hugged the lady and took some melon pieces home. They learned that sometimes things don't fit, but that's okay. They can still enjoy them and share them with others.

One day, an elderly lawyer was walking down the street when he saw a three year old child who had a problem. The lawyer asked the little boy what was wrong and the boy said, "I have a question and I don't know who to ask." The lawyer decided to answer the question for the boy.
The boy asked, "What is a lawyer?" The lawyer replied with a smile, "A lawyer is someone who helps people understand the laws and figure out what to do when the laws are broken."
The lawyer then asked the boy what his name was. The little boy said, "My name is John." The lawyer smiled and told John that he was happy to help.
John thanked the elderly lawyer for his help and the lawyer went on his way. This was a special moment for the lawyer, because he had given a three year old a valuable answer. He felt he had done a good deed for the day.


Once upon a time, there was a blue village. In the village, a young boy and girl lived together with their parents.
One night, the young boy heard a strange noise outside in the moonlight. He asked his parents what it was, but they could not explain.
The next day, the boy asked the other villagers, but they had no reply. So the boy decided to investigate for himself. He went out into the night and followed the noise.
The noise came from a figure in the shadows who said: "Come closer, brave boy."
The boy asked: "What do you want?"
The figure replied: "Give me your parents and I will give you a new life."
The boy thought carefully, but replied, "No."
The figure was angry and cursed the village. Fire and smoke filled the sky and destroyed the blue village forever. The boy and his parents were never seen again.


Lily and Ben were playing in the backyard. They liked to run, jump and swing on the big tree. They saw their dad cooking on the grill. He was making hot dogs and corn for lunch.
"Can we have some, dad?" Lily asked.
"Sure, sweetie. They are almost ready. Just wash your hands first," dad said.
Lily and Ben ran to the sink and washed their hands. They smelled the yummy food and their tummies growled. They sat at the table and waited for dad to bring the plates.
"Here you go, kids. Enjoy your lunch," dad said. He gave them each a hot dog, a corn and a glass of lemonade.
Lily and Ben took big bites of their hot dogs. They were hot and juicy. They liked the ketchup and mustard on them. They also nibbled on their corn. They were sweet and crunchy. They liked the butter and salt on them.
They drank their lemonade. It was cold and sour. They made funny faces and giggled.
"Dad, why is the lemonade sour?" Ben asked.
"Because it has lemons in it, buddy. Lemons are sour fruits. But they are good for you. They have vitamin C," dad explained.
"Oh, I see. I like lemons, but they make my mouth pucker," Ben said.
Lily and Ben finished their lunch. They thanked their dad and gave him a hug. They were full and happy.
"Dad, can we play some more?" Lily asked.
"Sure, honey. But don't forget to take a nap later. You need to sleep and rest your body and mind," dad said.
"OK, dad. We will sleep after we play," Lily said.
Lily and Ben ran back to the backyard. They played some more until they felt tired. They went to their room and lay down on their beds. They closed their eyes and fell asleep. They dreamed of hot dogs, corn and lemons.


Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a little girl named Lily. Lily loved her pink umbrella. She took it everywhere she went, even when the sun was shining bright. Lily's friends would laugh and say, "Why do you have an umbrella when there is no rain?"
One day, Lily was playing outside with her friends. The sun was shining high in the sky. Lily had her pink umbrella with her. She opened it and held it above her head. Her friends asked, "Why do you have your umbrella now? It's not raining!"
Lily smiled and said, "Watch!" She held her umbrella high and started to spin around. As she spun, the umbrella began to rise up into the sky. Lily's friends watched in amazement as the pink umbrella carried her higher and higher. They cheered and clapped as Lily floated above them.
Finally, Lily floated back down to the ground. Her friends gathered around her and said, "Wow! Your pink umbrella is magical!" Lily just smiled and said, "It's always good to be prepared for anything, even a little bit of magic!"
From that day on, Lily and her friends always believed in the power of the pink umbrella. They knew that even on the sunniest of days, a little bit of magic could be found in the most unexpected places.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy cat named Tim. Tim was always cold, so he had a jacket to wear. One day, Tim went for a walk in the park. He wore his jacket because it was cold outside. Tim saw a big tree and wanted to climb it.
As Tim climbed the tree, the wind blew strong. It blew Tim's jacket right off! Tim was sad and cold. He looked for his jacket but could not find it. He saw a dog and asked, "Did you see my jacket?" The dog said, "No, but I will help you look for it."
Tim and the dog looked everywhere for the jacket. They looked under the tree, behind the bushes, and even in the pond. Then, something unexpected happened. A bird came down from the sky and said, "I have your jacket, Tim!" The bird had taken the jacket to make her nest warm. Tim was happy to have his jacket back and thanked the bird. From that day on, Tim, the dog, and the bird were best friends. They played together in the park every day, and Tim was never cold again.


Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She had a favorite toy, a pretty doll. Lucy loved to play with her doll every day. One day, she found an ugly bug in her room. She was scared and didn't know what to do.
Lucy asked her mom, "Mom, can you help me? There's an ugly bug in my room!" Her mom came quickly and saw the bug. She said, "Don't worry, Lucy. I'll take the bug outside, and it won't bother you anymore."
After the bug was gone, Lucy's mom told her a secret. "You know, Lucy, the bug was hiding in your open drawer. If you keep your drawers closed and your room clean, the bugs won't come in and spoil your toys."
From that day on, Lucy always kept her room clean and her drawers closed. She learned that taking care of her things and her space would keep her toys safe and her room free from ugly bugs.
The moral of the story is to always keep your things clean and tidy, so nothing can spoil them.

"Ben, Lily, what are you doing? You are so dirty! Come here right now!" Mom says. She is not happy.

Lily was a patient in a big hospital. She had to stay in a bed with wires and tubes. She did not like it. She wanted to go home and play with her toys and her dog.
One day, she saw a bird outside her window. It was blue and yellow and very pretty. It sang a happy song. Lily wished she could be like the bird and fly away.
She looked around and saw that no one was watching. She pulled off the wires and tubes and got out of the bed. She put on her shoes and coat and opened the door. She ran down the hall, looking for the way out.
"Hey, where are you going?" a nurse shouted. She tried to catch Lily, but Lily was too fast. She dodged and weaved and found the stairs. She ran down the stairs and saw the exit.
She pushed the door and ran outside. She felt the sun and the wind on her face. She saw the bird on a tree. It looked at her and sang again.
"Hello, bird," Lily said. "You are different from the other birds. You are very pretty. Can I be your friend?"
The bird nodded and flew down to Lily. It landed on her shoulder and nuzzled her cheek. Lily smiled and hugged the bird.
"I escaped from the hospital," she said. "I don't want to go back. I want to be with you."
The bird nodded again and flew up in the air. It circled around Lily and called to her.
"Come with me," it said. "I will show you the world."
Lily nodded and followed the bird. She ran and jumped and laughed. She felt free and happy. She did not look back.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Emily. She loved to go on adventures and explore different places. One day, she was walking in a park and suddenly she saw a penny lying on the ground. She went to pick it up and she was so excited because she had never seen a penny in real life before.
Emily quickly ran home and asked her mom what she should do with the penny. Her mom looked surprised and told Emily, "A penny is very special. You should do something special with it." Emily thought about it for a while and decided to ask a difficult question to the penny.
So Emily asked her penny a difficult question: "What's my name?" But the penny didn't answer. Emily asked it again but still, nothing. Emily was confused and started to get frustrated. She tried another question: "Where do I live?" After a few moments, the penny started to move and it answered "Emily, you live in your house."
Emily was so amazed that the penny had answered her questions. She thanked the penny and ran back home and showed her mom. Her mom laughed and said, "See! A penny can be special!" Emily agreed and never forgot her amazing adventure with the penny.

Once upon a time, there was a big bookshelf. On the bookshelf, there were many books. A little girl named Lily loved to read the books. She would sit by the bookshelf every day and read.
One day, while Lily was reading a book, she heard a tiny voice say, "Help me, please!" Lily looked around and saw a small, fierce bug stuck in a spider web near the bookshelf. The bug was very scared.
Lily knew she had to save the fierce bug. She carefully took the bug out of the spider web. The bug was so happy to be free. "Thank you, Lily!" said the bug. Then, something unexpected happened. The bug turned into a beautiful fairy! The fairy said, "You saved me, so now I will grant you one wish."
Lily thought for a moment and said, "I wish for more books on my bookshelf!" The fairy waved her wand, and the bookshelf was filled with new books. Lily was so happy, and she and the fairy became best friends. They read books together every day.


Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They saw a big ladder leaning on the wall. They wanted to climb it and see what was on the other side.
"Let's go up the ladder!" Tom said. "Maybe we can find something beautiful!"
Lily nodded. She liked beautiful things. She followed Tom to the ladder. They started to climb, one step at a time.
But the ladder was not very strong. It began to shake and wobble. Lily and Tom felt scared. They held on tight to the ladder.
"Help! Help!" they shouted. "The ladder is shaking!"
Mama heard their cries. She ran to the garden. She saw Lily and Tom on the ladder. She was very angry and worried.
"What are you doing on the ladder?" she asked. "You could fall and hurt yourself! Come down right now!"
Lily and Tom obeyed. They climbed down the ladder. They were sorry for being naughty.
Mama hugged them. She was glad they were safe. She told them to never play with the ladder again. She said the ladder was not a toy. It was a tool for grown-ups.
Lily and Tom learned their lesson. They said sorry to Mama. They promised to be careful and listen to her. They realized that being safe was more beautiful than being curious.

They asked their mom if they could go in. Mom said yes, but they had to hold her hand and be careful. She paid for the tickets and they entered the tent.
Inside, they saw many strange and colorful objects. Some were furry, some were shiny, some were spiky. They were all different shapes and sizes. Lily and Ben pointed and gasped at each one.
"Look, mom, a wild object!" Lily said, pointing at a stuffed lion with a mane and a tail.
"That's not a wild object, silly, that's a toy animal!" Ben said, laughing.
"No, it's a wild object, it has teeth and claws!" Lily said, sticking out her tongue.
Mom smiled and explained that the lion was a toy, but it was made to look like a real animal that lived in a faraway place called Africa. She said that some of the objects were toys, and some were things that people found or made from nature.
Lily and Ben learned a lot from the display of wild objects. They saw feathers, shells, rocks, bones, masks, baskets, and more. They asked mom many questions and she tried to answer them.
They had so much fun that they didn't want to leave. But mom said it was time to go home and have lunch. They thanked the people who showed them the wild objects and said goodbye.
They walked out of the tent, holding mom's hand and talking about what they saw. They agreed that the display of wild objects was the best thing in the park.

"It's too dangerous," replied her mom.
But Daisy was determined to explore. She showed her mom she could be brave and soon they were both inside the mill.

From then on, Daisy and her mom spent lots of time together exploring the magical world inside the high mill.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big pond with ducks and fish. They wanted to feed them, so they asked their mom for some bread.
"Here you go, but be careful not to fall in the water," mom said, giving them each a slice.
Tom and Lily ran to the pond and threw some bread to the ducks and fish. They were happy to see them eat and swim. But Tom wanted to have more fun. He saw a big stick and had an idea.
"Hey, Lily, watch this!" he said, and swung the stick at the water. He made a big splash that wet his clothes and shoes.
"Tom, stop that! You are making a mess!" Lily said, feeling angry. She did not like to get wet.
But Tom did not listen. He swung the stick again and again, making more splashes. He laughed and said, "This is fun!"
Then he saw something in the water. It was an old turtle with a hard shell and a long neck. It looked at Tom with its small eyes.
"Hello, turtle," Tom said, and tried to touch it with his stick. But the turtle did not like that. It snapped at the stick and broke it in half.
"Ow!" Tom said, dropping the stick. He felt scared and sorry. He had hurt the turtle and its home.
"Tom, you are naughty! You should not bother the turtle. It is old and honest. It does not hurt anyone," Lily said, feeling sorry for the turtle.
She picked up some bread and threw it to the turtle. The turtle ate it and swam away. Lily smiled and said, "Bye, turtle. I hope you are okay."
Tom felt bad. He knew he had done wrong. He looked at his wet clothes and shoes. He looked at his mom, who was coming to get them.
"Mom, I am sorry. I was silly. I splashed the water and broke the stick and hurt the turtle. I will not do it again," he said, feeling sad.
Mom hugged him and said, "I am glad you are honest, Tom. But you have to be careful and kind. The pond is not a toy. It is a home for the ducks and fish and the turtle. They have feelings too. You have to respect them and their space."
Tom nodded and said, "I understand, mom. I will respect them and their space. And I will say sorry to the turtle."
Mom smiled and said, "That is good, Tom. Come on, let's go home and change your clothes. And maybe next time, you can play with Lily and the turtle nicely."
Tom and Lily held mom's hand and walked home. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to be careful and kind and honest. And they hoped the turtle would forgive them.

Tom and Lily go to Rex. They say hello to him. Rex wags his tail. He licks their faces. Tom and Lily giggle. They pet his fur. They give him a rub on his belly. Rex rolls over and makes a happy sound.

"Yes, please," Tom and Lily say.

"Say 'sit', Rex," the man says.
"Sit, Rex," Tom and Lily say.
Rex sits down. He looks at them with his big eyes.
"Give him the biscuit," the man says.
Tom and Lily give Rex the biscuit. Rex takes it gently. He crunches it in his mouth. He licks his lips. He looks at them again.
"Say 'good boy', Rex," the man says.
"Good boy, Rex," Tom and Lily say.
Rex barks. He jumps up and down. He wags his tail.
"Thank you, Rex," Tom and Lily say.
"Thank you, sir," they say to the man.
"You're welcome," the man says. "Rex likes to make new friends. He thinks you are very nice."
Tom and Lily smile. They hug Rex. They say goodbye to him and the man. They go back to play in the park. They are happy. They think Rex is a wonderful dog. They think his biscuit is delicious.

One day, a big lion with a loud roar lived in the forest. He was slow and had a big lung. All the animals were scared of him. They did not want to play with him.
One day, a little rabbit came to the lion. The rabbit said, "Why do you roar so loud? It makes us all scared." The lion just looked at the rabbit and roared again. The rabbit jumped back, but did not run away.
The rabbit had an idea. "If you do not roar so loud, we can all play together," said the rabbit. The lion thought about it. He wanted to have friends too. So, he tried to roar softly. The animals heard him and they were not scared anymore.
Now, the lion and the other animals played together every day. The lion was not slow anymore, and his roar was not so loud. They all had fun in the forest, and the lion was happy to have friends.

Mom and Dad say it is a bison. A bison is a kind of cow that lives in the wild. They say the bison is a guest at the ranch. He came from another place and he will go back soon.
Ben and Mia want to get closer to the bison. They think he looks friendly and soft. They ask Mom and Dad if they can feed him and pet him. Mom and Dad say no. They say the bison is not used to people and he might be scared or angry. They say the bison needs space and respect. They say they can watch him from a distance and say hello.
Ben and Mia listen to Mom and Dad. They stay away from the bison. They watch him eat grass and walk around. They say hello to him and wave. The bison looks at them and snorts. He does not seem to mind them. Ben and Mia smile. They think the bison is cool and interesting. They hope he likes the ranch and has a good time. They say goodbye to him when they go home. They wonder if they will see him again.

Once upon a time, there was an old dog called Buddy. He lived in a peaceful town and ate the same old food every day.

Buddy was very worried, so he went and spoke to the pup. He said, "Please be careful my friend! Eaters can get sick when they don't eat the same food each day." But the pup didn't listen.
Soon the pup was very ill. The other animals were sad and even the old dog was very worried. Buddy had to look for a way to help his friend.
Suddenly he had an idea. He quickly found some of his old food and brought it to the pup. The pup ate it, and soon he was feeling better.
Buddy and the pup shared a peaceful moment, and the pup learned a valuable lesson: eat the same food every day and stay healthy!

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run, jump and slide on the grass and the swings. But it was a very hot day and the sun was bright. They felt tired and thirsty.
"Let's find some shade," Anna said to Ben. "We can rest and drink some water."
They looked around and saw a big tree with many green leaves. They ran to the tree and sat under it. The shade was cool and nice. They drank some water from their bottles and felt better.
"Look, what is that?" Ben pointed to something shiny on the ground. It was a small metal ring with a red stone in it. It sparkled in the sun.
"Maybe it is a treasure," Anna said. She picked up the ring and examined it. She turned it around and looked at the stone. It was smooth and bright.
"Can I see it?" Ben asked. He reached out his hand.
"OK, but be careful," Anna said. She gave the ring to Ben. He examined it too. He rubbed the stone and felt its warmth.
"It is very pretty," Ben said. "Do you think someone lost it?"
"Maybe," Anna said. "Or maybe it is a magic ring. Maybe it can make wishes come true."
"What would you wish for?" Ben asked.
Anna thought for a moment. She looked at the ring, then at Ben, then at the park. She smiled.
"I would wish for more days like this," she said. "More days to play with you and have fun."
Ben smiled too. He nodded.
"Me too," he said. He put the ring on his finger. It fit perfectly.
They held hands and closed their eyes. They made their wish together. Then they opened their eyes and laughed.
They did not know if the ring was magic or not. But they felt happy and lucky. They decided to keep the ring as a secret. They put it in their pocket and got up.
"Let's play some more," Anna said.
"OK, let's go," Ben said.
They ran to the slide and slid down. They felt the wind in their hair and the sun on their skin. They were not tired anymore. They were having the best day ever.


Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play with clay. They had many colors of clay, but their favorite was gray. They said gray clay was the best because it had a soft texture and could make any shape.
One day, they decided to make a big castle with gray clay. They worked hard and used all their gray clay to build the walls, the towers, and the gate. They were very proud of their castle and put it on the table to dry.
But then, they saw that their little brother, Sam, had taken some of their gray clay and made a ball. He was bouncing the ball on the floor and laughing.
"Hey, that's our clay!" Anna shouted. "Give it back!"
"No, it's mine!" Sam said. "I like the ball!"
Ben ran to Sam and tried to grab the ball, but Sam was faster and ran away. Anna and Ben chased him around the house, but they could not catch him. They were angry and sad.
Mom saw what was happening and called them to the living room. She asked them why they were fighting over the clay.
"Because he took our clay!" Anna and Ben said.
"But you have so much clay!" Mom said. "Can't you share with your brother?"
"No, we can't!" Anna and Ben said. "We need all the gray clay for our castle!"
Mom looked at their castle and smiled. She said it was very beautiful and creative, but she also said that clay was meant to be played with, not to be kept on the table.
She told them a story about how she and her sister used to play with clay when they were little. They made different things every day and had fun. They also shared their clay with their friends and learned new ideas. She said that playing with clay was more fun when you share and learn from others.
She asked them if they wanted to try that with Sam. She said that maybe they could teach him how to make a castle, or learn how to make a ball. She said that sharing and learning would make them happy and smart.
Anna and Ben thought about it and agreed. They said they were sorry to Sam and asked him if he wanted to play with them. Sam was happy and said yes. They went to the table and started to play with the gray clay. They made a bigger castle, a ball, and some other things. They had fun and laughed.
They learned that sharing and learning is better than fighting and settling. They also learned that gray clay can make many things, not just one. They thanked Mom for her story and her advice. Mom hugged them and said she was proud of them. She said that gray clay was the best because it had a soft texture and could make any shape, but also because it could make them happy and smart.

Spot pushed and pulled the cushion with his paws. He tried very hard, and finally, the cushion moved away from his bowl. Spot was so happy! He drank lots of water from his big, blue bowl. After that, Spot laid down on his favorite cushion and took a nice, long nap.


Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue had a favorite cloth. It was soft and pretty. She took the cloth everywhere. One day, she saw a boy with an unknown cloth. It was a different color. Sue wanted that cloth too.
Sue asked her mommy for the unknown cloth. Her mommy said, "You already have a cloth, Sue. You don't need another one." Sue was sad but listened to her mommy. The next day, Sue saw the boy again. He was crying because he lost his cloth. Sue felt bad for the boy.
Sue went to the boy and gave him her favorite cloth. The boy was happy, and they became friends. Sue learned that it's nice to share and help others. She didn't need the unknown cloth after all.


Lily and Tom were going to church with Mom and Dad. They liked church because they could sing and pray and see their friends. They also liked to pick flowers from the garden outside the church. They always asked Mom and Dad if they could pick some flowers to take home.
One day, as they were walking to church, they saw a big dog on the street. The dog was barking and running towards them. Lily and Tom were scared and held Mom and Dad's hands. Mom and Dad told them not to worry, they would keep them safe.
"Shoo, shoo, go away!" Mom said to the dog. "You are not nice, you are scaring the children!"
The dog stopped and looked at Mom. Then it wagged its tail and licked Mom's hand. Mom smiled and petted the dog. She said the dog was just lonely and wanted to play.
"Can we play with the dog, Mom?" Lily asked.
"Only if the dog's owner says it's okay," Mom said. "We don't know if the dog is friendly or not."
They looked around and saw a man coming towards them. He was holding a leash and a collar. He said he was sorry, he had lost his dog and was looking for him. He thanked Mom and Dad for stopping the dog and said his name was Max.
"Can we play with Max, please?" Tom asked the man.
"Sure, you can play with Max for a little while," the man said. "He is very gentle and loves children. But don't pick his fur, he doesn't like that."
Lily and Tom nodded and played with Max. They threw a ball and Max fetched it. They rubbed his belly and Max wagged his tail. They had fun with Max and forgot they were scared.
"Okay, kids, it's time to go to church," Dad said. "We don't want to be late."
"Bye, Max, we'll see you again," Lily and Tom said. They gave Max a hug and a kiss.
"Bye, kids, thank you for playing with Max," the man said. He put the leash and the collar on Max and waved goodbye.
Lily and Tom went to church with Mom and Dad. They sang and prayed and saw their friends. They also picked some flowers from the garden outside the church. They gave some to Mom and Dad and some to Max's owner. They were happy and safe.


Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play in the yard. Sometimes they fight over toys. Mom does not like it when they fight. She tells them to share and be nice.
One day, Mom makes a meal for them. She puts it on the table. She calls them to come and eat. Tom and Sam run to the table. They see two plates of food. One has a sandwich and one has a salad.
Tom likes sandwiches. Sam likes salads. But they do not know which plate is for whom. They both want the sandwich. They start to fight over it. They pull and tug and yell.
"Stop it!" Mom says. "You are being silly. You can both have what you want. I have a hidden plate for each of you. Look under the tablecloth."
Tom and Sam look under the tablecloth. They see two more plates of food. One has a sandwich and one has a salad. They are happy. They say sorry to each other. They thank Mom for the meal. They sit down and eat. They do not fight anymore. They share and are nice.


One day, a red dog named Max went for a walk. He saw a big tree with a sign on it. Max could not read, but he knew the sign was important. He sat under the tree, thinking about what the sign said.
A little boy named Tim saw Max and walked over. "Hi, Max! I can read the sign for you," Tim said. Max wagged his tail, happy that Tim could help. Tim read the sign out loud: "Do not sit under this tree. Bees live here." Max and Tim looked up and saw a big bee nest in the tree.
Max and Tim ran away from the tree as fast as they could. They did not want the bees to sting their skin. They found a safe spot to rest and play. Max was happy that Tim read the sign, and they both learned to be careful around bees.


One day, a girl named Lily wanted to write a letter to her friend. She needed a pen to write the letter. So, she went to the shop to buy a pen. The shop was open, and she saw many pens inside.
In the shop, Lily met a boy named Tom. Tom wanted the same pen as Lily, but there was only one left. They both looked at each other and said, "I want the pen!" They did not know what to do.
Lily thought for a moment and said, "Tom, let's share the pen. You can use it first to write, and then I will use it." Tom agreed, and they both were happy. They learned that sharing is a good thing and made a new friend.


One dark night, Jim saw a crane stretching its long neck towards the moon. He was so excited and wanted to get closer, so he followed it. When they arrived at the pond, Jim asked the crane why it was stretching.
The crane replied, "I am stretching because I want to touch the moon. I can't reach it yet, but I'm almost there!
Jim said, "That's so cool! Can I help you reach the moon?"
The crane replied, "Of course. I need a few more stretches. Can you help me?"
So, Jim and the crane stretched their necks together while they stared at the moon. After a few minutes, the crane finally touched the moon and said, "I did it! Thank you for helping me, Jim."
Jim smiled and said, "No problem. We did it together!"

Once upon a time, there was a baby who loved to play with his toys. He had a big, red ball and a soft, blue bear. The baby and the bear were best friends. They played together every day.
One day, the baby and the bear were playing in the kitchen. The baby saw a spicy pepper on the table. He thought it was a toy and picked it up. The baby said to the bear, "Look, I found a new toy!"
The bear knew the pepper was not a toy, but he didn't want the baby to feel sad. So, the bear said, "Let's show it to Mommy first." The baby and the bear went to Mommy, who was cooking dinner. She saw the spicy pepper and said, "Oh no, baby! That's not a toy. It's a spicy pepper for our food!"

Anna and Ben like to play on the beach. They pretend they are pirates and look for treasure. They dig holes in the sand and find shells and stones. They put them in a bucket and say, "Arrr, we are rich!"
One day, they play too close to the water. They do not see the tide coming in. The tide is the water that goes up and down. Sometimes it is low and sometimes it is high. When it is high, it covers more of the beach.
"Look, Ben, I found a big shell!" Anna says. She holds it up and smiles.
"Wow, that is a nice shell, Anna!" Ben says. He runs over to see it.
But then, a big wave comes and splashes them. It is cold and salty. It takes their bucket and their shells and stones. It also takes Anna's shell. They are wet and sad.
"Hey, give us back our treasure!" Ben shouts at the water. He tries to chase the wave, but it is too fast and too strong.
"Ben, come back!" Anna cries. She is scared. She does not want to lose Ben too.
But Ben does not hear her. He runs into the water and tries to grab the bucket. He does not see the next wave coming. It is bigger and stronger than the first one. It knocks him down and pulls him under. He cannot breathe. He cannot swim. He cannot scream.
Anna watches in horror. She screams for help, but no one hears her. She is alone on the beach. She wishes they had not played so close to the water. She wishes they had not pretended to be pirates. She wishes Ben was still with her. She wishes the water was clean and not dirty. She wishes the tide would go away and never come back.

Anna liked to help her mom in the garden. She liked to dig, water, and watch the plants grow. She did not like the rabbits that came at night. They would steal the vegetables and leave holes in the ground.
One day, Anna had an idea. She asked her mom for some carrots and lettuce. She put them in a basket and went to the garden. She found a spot where the rabbits liked to come in. She made a trail of carrots and lettuce leading to the basket. She hid behind a bush and waited.
Soon, she saw a rabbit hop into the garden. It smelled the carrots and lettuce and followed the trail. It reached the basket and jumped inside. Anna ran out and closed the basket. She caught the rabbit!
She was very happy and proud. She showed her mom the rabbit and told her what she did. Her mom was surprised and impressed. She said Anna was very clever and brave. She also said it was difficult to keep a rabbit as a pet. She asked Anna what she wanted to do with it.
Anna thought for a moment. She looked at the rabbit. It was cute and soft. But it also looked scared and sad. Anna felt sorry for it. She decided to let it go. She said she did not want to steal the rabbit from its home and family. She wanted it to be free and happy.
She took the basket to the edge of the garden and opened it. The rabbit hopped out and ran away. Anna waved goodbye and smiled. She hoped the rabbit would not steal her vegetables again. But she also hoped it would find some food and friends in the woods. She went back to her mom and hugged her. She said she loved her and the garden. Her mom hugged her back and said she loved her too. They went inside to have some soup and bread. They did not need carrots and lettuce today.


The beach was busy and full of people. Bobby looked out at the sea, its waves lapping against the shore. He couldn't believe his luck. Today, he was going to try and manage to sail across it.
"Ready, Bobby?" His dad asked.
Bobby nodded and clambered into the small boat. He was both excited and scared - he'd never sailed across a sea before! But he was determined to do it.
Bobby and his dad worked together, and soon they had managed to get the boat into the sea. Bobby's dad gave him one last wave, and then he was on his own.
The sea was huge, and Bobby was very scared, but determined not to give up. He held on tight, managing to keep the boat steady and make slow progress.
Hours later, Bobby finally arrived at the other shore. He was exhausted, but grateful that he had done it. He'd managed to sail across the sea!

Once there was a boy called Fabian who was very excited to try kayaking. His mum had taken him to a nearby lake so he could have a go.
Fabian had never kayaked before and he was a bit impatient. He wanted to get in the kayak right away and try paddling the lake.
His mum said "OK, Fabian, now first of all you need to sit in the middle of the kayak so it doesn't rock. Then you need to start paddling."
Fabian was so excited, he hopped into the kayak and started paddling as fast as he could with his little arms. But as he got further out into the lake the kayak started rocking more and he started sinking lower into the water.
His mum shouted "Stop!" She explained to Fabian that he needed to paddle more gently and slowly, so the motion of the kayak would increase the more he paddled.
Fabian listened and started paddling slowly. This time the kayak stayed up higher in the water and he felt a lot more stable.
He waved to his mum proudly and shouted "I'm kayaking now!"

Sam and Ben are brothers. They like to play on the farm with the animals. One day, they see a big cow in the field. The cow is black and white and has a bell around her neck.
"Look, a cow!" Sam says. "Can we pet her?"
Ben nods. "Yes, let's go. Maybe she will give us some milk."
They run to the cow and try to touch her. But the cow does not like it. She moos loudly and shakes her head. She kicks her legs and runs away.
"Hey, come back!" Ben shouts. "We just want to be your friends."
But the cow does not listen. She runs to the fence and jumps over it. She runs to the road, where there are many cars and trucks.
"Oh no!" Sam says. "The cow is in danger. She might get hit by a car. We need to help her."
They run after the cow, but they are too slow. The cow is faster and runs across the road. The cars and trucks honk and brake. The drivers are angry and scared.
"Stop, cow, stop!" Sam and Ben yell. "You are not safe there. Come back to the farm."
But the cow does not stop. She runs to the woods, where there are many trees and animals. She thinks she is free and happy.
Sam and Ben are sad and worried. They do not know what to do. They need to find the cow and bring her back. They need to tell their dad what happened. They hope the cow is okay.
They look around and see a man on a bike. He is wearing a helmet and a bright vest. He is alert and smart. He sees the cow and the boys.
"Hey, kids, what are you doing here?" he asks. "Do you know that cow?"
Sam and Ben nod. "Yes, she is from our farm. She ran away and we followed her. But we can't catch her. She is too fast and wild."
The man smiles. "Don't worry, I can help you. I have a rope and a whistle. I can call the cow and tie her to my bike. Then we can take her back to your farm. Do you want to come with me?"
Sam and Ben smile. "Yes, please. Thank you, mister. You are very kind and brave."
They get on the bike with the man. He blows his whistle and waves his rope. The cow hears him and stops. She is curious and tired. She comes closer and lets him tie her to the bike.
"Good girl, cow," the man says. "You are safe now. Let's go home."
They ride back to the farm. The cow moos softly and follows the bike. Sam and Ben are happy and relieved. They hug the cow and the man.
"Thank you, thank you, thank you," they say. "You saved the cow and us. You are our hero."
The man laughs. "You're welcome, kids. You are very brave and caring. You love the cow and the farm. You are good friends."
They reach the farm and see their dad. He is surprised and glad. He sees the cow and the man and the boys.
"What happened?" he asks. "Where did you go? How did you find the cow?"
Sam and Ben tell him everything. They tell him how the cow ran away and how the man helped them. They tell him how they learned a lesson.
"We are sorry, dad," they say. "We did not mean to scare the cow. We just wanted to pet her. But we learned that we need to be gentle and respectful with the animals. We need to listen to them and watch them. We need to keep them safe and happy."
Dad smiles and hugs them. "I'm proud of you, boys. You did the right thing. You helped the cow and the man. You are good sons."
He thanks the man and gives him some milk and cheese. He invites him to stay for dinner. He is grateful and friendly.
They all go inside the house. They eat and talk and laugh. They are a big family. The cow is in the barn. She is calm and warm. She has a new friend. She is a happy cow.

The moral of this story is that it's better to create something positive instead of taking something that doesn't belong to you.

He asks his mom, who is watching him from the porch. "Mom, what is this?" he says, pointing at the root.

Tom is sad to hear that the old tree died. He likes trees. They are green and nice and give shade and fruits. He says, "Can we wake the old tree, mom? Can we make it grow again?"
His mom shakes her head and says, "No, Tom, we can't wake the old tree. It is gone forever. But we can plant a new tree, if you want. A new tree that will grow and live and be your friend. Do you want to do that?"
Tom nods and says, "Yes, mom, I want to plant a new tree. A new tree that will be happy and strong and beautiful."
His mom hugs him and says, "That's a good idea, Tom. Let's go and get a seed and some water and some dirt. And we will plant a new tree together, right next to the old root. And we will watch it grow and take care of it. And maybe, one day, it will have roots of its own."

Tom and Lily are friends who like to joke with each other. They play games and try to make each other laugh. Sometimes they are competitive and want to win.
One day, they go to the park with their moms. They see a big cooler with drinks and snacks. They are thirsty and hungry, so they run to the cooler.
"Can I have a juice, please?" Tom asks his mom.
"Me too, me too!" Lily says.
Their moms give them each a juice box and a cookie. They sit on the grass and enjoy their treats.
"Hey, Lily, do you want to hear a joke?" Tom says.
"Sure, Tom, tell me a joke," Lily says.
"Okay, here it goes. Why did the chicken cross the road?" Tom says.
"I don't know, why?" Lily says.
"To get to the cooler!" Tom says and laughs.
Lily thinks for a moment, then shakes her head.
"That's not a joke, Tom, that's silly. The chicken would not want a juice or a cookie. The chicken would want seeds or worms," Lily says.
Tom frowns. He thinks his joke is funny.
"No, Lily, you don't get it. It's a joke because it's unexpected. The chicken does something different than usual. That's what makes it funny," Tom says.
Lily shrugs. She does not think it's funny.
"Well, I have a better joke, Tom. Do you want to hear it?" Lily says.
"Okay, fine, tell me your joke," Tom says.
"Okay, here it goes. What do you get when you cross a cooler and a competitive kid?" Lily says.
"I don't know, what?" Tom says.
"A cool kid!" Lily says and laughs.
Tom rolls his eyes. He thinks his joke is better.
"That's not a joke, Lily, that's lame. The cooler and the kid have nothing to do with each other. That's what makes it boring," Tom says.
Lily smiles. She thinks her joke is clever.
"No, Tom, you don't get it. It's a joke because it's a pun. The cooler and the kid sound the same. That's what makes it funny," Lily says.
Tom and Lily look at each other. They realize they have different kinds of jokes. They decide to agree to disagree.
They finish their juice and cookies and go back to playing. They still like to joke with each other, but they also respect each other's humor. They are friends who have fun.

Then, something unexpected happened. When Amy pulled her camera out of the hole, there was a new picture on it. The picture was not of the inside of the tree, but of a secret party with animals! They were dancing and playing games. Amy showed the picture to her mom and dad, and they all laughed. They never knew that the tree was hiding such a fun secret.


Sara and Ben were playing with their blocks. They wanted to build a big castle with towers and walls and a gate. They worked hard and helped each other. They put the blocks on top of each other and made shapes and patterns.
"Look, our castle is almost done!" Sara said. "We just need a flag for the top."
"I have a red cloth we can use," Ben said. He ran to his room and came back with the cloth. He tied it to a stick and put it on the highest tower. "There, now it looks like a real castle!"
Sara and Ben were very proud of their castle. They clapped their hands and cheered. "Yay, we did it!" they said.
Mom and Dad heard the noise and came to see what they were doing. They saw the castle and smiled. They were happy that Sara and Ben played nicely and shared their blocks. They also clapped their hands and praised them.
"Wow, what a beautiful castle you made!" Mom said. "You are very creative and clever."
"And you are very obedient and kind," Dad said. "You followed the rules and cleaned up your mess."
Sara and Ben hugged Mom and Dad. They felt good and loved. They learned that building a castle was fun, but building a family was even better.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to ride his big pillow like a horse. One day, Tim saw an empty box in his room. He had an idea. He wanted to ride his pillow horse into the box and pretend it was a secret cave.
As Tim rode his pillow horse towards the empty box, he met his friend, Sally. "What are you doing?" asked Sally. "I'm riding my pillow horse to the secret cave," said Tim. Sally wanted to join, so she grabbed her own pillow and they both rode their pillow horses into the empty box.
Inside the box, it was dark and scary. Tim and Sally tried to be brave, but they were not happy. They heard a loud noise and both started to cry. The box fell over, and they were still sad. They never played in the empty box again.


Tom and Sue were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, it was very hot and they were thirsty. They saw a fountain with water in the park. Tom ran to the fountain and drank some water. He did not offer any water to Sue. Sue was sad and angry.
Sue said to Tom, "You are not a good friend. You did not share the water with me. You only think of yourself. I do not want to play with you anymore." She walked away from Tom.
Tom felt ashamed. He knew he was wrong. He wanted to say sorry to Sue. He looked for her in the park. He saw her sitting on a bench. He went to her and said, "Sue, I am sorry. I was selfish. I should have offered you some water. Will you forgive me? Will you be my friend again?"
Sue looked at Tom. She saw that he was sorry. She said, "Tom, I forgive you. You made a mistake, but you learned from it. You are still my friend. Come, let us drink some water together." She smiled at Tom.
Tom and Sue drank some water from the fountain. They felt happy and refreshed. They hugged each other and went to play again. They learned to be kind and generous to each other.
The moral of the story is: We should share what we have with others and not be selfish. We should also say sorry when we hurt someone and forgive when someone hurts us.


Tommy did not like bath time. He hated the water and the soap. He thought they were terrible. He always tried to hide when Mommy said it was time for a bath. But Mommy always found him.
"Tommy, where are you?" Mommy called. "It's time for your bath. Don't make me count to three."
Tommy was under his bed. He hoped Mommy would not see him. He held his breath and closed his eyes.
"One...two..." Mommy said. Tommy heard her footsteps coming closer. He felt scared.
"Three!" Mommy said. She lifted the bed sheet and saw Tommy. "There you are, you silly boy. Come on, let's go to the bathroom. It won't be so bad, I promise."
Tommy sighed. He knew he had no choice. He crawled out from under the bed and followed Mommy. He wished he could stay dirty and play with his toys.
Mommy filled the tub with warm water and bubbles. She put some toys in the water. She smiled at Tommy and said, "Look, it's fun. You can splash and play with your duck and your boat. And you can make funny shapes with the soap. Here, I'll show you."
She took a bar of soap and rubbed it in her hands. She made a ball of soap and threw it to Tommy. Tommy caught it and felt it. It was soft and slippery. He threw it back to Mommy. Mommy caught it and made a star. She threw it to Tommy again. Tommy caught it and made a heart. He threw it to Mommy again. They laughed and played catch with the soap.
Tommy forgot that he hated bath time. He forgot that he hated the water and the soap. He thought they were fun. He smiled at Mommy and said, "Thank you, Mommy. I like bath time now. You are the best."
Mommy hugged him and said, "You're welcome, Tommy. I love you. You are the best, too."

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Maggie and Kelly. They were always having lots of fun together.
One day, they decided to pretend to be mommies and daddies. Maggie said, "Let's pretend to cook some food! What shall we make?" Kelly thought for a moment and then said, "Let's make blue cakes!"
So they set to work making the cakes. Maggie pretended to mix the ingredients while Kelly pretended to put them in the oven. They had lots of fun!
But then Kelly said, "Let's pretend to eat the cakes!" But Maggie said, "No, we can't! We don't have any real food."
Kelly was very upset and argued, "But we made them!" Maggie calmly replied, "Yes, but imaginary food isn't real food. We can't eat it."
So, instead of pretending to eat the imaginary cakes, Maggie and Kelly decided to make real food. Maggie said, "Let's make some fruit salad!" So they did, and it tasted delicious!
Moral of the story: You can't pretend to eat food, but you can make real food to eat instead.

Once upon a time there was a prince and a princess who lived in a green castle. The prince and princess were very sad and did not know why. Then, one day, the prince and princess heard a voice. The voice came from a tiny, green bird who sat on the castle window sill. The bird said,
"You two should hope, and your sadness will go away!"
At first, the prince and princess did not understand the bird's message. They asked the bird what they should do and how they could hope. The green bird said that they should follow it and they would find out the answer.
The prince and princess followed the bird and soon they reached a lake. The lake was so large and still that they could see their reflection in it. The bird said
"Hope is always within you! Just take a look at your reflection in the lake and you will understand!"
The prince and princess looked at the lake and for the first time, they felt happy. They had found the answer within themselves. They thanked the green bird and said goodbye, before walking back to their castle with hope in their hearts.

"Tom, you are mean! You broke our restaurant! We worked hard to build it! Go away!"
Tom laughed. He did not care. He liked to make Sam and Lily cry. He was fierce and rude. He kicked more blocks and ran away.
Sam and Lily felt bad. They wanted to build their restaurant again, but they did not have enough blocks. Some blocks were broken and some blocks were lost. They did not know what to do.
Then Ben came. Ben was a nice boy who liked to help. He saw Sam and Lily's problem and he felt sorry for them. He had some blocks in his backpack. He took them out and gave them to Sam and Lily.
"Here, you can have my blocks. I have plenty. You can build your restaurant again. I can help you if you want."
Sam and Lily smiled. They thanked Ben. They took his blocks and started to build their restaurant again. They invited Ben to join them. They used his blocks and their blocks and made a bigger and better restaurant. They had fun together. They were happy and friendly.
Tom saw them from afar. He felt lonely and bored. He wished he had friends to play with. He realized he was wrong to break Sam and Lily's restaurant. He learned that being fierce and rude does not make you happy. He learned that being nice and helpful makes you happy. He decided to change his ways. He walked over to Sam and Lily and Ben and said sorry.
"Can I play with you? I am sorry I broke your restaurant. I was bad. I want to be good. I want to be your friend."
Sam and Lily and Ben looked at him. They were surprised. They saw that Tom was sincere. They decided to give him a chance. They forgave him. They welcomed him to their restaurant. They shared their blocks with him. They played together. They were happy and friendly.
The moral of the story is: Being nice and helpful is better than being fierce and rude. Sharing and forgiving make you happy and make friends.
