Sara and her mom baked the pie together. They mixed the flour, the butter, the sugar and the eggs. They rolled the dough and put it in the pan. They filled it with blueberries and sprinkled some more sugar on top. They put the pie in the oven and waited for it to bake.
When the pie was ready, Sara and her mom took it out of the oven. It smelled so good. Sara was proud of her pie. She wrapped it in a cloth and put it in a basket. She and her mom got in the car and drove to grandma's house.
Sara was excited to see her grandma. She ran to the door and knocked. Grandma opened the door and smiled. She hugged Sara and her mom and invited them in. Sara gave her the basket and said, "Grandma, I made you a blueberry pie. I hope you like it."
Grandma was very happy. She thanked Sara and her mom and took the basket to the kitchen. She opened the cloth and looked at the pie. She gasped. The pie was not blue. It was purple. The blueberries had burst and leaked their juice all over the dough. The pie looked messy and ugly.
Sara followed her grandma to the kitchen. She saw the pie and felt sad. She had worked so hard to make a nice pie for her grandma. She thought her grandma would not want to eat it. She thought her grandma would be mad at her. She said, "Grandma, I'm sorry. I don't know what happened. The pie was blue when I put it in the oven. I wanted to make you a good pie. Please don't be mad at me."
Grandma looked at Sara and smiled. She hugged her and said, "Sara, don't be sorry. I'm not mad at you. I'm very proud of you. You made me a pie with your own hands. You used your favorite fruit. You wanted to make me happy. That's the best gift you could ever give me. I don't care what color the pie is. I'm sure it tastes delicious. Let's serve it to your mom and have some tea. We'll have a wonderful time together."
Sara felt better. She smiled and hugged her grandma back. She helped her grandma cut the pie and put it on plates. They served it to her mom and sat down at the table. They ate the pie and drank the tea. They talked and laughed and told stories. Sara realized that the pie was not miserable. It was special. It was a pie made with love. And love made everything taste better.

"Wow, look at these!" Tom said. "They are from history. They are very old and special. I want them all!"
"No, Tom, you can't have them all!" Sam said. "We have to share. Maybe someone else needs them. They are not ours."
Tom did not listen. He grabbed the hat, the map, the coin, and the medal. He ran away from Sam. He was very happy. He thought he was successful.
But Sam was very sad. He felt lonely and angry. He followed Tom to his house. He knocked on the door. He wanted to talk to Tom.
"Tom, please open the door!" Sam said. "We are friends. We have to be nice to each other. You have to accept that you can't have everything. You have to give some things back."
Tom heard Sam. He felt sorry. He knew he was wrong. He opened the door. He gave Sam the hat, the map, the coin, and the medal. He said sorry to Sam.
"Sam, I am sorry. You are right. I was greedy and mean. I don't need these things. They are from history. They belong to someone else. I accept that I can't have everything. I want to share with you. Can we still be friends?"
Sam smiled. He hugged Tom. He said yes. They were friends again. They decided to return the box to the park. They hoped someone would find it and learn from history. They learned that being successful is not about having everything, but about being kind and generous.

Ben laughs and says, "Sorry, Mia, you can't eat the candy. It is too small. But I have a real candy for you. Here, take one. It is sweet and yummy. We can share."
Mia takes the candy and says, "Thank you, Ben, you are a good friend. I like your microscope. It is a fun toy. We can see many things with it. But I like candy more."
Ben and Mia eat the candy and laugh. They are happy. They like to play with the microscope and with each other. They are good friends.

One day, Tom saw a big hole in the ground. He was curious and wanted to see what was inside. He got off his bicycle and walked to the hole. He leaned over and saw something shiny. He reached out his hand and touched it. It was a metal box.
Tom wanted to open the box and see what was inside. He tried to pull it out of the hole, but it was too heavy. He looked around and saw a shovel. He had an idea. He took the shovel and started to dig around the box. He thought he could make the hole bigger and then lift the box.
But he did not see his dad coming. His dad was looking for him and saw him digging in the hole. His dad was angry and shouted at him. He said, "Tom, what are you doing? You are making a mess and you are ruining the grass. And where is your bicycle?"
Tom felt scared and sad. He dropped the shovel and pointed to his bicycle. He had left it next to the hole, but he did not see that a dog had come and taken it away. The dog had dragged it to a corner and started to chew on it. The bicycle was broken and dirty.
His dad saw the bicycle and was even more angry. He said, "Tom, you are very naughty. You did not take care of your bicycle and you lost it. Now you have no bicycle and you have to go home. And you have to help me bury this hole and fix the grass."
Tom cried and said, "I'm sorry, dad. I just wanted to see the box. I did not mean to lose my bicycle. Please don't be harsh with me."
His dad sighed and said, "I know, Tom. But you have to learn to be careful and responsible. Come on, let's go and find the dog and get your bicycle back. Maybe we can fix it and ride it again. And maybe we can come back another day and see what is in the box. But only if you promise to listen to me and not dig in the ground again."
Tom nodded and said, "I promise, dad. I love you and I love my bicycle. Can we still be friends?"
His dad smiled and said, "Of course, Tom. We are always friends. Now let's go and find that dog and your bicycle."

Suddenly, the dog bumped into the tree. The baby bird woke up and started to cry. The cat and the dog felt bad. The mommy bird came and was angry. She chased the cat and the dog away. They were sad because they didn't mean to disturb the baby bird.


Lily and Ben went to the farm with Mom and Dad. They wanted to pick pumpkins for Halloween. Mom and Dad gave them each a basket and said, "You can pick any pumpkin you like, but only one. Look for a big, round, orange one."
Lily and Ben ran to the pumpkin patch. They saw many pumpkins, but some were too small, some were too green, and some had holes or spots. They looked and looked, but they could not find the perfect pumpkin.
Then, Lily saw something shiny in the grass. She went closer and saw a gold coin. She picked it up and showed it to Ben. "Look, Ben, I found a treasure!" she said.
Ben was happy for Lily, but he was also sad. He wanted to find a treasure too. He looked around, but he could not see anything shiny. He felt like crying.
Lily saw Ben's face and felt sorry for him. She remembered that Mom and Dad said they could only pick one thing. She thought for a moment, and then she had an idea. She gave the coin to Ben and said, "Here, Ben, you can have the treasure. I don't need it. I already have something better."
Ben looked at Lily and smiled. He took the coin and hugged her. "Thank you, Lily, you are very kind. What do you have that is better than the treasure?" he asked.
Lily pointed to a big, round, orange pumpkin that was hiding behind a scarecrow. "I have this pumpkin. It is the perfect pumpkin for Halloween. And I have you, Ben. You are my best friend. I am very grateful for you."
Ben and Lily carried their pumpkin and their coin to Mom and Dad. They were very happy and proud. Mom and Dad praised them for their good choices and their good hearts. They said, "You are very lucky, Lily and Ben. You have found the best things in the pumpkin patch."


One day, a little cat named Lucy walked in the park. She saw a big tree and wanted to climb it. Lucy climbed up the tree and sat on a branch. She looked around and saw many pretty things. But then, she saw a unique bird. The bird had many colors and looked very nice. Lucy wanted to be friends with the bird.
Lucy said with a soft voice, "Hi, bird! I am Lucy. Do you want to be friends?" The bird looked at Lucy and sighed. The bird said, "I am sorry, Lucy. I am very shy. I don't have many friends."
Lucy felt sad for the bird. She said, "Don't worry, bird. I can help you make friends. We can play together and have fun. You can meet my friends too." The bird smiled and said, "Thank you, Lucy. That sounds nice. I would like that."
So, Lucy and the bird became friends. They played together in the park and had a lot of fun. The bird was not shy anymore, and he made many new friends. Lucy and the bird were very happy to have each other.


Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. She was very proud of her big, red ball. One day, Sue met a boy named Tim. Tim had some gum in his hand. He said, "Sue, do you want some gum?"
Sue said, "Yes, please!" But she did not trust Tim. She had a feeling he was not nice. So, she held her big, red ball close to her. Tim gave Sue the gum, and they played together. They had fun, but Sue still did not trust Tim.
Later, Tim said, "Sue, let's play a game. Close your eyes and count to ten." Sue did as Tim said. When she opened her eyes, her big, red ball was gone! Tim had taken it. Sue was sad, but she knew she should have trusted her feeling.


Once there was a pretty little girl named Jasmine. She loved to study and she was always trying to learn new things.
One day Jasmine was busy studying at her desk when her mum came into the room with a plate of warm toast. She said to Jasmine, "I made this toast for you. Why don't you take a break from studying and have a snack?"
Jasmine thought for a moment and said, "No thanks mum, I want to keep studying."
Her mum smiled and said, "That's a very good idea. It's nice to take a break every once in a while though. Have some toast and then go back to your studies."
Jasmine took a break, ate the toast, and then went back to studying. She knew that studying was very important but taking a break every once in a while was good too.
The moral of this story is that it is important to work hard but to also take some time to relax and enjoy life.


Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a cute little bear named Ben. Ben loved honey very much. One day, it was very wet and rainy outside, but Ben still wanted to find some honey to eat. He put on his rain boots and went out to look for honey.
Ben walked for a long time and saw a big tree. He thought, "I hope there is honey in this tree!" Ben climbed up the tree and found a beehive full of honey. He was so happy! But he also saw a sad bee sitting on a branch. "Why are you sad?" Ben asked the bee.
The bee said, "I am sad because my wings are wet and I can't fly home." Ben wanted to help the bee. He said, "I will help you get home, and then we can share the honey together!" The bee smiled, and they became friends. Ben carried the bee on his back, and they went to the bee's home.
When they got to the bee's home, the bee's family was so happy to see her. They thanked Ben for helping her. The bee's family gave Ben lots of honey to take home with him. Ben and the bee were both very happy, and they knew they would be friends forever.
From that day on, Ben and the bee always shared honey together, even on wet and rainy days. And they always remembered to help each other when they needed it.

From that day on, Amy and Tom always helped each other and their friends whenever they needed it. They knew that it was good to accept help and to help others too.

Later, Tim needed to use the toilet, so his mom took him to the park's toilet. Tim remembered what his mom said about being careful with things he found. He washed his hands with soap and water after using the toilet, just like his mom taught him.

One day, Lily wanted to write a story. She thought hard and made up a story about a princess and a dragon. She wrote the story in her book and drew the princess and the dragon. She was very proud of her story.
She showed her story to her brother Max. Max was older and he liked to read. But he was also bossy. He looked at Lily's story and said, "This is not a good story. The princess is too small and the dragon is too big. And you spelled some words wrong. You should write like me."
Lily felt sad and angry. She said, "This is my story. I can write how I want. You are not the boss of me. Go away!"
She grabbed her book and hugged it to her waist. She ran to her room and closed the door. She did not want to talk to Max. She wanted to write more stories. She liked to write.

Sara liked to help her mom in the garden. She liked to dig and water and pull out weeds. She also liked to pick the carrots that grew under the ground. They were orange and crunchy and sweet.
One day, Sara saw a small white rabbit hopping near the fence. She was curious and wanted to make friends with it. She ran to the garden and picked a big carrot. She broke it in half and held one piece in her hand. She walked slowly to the rabbit and said, "Hello, bunny. Do you want a carrot?"
The rabbit looked at Sara and twitched its nose. It smelled the carrot and came closer. It took a bite and nibbled happily. Sara smiled and stroked its soft fur. She said, "You are very cute and delicate. I like you. What is your name?"
The rabbit did not answer, but it licked Sara's hand and cuddled with her. Sara felt happy and warm. She said, "I will call you Fluffy. Do you want to be my friend?"
The rabbit nodded and snuggled with Sara. Sara said, "I recommend that you come back tomorrow. I will bring you more carrots and we can play together. OK?"
The rabbit agreed and hopped away. Sara waved goodbye and ran to her mom. She told her about Fluffy and how they shared a carrot. Her mom hugged her and said, "That sounds wonderful, Sara. You are very kind and generous. I am proud of you."

Tim and Lily were playing hide and seek in the garden. Tim was the seeker and Lily was the hider. Lily ran behind the big hedge and hid there. She was very quiet and hoped Tim would not find her.
Tim looked around the garden and tried to find Lily. He could not see her anywhere. He checked behind the tree, under the slide, and in the sandbox, but Lily was not there. He started to feel sad and worried. Where was Lily?
He decided to shout and ask Lily to come out. He said, "Lily, where are you? I can't find you. Please come out. I miss you." He waited for Lily to answer, but he heard nothing. He shouted again, "Lily, please come out. It's getting dark and I'm scared. Don't hide anymore."
Lily heard Tim's voice and felt sorry for him. She did not want to make him sad and scared. She wanted to play with him and have fun. She came out from behind the hedge and said, "Tim, I'm here. I'm sorry I hid too well. I didn't mean to scare you. Let's play together."
Tim saw Lily and smiled. He ran to her and gave her a hug. He said, "Lily, I'm so happy to see you. You're a very good hider, but I'm a very good seeker. Let's play something else. How about tag?"
Lily nodded and said, "OK, let's play tag. You're it!" She tapped Tim on the shoulder and ran away. Tim chased her and they laughed and played until it was time to go inside. They had a lot of fun and forgot about the dark.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved swimming in the sea. She was very brave, and always trusted in the ocean. One day, she went for a swim and saw something pretty in the water.
It was a shark!
The girl was scared, but she trusted that the shark was not dangerous. She tried to be brave and talk to the shark.
"Hello, I'm scared, will you please leave?" She said.
Suddenly, the shark started to move closer to her. It was getting very close - closer than the girl expected! She swam as fast as she could, but the shark was so quick, it was right behind her.
The girl trusted that the shark would not hurt her, but sadly, the shark understood her words as an invitation to play. It grabbed her with its sharp teeth and pulled her under the waves. The poor girl was never seen again.
The girl's family trusted the ocean, but unfortunately the ocean was full of danger.

Suddenly, somebody burst through the kitchen door! Startled, Lucy dropped the mop and started to tremble. She looked up and saw a big scary monster. The monster growled and said, "Give me all the food you have here!"
Lucy tried to stay brave, but she couldn't stop trembling. She shook her head and said, "No. I can't give you all the food. I'm so sorry."
The monster seemed angry, but he leaned down and said, "Just don't be scared. I won't take all the food, I promise."
Lucy gave a tiny smile and the monster smiled back. He walked away with just a few pieces of food.
From that day onward, Lucy was no longer scared of monsters. Whenever she felt scared, she remembered the monster's kind words and her fear went away.

Tim had an idea. He said, "Let's try to push the button harder!" So, they both pushed the button together. The screen turned on! Tim and Sue were very happy. They watched their favorite show and had a fun day.

Fred asked his friend, the big green tree, "Do you know who made this print?" The tree shook its leaves and said, "I do not know." Fred and the tree looked around. They saw a big green dinosaur. The dinosaur said, "I made the print. I am sorry, Fred. I did not mean to make you sad." Fred, the tree, and the dinosaur became friends and played together every day.


Once upon a time, in a big green forest, there lived a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her friends, but she had one big wish. She wanted to climb the tallest tree in the forest. But her mom and dad did not permit her to do that because it was too high and not safe.
One sunny day, Lily saw a small bird on the ground. The bird looked ready to fly, but it was too small. Lily wanted to help the bird. She asked the bird, "Do you want to go up in the tree?" The bird chirped and nodded its head.
Lily thought of a plan. She would ask her mom and dad if she could climb the tree to help the bird. She went to her mom and dad and said, "I want to help the bird. Can I please climb the tree?" Her mom and dad thought about it and finally said, "Yes, you can, but be very careful."
Lily was very happy. She carefully climbed the tree with the bird in her hand. When she reached the top, she put the bird in its nest. The bird chirped happily and thanked Lily.
From that day on, Lily and the bird became best friends. And Lily's big wish came true. She was so proud of herself for helping her new friend.

He takes his truck and goes to Lily's yard. He knocks on her box and says, "Lily, can I play with you? I am sorry I did not share my truck. You are clever and have a cool truck. Can we be friends again?"

Once upon a time, there was a brave little bird named Bob. Bob loved to fly high in the sky and play with the clouds. One day, as Bob was flying, he saw a big cloud with a sad face. Bob flew closer to the cloud and asked, "Why are you sad, Mr. Cloud?"
The cloud looked down at Bob and said, "I am sad because I can't raise high in the sky like you, Bob. I am stuck here, and I can't move."
Bob wanted to help the cloud, so he thought of a plan. He called all his bird friends and asked them to help him push the cloud up. The birds gathered around the cloud and started to push with all their strength.
Suddenly, the cloud began to move! It went up and up, and the cloud became very happy. The cloud said, "Thank you, Bob and friends! Now I can be high in the sky like you!"
From that day on, the brave little bird and the cloud became best friends, and they played together in the sky every day. The cloud was never sad again, all thanks to Bob's kind heart and bravery.

But then he felt a sharp pain in his hand. He looked at his glove and saw smoke. His glove was on fire. He screamed and dropped the ball. His dad ran to him and took off his glove. He saw Sam's hand was burned and blistered. He hugged Sam and said he was sorry.
He said he did not know the glove was bad. He said he got it from a man who said it was special. He said he wanted to make Sam happy. He said he would take Sam to the doctor and get him a new glove. Sam cried and said he did not want a new glove. He said he wanted his hand to be okay. He said he hated the glove and the man who sold it. He said he wished he never tested it.

But soon, they started to feel tired. They had been playing for a long time. They began to yawn and rub their eyes.

"Yes, Ben. I'm sleepy too. Let's go inside and find our beds." Lily said, yawning.
They cleaned up their toys and put them away. They walked to the house, holding hands. They were happy and sleepy.
But they forgot one thing. They forgot to turn off the grill. The grill was still on, and it was very hot. The grill was not a toy. It was a real grill, that Daddy used to make food sometimes. The grill was delicate, and it could break or catch fire if left on too long.
What will happen to the grill? Will Lily and Ben remember to turn it off? Will Daddy find out? You will have to wait and see. The end.


Once upon a time, there was a big whale. The whale lived in a mild sea. The sea was not too hot and not too cold. The whale had many friends in the sea, like fish and turtles.

The whale thought for a moment and then said, "I recommend you go to the coral reef. It is a fun place to play and meet new friends." The little fish was happy and thanked the whale.
The whale and the little fish swam to the coral reef together. They played with other fish and had a great time. The little fish was not sad anymore. The whale and the little fish became best friends and had many fun adventures in the mild sea.

But then they saw a ladybug on a flower. The ladybug was red and black and had spots. It looked scared and sad.
"Hello, ladybug. Why are you sad?" asked Lily.
"I'm sad because you picked my flower. This was my home and my food. Now I have nowhere to go," said the ladybug.
Lily and Ben felt sorry for the ladybug. They did not know that they were hurting the flowers and the bugs.
"We're sorry, ladybug. We did not mean to hurt you. We just wanted to join the flowers and smell them," said Ben.
"Can we help you find a new flower?" asked Lily.
The ladybug smiled and nodded. "That would be very helpful. Thank you, friends."
Lily and Ben put the flowers back on the hill and looked for a new flower for the ladybug. They found a yellow one with a big center. The ladybug liked it and crawled on it.
"Thank you, friends. You are very kind and helpful. You can join me and smell this flower. It smells very nice," said the ladybug.
Lily and Ben smiled and joined the ladybug and the flower. They smelled the flower and felt happy. They learned that they should not pick the flowers, but enjoy them with the bugs. Sara and Tom were playing with their toy boats in the harbor. They liked to watch the big boats come and go, and make noises like horns and engines. Sometimes they saw fish and birds in the water, too.
One day, they saw a new boat that was very big and shiny. It had a lot of flags and people on it. Sara and Tom wanted to see it closer, so they ran to the edge of the harbor. But they were not careful, and they dropped their toy boats on the ground.
"Oh no!" Sara cried. "Our boats are broken! They are fragile and the ground is hard!"
Tom was sad, too. He picked up his boat and saw a big crack in it. He tried to fix it, but it did not work. He looked at Sara's boat and saw that it was worse. It had lost its mast and its sail.
"Maybe we can ask the people on the big boat to help us," Tom said. "They have tools and glue and stuff."
Sara nodded. She liked Tom's idea. She saw a man on the big boat who was wearing a hat and a uniform. He looked like he was in charge. She waved her hand and called to him.
"Excuse me, sir! Can you help us, please? Our toy boats are broken and we don't know what to do!"
The man heard Sara's voice and looked down. He saw the two children and their toy boats. He smiled and walked to the side of the big boat. He leaned over and said:
"Hello, there! I'm sorry to hear that your toy boats are broken. They look very nice. What are their names?"
Sara and Tom told him their boat names. Sara's boat was called Lily and Tom's boat was called Max. The man nodded and said:
"Well, Lily and Max are very lucky to have you as their owners. You know what? I have some spare parts and some glue in my cabin. Why don't you come up and I'll see what I can do to fix them?"
Sara and Tom were very happy. They thanked the man and followed him to the big boat. He helped them climb up and took them to his cabin. There, he had a lot of things that looked like toys, but they were for real boats. He found some pieces that matched Lily and Max and glued them together. He also gave them some stickers and some paint to decorate them.
"There you go," he said. "Lily and Max are good as new. Maybe even better. They are very strong and beautiful now. You can take them back to the harbor and play with them again."
Sara and Tom were overjoyed. They hugged the man and thanked him again. They took their toy boats and ran back to the harbor. They put them in the water and watched them float and sail. They were very careful not to drop them or bump them. They knew they were fragile, but they also knew they were loved.

As they played, they saw a big box. The strong deer and his friends did not know what was inside. They all wanted to see, but they were scared. The deer was brave and said, "I will open it!"
When the strong deer opened the box, they found a funny hat. The deer put the hat on his head and started to joke. All his friends laughed and laughed. They did not know that the hat was magic.
Suddenly, the strong deer turned into a big, funny bird! His friends were so surprised. Now, the deer could fly with the birds and joke with them in the sky. The strong deer loved being a bird, and they all played happily ever after.


Once upon a time, there was a kind little girl called Sarah. Every day she would go outside to play in the garden. One day, she saw a bee buzzing around her. Sarah stopped to watch the bee buzzing around in the sun. She smiled and said hello to the bee. Suddenly, the bee stopped and smiled back at Sarah.
Sarah got very excited and asked the bee if she wanted to play. The bee nodded her head and they started to play together.
They ran around the garden, played hide and seek and made each other laugh. Eventually, Sarah said it was time to go home. She gave the bee a big hug and said goodbye.
The bee smiled and waved as Sarah ran back home. Sarah was very happy that the bee was so kind and that they were able to play together.

After a while, the wind slowed down, and the kite came back down. Tim and his friends were tired from their busy day of play. They said goodbye and went home. Tim was happy to have spent the day with his friends and the wind. He couldn't wait for more fun days to come.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a little girl named Lily. She was a happy girl who loved to play with her friends. One day, she went to the forest to play with her best friend, a cute bunny named Binky. They played hide and seek, and Lily had so much fun.
While they were playing, Lily forgot the way back home. She started to cry and said, "Binky, I don't know how to go back home. I'm scared!" Binky hugged her and said, "Don't worry, Lily. I will help you get back home safe."
Binky and Lily walked together, looking for the way home. They saw a big tree with a hole in it. Binky said, "I think I remember this tree. Your house is close!" Lily felt happy and safe with her friend.
As they walked, they saw a big rock. Binky said, "Yes, I know this rock! Your house is just around the corner!" And just like that, they found Lily's house. Lily hugged Binky and said, "Thank you for helping me get home safe. You are the best friend ever!"
From that day on, Lily never forgot the way home. She and Binky played in the forest every day, and they always made sure to stay safe and remember the way back home.

At home, Mia put the cauliflower on the table. Suddenly, the cauliflower started to grow bigger and bigger! It was not a normal cauliflower; it was a magic cauliflower! Mia and her family were very surprised. They all laughed and played with the big cauliflower.

"Let's open it!" Ben says. He runs to the sack and pulls the string. Mia follows him. She is alert. She thinks there might be something bad in the sack.
The sack opens. Out comes a big, loud, angry dog. It has sharp teeth and red eyes. It wants to bite Ben and Mia. It jumps at them and barks.
"Help! Help!" Ben and Mia scream. They are scared. They try to run away, but the dog is faster. It catches them and bites them hard. They cry and bleed.
No one hears them. No one helps them. The dog has power. It hurts Ben and Mia. They are in pain. They wish they never opened the sack. They are sorry. They are sad. The end.

Sara liked to play with yarn. She had many colors of yarn in her basket. She liked to make things with yarn, like hats and scarves and dolls. One day, she found a new yarn in her basket. It was unusual. It was not one color, but many colors. It was not smooth, but fuzzy. It was not thin, but thick.
Sara wanted to examine the unusual yarn. She took it out of her basket and held it in her hands. She felt it and looked at it. She wondered what it was and where it came from. She asked her mom, who was sitting on the couch.
"Mom, what is this yarn?" Sara asked.
"That is a special yarn, Sara. It is called rainbow yarn. It is made from the wool of a special sheep. The sheep has many colors of wool. It is very rare and very soft. Do you like it?" Mom said.
Sara nodded. She liked the rainbow yarn. She thought it was beautiful and cozy. She wanted to make something with it. She asked her mom, who was smiling.
"Mom, can I make something with this yarn?" Sara asked.
"Of course, Sara. You can make anything you want with this yarn. What do you want to make?" Mom said.
Sara thought for a moment. She had an idea. She smiled and said, "I want to make a rainbow scarf for you, Mom. You are special, like the rainbow yarn. And you are always warm and soft, like the rainbow yarn. I love you, Mom."
Mom hugged Sara and said, "I love you too, Sara. And I would love a rainbow scarf from you. You are very sweet and creative, Sara. You make me happy."
Sara and Mom smiled and kissed. Then Sara took the rainbow yarn and her needles and started to make the rainbow scarf. She was happy. She liked to play with yarn. She liked to make things with yarn. She liked to make things for Mom.

One day, a playful cat named Tom saw a big hole in the ground. He wanted to fill the hole with dirt. So, he started to dig with his paws. As he dug, he found a little toy car. Tom was very happy.
Tom showed the toy car to his friend, Sam the dog. Sam said, "Wow! That's a nice toy car. Let's play with it!" Tom replied, "Yes, let's play, but we should fill the hole first. I think something fun will happen when we do."
Tom and Sam worked together to fill the hole with dirt. They pushed and pushed until the hole was full. Then, they put the toy car on top of the filled hole. Suddenly, the toy car started to grow bigger and bigger! It turned into a real car that they could both ride in.
Tom and Sam were so excited. They jumped into the big car and went for a fun ride. They knew that filling the hole was a good idea. Now, they had a new car to play with and enjoy together.

The bird flew away and came back with a magic leaf. The bird put the leaf on Tim's toe, and just like that, his toe felt better! Tim was happy and not sad anymore. He thanked the bird and they became best friends. From that day on, Tim and the bird played together every day, and Tim never hurt his toe again.

One day, a boy named Tom found some gum. The gum was incredible! It was big and pink. Tom loved gum, so he put it in his mouth. He chewed it and blew a big bubble. The bubble was so big that it lifted him up into the sky. Tom was scared.
As Tom went up, he saw a big bird. The bird did not like Tom in the sky. The bird said, "You should not be here!" The bird tried to pop the bubble. Tom was scared and said, "Please, do not pop my bubble!" The bird thought about it and said, "Okay, I will not pop your bubble, but you must go back down."
Tom did not want to fall, but he knew he had to go back down. He let some air out of the bubble. The bubble got smaller and Tom started to fall. He fell slowly and safely back to the ground. Tom was happy to be back on the ground, but he knew he would never forget his incredible gum adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She had a toy box full of fun things to play with. One day, she found a big cube in the box. The cube was new, and she did not know what it was for. She decided to play with it and see what would happen.
Lucy played with the cube all day long. She rolled it, threw it, and even sat on it. As she played, she started to feel hungry. She remembered that her mom had put a small, round fruit in her lunch box. She decided to eat the fruit to make her tummy happy.
Lucy took a big bite of the fruit. But, oh no! The fruit was very sour! Her face went all funny, and she did not like it at all. She knew that she should not play with the cube and eat at the same time. From that day on, Lucy decided to play with her toys and eat her food only when it was time to eat. And she never forgot the sour fruit that taught her a lesson.


Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim had a toy alarm that he loved very much. He would play with it all day, making it beep and light up. At night, he would take it to bed with him so he could feel safe.
One day, Tim's mom wanted to add something new to his toy alarm. She found some colorful stickers and put them on the alarm. Tim was so happy to see his alarm looking even more fun. He couldn't wait to show it to his friends.
Tim took his alarm with the new stickers to the park. He showed it to his friends, and they all thought it was very cool. They played with the alarm, making it beep and light up. Tim felt safe and happy because his toy alarm was with him, and he had his friends by his side.


Sara and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Sara had a long, pink rag that she liked to pretend was a scarf. Ben had a big, blue truck that he liked to drive around. They were having fun until Ben saw Sara's rag and wanted it.
"Give me your rag!" Ben said to Sara.
"No, it's mine!" Sara said to Ben.
"Why?" Ben asked.
"Because it's pretty and soft and I like it," Sara explained.
"But I want it too," Ben said. "It can be a flag for my truck."
He tried to grab the rag from Sara, but she held on tight. They started to pull and tug on the rag, making loud noises.
"Stop it, you two!" their mom said, coming into the room. "What are you doing?"
"Sara won't share her rag with me," Ben said.
"Ben tried to take my rag from me," Sara said.
Mom looked at them with a stern face. "You both need to learn to share and be nice to each other. Rag is just a thing. Friends are more important. How would you feel if someone took your toy away?"
Sara and Ben thought for a moment. They felt sorry for being mean to each other.
"I'm sorry, Sara," Ben said. "You can have your rag back."
"I'm sorry, Ben," Sara said. "You can play with my rag if you want."
They hugged and smiled. Mom was happy to see them make up.
"That's better," she said. "Now, why don't you play together nicely? I'll make you some cookies for a snack."
Sara and Ben nodded and went back to their toys. They decided to use the rag as a bridge for the truck. They were having fun again until they heard a loud rip. They looked at the rag and saw that it was torn in half.
"Oh no!" Sara cried.
"Oh no!" Ben cried.
They had pulled the rag too hard and broke it. They felt sad and angry. They blamed each other for the rag's ruin.
"It's your fault!" Sara said to Ben.
"No, it's your fault!" Ben said to Sara.
They started to fight again, hitting and kicking each other. Mom heard the noise and came back into the room. She saw the rag and the children.
"What happened?" she asked.
"They broke my rag!" Sara said.
"They broke my flag!" Ben said.
Mom was very disappointed and angry. She took away their toys and sent them to their rooms. She told them they had to stay there until they learned to share and be nice to each other.
Sara and Ben went to their rooms, crying and sulking. They wished they had listened to Mom and not fought over the rag. They realized they had lost their toy and their friend. They felt lonely and sorry.
The moral of the story is: Don't be greedy and selfish. Share and be nice to your friends. Things can break, but friends can last.

"Thank you, Tim!" said the little bunny. "You are a good person. I am happy to have a new friend like you." Tim smiled and said, "You're welcome, little bunny. I am happy to help you." From that day on, Tim and the little bunny became best friends and played together in the woods every day.

Once upon a time, there was a huge steak. The steak was so big it would feed many people. Every day when the sun rose, the steak would smile. One day, two friends named Jack and Jill saw the steak and they were very hungry.
Jack said to the steak, "Let's take you home and eat you!". But Jill said "No, we can't do that. This steak could make many people happy."
So instead of taking the steak and eating it, Jack and Jill invited all their friends over. They each took a portion of the steak and shared it together. Everyone was very happy and the steak smiled even bigger.
The moral of the story is it's better to share than to take for yourself. When you share, everyone can smile!


Once upon a time, in a big field, there was a rare flower named Poppy. Poppy was very pretty and loved to eat sun and rain to grow big and strong. One day, Poppy met a small bug named Buzz.
"Hi, I am Poppy," said the pretty flower. "Who are you?"
"Hi Poppy, I am Buzz," said the small bug. "I like to fly and play all day."
Poppy and Buzz became good friends. They played together every day. Poppy loved to watch Buzz fly high in the sky. Buzz loved to see Poppy eat sun and rain to grow.
One day, Poppy felt sad because she could not fly like Buzz. Buzz saw Poppy's sad face and said, "Don't be sad, Poppy. You are a rare and pretty flower. You can eat sun and rain to grow big and strong. I cannot do that."
Poppy smiled and felt happy again. She knew that even if she could not fly, she was still special. Poppy and Buzz played together every day, and they were very happy.


Lily liked to help her mom in the garden. She watered the plants and pulled out the weeds. She saw a big white flower in the ground. She asked her mom, "What is this?"
Her mom smiled and said, "That is a cauliflower. It is a vegetable that we can eat. It grows from a seed and it increases in size as it gets more sun and water."
Lily was curious. She wanted to taste the cauliflower. She asked her mom, "Can we pick it and cook it?"
Her mom nodded and said, "Yes, we can. But first, we have to share some with our neighbor, Mr. Lee. He is very kind and he gave us some tomatoes last week. He likes cauliflower too."
Lily agreed. She thought sharing was nice. She helped her mom cut the cauliflower and put it in a basket. They walked to Mr. Lee's house and knocked on the door. Mr. Lee opened the door and smiled when he saw them.
"Hello, Lily and mom. What a lovely surprise. What do you have in the basket?" he asked.
Lily said, "We have a cauliflower from our garden. We want to give you some because you are kind and you gave us tomatoes."
Mr. Lee thanked them and said, "That is very generous of you. I love cauliflower. It is one of my favorite vegetables. Can I give you something in return?"
Lily and her mom said, "No, thank you. We have enough. We just want to make you happy."
Mr. Lee hugged them and said, "You have made me very happy. You are very kind too. Thank you for being my friends."
Lily and her mom said goodbye and went back to their house. They cooked the cauliflower and ate it for dinner. It was delicious. Lily felt proud and happy. She had learned something new and she had done something good. She had a good day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue lived on a farm with her mom and dad. They had a big garden where they grew many things to eat. One day, Sue looked at the garden and saw that the earth was very dry. She wanted to make it wet so the plants could grow.
Sue went to her mom and said, "Mom, the earth is dry. Can we make it wet?" Her mom looked at the sky and said, "Yes, Sue. We need rain to make the earth wet. Let's do a rain dance and hope the rain comes."
Sue and her mom danced in the garden, hoping for rain. They danced and danced, but the rain did not come. The sun shone brighter and the earth became even more dry. The plants in the garden started to die.

Tom and Ben nod. They understand. They want to be good and kind. They want to be better friends. They hug Mom and say thank you. They hug each other and say sorry. They learn their lesson.
The end.

But something unexpected happened. When Amy opened the oven, there was no cake! Instead, there was a big, friendly bear. The bear had eaten the cake. Amy was surprised, but she was not scared. She laughed and said, "Silly bear, let's cook another cake together!" So, Amy and the bear cooked a new cake and became best friends.


One day, a little dog named Max was very thirsty. He wanted to drink some cool water. He walked to his bowl on the floor and saw that it was empty. Max was sad and didn't know what to do.
Max saw his friend, a little bird named Sam. Max said, "Sam, I want to drink cool water, but my bowl is empty." Sam thought for a moment and said, "I know where we can find cool water. Follow me, Max!"
They went to a big tree and saw a hole in the tree. Sam said, "Look, Max. There is cool water in the tree hole." Max was happy and started to drink the water. But, surprise! The water started to talk! It said, "Hello, Max and Sam. I am a magic water. If you drink me, you can talk to all the animals in the world."
Max and Sam were very happy. They drank the magic water and could talk to all their animal friends. They had lots of fun and made many new friends.

As Tom went up, he saw many things on the shelf. He saw a ball, a toy car, and a book. Tom liked the ball and played with it for a little bit. Then, he went higher on the shelf.
When Tom got to the top of the shelf, he saw a big, soft bed. He was very tired from climbing slow and playing with the ball. So, Tom lay down on the bed and took a long nap. He was very happy he climbed the shelf.


One day, a little girl named Lucy found a long cord in her room. She did not know what it was for, but she liked it. Lucy started to imagine all the fun things she could do with the cord. She thought about making it into a jump rope or a leash for her toy dog.
Lucy took her cord outside to play. She saw her friend Tom from next door. Tom was sad because he lost his kite. The kite was stuck high up in a tree. Lucy wanted to help Tom feel better.
Lucy had an idea! She tied the cord to a strong stick. Then, she threw the stick up into the tree. The stick hit the kite and it fell down. Tom was happy to have his kite back. Lucy was glad that her cord helped her friend. They played together all day and had lots of fun.


Once upon a time, there was a big firework show in the town. All the kids were very excited to see the bright colors in the sky. Tim, a little boy with a generous heart, wanted to share his fireworks with his best friend, Ben.
But Ben's mom said, "No, it's too late. Ben needs sleep." Tim was sad because he wanted to share the fun with his friend. Tim's mom saw her son's sad face and wanted to help.
She said, "Why don't we suggest to Ben's mom that we can have a small firework show tomorrow during the day?" Tim liked the idea and went to talk to Ben's mom. She agreed, and the next day, they all had a great time watching the fireworks together.


One sunny day, a boy named Tim went to the beach with his mom and dad. They took a big sail with them to play with. Tim felt very lucky because he loved playing at the beach. He liked to run and jump in the sand.
While they were playing, a big wind came and took the sail up in the air. Tim yelled, "Mom, Dad, look! The sail is flying!" His mom and dad looked up and saw the sail flying high in the sky. They all laughed and clapped their hands.
Just then, a big bird saw the sail and thought it was a friend. The bird grabbed the sail and flew away with it. Tim was sad, but then the bird came back and dropped the sail right in front of Tim. He was so lucky! Tim said, "Thank you, bird!" and the bird sang a happy song. From that day on, Tim and the bird were the best of friends.


One day, Tom and Lily went to the park with their mom. They saw a big fountain with many coins in the water. Tom wanted to take some coins and put them in his pocket.
"Look, Lily, shiny pennies!" he said. "Let's get some!"
"No, Tom, we can't do that!" Lily said. "That's not nice. Mom will be angry. And the pennies are for wishes. People throw them and hope for good things."
But Tom did not listen. He ran to the fountain and reached for a penny. He did not see the sign that said "Do not touch the water".
Suddenly, a loud voice warned him. "Hey, kid, stop that! You can't take the coins! That's stealing!"
Tom was scared. He looked up and saw a man in a blue uniform. He was a guard. He had a big hat and a whistle.
"Sorry, sir, I didn't know," Tom said. He dropped the penny and ran back to Lily.
The guard followed him. He looked angry. He wanted to tell Tom's mom what he did.
But Lily was compassionate. She felt sorry for Tom. She knew he made a mistake. She did not want him to get in trouble.
"Please, sir, don't be mad at Tom," she said. "He's only three. He didn't mean to be bad. He just liked the pennies. He won't do it again. I promise."
The guard looked at Lily. He saw her big eyes and her sweet smile. He softened a bit. He decided to give Tom a chance.
"Okay, okay, I'll let it go this time," he said. "But you have to promise me something. You have to make a wish with the penny you dropped. And you have to wish for something good. Something that will make you a better person. Can you do that?"
Tom nodded. He felt ashamed. He did not want to steal anymore. He wanted to be good.
"Thank you, sir," he said. "I'm sorry. I'll make a wish."
He picked up the penny and threw it back into the fountain. He closed his eyes and wished.
"I wish I could be more like Lily," he said. "She's kind and smart and compassionate. She's the best sister ever."
Lily hugged him. She was proud of him. She loved him.
Mom came back from the bench. She did not know what happened. She saw Tom and Lily smiling.
"Did you have fun, kids?" she asked.
"Yes, mom, we did," they said.
They did not tell her about the pennies. They kept it as a secret. A secret wish.


Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the garden. They see some bees flying around the flowers. They wonder where the bees go.
"Let's follow them!" Lily says. "Maybe they have honey!"
"OK!" Ben says. "But be careful. Bees can sting!"
They run after the bees. They see a big tree with a hole. The bees go inside the hole. Lily and Ben hear a buzzing sound.
"Look! There is honey in the tree!" Lily says. She points to a sticky yellow thing.
"Wow! Can we have some?" Ben asks.
"I don't know. Maybe the bees will be angry." Lily says.
They think for a moment. Then they have an idea.
"Let's prepare a gift for the bees!" Lily says. "Maybe they will share their honey with us!"
"What kind of gift?" Ben asks.
"Something sweet and smooth!" Lily says. "Like jam or peanut butter!"
They run back to the house. They find some jam and peanut butter in the kitchen. They put some on a plate. They also find some bread and cut it into small pieces. They put some jam and peanut butter on the bread.
"Let's go back to the tree!" Lily says. "Maybe the bees will like our gift!"
They carry the plate to the tree. They put it near the hole. They wait for the bees to come out.
"Hello, bees!" Lily says. "We have a gift for you! It is sweet and smooth! We hope you like it!"
The bees come out of the hole. They see the plate. They smell the jam and peanut butter. They fly around the plate. They taste the bread. They like it!
"Thank you, children!" The bees say. "You are very kind! We have a gift for you too! It is honey! It is sweet and smooth too! We hope you like it!"
The bees bring some honey from the tree. They put it on another plate. They give it to Lily and Ben.
"Thank you, bees!" Lily and Ben say. "You are very generous! We love honey!"
They taste the honey. It is sweet and smooth. They smile.
Lily and Ben are happy. The bees are happy. They share their gifts. They become friends. They play in the garden.

Sam went to look for food. He walked and walked until he found a big bag of food. Sam was so happy that he jumped and danced. But then, something unexpected happened. The bag of food started to move! Sam was very scared and jumped back.
Out of the bag came a small mouse named Tim. Tim was also thin and hungry. Sam and Tim looked at each other and decided to share the food. They became best friends and ate from the same bowl every day. They learned that love and sharing were better than owning things alone.

Lily liked to polish her books. She had many books in her room. She liked to make them shiny and clean. She used a soft cloth and some water. She rubbed the cloth on the books gently.
One day, Lily went to the library with her mom. The library had many more books than her room. Lily wanted to polish them all. She took a cloth from her bag and started to polish a book on a shelf. But the librarian saw her and said, "No, no, no! You can't polish the books here. They are not yours. You have to be careful with them. Put the cloth away and use your eyes, not your hands."
Lily felt frustrated. She did not understand why she could not polish the books. She liked to polish books. She thought she was helping. She did not want to use her eyes. She wanted to use her hands. She started to cry.
Her mom heard her cry and came to her. She hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I know you love books. But the library books are for everyone to share. You can't polish them because you might damage them or make them wet. You can look at them and read them, but you have to be gentle and respectful. Do you understand?"
Lily nodded. She wiped her tears and said, "I'm sorry, librarian. I won't polish the books anymore. Can I still read them?"
The librarian smiled and said, "Of course you can, Lily. You are a good reader. And you can polish your own books at home as much as you like. Just don't bring the cloth to the library again, okay?"
Lily agreed. She put the cloth back in her bag and picked a book to read. She was still a little frustrated, but she also felt curious and happy. She liked the library. She liked books. And she liked to polish them.

Ben and Jen are twins. They like to play in the park. They have a big red ball. They like to kick the ball and catch the ball.
One day, they see a big tree in the park. The tree has many fruits. They see apples, oranges, bananas, and grapes. They want to eat the fruits. They say, "Let's get some fruits!"
They run to the tree. But the tree is too tall. They cannot reach the fruits. They try to jump. They try to climb. They try to throw the ball. But they cannot get the fruits. They are sad.
They see a boy and a girl. They are also twins. They have a big blue ball. They also want to eat the fruits. They say, "Hello, we are Sam and Pam. Can we play with you?"
Ben and Jen say, "Hello, we are Ben and Jen. We want to play with you. But we also want to eat the fruits. Can you help us?"
Sam and Pam say, "Yes, we can help you. We have an idea. Let's unite our balls. Then we can make a big ball. Then we can roll the big ball to the tree. Then we can stand on the big ball. Then we can reach the fruits. It is easy!"
Ben and Jen say, "That is a good idea. Let's do it!"
They unite their balls. They make a big ball. They roll the big ball to the tree. They stand on the big ball. They reach the fruits. They pick the fruits. They share the fruits. They eat the fruits. They are happy.
They say, "Thank you for helping us. You are our friends. We like to play with you. We like to eat fruits with you. Fruits are yummy!"
They play and eat and laugh. They have fun in the park. They are happy twins.

Tommy loved to play with his toy dragon. He named it Spike and he liked to imagine that it was a real dragon that could fly and breathe fire. He would make Spike roar and flap his wings and chase his other toys around the room.
One day, Tommy's mom brought home a surprise for him. It was a big box with a bow on it. "What is it, Mommy?" Tommy asked, excited.
"It's a gift for you, Tommy. Open it and see," Mommy said, smiling.
Tommy tore off the bow and the paper and opened the box. Inside was a huge stuffed dragon, much bigger than Spike. It was green and chubby and had shiny scales and a long tail. Tommy gasped and hugged the dragon. "Wow, Mommy, thank you! It's a giant Spike!"
Mommy laughed and said, "You're welcome, Tommy. I thought you would like it. You can play with it and imagine that it's a real dragon, too."
Tommy was very happy. He put the giant Spike next to his bed and played with it every day. He imagined that they were flying over mountains and forests and having adventures. He still loved his toy Spike, but he liked the giant Spike more. He thought it was more fun and more real.

Lily and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They wanted to make a cake for Mommy. They found a big bowl, some flour, some eggs, and some butter. They also saw a jar of sugar on the shelf.
"Let's put some sugar in the cake," Lily said. "It will make it sweet and yummy."
"Okay," Ben said. "But how much?"
Lily shrugged. "A lot," she said. She climbed on a chair and reached for the jar. She opened it and poured some sugar into the bowl.
"Is that enough?" Ben asked.
"No, more," Lily said. She poured more sugar into the bowl. The jar was almost empty.
"Stop, Lily, that's too much!" Ben said. "Mommy will be mad."
But Lily did not listen. She poured the rest of the sugar into the bowl. She smiled and said, "Now it will be brilliant!"
She got down from the chair and picked up a big spoon. She started to stir the mixture in the bowl. Ben watched her with a worried look.
Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was Mommy. She came into the kitchen and saw the mess. She saw the empty jar, the sugar everywhere, and the sticky bowl.
"What are you doing?" Mommy asked. She was very angry.
"We're making a cake for you, Mommy," Lily said. She held up the spoon and showed her the mixture.
Mommy looked at the mixture. It was not a cake. It was a gooey mess. It was too sweet and too sticky. It was not brilliant. It was awful.
Mommy sighed. She took the bowl and the spoon from Lily. She threw them in the trash. She said, "You can't make a cake like this. You wasted all the sugar. You made a big mess. You have to clean it up. And you have to say sorry."
Lily and Ben felt sad. They did not want to make Mommy angry. They did not want to waste the sugar. They did not want to clean the mess. They wanted to make a cake for Mommy. But they did not know how.
They said sorry to Mommy. They helped her clean the kitchen. They did not play with the sugar anymore. They learned their lesson. But they still wished they could make a cake for Mommy. Maybe next time, they would ask her for help.

They pushed their small boat into the water and started to row. They got closer and closer to the big boat. They could hear the horn and see the people on the deck.
"Hello!" Sara shouted.
"Hello!" a man shouted back. He had a hat and a beard. He smiled at them.
"Who are you?" Tom asked.
"I'm the captain of this boat. Do you want to come aboard?" the man asked.
Sara and Tom looked at each other. They were curious and excited. They nodded.
"OK, but you have to guess the name of my boat first. It's a playful word that rhymes with boat," the man said.
Sara and Tom thought hard. They tried to think of words that rhymed with boat.
"Is it goat?" Sara asked.
"No, that's not it," the man said.
"Is it coat?" Tom asked.
"No, that's not it either," the man said.
"Is it float?" Sara asked.
"Close, but no," the man said.
"Is it note?" Tom asked.
"No, no, no," the man said.
Sara and Tom were running out of words. They looked at the boat again. They noticed something on the side. It was a picture of a fish with a big smile.
"Is it moat?" Sara asked.
"No, but you're very warm," the man said.
"Is it...gloat?" Tom asked.
"No, but you're almost there," the man said.
Sara and Tom looked at each other. They had one more word in their minds. They said it together.
"Is it...dote?"
"Yes, that's it! You guessed it! Dote is the name of my boat. It means to love and care for someone very much. I named it after my wife, who is very playful and sweet. You're very smart and brave. Come aboard, I have some treats and toys for you," the man said.
Sara and Tom cheered. They had guessed the name of the boat. They were happy and proud. They climbed aboard the big boat and met the captain's wife. She was very playful and sweet. She gave them cookies and juice and showed them her dolls and books. They had a wonderful time on the dote boat. They made new friends and learned new words. They thanked the captain and his wife and went back to their small boat. They waved goodbye and rowed back to the shore. They had a lot of fun.

While playing near the pond, Sam's hand slipped and he dropped the copper coin. It fell into the pond and sank to the bottom. Tim and Sam tried to get it back, but they couldn't. They were both sad and went home. The copper coin was lost in the pond forever.


Jill liked to wave at the big trucks that passed by her house. She knew that every Tuesday, the garbage truck would come and make a loud noise. She liked to watch how the men threw the bags into the back of the truck and pushed a button. She thought they were very organized and fast.
One day, she decided to make a sign for them. She took a big piece of paper and some crayons and wrote "THANK YOU" in big letters. She also drew some flowers and stars to make it pretty. She was very proud of her sign and wanted to show it to the garbage men.
She waited by the window with her sign, holding it up high. She saw the garbage truck coming down the street and got very excited. She ran outside and waved at the men with her sign. They saw her and smiled. They stopped the truck and got out.
"Hi, little girl, what's your name?" one of them asked.
"I'm Jill, and this is for you," she said, handing them the sign.
"Wow, this is very nice of you, Jill. Thank you for making this for us. You are very kind and creative," the other one said.
They gave her a high five and a sticker that said "I love garbage trucks". They put her sign on the front of the truck and waved at her as they drove away.
Jill was very happy. She waved back at them and ran inside to tell her mom what happened. She put the sticker on her shirt and said, "Mom, I made some new friends today. They are very organized and fast. And they like my sign."


Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. They had a big bucket and a small shovel to make sand castles. They worked together and had fun.
One day, they saw a new boy in the park. He had a red truck and a blue hat. He came over to Anna and Ben and said, "Hello, can I play with you?"
Anna and Ben said, "Yes, you can play with us. We are making sand castles. Do you want to help?"
The new boy said, "Yes, I want to help. But I want to use your bucket and shovel. They are better than mine."
Anna and Ben did not like that. They said, "No, you cannot use our bucket and shovel. They are ours. You can use your truck and hat."
The new boy got angry. He said, "No, I want to use your bucket and shovel. Give them to me now!"
He tried to grab the bucket and shovel from Anna and Ben. They held on tight and said, "No, go away!"
They started to quarrel. They pulled and pushed and shouted. The sand castles they made were ruined. They were not happy.
A lady who worked in the park saw them. She came over and said, "Stop, stop, what are you doing? Why are you quarreling? You should share and be nice to each other."
She took the bucket and shovel and the truck and hat. She said, "You cannot play with these toys until you calm down and say sorry. Go and sit on that bench and think about what you did."
Anna and Ben and the new boy felt ashamed. They went and sat on the bench. They did not look at each other. They were quiet.
After a while, Anna said, "I'm sorry. I did not mean to quarrel with you. I like to play with you. You are my friend."
Ben said, "I'm sorry too. I did not mean to quarrel with you. I like to play with you. You are my friend."
They looked at the new boy. He said, "I'm sorry too. I did not mean to quarrel with you. I was rude and selfish. I want to play with you. Can you be my friends?"
Anna and Ben smiled and said, "Yes, we can be your friends. You can play with us. We can share our toys. We can make new sand castles together."
They hugged and said, "We are sorry, lady. We will not quarrel again. We will be nice to each other."
The lady smiled and said, "That's good. I'm glad you are friends. You can have your toys back. But remember, be kind and dependable. That's how you make good friends."
Anna and Ben and the new boy said, "Thank you, lady. We will remember. We will be kind and dependable."
They took their toys and went back to the sand. They played together and had fun. They made new sand castles. They were happy.

"What is this?" Lily asked.
"It's a map, silly," Ben said. "It shows us where the treasure is. Maybe it's buried somewhere in the park. Let's follow it!"

Lily and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make yummy food. They had a big bowl, some flour, some eggs and some milk. They wanted to make pancakes.
"First, we need to crack the eggs," Lily said. She took an egg and tapped it on the edge of the bowl. But she tapped too hard and the egg broke in her hand. She felt the sticky yolk and the sharp shell. She made a face and said, "Ew!"
Ben laughed and said, "That's okay, Lily. We have more eggs. Here, let me help you." He took another egg and cracked it gently into the bowl. He gave Lily a spoon and said, "Now, we need to stir the eggs with the milk and the flour."
Lily and Ben took turns stirring the batter with the spoon. They made sure there were no lumps. They were having fun. They sang a song as they stirred. "Stir, stir, stir the batter, make it nice and smooth. Stir, stir, stir the batter, we will eat it soon."
When the batter was ready, Lily and Ben poured some of it onto a hot pan. They watched as it bubbled and turned golden. They smelled the sweet aroma. They were hungry and excited. They wanted to flip the pancake.
"Can I flip it, Ben?" Lily asked. She felt nervous. She had never flipped a pancake before. She was afraid she would drop it or burn it.
"Sure, Lily. You can flip it. Just be careful and use the spatula," Ben said. He handed her a flat tool. He was nervous too. He hoped Lily would do it right.
Lily took the spatula and slid it under the pancake. She lifted it up and tried to toss it in the air. But she did not toss it high enough. The pancake fell back onto the pan and folded in half. It looked like a taco.
Lily and Ben gasped. They looked at the pancake. They looked at each other. They did not know what to do. They felt sad and disappointed. They had ruined their pancake.
But then, they heard a voice behind them. It was their mom. She had been watching them from the door. She smiled and said, "Wow, what a beautiful pancake! I love how you folded it. It looks like a special treat. Can I have a bite?"
Lily and Ben smiled too. They realized their pancake was not ruined. It was just different. They were proud of their pancake. They said, "Yes, mom. You can have a bite. We made it for you."
They cut a piece of the pancake and gave it to their mom. She tasted it and said, "Mmm, this is delicious. You are such good chefs. Thank you for making me this pancake."
Lily and Ben hugged their mom and said, "You're welcome, mom. We love you."
They shared the rest of the pancake and enjoyed it. They did not care that it was folded. They thought it was yummy and fun. They learned that sometimes, mistakes can be good. They decided to make more pancakes and fold them in different ways. They called them foldy-cakes. They had a great time.

Sara and Tom were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. But they were not allowed to go too far, because there might be sharks in the deep.
One day, they saw a big boat on the water. It had a sign that said "Shark Tour". Sara and Tom wanted to go on the boat and see the sharks. They asked their mom and dad, but they said no. They said it was too dangerous and scary.
"But we want to see the sharks!" Sara and Tom said. "They are not scary, they are cool!"
"No, they are not cool, they are dull," their mom and dad said. "They have no colors, no smiles, no fun. They only have sharp teeth and fins. They are not nice to other fish or people. You would not like them."
Sara and Tom were sad and angry. They did not understand why their mom and dad did not let them see the sharks. They thought their mom and dad were dull and boring.
They decided to sneak away from their mom and dad and go on the boat. They ran to the boat and climbed on board. They saw a man with a hat and a net. He was the shark tour guide.
"Hello, kids," he said. "Are you ready to see the sharks?"
"Yes, we are!" Sara and Tom said. "We love sharks!"
The man smiled and took them to the side of the boat. He pointed to the water and said, "Look, there they are!"
Sara and Tom looked and saw many sharks swimming around the boat. They were big and gray and had sharp teeth and fins. They looked dull and scary.
Sara and Tom felt afraid. They did not love sharks anymore. They wanted to go back to their mom and dad.
"Can we go back, please?" they asked the man.
"Sorry, kids, you can't," the man said. "You have to stay here and watch the sharks. That's what you wanted, right?"
Sara and Tom realized they made a mistake. They wished they had listened to their mom and dad. They wished they had accepted their mom and dad's words and not gone on the boat.
They learned a lesson that day. They learned that sharks are not cool, they are dull and dangerous. They learned that their mom and dad are not dull and boring, they are wise and caring. They learned that they should accept their mom and dad's rules and not do things that might hurt them. They learned that sometimes, the best things are not on the boat, but on the beach.

"Of course, fox," the owl said. "What do you want to know?"
The fox smiled.
"Can I clean myself again tomorrow?" he asked.

Once there was a little boy who was playing in the garden. He saw a delicate wheat field nearby. His eyes sparkled with excitement. He ran over to the wheat field and opened the gate.
'Hi, who are you?' asked a voice.
The little boy looked up and saw a mouse standing in the wheat.
'My name is Thomas,' he replied.
The mouse smiled. 'It's so nice to meet you, Thomas. I'm Millie. Would you like to help me pick some wheat?'
Thomas nodded eagerly. He carefully picked the delicate wheat and helped Millie fill a basket. When they were finished, they opened the gate and said goodbye.
Thomas went home feeling happy. He had made a new friend and had a lot of fun finding the wheat.


Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She had a favorite cloth. It was very soft and she took it everywhere she went. One day, Lucy went to the park with her mom and her cloth.
At the park, Lucy saw a boy named Tom. He wanted to play with Lucy's cloth. Lucy said, "Okay, but be careful." Tom played with the cloth, but he did not listen to Lucy. He got the cloth dirty. Lucy was sad and Tom was ashamed.
Tom said, "I'm sorry, Lucy. I will clean it." He took the cloth to his mom. She washed it and made it clean again. Tom gave the clean cloth back to Lucy. He promised to be careful next time. Lucy smiled and they played together. From then on, Tom always listened and did not repeat his mistake.


One day, a little shrimp was swimming in the sea. He was a selfish shrimp and did not like to share his toys with other sea friends. He loved to play with his ball all by himself.
A big fish saw the shrimp playing alone and swam over to him. "Can I play with you?" the big fish asked. The selfish shrimp thought for a moment, and then he said, "No, I want to play alone."
The big fish felt sad and swam away. Then, a little crab came up to the shrimp and said, "Let's clap and dance together!" The shrimp thought about it and decided to give it a try. They clapped their little claws and danced around in the water.
As they danced, more sea friends joined them. The shrimp began to feel happy playing with his friends. He learned that sharing and playing together was more fun than being selfish and playing alone. From that day on, the shrimp shared his toys and played with all his sea friends.


Ben and Lily are twins. They like to play in the garden with their dog, Spot. One day, they see a big green plant with red balls on it. They run to the plant and pick some red balls.
"Look, Spot, we have peppers!" Ben says. He holds a pepper in his hand and shows it to the dog. Spot sniffs the pepper and barks.
"Can we eat them, Ben?" Lily asks. She likes to eat fruits and vegetables. She thinks they are healthy and yummy.
"I don't know, Lily. Maybe we should ask Mommy first," Ben says. He is not sure if the peppers are good or bad. He remembers that some plants can make you sick.
They take the peppers to the kitchen, where Mommy is making lunch. They show her their peppers and ask her if they can eat them.
"Wow, you found some peppers in the garden! Good job, Ben and Lily!" Mommy says. She smiles and hugs them. "Yes, you can eat them. They are healthy and tasty. But be careful, some of them are very hot and spicy. They can make your mouth burn."
Mommy washes the peppers and cuts them into pieces. She gives each twin a piece of pepper to try. Ben bites his pepper and makes a funny face. He spits it out and drinks some water.
"Ow, ow, ow! This pepper is too hot! It hurts my mouth!" Ben says. He does not like the pepper.
Lily bites her pepper and smiles. She likes the pepper. It is sweet and crunchy.
"Yum, yum, yum! This pepper is good! It makes my mouth happy!" Lily says. She eats more pepper.
Mommy laughs and gives them some bread and cheese to eat with the peppers. She tells them that peppers are good for them. They have vitamins and colors. They can make them strong and smart.
Ben and Lily eat their lunch and share some peppers with Spot. They like to try new things. They start to like peppers more and more. They say thank you to Mommy and the plant. They are happy and healthy.


One day, a sweet cat named Kitty was playing with her ball. She loved to have fun with her friends. They played all day in the sun.
But then, something unexpected happened. Kitty's ball rolled into the street. She ran after it and got hurt. Her friends were so sad and scared.
A big, red ambulance came to help Kitty. The nice people took care of her. And guess what? The ambulance driver was Kitty's long-lost brother! They were so happy to see each other. Kitty got better and they all played together again.


One day, a little dog named Max went for a walk. He saw many cars in the traffic. Max wanted to cross the road, but there were too many cars. He had to wait for the cars to stop. Max started to shiver because it was cold and windy.
Max saw a girl named Lily on the other side of the road. She had a big, warm coat. Lily called out to Max, "Don't shiver, little dog! I will help you cross the road."
When the cars stopped, Lily took Max's paw and they crossed the road together. Max was happy and stopped shivering. Lily said, "Let's go to the store and buy you a coat."
At the store, they found an expensive coat for Max. It was too much money. They looked more and found a coat that was not expensive. Max put on the coat and felt warm. Max and Lily were happy and walked home together.


Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She had a hidden toy box in her room. Mia loved to play with her toys and share them with her friends.
One day, Mia's friend, Tim, came to play. Tim had an opinion about the toys. He said, "I think the blue bear is the best toy." Mia did not agree. She liked the red ball more. But Mia knew it was okay to have different ideas. So, she accepted Tim's opinion.
Mia and Tim played with the blue bear and the red ball all day. They had so much fun together. In the end, they both learned that it was good to listen and accept what others think. And they stayed best friends forever.


Once upon a time, there was a little gray cat. The cat lived near a big house with a tall chimney. One day, the cat climbed up the chimney and got stuck. The cat was scared and sad.
A little boy named Tim saw the cat in the chimney. He wanted to help the cat. Tim said, "Don't worry, cat! I will care for you and get you out!" Tim tried to reach the cat, but the chimney was too high.
Tim asked his big sister, Sue, for help. Sue was mad at first because she was busy. But she saw the cat and knew she had to help. Together, Tim and Sue found a long stick. They used the stick to get the cat out of the chimney.
The gray cat was happy and thanked Tim and Sue. Tim said, "We are glad we could help you, cat. We will always care for you." From that day on, the cat lived with Tim and Sue, and they all became the best of friends.
